name: 2-Step Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013803/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/2-step-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 can (10.75 ounces) reduced-sodium cream of chicken soup

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a skillet at a medium-high setting.
Add chicken and cook for ten minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Stir the soup and water together in the skillet and heat it to a boil.
Return the chicken to the skillet. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for an additional 10 minutes, or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 degrees F.

notes.text: This recipe uses reduced-sodium cream of chicken soup.

name: 20-Minute Chicken Creole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013807/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/20-minute-chicken-creole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 can (14.5 ounces) no salt added diced tomatoes

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat pan over medium-high heat (350 degrees F in an electric skillet). Add vegetable oil and chicken and cook until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 degrees F (3-5 minutes).
Reduce heat to medium (300 degrees F in electric skillet).
Add tomatoes with juice, chili sauce*, green pepper, celery, onion, garlic, basil, parsley, and cayenne pepper..
Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and simmer, covered for 10-15 minutes.
Serve over hot, cooked rice or whole wheat pasta.

* Store bought chili sauce can be high in sodium. You can make your own chili sauce by mixing these ingredients: 1 can (8 ounces) tomato sauce; 1 Tablespoon vinegar; 1 teaspoon packed brown sugar; 1 teaspoon chili powder

name: 3-Can Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013810/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/3-can-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium black beans, undrained (or pinto, kidney, or red beans)
1 can (15.2 ounces) reduced sodium corn, drained (or 10-oz package of frozen corn)
1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium crushed tomatoes, undrained
1 teaspoon chili powder (or more, to taste)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place the contents of all 3 cans into a pan.
Add chili powder to taste.
Stir to mix.
Continue to stir over medium heat until heated thoroughly.
Refrigerate leftovers.

name: 5 A Day Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013814/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/5-day-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups chopped green peppers (or red, yellow, or orange peppers)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash all of the vegetables and mix them together in a large mixing bowl.
Top this colorful meal with the nonfat or low-fat dressing of your choice.

notes.text: The dressing is not included in the nutritional analysis. Each serving = 5 cups of vegetables (Eight 5-A-Day servings).

name: Ambrosia
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013818/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/ambrosia
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (20 ounces) pineapple chunks in juice, drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain pineapple and oranges. Use juice as beverage.
Combine fruit with marshmallows and coconut.
Fold in yogurt.
Chill.
Serve.

name: Angel Food Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013822/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/angel-food-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F. In a large mixing bowl, beat the egg whites until they are foamy.
Add the cream of tartar and beat until stiff, but not dry. Gradually beat in the sugar
Add the vanilla and salt and then gently fold in the flour.
Pour the mix into an angel food tubular 10-inch pan and bake for 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until the top is nicely browned.

name: Anytime Pizza
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013824/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/anytime-pizza
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 mini baguette or Italian bread, about 9" long (split lengthwise, or 2 split English muffins)
1/2 cup part-skim mozzarella or cheddar cheese, shredded
1/4 cup mushrooms, fresh or canned, sliced

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toast the bread or English muffin until slightly brown.
Top bread or muffin with pizza sauce, vegetables and low-fat cheese.
Sprinkle with Italian seasoning as desired.
Return bread to toaster oven (or regular oven preheated to 350 degrees F).
Heat until cheese melts.
serving_size: 1 slice, 1 English muffin or 1/2 of recipe

name: Apple Banana Salad with Peanuts
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013851/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-banana-salad-peanuts
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 1/2 medium apples, sliced (14 oz. of sliced apples)

steps: Whisk together dressing ingredients.
Slice bananas.
In a large salad bowl, toss mixed greens, banana and apple slices, peanuts, and dressing.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with 8 ounce non-fat milk and one slice of rustic whole-grain bread. Tips on how to select and store bananas:

name: Apple Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013859/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 10 tablespoons unsalted butter (1 full stick + 2 tablespoons)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Beat butter with sugar until creamy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating until well blended.
Add flour, baking powder, and lemon rind, beat 4 minutes.
Pour into greased 9-inch spring-form pan.
Arrange the apples on the batter, sprinkle with 2 teaspoons sugar.
Bake 1 hour at 350 degrees F in preheated oven.
Remove from pan, brush apples with jam, cool.

name: Apple Carrot Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013902/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-carrot-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound lean pork, cut into chunks
4 medium apples, cored and quartered (with skin)
4 large carrots, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot over high heat, combine all ingredients, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium and simmer until soup reduces to about 8 cups of liquid, about 3 to 4 hours.
Skim fat from surface and serve.
Store leftover soup covered in refrigerator for up to 3 days.

name: Apple & Chicken Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013848/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-chicken-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 chicken breasts (skinless, cooked, diced, about 2 cups)
16 lettuce leaves (Bibb, Romaine, green or red leaf)

steps: Cut apples in quarters; remove core and chop.
In a medium size bowl, mix all ingredients, except lettuce.
To serve, arrange lettuce on serving plates top with apple and chicken salad.

notes.text: Weekly Menu Planning Tip: When you're planning a dinner with chicken cook up extra chicken breast and refrigerate for later use in this salad. Serve with 8 ounce non-fat milk and 1 slice rustic whole grain bread.

name: Apple Chunk Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013908/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-chunk-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
4 cups apples, divided (2 cups chopped into chunks, 2 cups sliced)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
In a large bowl, mix sugar, oil and eggs together. Beat well.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, salt, cinnamon, and baking soda. Add to egg batter and mix well.
Add 2 cups of apple chunks and applesauce to the batter. Stir to combine.
Coat an 8x8-inch baking pan with vegetable oil spray and pour in batter.
Bake until done, about 1 hour.
Place 2 cups of apple slices on top of apple cake and serve.

notes.text: Batter will be very thick. This is normal.

name: Apple Cinnamon Bars
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013911/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-cinnamon-bars
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Put the flour, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, brown sugar, and oats in the mixing bowl. Stir together.
Add the margarine to the bowl. Use the 2 table knives to mix the ingredients and cut them into crumbs.
Lightly grease the bottom and sides of the baking dish with cooking spray.
Spread half of the crumb mixture in the greased baking dish.
Remove the core from the apples and slice them. Put the apple slices into the baking dish.
Top the apples with the rest of the crumb mixture.
Bake in the oven for 40-45 minutes.
Cut into squares. It will fall apart easily.

notes.text: You can use applesauce (16 ounces) or canned apples in place of fresh apples. You can use either peeled or unpeeled apples.

name: Apple Coffee Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013916/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-coffee-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 5 cups tart apples, cored, peeled, and chopped
1/4 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Lightly oil a 13x9x2 inch pan.
In a large mixing bowl, combine apples with sugar, raisins, and pecans; mix well. Let stand 30 minutes.
Stir in oil, vanilla, and egg. Sift together flour, baking soda, and cinnamon; stir into apple mixture about 1/3 at a time, just enough to moisten dry ingredients.
Turn batter into pan. Bake 35-40 minutes. Cool cake slightly before serving.

name: Apple Coleslaw
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013920/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-coleslaw
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Wash the cabbage. Cut it into fine shreds, until you have 2 cups of cabbage.
Peel the carrot. Grate it with a grater.
Chop half a green pepper into small pieces.
Remove the core, and chop the apple.
Put the cabbage, carrot, green pepper, and apple in a large mixing bowl. Stir together.
Put the yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, and dill weed in a small bowl. Stir together to make a dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad. Toss to mix.
Add salt and pepper to taste.

name: Apple Corn Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013925/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-corn-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 ounces boneless, skinless chicken breast (cut to 1/2" cubes)
1 3/4 cups canned yellow corn (15.2 ounce can, no-salt-added, drained)
2 red apples, such as Braeburn, Empire, or Fuji (chopped, skin on)
1 can can (15 oz) black beans (low sodium, drained and rinsed)

steps: In a stockpot, heat 1 tbsp. olive oil; add chicken and brown (about 5 minutes). Remove chicken from pan.
Heat remaining olive oil in same pot; add onions and garlic and sauté until soft.
Add corn and sauté until golden brown. Add apple, cumin, and cayenne pepper (if desired); cook about 3-4 minutes. Let cool about 5 minutes.
Set aside about 1 cup of mixture. Purée remainder in food processor or blender, adding a portion of water, if needed, and return to pot.
Add browned chicken, black beans, chiles, bouillon, and water. Bring to boil and simmer about 15 minutes. Chicken should be cooked to 165 ºF.
To serve, ladle soup in bowls and top with non-puréed portion of apple corn mixture.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a whole-grain tortilla and an 8 ounce glass of fat-free (skim) milk.

name: Apple Cranberry Salad Toss
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013928/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-cranberry-salad-toss
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss lettuce, apples, walnuts, cranberries, and onions in a large bowl.
Add dressing; toss to coat. Serve immediately.

name: Apple Crisp
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013931/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-crisp-0
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Grease the bottom and sides of a square 9 x 9" pan.
Remove the cores from the apples. Slice the apples. Spread the sliced apples on the bottom of the pan.
Cut the margarine into small pieces and put in a medium-sized bowl.
Add the oatmeal, flour, brown sugar and cinnamon.
Using two knives, cut the margarine into the mixture until it looks like small crumbs.
Sprinkle the mixture over the top of the apples.
Bake in the oven for about 20 minutes.

notes.text: For different tastes, try other fruits like cherries, pears, peaches, or plums.

name: Apple, Fennel & Chicken Salad with Couscous
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042559/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-fennel-chicken-salad-couscous
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/8 cup walnuts (chopped, may use pecans or almonds)

steps: Slice chicken breasts crosswise into 1/2 inch strips.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in large skillet over medium heat.
Add chicken, cook 8-10 minutes until done, stirring occasionally, remove from heat.
While chicken is sautéing, cook couscous according to package directions, let cool.
Core and chop apples, place in large bowl; toss with 1 tablespoon lemon juice.
Chop fennel bulb (discarding stem and fronds) and add to bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk remaining oil and lemon juice with balsamic vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Add chicken, couscous, spinach, and nuts to bowl with apples and fennel.
Drizzle with dressing, toss to coat, and serve.
Can be made several hours ahead and refrigerated.

notes.text: Weekly Menu Planning Tip : When you are planning a dinner with chicken, cook up extra chicken breast and refrigerate for later use with another recipe. Serve with 8 ounce non-fat milk.

name: Apple Oatmeal Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013933/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-oatmeal-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Place 6 cupcake holders in baking tin.
In a mixing bowl, add milk and applesauce. Stir until blended.
Stir in flour, oats, sugar, baking powder, and cinnamon. Mix until moistened (do not over mix).
Gently stir in the chopped apples.
Spoon into cupcake holders.
Bake for 15-20 minutes or until an inserted toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in pan 5 minutes before serving. Store unused portions in an airtight container.

notes.text: Optional toppings: raisins, walnuts.

name: Apple Pistachio Crisp
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013937/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-pistachio-crisp
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 apples (such as Honeycrisp, cored and cut into 1” chunks and unpeeled)

steps: Place rack in center of oven and preheat to 350 ºF.
Place sliced apples, raisins, and lemon juice in 8x8 inch pan or baking dish; toss.
In a bowl, mix remaining ingredients except melted margarine.
Add melted margarine and mix until texture is consistent. Sprinkle over apple-raisin mixture.
Bake uncovered 45-50 minutes or until apples are tender.

notes.text: Serving Suggestion: Serve with an 8 oz. glass of fat-free (skim) milk, 3 oz. boneless, skinless chicken breast, and ½ cup green beans.

name: Apple-Sage Wild Rice Stuffing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021820/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-sage-wild-rice-stuffing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 medium red apple, such as Jonathan or Gala (halved, cored, and diced, about 1 1/2 cup total)
1 medium jalapeno pepper (seeded (if desired) and finely chopped OR 1/4 tsp dried pepper flakes)
1 1/2 tablespoons chopped fresh sage (or 1 1/2 tsp dried rubbed sage)

steps: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pecans and cook 2-3 minutes or until beginning to brown, stirring frequently. Set aside on separate plate.
Heat 1 teaspoon of the oil over medium heat. Cook the celery and onion 8 minutes or until beginning to lightly brown on edge, stirring occasionally.
Add the apples and cook 4 minutes or until tender crisp.
Stir in the pecans and the remaining ingredients and cook 3-4 minutes or until the rice mixture is heated, stirring occasionally.

notes.text: Chef's Notes: Use any of your favorite nuts in place of pecans. Or, leave them out if someone is allergic. Materials: You will need a large skillet, measuring cups, measuring spoons, mixing spoon, and a sharp knife.

name: Apple Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031540/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons lite mayonnaise-type dressing (or light mayonnaise)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix orange juice with salad dressing or mayonnaise.
Toss apples, celery, raisins and nuts with the dressing mixture.

name: Apple Salad with Sweet & Tangy Yogurt Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215050/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-salad-sweet-tangy-yogurt-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash apples, celery, and carrots before dicing/grating.
Toss apples with lemon juice.
Add celery, carrots and raisins.
Fold yogurt into apple mixture.
Cover. Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.
Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Apple Sandwiches
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020536/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-sandwiches
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut apple in half from the stem down and lay each half cut-side down on a cutting board. Slice each half into 6 half-round slices and cut out the core.
Spread 1/2 teaspoon peanut butter on one side of each apple slice.
Put 4 to 6 raisins on top of the peanut butter on one apple slice. Top with another apple slice, peanut-butter side down. Squeeze gently.
Continue with remaining apple slices.

name: Apple Slice Pancakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035625/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-slice-pancakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lightly coat a griddle or skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium heat.
Peel, core and thinly slice apple into rings.
In a large mixing bowl, combine ingredients for pancake batter. Stir until ingredients are evenly moist. (Small lumps are ok! Over-mixing makes pancakes tough.)
For each pancake, place apple ring on griddle and pour about 1/4 cup batter over apple ring, starting in the center and covering the apple.
Cook until bubbles appear. Turn and cook other side until lightly brown.

notes.text: To test the griddle to see if it is hot, sprinkle it with a few drops of water. When the drops sizzle and dance, you are ready to cook! The easiest way to pour the batter onto the hot griddle is to use a 1/4 cup measuring cup for each pancake. If the first pancake is too brown, lower the heat.

name: Apple-Stuffed Squash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034953/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-stuffed-squash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut squash into halves and remove seeds. Place in a glass dish, cover with plastic wrap and microwave on high for 5 minutes.
Melt butter in a separate bowl in the microwave. Mix in apples, sugar, and cinnamon. Microwave for 1 1/2 minutes.
Spoon apple filling into each squash half. Cover and microwave on high for 3-5 minutes until squash and apples are tender.
Serve warm.

name: Apple Wedges with Pumpkin Almond Butter
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032546/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apple-wedges-pumpkin-almond-butter
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup pumpkin puree (canned or from scratch)
1/3 cup almond butter (or crunchy peanut butter)

steps: Mix together dip ingredients.
Serve with apple slices.

name: Applesauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035014/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/applesauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and then cut apples in quarters. Apples can be peeled, but fiber will be decreased.
Combine apples and water in saucepan. Heat to boiling. Turn heat to low as soon as the water is boiling.
Simmer over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes or until apples are tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Stir in sugar and heat until sugar is dissolved.

notes.text: Serving suggestion: Add 1 tablespoon cinnamon and stir before serving. Additional sugar can be added to increase sweetness. Brown sugar can be used instead of white.

name: Applesauce Cookies
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034822/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/applesauce-cookies
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup (1 stick) margarine (or butter or shortening)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F. Prepare pan or cookie sheet (see below).
Cream together sugar, margarine, and egg.
In a separate bowl, combine baking soda, flour, salt, and cinnamon. Mix well.
Stir flour mixture into shortening mixture just until moist.
Add applesauce, raisins, and nuts (if using).
For Cookies: Drop dough by heaping teaspoon several inches apart on a greased baking sheet. Bake at 350 °F for 10 to 12 minutes. For Cake: Bake at 350 °F in an 8x8 inch pan for 40 minutes.

notes.text: To check cake for doneness, pierce top of cake with a toothpick. Cake is done when toothpick comes out clean.

name: Applesauce Loaf Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033353/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/applesauce-loaf-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands well with soap and warm water.
Pre-heat the oven to 350 degrees F. Grease two 8x4x2 inch loaf pans.
Toast walnuts in an ungreased skillet pan. Stir while heating on medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes. They are done when they are brown and smell nutty. Set aside to cool.
Mix applesauce, egg, sugar, oil and vanilla in a large bowl.
Mix flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and nutmeg together in a smaller bowl.
Pour flour mixture into applesauce mixture.
Stir in raisins and cooled toasted nuts.
Pour half of the batter into each greased pan. Bake for 45-55 minutes.
Remove cakes from the oven. Cool for 10 minutes. Remove from pans to finish cooling. For best taste, let cakes cool a few hours before serving.

name: Applesauce Pancakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022211/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/applesauce-pancakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup dry milk powder, non-fat instant
1 tablespoon canola oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water and clean food preparation area.
In a medium mixing bowl, combine applesauce, dry milk powder, water, eggs, and oil.
Add flour, sugar, cinnamon, and baking powder.
Stir until mixture has only small lumps.
Place large skillet on medium-high heat.
Spray skillet with non-stick cooking spray.
Pour 1/2 cup batter onto skillet.
Turn pancake when bubbles form on top of batter.
Cook the other side for about 1 minute or until golden brown.

name: Apricot & Lemon Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042110/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/apricot-lemon-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rub cumin over chicken and place in skillet.
Cook on medium-high for 6 minutes on each side, or until cooked through. Remove from pan and keep warm.
Add apricot spread, lemon juice, and water to skillet. On medium heat, stir until smooth.
Spoon sauce over chicken and serve warm.

notes.text: May substitute approximately 3 Tablespoons of lemon juice for 1 fresh lemon, juiced. Could also substitute honey for apricot spread. · Honey should not be fed to children under 1 year of age.

serving_size: 1 chicken breast with sauce (1/4 of recipe)

name: Argentinean Grilled Steak with Salsa Criolla
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045719/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/argentinean-grilled-steak-salsa-criolla
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 large, ripe tomato (cored, seeded, and finely chopped, about 1/2 cup)
1/4 small red onion (finely chopped, about 1/4 cup)

steps: In a small bowl, mix together tomato, onions, parsley, olive oil, vinegar, garlic, oregano, low-sodium adobo seasoning and crushed red pepper.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or up until 48 hours.
Heat grill to medium-high heat. Sprinkle steak on both sides with low-sodium adobo seasoning. Place steak on hot, greased grill grates.
Cook, flipping once, until steak is well browned on both sides and cooked to 145 °F (about 6 minutes for medium-rare).
Let rest for 5 minutes. Thinly slice steak.
Divide steak evenly among serving plates. Top with reserved Salsa Criolla.
For the sauce: For the steak:

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Pair with Arepas (cornmeal patties popular in Colombia and Venezuela) and a healthy Quinoa Salad for a South American Steak Supper.

name: Chicken and Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020629/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/arroz-con-pollo-chicken-and-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 whole chicken, cut up, skin removed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet heat oil over medium-high heat and brown chicken on both sides.
Add green pepper, onion, and garlic and cook for about 5 minutes.
Add tomato, chicken broth, bay leaf. Add salt & pepper to taste.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Add rice, stir well, cover and simmer for 20-30 minutes longer, or until all liquid has been absorbed and chicken is tender.
Add peas, cook until hot. Remove bay leaf before serving.

name: Asian Mango Chicken Wraps
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042602/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/asian-mango-chicken-wraps
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 cups shredded Savoy or Napa cabbage

steps: Cut mangos, vegetables, and chicken. Place in a mixing bowl and toss until well mixed.
In a small mixing bowl, whisk together cream cheese, peanut butter, and soy sauce.

To assemble: lay out tortillas on a flat surface. On each tortilla, spread 1/4 of cream cheese mixture and top with mango, vegetable, and chicken mix. Roll up tightly, tucking in ends of tortilla. Secure with toothpicks.
To serve, cut each wrap in half.
If not serving immediately, refrigerate; keeps well overnight.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of non-fat milk.

name: Asparagus with Gremolata Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040501/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/asparagus-gremolata-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups asparagus, washed and trimmed (about 8 ounces)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook asparagus in a large pot of boiling water until tender, about 4 minutes.
Drain: rinse with cold water to cool quickly, and drain again.
Pat dry; wrap in a paper towel and then plastic wrap and refrigerate.
Melt margarine in a heavy large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add lemon peel and garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Add asparagus and toss to coat.
Sprinkle with lemon juice. Sauté until asparagus is heated through and coated with Gremolata sauce, about 3 minutes.
Transfer to platter. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

name: Asparagus, Mandarin Orange, Chicken, and Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042317/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/asparagus-mandarin-orange-chicken-and-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 tablespoons mandarin orange juice (reserved from oranges)
2 - 11 oz cans mandarin oranges (drained, reserve juice)
12 ounces cooked chicken breast (cut into chunks)

steps: In a small bowl, whisk vinaigrette ingredients, set aside.
Cook rice according to package directions.
Place whole trimmed asparagus in a large skillet with 1 1/2 inches of water.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, for 2-5 minutes.
Rinse with cool water and cut into 1-inch pieces.
In a medium size bowl, toss all ingredients.

notes.text: Weekly Meal Planning Tip: When you're planning a dinner with chicken, cook up extra chicken breast and refrigerate for later use in this salad.

name: Au Gratin Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034934/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/au-gratin-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 medium russet potatoes, peeled and sliced into 1/4 inch slices

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare a large casserole baking pan (9" x 13") by coating lightly with oil or cooking oil spray.
Place a layer of potatoes in pan, using approximately 1/4 of potatoes.
Sprinkle layer with 1/4 cup chopped raw onion, 1/4 of the cheese, 1/2 tablespoon margarine, 1 tablespoon flour, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and sprinkling of black pepper.
Repeat layers, making a total of 4.
Meanwhile heat milk over low heat.
Pour warm milk over all ingredients in casserole dish.
Bake at 350 degrees F for one hour.
Refrigerate leftovers within two hours.
Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare a large casserole baking pan (9" x 13") by coating lightly with oil or cooking oil spray.
Make a white sauce by melting margarine in a small pan. Stir in flour. Gradually add milk, stirring constantly.
Cook, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened. Remove from heat. Stir in cheese until melted and smooth.
Add salt and pepper.
Place a layer of potatoes and onion in a prepared casserole pan, using approximately 1/4 of the potatoes and 1/4 cup onion.
Spread with 1/2 cup of the sauce prepared in steps 2 and 3.
Repeat layers, making a total of 4.
Bake at 350 degrees F for one hour.
Refrigerate leftovers within two hours.
Quickest Method: Creamiest Method:

name: Autumn Vegetable Succotash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040834/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/autumn-vegetable-succotash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
2 teaspoons dried sage (or 2 tablespoons fresh, coarsely chopped)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large deep skillet over medium-high heat, add oil.
Add onion; cook until translucent (2 minutes). Add garlic, bell peppers, zucchini, squash, lima beans, and corn.
Season as desired; cook, stirring, until vegetables are tender (10 minutes or longer).
Stir in sage and serve.

notes.text: Can use dry or fresh herbs. Add others as desired.

name: Avocado and Corn Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022515/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/avocado-and-corn-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss avocado, corn, tomatoes, cilantro, lime juice, and salt in a medium bowl.
Chill one hour and then serve.

name: Avocado Black Bean Taquitos
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042404/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/avocado-black-bean-taquitos
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 ripe, fresh avocado, halved, pitted, peeled, and mashed
1/2 cup canned black beans, rinsed (low sodium)
1/2 cup red or yellow bell peppers, seeded and diced
1 tablespoon fresh jalapeño, seeded and minced
1/2 cup plain non-fat Greek yogurt (4 oz)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Using a fork, mash the avocado and black beans together in bowl. Stir in cumin, garlic powder and salt.
Spread approximately 2 Tbsp. of the mixture onto a corn tortilla, dividing equally between 10 tortillas. Roll tightly to form 10 taquitos.

Place taquitos into air fryer at 400°F degrees for 5 minutes. When timer goes off, flip and put back into air fryer for 5 more minutes. Depending on air fryer you may need to decrease time to 3 to 4 minutes per side.
While taquitos are cooking, combine cherry tomatoes, bell peppers, jalapeño, onion, cilantro, and lime juice in a small bowl to make fresh pico de gallo.
Once taquitos are golden brown and crispy, remove from air fryer and top with fresh pico de gallo and Greek yogurt.

notes.text: For more information, visit: https://loveonetoday.com/

name: Avocado Breakfast Bruschetta
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042409/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/avocado-breakfast-bruschetta
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup chopped fresh basil (plus 2 tablespoons for garnish)

steps: Dice avocado, tomatoes, and green onions.
Peel and chop hard-boiled eggs.
Reserving 2 tbsp. basil for garnish, gently toss first five ingredients in a small bowl. Add pepper to taste.
Toast baguette slices and smear with ricotta cheese.
Top with avocado mix and garnish with chopped basil.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of fat-free (skim) milk.

name: Avocado Melon Breakfast Smoothie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020350/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/avocado-melon-breakfast-smoothie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup 100% apple juice or white grape juice

steps: Cut avocado in half, remove pit.
Scoop out flesh, place in blender.
Add remaining ingredients; blend well.
Serve cold. (Keeps well in refrigerator up to 24 hours. If made ahead, stir gently before pouring into glasses.)

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with one slice toasted whole-wheat bread.

name: Avocado Pita Pockets
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020413/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/avocado-pita-pockets
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 ripe, fresh avocado, halved, pitted, peeled and diced
2 whole grain pita bread pockets, cut in half
1/4 cup canned chickpeas, rinsed and drained
2 tablespoons crumbled Cotija or Feta cheese

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Fill pita pocket half with avocado, chickpeas and cheese, dividing evenly. Heat in microwave for 15 to 20 seconds if desired. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

notes.text: For more information, visit: https://loveonetoday.com/

name: Avocado, Potato, and Grilled Chicken Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021858/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/avocado-potato-and-grilled-chicken-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 ounces frozen pre-cooked grilled chicken strips (about 8 strips) (thawed, cut into bite-size pieces)

steps: In a medium sauce pan, boil potatoes about 20 minutes, until just tender; run under cold water to cool, and cut into chunks.
Peel avocado and cut into chunks; coat with lemon juice.
Whisk olive oil, vinegar, yogurt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Place all ingredients in large bowl. Gently toss.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of non-fat milk, 1 slice of whole-grain bread, and apple slices.

name: Avocado Veggie Bake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215409/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/avocado-veggie-bake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 medium head of cauliflower, cut into 1/2-inch thick slices, then cut into 2-inch pieces, 8 oz. total
1 medium zucchini, sliced into 1/2-inch thick rounds
1 cup reduced fat shredded Mexican or taco seasoned cheese
1 can low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed (~15 oz)
1 ripe, fresh avocado, halved, pitted, peeled and diced

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425F.
Combine olive oil, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and salt.
Brush half of oil mixture on bottom of a 15-inch x 10-inch baking sheet with shallow sides.
Arrange cauliflower and zucchini on baking sheet in single layer and brush with remaining oil mixture.
Roast 20 minutes or until fork tender. Top with black beans, corn and cheese and roast an additional 5 minutes or until heated through and cheese is melted.
Top with tomatoes, avocado, scallions, jalapeño and cilantro.

notes.text: For more information, visit: https://loveonetoday.com

name: Baked Apples and Sweet Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020335/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-apples-and-sweet-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil 5 sweet potatoes in water until they are almost tender.
After the sweet potatoes cool, peel and slice them.
Peel the apples. Remove the cores, and slice the apples.
Preheat the oven to 400 °F.
Grease the casserole dish with butter or margarine.
Put a layer of sweet potatoes on the bottom of the dish.
Add a layer of apple slices.
Add some sugar, salt, and tiny pieces of margarine to the apple layer.
Repeat steps 6, 7, and 8 to make more layers of sweet potatoes, apples, and sugar/salt.
On the top layer of apples, sprinkle the rest of the brown sugar and margarine pieces.
Sprinkle the top layer with nutmeg.
Mix the hot water and honey together. Pour the mix over the top layer.
Bake for about 30 minutes until apples are tender.

notes.text: Honey should not be fed to children under 1 year of age.

name: Baked Bananas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042441/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-bananas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup raisins, or other dried chopped fruit

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Lightly grease a 9x13 inch pan.
Arrange the split bananas in the pan.
Top evenly with brown sugar, small pieces of margarine, raisins, and pecans.
Bake for 30 minutes.

name: Baked Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040918/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 cups navy, kidney, or lima beans (dry, sorted, and rinsed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine apple juice and water. Bring to a boil.
Add beans and simmer for 2 1/2 hours until beans are tender.
Drain beans, reserve the liquid.
Put beans and other ingredients in greased baking dish.
Cover and bake at 250 °F for 3 to 4 hours.
Uncover the last hour of baking and add some reserved liquid if beans become dry.

name: Baked Cauliflower Tots
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042608/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-cauliflower-tots
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups grated or finely chopped cauliflower rice (about half a medium head)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Lightly grease a baking sheet.
In a medium bowl, combine all ingredients and mix well.
Press mixture together to make about 15 small balls or logs and put them on the baking sheet with space between each one.
Bake for 20 minutes or until cooked through. For extra crispy tots, broil for an extra 2 minutes. Watch closely to avoid burning.

name: Baked Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022327/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Put the chicken in a baking pan or casserole dish.
Sprinkle with garlic powder and pepper to taste.
Bake for 1 hour.

name: Baked Chicken Nuggets
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033410/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-chicken-nuggets
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Remove skin and bone; cut thighs into bite-sized pieces.
Place cornflakes in plastic bag and crush by using a rolling pin.
Add remaining ingredients to crushed cornflakes. Close bag tightly and shake until blended.
Add a few chicken pieces at a time to crumb mixture. Shake to coat evenly.
Preheat oven to 400 °F. Lightly grease a cooking sheet.
Place chicken pieces on cooking sheet so they are not touching.
Bake until golden brown, about 12 to 14 minutes.
Lightly grease an 8x12 inch baking dish.
Place chicken pieces on baking dish so they are not touching. Cover with waxed paper and cook on high.
Rotate chicken every 2 to 3 minutes. Cook until tender, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Conventional Method: Microwave Method:

notes.text: To remove bone from chicken thigh: Place chicken on cutting board. Remove skin from thighs. Turn chicken thighs over. Cut around bone and remove it.

name: Baked Chicken with Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031424/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-chicken-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 whole chicken, raw, cut into pieces, skin removed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Place potatoes, carrots, and onions in a large roasting pan.
Put chicken pieces on top of the vegetables.
Mix water, thyme, and pepper. Pour over chicken and vegetables.
Spoon juices over chicken once or twice during cooking.
Bake at 400 °F for one hour or more until browned and tender.

name: Baked Eggs & Cheese
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034557/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-eggs-cheese
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Put oil in a medium baking dish or small cake pan and heat in the oven for a few minutes.
In a medium bowl, beat eggs. Mix in remaining ingredients. Pour into hot pan.
Bake 20 minutes or until eggs are firm. Serve immediately.

notes.text: * 4 eggs and 4 egg whites may be used instead of 6 eggs to reduce fat and cholesterol.

name: Baked Fish
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231030842/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-fish
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound fish fillets (whitefish, trout, or tilapia)

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Place about a 12-inch piece of foil on the counter. Coat the foil with nonstick cooking spray.
Place the fillets in the middle of the foil. If the fillets have skin, place the skin side down.
Spread the onions, salt, pepper, and oil on top of the fillets. If using lemon pepper seasoning, add that too.
Fold the foil over the fish to wrap it. Place foil pouch on a baking sheet, and place it in the oven.
Bake the fish for 15 to 20 minutes until the fish is flaky when tested with a fork.
Divide into four portions and serve.

notes.text: Tip for cooking fish: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for fish is 145 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.

name: Baked Fish and Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020317/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-fish-and-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 white fish fillets (frozen, or cod or perch 4 oz each)
2 cups frozen mixed vegetables (or other vegetables you have on hand)
1 teaspoon lemon juice (or fresh lemon, sliced thin)
1 tablespoon parsley flakes, dried (or fresh, chopped)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 450 °F.
Separate and place fish fillets in center of each tin foil square.
Combine vegetables and diced onion in bowl and mix. Spoon vegetables around fillets.
Sprinkle with lemon juice, top with lemon slices or add lemon zest.
Top with parsley or other herbs if desired.
Fold ends of tin foil together to form leak-proof seal.
Bake for 20 minutes. Serve.
Refrigerate leftovers.
serving_size: 4 oz. fish and 1/2 C. vegetables, 1/4 of recipe (306g)

name: Baked Fish with Creole Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031545/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-fish-creole-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound fish fillets (fresh or frozen, unbreaded)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Thaw fish in refrigerator overnight.
Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Arrange fish in a single layer in baking dish.
Top fish with onion and pepper slices.
In a separate bowl, mix tomato sauce, chili powder, salt, and pepper.
Pour tomato sauce mixture over fish and vegetables.
Cover dish and bake until fish flakes easily with a fork (20-30 minutes).
Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Baked Fish with Tomatoes, Peppers, and Onions
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040447/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-fish-tomatoes-peppers-onions
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound cod fillets, fresh or frozen, skinless and thawed (or other white fleshed fish)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F. Oil or spray a 9 x 13-inch baking dish with vegetable spray.
Cut fish into four pieces and place in baking dish.
Top fish with green peppers, tomatoes, onions and oregano. Bake about 20 minutes or until fish flakes.

name: Baked Lemon Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020623/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-lemon-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 1/2 pounds whole chicken, skinned and cut into 10 pieces
1 1/2 cloves of garlic, thinly sliced (or 1 tsp garlic powder)
4 teaspoons fresh thyme (or 1 tsp dried thyme)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine salt, pepper, garlic, and thyme.
Lay chicken pieces into a 11x13 inch baking pan. Sprinkle seasonings over chicken.
Combine onions, stock, and lemon juice in a sauce pan. Heat to a boil.
Pour hot lemon mixture around chicken. Top each chicken piece with a lemon slice.
Bake for 30 minutes at 400 °F until golden brown and juices are clear colored.

name: Baked Lentils Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041804/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-lentils-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Combine lentils, water, seasonings, onion, and tomatoes.
Place in 2 quart casserole dish.
Cover tightly with lid or foil.
Bake at 350 °F for 30 minutes.
Remove from oven and add carrots. Stir.
Cover and bake 30 minutes longer.
Remove cover and sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake, uncovered 5 minutes, until cheese melts.

name: Baked Meatballs
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214933/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-meatballs
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound ground beef, 90% lean (or ground turkey)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 °F.
Mix all ingredients, shape into balls (about 24 meatballs).
Arrange on baking sheets that have been sprayed with non-stick cooking spray.
Bake at 425 °F for 12-15 minutes. It is best to use a food safety thermometer to check for doneness. It should read 160 °F for ground beef and 165 °F for ground turkey.
If meatballs are being saved for future use, chill rapidly; package in amounts needed per meal and freeze immediately.

name: Baked Parmesan Fish
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031910/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-parmesan-fish
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon thyme sprigs, leaves removed and crushed
4 (6 ounces each) tilapia fish fillets (or other white fish)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F. Place cheese, flour, and thyme in paper bag.
Individually coat fish by gently shaking in bag; discard coating ingredients.
Place fillets in baking pan on rack. Bake for 20 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with fork.
Heat skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion, mushrooms, green onions, and garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, until onions are tender. Season with ground black pepper.
Serve baked fish topped with mushroom mixture.
serving_size: 1 fish fillet with toppings (1/4 of recipe)

name: Baked Pork Chops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231014639/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-pork-chops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Trim fat from pork chops. Place chops in a 13x9 inch baking pan.
Spread onion and peppers on top of chops. Sprinkle with pepper and salt. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Cover pan and cook 30 minutes.
Uncover, turn chops and re-cover with onions and peppers, and continue cooking for an additional 15 minutes or until internal temperature reaches 145 °F.
Garnish with fresh parsley.

name: Baked Potatoes Primavera
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031607/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-potatoes-primavera
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pierce each potato several times with a fork. Microwave on high until tender, about 3-4 minutes per potato.
Steam mixed vegetables until hot.
Mix the sour cream with the herbs and pepper.
Split the potatoes in the center and fill with steamed veggies. Top with sour cream and serve hot.
serving_size: 1 potato with 1/4 of topping, 1/4 of recipe (475g)

name: Baked Rice with Spinach
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045428/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-rice-spinach
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Spray a 2-quart baking dish with vegetable oil spray.
Place thawed spinach in a colander and press to remove excess water.
Place the spinach in a large mixing bowl and add remaining ingredients. Mix until combined.
Transfer the mixture to the baking dish and place in the preheated oven. Bake for 30 minutes.
Cut the casserole into eight squares and serve.

notes.text: Source "Brazilian Rice" This casserole can be prepared 1 day in advance and refrigerated.

name: Baked Salmon with Herbs and Lemon
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215133/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-salmon-herbs-lemon
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 16 ounces salmon, fresh or frozen (or any white fish)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
If using frozen fish, thaw in refrigerator according to package directions.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Separate (or cut) fish into 4 pieces. Place fish in a 13x9x2-inch baking pan.
Combine paprika, garlic and onion powders, pepper, oregano, and thyme in a small bowl.
Sprinkle herb mixture and lemon juice evenly over the fish. Then drizzle melted margarine on top.
Bake until fish flakes easily with a fork, about 20 to 25 minutes.
serving_size: 4 oz. prepared fish or 1/4 of recipe

name: Baked Squash with Apples and Spices
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041644/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-squash-apple-spices
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 1/2 cups winter squash (acorn, butternut, or Hubbard)
1 1/2 cups apples (Macintosh, Granny Smith, or Rome)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Wash and prepare squash and apples (for extra fiber, keep peel on apples).
Cut squash and apples into slices.
Alternate layers of squash and apples in 8x8-inch pan; end with apples.
Sprinkle spices over top layer.
Cover with aluminum foil.
Bake in preheated oven for 45 to 60 minutes, until squash is tender.

name: Baked Tofu
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021714/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-tofu
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 clove garlic, minced (or 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder)
1 teaspoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 package (14 ounces) firm or extra firm tofu, water packed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil.
Drain water from tofu. Wrap tofu in paper towels. Let set for about 5 minutes.
While tofu is draining, combine soy sauce, garlic, ginger, and vegetable oil in a small bowl.
Slice tofu into 1/2 inch thick slices. Place tofu slices on foil lined baking sheet.
Pour soy sauce mixture over tofu. Using a spatula or pancake turner, gently turn slices over to coat both sides with sauce.
Bake tofu for 15 minutes. Turn slices over and bake for another 15 minutes. Tofu should be light golden brown and firm.
Serve hot in place of meat or cut into slices or cubes and add to a stir-fry, fried rice, soup, or salad.

name: Baked Tortilla Chips
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033940/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-tortilla-chips
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven or toaster oven to 400 °F.
Lightly grease a baking sheet with the cooking spray.
Cut tortillas into 8 sections (as if you were cutting a pizza) and place on baking sheet.
Spray tops of tortilla sections with cooking spray and lightly salt, if desired.
Bake for 10 minutes, until crisp and light brown, watching closely so the chips don't burn.

notes.text: Corn tortillas may also be used for less calories and fat.

name: Baked Trout
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035948/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/baked-trout
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 pounds trout fillets, cut into six pieces (or other fish)
1/2 teaspoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Pat fish dry and place in baking dish.
In a separate dish, mix remaining ingredients together and pour over fish.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until fork-tender.

name: Banana Berry Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251223165155/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/banana-berry-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup blueberries or strawberries (fresh or frozen)

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F. Spray a 12-cup muffin pan with non-stick cooking spray.
In a medium-size bowl, combine applesauce, sugar, dried egg mix, banana, and water. Mix well.
In a large bowl mix flours, oats, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Add the applesauce mixture to the bowl with the dry ingredients; mix just until the batter is moist.
Gently add berries into the mixture.
Fill each muffin cup about 3/4 full of batter.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until lightly brown.
Cool for 10 minutes and remove from pan.

name: Banana Bread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033920/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/banana-bread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Peel the bananas. Put them in a mixing bowl. Mash the bananas with a fork.
Add the egg, oil, milk, sugar, salt, baking soda, and baking powder. Mix well with the fork.
Slowly stir the flour into the banana mixture. Stir for 20 seconds until the flour is moistened.
Lightly grease a 8 x 4-inch to 10 x5-inch bread pan with a little oil or cooking spray. Or, line the pan with wax paper.
Pour the batter into the bread pan.
Bake for 45 minutes until a toothpick inserted near the middle comes out clean.
Let the bread cool for 5 minutes before removing it from the pan.

notes.text: The key to good banana bread is to use well-ripened bananas that are covered with brown speckles. Try using half whole wheat flour to add some fiber.

name: Banana Cocoa Yogurt Pops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032550/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/banana-cocoa-yogurt-pops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: mini muffin cups or paper cups

steps: Mash banana with a fork.
Add yogurt to banana and mix well.
Stir in cocoa powder.
Divide into 8 mini muffin cups or 4 small paper cups.
Place in cut paper straws or popsicle sticks.
Freeze and enjoy!

notes.text: Create your own yogurt pops and experiment with different flavors or try out one of these recipes:

name: Banana Cupcakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050720/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/banana-cupcakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a large mixing bowl, cream shortening and sugar using an electric mixer. Add eggs and vanilla, mixing well.
In a medium mixing bowl, combine flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Add dry ingredients (flour mixture) and bananas to creamed mixture (the egg mixture). Mix well until combined.
Place paper baking cups in muffin tin or lightly coat muffin tin with cooking spray. Fill muffin cups 2/3 full of batter.
Bake 20-22 minutes, until golden brown. Remove cupcakes from muffin tin and place on a rack to cool.

name: Banana Oat Cookies
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032021/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/banana-oat-cookies
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup banana, mashed, use overripe banana

steps: Wash hands with soap and water. Make sure utensils and counter top are clean.
Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Mix mashed bananas with yogurt and water.
Add quick oats. Mix well.
Add optional raisins or sunflower seeds if you wish and mix well.
Add optional cinnamon to taste if you wish and mix well.
The batter should be thick and easily to scoop with a spoon.
Grease a baking sheet. Place a tablespoon of dough on the sheet, press lightly a make a flat disk. Repeat with remaining dough. Refrigerate if any is remaining in the bowl.
Bake at 375 °F for 20 minutes. Flip cookies over and return to oven to bake 15 minutes longer or until cookie are crisp.

name: Banana Oatmeal Pancakes with Lentils
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045024/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/banana-oatmeal-pancakes-lentils
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup canola oil (or melted butter or cooking oil of choice)
maple syrup (optional, to serve with pancakes)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small saucepan of boiling water, cook the lentils for 15-20 minutes, until soft. Drain well and set aside.
In a large bowl, stir together the oats, flour, brown sugar, cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
In a smaller bowl, whisk together the yogurt, milk, oil, eggs, and vanilla. Add to the dry ingredients along with the mashed banana and lentils, and stir until just combined.
Set a heavy skillet over medium-high heat, add a drizzle of oil and wipe it around with a paper towel to coat the bottom of the pan.

Cook about 1/2 a cup of batter at a time, spreading it out with the back of a spoon if needed (it will be thick). Cook for a couple of minutes, until bubbles begin to break through the surface and the bottom is golden. Keep the heat to medium, as these will take longer to cook through that most pancakes, and you do not want to burn the bottoms.

Flip with a thin spatula and cook until they are golden on the other side, and springy to the touch. Keep the pancakes warm on a rack set on a baking sheet in a 250 °F oven while you finish cooking the rest.
Serve drizzled with maple syrup, if desired.

name: Banana Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044733/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/banana-oatmeal-raisin-cookies
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Put the margarine in a small saucepan. Melt it on low heat.
Put all the ingredients in a mixing bowl. Mix really well.
Let the mix stand for about 5 minutes, until the oats are wet.
Lightly grease the cookie sheet.
For each cookie, spoon out about 1 tablespoon of dough and drop it onto the greased cookie sheet.
Bake the cookies for 15 to 20 minutes.
Let the cookies cool on the cookie sheet for about 1 minute.
Move the cookies to wire racks or a towel. Let them cool completely.

name: Banana Pancakes with Apple Topping
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041728/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/banana-pancakes-apple-topping
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash apples, remove cores, and slice thinly with peel still on.
Combine apples with the sugar, cinnamon, and water.
Cook in skillet for 10 minutes. Set aside while making pancakes.
Beat eggs. Beat in milk, honey, and oil.
Add flours and baking powder.
Slice bananas and add to mixture.
Coat a large, non-stick frying pan or griddle with non-stick cooking spray. Warm the pan over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Spoon 1/4 cup of the batter onto the heated griddle for each pancake (adjust more or less depending on pancake size).
Cook until the tops are bubbly and the pancakes are dry around the edges. Flip and cook for 2-3 minutes or until golden on both sides. Place pancakes on a platter and keep warm.
Repeat steps 5 and 6 until batter has been used, using more nonstick cooking spray as needed.
Serve pancakes topped with cooked apples.
Apple Topping: Pancakes:

notes.text: Infants 12 months and under should NOT be given honey.

name: Banana Pudding
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031744/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/banana-pudding
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 (3.4 ounce) box instant pudding mix, banana or vanilla
1 (8 ounce) container of fat-free plain yogurt (or non-dairy whipped topping)
2 medium bananas, sliced (or other sliced fruit)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium bowl, combine pudding and milk. Beat with wooden spoon, wire whisk, or electric mixer on lowest speed for 2 minutes
Gently mix yogurt (or whipped topping) with pudding mixture. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Layer fruit slices in the bottom of 8 dessert cups.
Pour the pudding mixture over sliced fruit. Top with more fruit.
Refrigerate until ready to serve, at least 5 minutes. The taste is better if it's refrigerated longer.

name: Banana Split Oatmeal
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215339/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/banana-split-oatmeal
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a microwave safe cereal bowl, mix together the oatmeal and salt. Stir in water.
Microwave on high power for 1 minute. Stir. Microwave on high power for another minute. Stir again.
Microwave an additional 30-60 seconds on high power until the cereal reaches the desired thickness. Stir again.
Top with banana slices and frozen yogurt.

notes.text: The banana split oatmeal can be a snack by itself.

name: Banana Walnut Oatmeal
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033853/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/banana-walnut-oatmeal
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2/3 cup non-fat dry milk mixed with 2 cups water (or 2 cups fluid non-fat or low-fat milk)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small saucepan, combine reconstituted non-fat dry milk, salt, and additional water. Heat over medium heat until steaming hot, but not boiling.
Add oats and cook, stirring until creamy, 1 to 2 minutes.
Remove the pan from heat and stir in mashed banana and maple syrup. Divide between 4 bowls, garnish with walnuts, and serve.

notes.text: You can substitute 2 cups water or 2 cups skim milk for the reconstituted non-fat dry milk.

name: Bananas with Caramel Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022344/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/bananas-with-caramel-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons cornstarch, dissolved in 2 teaspoons water

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Place unpeeled banana on a baking sheet. Prick the skin of each banana several times with the prongs of a fork.
Cook the bananas for about 8 minutes. The skin will turn black.
Over moderate heat, cook the butter, water, and sugar to a medium brown color (it will look like caramel). Remove from heat.
Combine the milk and cornstarch slurry to the caramel mixture. Stir to dissolve.
Return to the heat and bring to a boil, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and cool slightly.
Serve on top of the bananas that have been peeled and sliced lengthwise.

name: Barley Jambalaya
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215235/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/barley-jambalaya
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup diced green, red, yellow, or orange bell pepper

steps: In a colander, rinse barley under cold water.
In a medium pot over high heat, bring barley, water, and bay leaves to a boil. Reduce heat to low and cover. Cook barley until tender and water is absorbed, about 20-30 minutes.
In a colander, drain barley. Set aside.
Peel, rinse, and dice onions. Rinse and dice celery and pepper. Peel and mince garlic.
In a large pot over medium-high heat, heat oil.
Add onions, celery, pepper, and garlic to pot. Mix well. Cook until veggies are soft, about 5 minutes.
Add ground turkey. Cook until internal temperature registers 165 °F on a food thermometer, about 5 minutes more.
Add tomatoes and their juices. Bring to a simmer.
Add spices. Stir to combine. Cover and reduce heat. Cook at a low simmer for 15 minutes.
Add cooked barley to the mixture. Stir to combine. Add more water or broth, if needed. Cook over low heat to bled flavors, about 5-10 minutes more.
Remove bay leaves and serve.
In Advance: Preparation:

notes.text: Materials: You will need a can opener, colander, cutting board, large pot with lid, measuring spoons, medium pot with lid, mixing spoon, and a sharp knife.

name: Barley Pilaf
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021245/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/barley-pilaf
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
green or red bell pepper, chopped (1/2 cup, optional)
1 cup mushrooms, sliced (or 4 ounce can mushrooms, drained)
1 teaspoon low-sodium bouillon (vegetable, beef or chicken)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place a medium pan over medium heat; add vegetable oil, onion and celery. Cook, stirring often until onion is soft.
Add bell pepper (if using), mushrooms and pearl barley. Stir well.
Add water and bouillon and stir to dissolve bouillon. Bring to a boil, lower heat and cover pan.
Cook for 50 to 60 minutes or until barley is tender and liquid is absorbed.

notes.text: Learn more about:

name: Basic Custard
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045328/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/basic-custard
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup skim milk (or reconstituted non-fat dry milk)

steps: Beat egg and sugar together in a saucepan.
Add milk.
Place saucepan with egg/milk mixture in another pan containing 1-2 inches boiling water.
Stir custard constantly while cooking. Cook until foam disappears and custard coats the spoon. Remove from heat.
Add vanilla, if using and stir. Pour into individual dishes and cool in the refrigerator. Custard will be soft.
Beat together egg and sugar in a baking dish.
Add milk and mix. Add vanilla, if using and mix thoroughly.
Set baking dish in a shallow pan of hot water.
Bake at 350 °F until the tip of a knife inserted in the center of the custard comes out clean (50-60 minutes). Do not overcook. Eat warm or refrigerate for later.
Wash hands with soap and water. Stovetop version: Baked version:

notes.text: An additional egg can be added during step 1.

name: Basic Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043032/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/basic-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: fat-free milk (1/2 cup optional, only if adding carrots, raisins or walnuts)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Line muffin tin with paper baking cups or grease bottom of tin with cooking spray.
Cream margarine and sugar with an electric mixer, or by hand.
Add egg, milk, and applesauce, mixing well.
Blend in cinnamon, baking soda, salt, and flour.
Add carrots, raisins, and/or walnuts if desired. If any of these items are added, also add milk and mix.
Fill muffin tins 2/3 full and bake for 15 to 18 minutes.

notes.text: Tip: Muffins turn out better when mixed by hand.

name: Basic Quiche
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013727/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/basic-quiche
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup vegetables, chopped (broccoli, zucchini, or mushrooms)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 375 °F.
Shred the cheese with a grater. Put it in a small bowl for now.
Chop the vegetables until you have 1 cup of chopped vegetables.
Cook the vegetables until they are cooked, but still crisp.
Put the cooked vegetables and shredded cheese into a pie shell.
Mix the eggs, milk, salt, pepper, and garlic powder in a bowl.
Pour the egg mix over the cheese and vegetables
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.
Let the quiche cool for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Basic Soup and Sauce Mix
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040647/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/basic-soup-and-sauce-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a plastic bag.
Mix well.
Combine 1/3 cup of dry mix with 1 1/4 cups of cold water.
Cook and stir on stove top or in microwave until thickened.
Add thickened mixture to casseroles as you would a can of soup.

Yield: Equal to about 3 cups dry or makes up to 9 cans equivalent cream soup. To use as a substitute for 1 can of cream soup: Storage: Store in closed plastic bag or air-tight container until ready to use. It does not have to be refrigerated.

notes.text: The final product of this recipe is intended to be used as an ingredient in other recipes. It is not intended as a ready-to-eat product.

name: Batido (Smoothie)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032454/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/batido-smoothie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Put all the ingredients in the blender.
Put the lid on tightly. Turn the blender to a medium setting and blend until the ice is chopped and the mixture is smooth, about 1 minute.
Serve right away or cover and refrigerate up to 4 hours.

name: BBQ Chicken Pizza
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035611/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/bbq-chicken-pizza
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 cups chicken breast, skinless, cooked (cut-up or shredded)
3/4 cup smoked cheddar cheese, shredded (or regular)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 450 °F.
Slice English muffins in half and place on ungreased, large cookie sheet.
Cut up bell pepper.
Spread barbecue sauce on English muffins to within ¼ inch of edges. Top with chicken, cheese and bell pepper.
Bake 7 to 12 minutes or until cheese is melted.
* Substitutions: English muffins = Pizza bread Chicken = Pinto beans, chopped tomatoes, and chopped onions

name: Bean and Rice Burritos
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044843/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/bean-and-rice-burritos
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups cooked kidney beans (1 (15 ounce) can, low-sodium, drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 300 °F.
Peel the onion, and chop it into small pieces.
Drain the liquid from the cooked (or canned) kidney beans.
Mix the rice, chopped onion, and beans in a bowl.
Put each tortilla on a flat surface.
Put 1/2 cup of the rice and bean mix in the middle of each tortilla.
Fold the sides of the tortilla to hold the rice and beans.
Put each filled tortilla (burrito) in the baking pan.
Bake for 15 minutes.
While the burritos are baking, grate 1/2 cup cheese.
Pour the salsa over the baked burritos. Add cheese.
Serve the burritos warm.

name: Bean and Vegetable Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035416/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/bean-and-vegetable-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cans (15.5 ounces each) low-sodium kidney beans or garbanzo beans

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash vegetables.
Thickly slice red cabbage, tear lettuce into pieces, peel and grate (or slice) carrots and cucumber
Dice the green pepper.
Cut broccoli into florets and tomato into wedges.
Combine all salad ingredients in a bowl.
Add salad dressing and toss together lightly just before serving.

name: Bean Dip
