steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a saucepan, cook the onion in the oil until soft but not brown. Add the tomatoes, tomato juice, carrots, salt, pepper, and sugar.

Cover and cook over low heat for 5 minutes. Remove the cover and cook over low heat, stirring often, for another 5 minutes, or until the carrots are tender and the tomatoes are cooked down to a sauce.
Stir in the parsley.
Mix the butter with the cooked macaroni.
Add the macaroni to the carrot mixture and stir together.

name: Catfish Stew and Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231023722/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/catfish-stew-and-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can low-sodium diced tomatoes (14.5 ounce can)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut potatoes into quarters.
In large pot, combine potatoes, tomatoes and their juice, onion, water, and garlic. Bring to boil and reduce heat. Cook covered over medium-low heat for 10 minutes.
Add cabbage and return to boil. Reduce heat. Cook covered for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, cut fillets into 2-inch lengths. Coat with Chili and Spice Seasoning.
Add fish to vegetables. Reduce heat and simmer covered for 5 minutes or until fish flakes easily with fork.
Serve in soup dishes. Garnish with sliced green onion, if desired. Serve with scoop of hot cooked brown rice.

name: Cauliflower Shells with Cheese
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231023739/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cauliflower-shells-cheese
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Fill 1 pot with 6 cups of water and bring to a boil. Once the water is boiling, add pasta and cook for 8 minutes.
Drain pasta and fill the same pot with 2 cups of water, bring to a boil.
Place the chopped cauliflower in the boiling water and cook until the florets are soft (about 4 minutes). Drain cauliflower.
Placed the cooked cauliflower, 1/2 cup milk, and garlic salt in a blender and blend until smooth.

In a separate pot, heat oil. Add the flour and whisk until the mixture is smooth. Add 1 cup of milk and cook the mixture until it bubbles and thickens. Add the cheese and cauliflower mixture and stir..
Remove from heat. Add the pasta back into the sauce and serve.

name: Celery with Apricot Blue Cheese Spread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032602/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/celery-apricot-blue-cheese-spread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Chop dried fruit and pecans.
Mix blue cheese, cream cheese, and yogurt with a fork or hand mixer until smooth.
Stir in chopped, dried fruit and pecans. Refrigerate spread until ready for use.
Slice celery stalks into 3-4 inch sticks.
Fill celery pieces with spread.

notes.text: Tips on how to select, store, and serve celery:

name: Chapatis Flatbread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034048/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chapatis-flatbread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place the flour in a large mixing bowl. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix with fork and then with hands. Keep mixing until you can make a ball.
Knead the dough for about 10 minutes. Let rest for 30 minutes in the bowl, covered with a damp cloth.
Roll the ball into a 12-inch log and cut into 6 chunks.
Roll each chunk into a very thin pancake, about 7 inches in diameter. Don't worry about making the dough into a perfect circle-just try to get it as thin as you can.
Heat a cast iron skillet (lightly greased) on medium-high heat. Place one chapati in the skillet and cook for 30 seconds.
Use a spatula to lift bread. When chapati gets brown spots and bubbles, flip it over and cook for another 30 seconds.
Wrap the cooked chapati in a cloth napkin while cooking the rest.
Eat them right away with a little butter or margarine, or use as scoops for eating other dishes.

name: Cheese and Corn Chowder
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031919/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cheese-and-corn-chowder
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup cheddar or American cheese, shredded

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine potatoes, carrots, celery, onion and seasonings in pan. Add 1 cup water. Cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Add corn and pepper. Cook 5 more minutes or until vegetables are cooked.
Add milk and cheese. Stir until cheese melts and chowder is heated through. Do not boil.
Serve hot.

notes.text: To make a Ham, Cheese, and Corn Chowder: Add 1/2 cup cubed, cooked ham.

name: Cheese-A-Roni Bake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215111/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cheese-roni-bake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 jar (24 ounces) spaghetti sauce, meatless, low-sodium
4 ounces mozzarella cheese, part skim, shredded

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a bowl combine sauce and water.
In another bowl combine cottage cheese, egg and oregano.
Grease 1 quart casserole.
Spoon in 1/3 sauce.
Layer with 1/2 cup macaroni, 1/2 cottage cheese mixture, 1/2 mozzarella cheese and 1/3 of the spaghetti sauce.
Repeat layers one more time.
Cover with aluminum foil.
Bake in a 350 °F oven for 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes longer.

name: Cheese Stuffed Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041859/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cheese-stuffed-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 °F.
Scrub the potatoes.
Put the potatoes in the oven. Bake 30 to 40 minutes until tender.
Slice each potato in half lengthwise.
Use a spoon to scoop out the inside of each potato. Leave about 1/2 inch of potato next to the skin. Save the inside part of each potato in a small bowl.
Peel the onion. Chop it to make 2 tablespoons chopped onion.
Put the cheese, milk, and onion in another small bowl. Add the insides of the potatoes. Mix with a fork until light and fluffy.
Divide this mix into 8 parts. Put part of the mix inside each potato.
Sprinkle paprika over the potatoes.
Return to the oven for 5 minutes to reheat.

name: Cheesy Chicken, Broccoli, and Rice Bake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033540/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cheesy-chicken-broccoli-and-rice-bake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (10.75 ounces) condensed cream of mushroom soup, reduced-sodium

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F. In large saucepan, bring water to boil. Add rice, onion, and garlic. Cook for about 30 minutes or until rice is soft.
While rice is cooking combine milk, soup, salt, and pepper, mix well. When rice is done combine with milk mixture, chicken, and broccoli. Mix well.
Grease 9x13 pan and pour mixture into pan. Bake in preheated oven for 18 minutes. Sprinkle with cheese. Bake for another 6 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Serve immediately.

name: Cherry, Melon, & Grape Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032608/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cherry-melon-grape-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup sweet cherries, pitted and cut in half
1 cup seedless green grapes, cut in half

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, mix together the cut fruit.
Pour orange juice over fruit and stir in coconut, if desired.

notes.text: Try using different types of melon or grapes.

name: Cherry Puff Pancake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045445/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cherry-puff-pancake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups halved, pitted sweet cherries, fresh or frozen, thawed and drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 450 °F.
In a medium bowl or blender, beat the eggs, milk, and vanilla together until well blended.
Mix the flour, sugar, and cinnamon together. Add to the liquid ingredients and mix until there are no lumps.

Put margarine or butter in a 10- or 11-inch oven proof skillet or a 2 1/2- to 3-quart baking dish. Place the skillet or dish in the hot oven until the margarine or butter is melted and bubbly. Remove from the oven. Quickly spread the cherries across the bottom of the hot skillet or dish.
Pour the batter over the cherries and sprinkle with almond slices, if using.

Return to the oven and bake for 15 to 20 minutes until the edges are browned and the puffs in the middle are golden. Cool slightly before cutting into 4 pieces. The center puffs will flatten during cooling.

name: Chicken and Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033218/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-and-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain and rinse beans.
Crush garlic.
Dice onion.
Dice chicken thighs.
In large, pot, cook chicken until half done.
Add tomato sauce, vinegar, onion, garlic, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Simmer for about 30 to 40 minutes or until chicken is tender.
Add kidney beans and simmer for 5-10 more minutes.

notes.text: Cider, white, and Japanese wine vinegars differ in flavor. Try other vegetables. Dry beans may be used. See package for cooking directions.

name: Chicken and Broccoli Bake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033517/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-and-broccoli-bake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook rice according to package directions.
Melt margarine in large sauce pan. Add flour to melted margarine and stir. This will be lumpy.
Slowly add chicken broth to margarine/flour mixture. Stir to remove lumps and thicken.
Add cheese and stir.
Add rice, broccoli, and chicken. Stir.
Put in a casserole pan and bake at 350 °F for 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated.

name: Chicken and Cranberry Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045422/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-and-cranberry-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 12 ounces chicken, cooked and diced (1 1/2 cups)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss chicken, cranberries, and almonds with dressing.
Serve on a mound of chopped lettuce.

name: Chicken and Dumpling Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214837/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-and-dumpling-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup celery, chopped, including some leaves
8 cups chicken broth, fat free, low sodium
2 cups fresh spinach leaves, coarsely chopped

steps: Heat oil in Dutch oven or soup kettle over medium-high heat.
Sauté carrot, onion and celery for 5 minutes; stir in broth, chicken, peppercorns, thyme, and bay leaves.
Reduce heat to low; simmer, partially covered for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, in small bowl, mix dumpling ingredients until well blended.
Drop small spoonsful of dumpling dough into simmering soup.
Cover soup and allow dumplings to cook for about 20 minutes (they will rise to the top of the soup as they cook).
Stir in spinach.
Remove bay leaves before serving soup.

name: Chicken and Dumplings
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033435/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-and-dumplings
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 dash black pepper (1/16 of a teaspoon)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix 2 tablespoons flour and water in a pan until smooth.
Slowly stir in broth.
Cook over medium heat until thickened.
Add chicken, salt (optional) and pepper.
Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a small bowl. Stir in milk until dough forms.
Drop dumpling dough from a tablespoon onto gently boiling chicken mixture, making 4 dumplings.
Cover pan tightly and cook slowly for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Make Dumplings:

name: Chicken and Spanish Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040536/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-and-spanish-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 can (8 ounces) tomato sauce, low sodium
5 cups cooked brown rice (cook rice in unsalted water)
3 1/2 cups cooked chicken breast, diced, skin and bone removed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet, sauté onions and green peppers in oil for 5 minutes on medium heat.
Add tomato sauce and spices. Heat through.
Add cooked rice and chicken. Heat through.

name: Chicken Apple Salad Sandwich
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034644/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-apple-salad-sandwich
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients except for bread together in a bowl.
Create 4 sandwiches on whole wheat bread.

name: Chicken Broccoli Alfredo
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045646/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-broccoli-alfredo
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup broccoli, fresh or frozen, chopped

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook fettuccine according to package directions. Add broccoli for the last 4 minutes of cooking time. Drain.
Heat butter in skillet. Add chicken and cook until browned, stirring often.
Combine sauce mix and water in saucepan. Bring to a boil and cook until thick. Add milk, cheese, pepper (if using), and fettuccine mixture and heat through.
Serve with additional Parmesan cheese.

notes.text: Recipe for Basic Soup and Sauce Mix. 1 serving = 1/3 cup. Learn more about:

name: Chicken Cacciatore
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032445/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-cacciatore
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 chicken pieces, skin removed (thighs, breasts, or legs)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the onion.
Put the chopped onion in a saucepan.
Add the tomatoes, tomato sauce, garlic powder, oregano, and pepper.
Simmer on low heat for 3 minutes.
If needed, remove the chicken skin.
Add the chicken to the sauce pan and cover.
Cook over low heat for about 1 hour until the chicken is tender.

name: Chicken Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035325/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound rotini or macaroni pasta (1 package)
1/2 can low-sodium green peas, drained (about 8 ounces)

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Cook rotini or macaroni according to package directions. Drain well.
In a large oven-safe dish, mix the chicken, tomato sauce, peas, and macaroni.
Add the 3 slices of cheese on top of the casserole.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes.
Serve hot.

name: Chicken Club Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031433/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-club-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup whole wheat pasta, uncooked (macaroni or rotelle)
6 cups Romaine lettuce, washed and torn (or spinach)
2 cups green peppers, chopped (or a combination of bell peppers, celery, cauliflower florets, cucumber, carrots*)
1 1/2 cups cubed cooked skinless chicken (1/2 pound)
1/2 Lite Italian Dressing (about 1/2 of what the recipe makes)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions; drain and cool.
Place 1 1/2 cups of the Romaine lettuce in each of 4 large bowls or plates.
Combine chopped vegetables, chicken, and pasta.
Add dressing; toss lightly to coat. Divide evenly among the 4 bowls.
Top each serving with a few egg slices, if desired, and 1 tablespoon of the shredded cheese.

notes.text: *2 cups of green bell peppers were used for cost analysis and nutrition calculations.

name: Chicken Mole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033420/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-mole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 fryer chicken, cut into pieces, skin and fat removed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place chicken in a large pot with the 1/4 cup of water. Cover and simmer until tender, about 45 minutes.
In a medium bowl, mix chili powder, oregano, cocoa, flour (1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons), pepper, and garlic powder along with 1 cup of water.
Add mixture from step 2 to chicken in pot; mix well.
Add peanut butter and 5 cups of water to chicken in pot; mix well.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes.
Stir and serve immediately.

name: Chicken Noodle Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021916/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-noodle-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Thaw frozen chicken in refrigerator (about 24 hours), or thaw in microwave just before cooking soup.
Place chicken pieces in large kettle. Cover completely with water. Cover, bring to boil, reduce heat, and simmer 2 to 3 hours.
With soap and water, carefully wash your hands and any counter surfaces and equipment that came in contact with raw chicken.
Remove cooked chicken pieces from broth with tongs or slotted spoon. Cool 10 to 15 minutes before separating bones from meat. Break meat into bite-sized pieces. Remove any bones from broth.
Remove fat from broth by skimming with spoon, adding and removing ice cubes, or blotting top of broth with paper towels.
Put chicken meat, seasonings and vegetables into stock.
Bring broth to a boil, cover, reduce heat and cook about 15 to 20 minutes on medium heat until sliced carrots are crispy-tender.
Add noodles and boil uncovered for about 6 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally to break up any noodles that might stick together.
Ladle into soup bowls.
Refrigerate or freeze leftovers within 2 hours of cooking. If refrigerated, use within 2 days. When reheating, bring to a boil.

name: Chicken Pasta Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033416/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-pasta-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup canned corn kernels, low-sodium, drained
1 can (15 ounces) black beans, low-sodium, rinsed and drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions, drain; rinse.
Combine first eight ingredients (pasta through black beans) in a large bowl.
Toss gently with salad dressing.
Chill for several hours to blend flavors.

name: Chicken Pot Pie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035436/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-pot-pie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (10.75 ounces) condensed cream of chicken soup, reduced-sodium

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pre-heat oven to 400 °F.
Mix vegetables, chicken, and soup in ungreased, 9-inch pie plate
Stir baking mix, milk, and egg in a mixing bowl with fork until blended. Pour over vegetables and chicken in pie plate.
Bake 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Let cool for 5 minutes and serve.

name: Chicken Pozole Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013758/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-pozole-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 whole chicken, skinned and cut into pieces
5 cups canned hominy, white or yellow, rinsed and drained (2 - 15 ounce cans)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put chicken pieces in a large pot and cover with the 8 cups of water. Simmer over medium heat for 1 hour.
Add the chopped onion, pepper, chili powder, tomato sauce, and oregano to simmering chicken.
After the chicken is thoroughly cooked take the pieces out of the pot and remove most of the bones from the chicken and the pot.
Return chicken to the pot.
Add the rinsed hominy to the pot of chicken and simmer for another 45 minutes.
Serve with lettuce and a wedge of lime.

notes.text: To make even healthier, use tomato sauce with no added salt. Chicken breasts or thighs can be substituted for the whole chicken.

name: Chicken Ratatouille
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032243/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-ratatouille
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 small eggplant, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
1 red or green bell pepper, cut into pieces

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Remove skin and fat from chicken and cut into 1-inch pieces
Heat oil in large non-stick skillet. Add chicken and sauté about 3 minutes, or until lightly browned.
Add zucchini, eggplant, onion, green pepper, and mushrooms. Cook about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add tomatoes, garlic, basil, parsley, and pepper; stir and continue cooking about 5 minutes, or until chicken is tender.

name: Chicken, Rice, and Fruit Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021053/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-rice-and-fruit-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons parsley, dried (or 2 Tablespoons fresh, finely chopped)
1 cup apple or cantaloupe, cut into chunks
1/3 cup grape halves, red or purple, cut into chunks
1 1/4 cups chicken, cooked, cut into bite-size pieces

steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
If not using leftover or "planned over" rice, cook rice according to package directions without adding salt. Chill.
In a serving bowl, mix parsley, black pepper, garlic, dressing, and mayonnaise together.
Add cooled rice, apple, grapes, celery, and chicken. Stir gently.
Serve cold on a bed of clean lettuce leaves, if desired.
Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Chicken Rice Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021148/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-rice-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
Italian herb mix and black pepper to taste (optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss all ingredients together in a large salad bowl.
Use personal taste preferences to determine the amounts of seasonings.
Serve immediately. This salad looks great when served on a large plate with a few of the seasonings sprinkled on top.

name: Chicken and Rice Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021814/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-rice-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Use leftover cooked chicken or cook enough chicken to make 1 cup of chicken pieces.
Place the cooked chicken in a large saucepan.
Add the broth and uncooked rice. Cover the pan.
Bring the broth and rice to a boil.
Cover the pan and turn the heat to low.
Stir and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the chopped onions, chopped vegetables, and seasonings.
Simmer for 10 to 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.

name: Chicken Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022139/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Use within 1-2 days. Chicken salad does not freeze well.
How to use: Make chicken salad sandwiches.; Make a pasta salad by mixing with 2 cups cooked pasta.; Kids will love this salad served in a tomato or a cucumber boat.

name: Chicken Salad and Peach Sandwich
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020419/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-salad-and-peach-sandwich
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup canned peach slices (drained and diced)

steps: Mix together the chicken, apples, peaches, celery, onion, walnuts, and mayonnaise in a small bowl.
Spoon mixture onto 2 slices of the bread.

name: Chicken Salad with Ramen Noodles
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024857/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-salad-ramen-noodles
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup red or green bell pepper
2 cooked chicken breast, chilled and cut into cubes
8 cups cabbage, shredded (or cabbage salad mix)
2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1/2 cup vinegar, rice or white wine

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Break up noodles. Set aside.
In a large bowl, add peppers, scallions, unsalted peanuts, and other vegetables if you like. Add cooked chicken and cabbage.
In a small bowl make dressing with sugar, vinegar, olive oil, and flavor packet. Stir well.
Pour the dressing over the salad and combine. Sprinkle noodles on top.
Serve cold.

name: Chicken Soup with Chiles
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031656/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-soup-chiles
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup mild chiles, canned and diced
2 cups pinto or garbanzo beans, canned or cooked and drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place chicken pieces in a large saucepan and add enough water to cover.
Cook over medium high heat until tender and chicken is cooked, about 25 minutes.
Remove chicken pieces from the broth.
Add tomatoes, garlic, onion, and chiles.
Remove chicken meat from the bones and return meat to broth.
Add beans and salt and pepper to taste. Simmer for about 15 minutes.

name: Chicken Soup for the Soul
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215319/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-soup-soul
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup cooked chicken, cubed, or canned (drained)
1/2 cup uncooked rice, macaroni, or small noodles

steps: Combine celery, carrots, onions, peas, and chicken broth in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Add chicken and reduce heat.
Add rice, macaroni, or noodles.
Simmer on low until rice, macaroni, or noodles are tender and flavors are mixed. Chicken should reach a final internal cook temperature of 165°F as measured with a food thermometer before serving.
Wash hands with soap and water.

name: Chicken Spaghetti
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032351/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-spaghetti
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 medium red bell pepper, thinly sliced
1 medium green bell pepper, thinly sliced
2 cups cooked chicken breast, skinless and diced (8 ounces)
1 can (14.5 ounces) tomatoes, low-sodium, diced undrained
1 can (10.75 ounces) cream of chicken soup, low-sodium
1/4 cup Parmesan cheese, shredded or grated

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F. Lightly spray an 8-inch square baking dish with vegetable oil spray.
Prepare the spaghetti using the package directions, omitting the salt and oil. Drain well in a colander.
Meanwhile, in a large skillet, heat the oil over medium heat, swirling to coat the bottom. Cook the bell peppers and onion for 4 to 5 minutes, or until tender, stirring occasionally.
Pour into a large bowl. Stir in the remaining ingredients, including the spaghetti. Pour into a baking dish.
Bake, covered, for 20 minutes. Bake, uncovered for 10 minutes, or until the mixture is warmed through and light golden brown on top.

name: Chicken Spanish Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025431/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-spanish-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook onion, green pepper, celery, and rice in vegetable oil at medium heat in a large saucepan until soft, about 5 minutes.
Drain tomatoes and save the liquid.
Chop tomatoes into small pieces.
Add tomatoes, liquid, chicken, water, chili powder, and pepper to rice mixture.
Bring to a boil and stir. Cover and cook on low heat. Cook until rice is tender (about 25 minutes).

name: Chicken Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040900/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Remove the skin from the chicken and any extra fat. In a large skillet combine chicken, water, garlic, onion, salt, pepper, tomatoes, and parsley. Tightly cover and cook over low heat for 25 minutes.
Add celery, potatoes, carrots, and bay leaves and continue to cook for 15 minutes or until chicken is cooked and vegetables are tender. Remove bay leaves before serving.

name: Chicken Stir-Fry
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251223185052/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-stir-fry
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup carrots, peeled, sliced thinly (or 1/2 can low-sodium carrots, about 8 ounces, drained)
1 pound chicken, cooked, skin removed, sliced into strips
3 cups white rice, cooked (or brown rice)

steps: Heat a large pan with vegetable oil over high heat.
Add vegetables and garlic to the hot pan. Stir until garlic is slightly brown. If using ginger, add that too.
Add the chicken and sugar to the pan, then add soy sauce.
Stir the food for about 1 minute in the pan.
Serve with cooked rice.

notes.text: Tip for cooking chicken: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for chicken is 165 °F, as measured by a food thermometer.

name: Chicken Vegetable Soup with Kale
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021842/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-vegetable-soup-kale
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 cup chicken, cooked, skinned and cubed
1/2 cup brown rice, cooked (or white rice)
1 cup kale, chopped (about one large leaf)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a medium sauce pan. Add onion and carrots. Sauté until vegetables are tender, about 5 to 8 minutes.
Add thyme and garlic. Sauté for one more minute.
Add water or broth, tomatoes, chicken, cooked rice, and kale.
Simmer for 5 to 10 minutes.

name: Chicken Waldorf Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024736/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chicken-waldorf-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup red or green grapes, halved
1/2 cup chopped walnuts, divided (toasted if desired)

steps: Whisk mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice and salt in a large bowl.
Add chicken, apple, grapes, celery, and half of the walnuts. Stir to coat well.
Serve topped with the remaining walnuts.

name: Chickpea Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034210/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chickpea-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 can (15 ounces) chickpeas, low-sodium, drained (garbanzo beans)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all ingredients into a food processor and blend until smooth.
Serve at room temperature with pita chips, crackers, carrots, or other dipping vegetables.

name: Chickpeas and Spinach Sauté
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033323/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chickpeas-and-spinach-saute
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, no salt added (including liquid)
1 can (16 oz) low-sodium chickpeas (drained and rinsed with cold water)
1 package (10 oz) frozen spinach (kale can be used instead of spinach)
1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice (or red vinegar)

steps: Put a skillet on the stove on medium high heat. When the skillet is hot, add oil.
Add onion, garlic, celery and carrot and cook about 15 minutes until the mixture is soft and the onions are lightly browned.

Raise the heat to high and add the tomatoes, beans (white beans instead of chickpeas) and water and cook for 5 minutes. Lower the heat to low and top the mixture with the spinach (don’t worry about stirring). Cover and cook until the spinach has thawed and heated throughout, about 10 minutes. Stir well.
Add the lemon juice and red pepper flakes and stir thoroughly.
Serve with cooked quinoa or brown rice.

name: Chili Bean Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044310/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chili-bean-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15.5 ounces) pinto beans, low-sodium (or 2 cups cooked dried beans)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mash beans in a bowl.
Add onion and chili powder and shredded cheese.
Serve warm or cold with raw vegetables or tortilla chips.

name: Chili Cheese Hominy
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024946/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chili-cheese-hominy
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
4 cups instant white or yellow hominy, cooked
2 cans (4 ounces each) chopped green chiles, drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium high heat (350 °F in an electric skillet). Add onion and cook until tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in hominy, green chiles, sour cream, chili powder and pepper. Add half of the cheese and mix well.
Reduce heat to medium (300 °F in an electric skillet). Cover and cook until heated through, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Sprinkle remaining cheese on top. Cover and cook until cheese melts, about 5 minutes.

notes.text: Try with different types of grated or crumbled cheese.

name: Chili Popcorn
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215341/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chili-popcorn
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix popcorn and margarine in a bowl.
Mix seasonings thoroughly and sprinkle over popcorn. Mix well.
Serve immediately and enjoy with family and friends.

name: Chili Tomato Macaroni
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020816/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chili-tomato-macaroni
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (14.5 ounces) diced tomatoes, low-sodium, undrained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef in a large skillet, drain the fat.
Add water, macaroni, tomatoes, chili powder, and seasoning mix. Stir.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low and simmer covered on low heat for 20 minutes or until macaroni is tender.
Taste, and add a small amount of salt if desired.
Top with shredded cheddar cheese. Put the lid back on for 1 minute until the cheese is melted.

name: Chilled Blueberry Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032457/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chilled-blueberry-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Rinse blueberries and set aside a few for garnishing.
Blend all ingredients in food processor or blender.
Serve immediately.
Garnish with mint leaves and blueberries, if desired.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with grilled salmon fish fillet (about 3 to 4 ounces), asparagus, and water with lemon slice.

name: Chilled Cantaloupe Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041117/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chilled-cantaloupe-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place cantaloupe and 1/2 cup orange juice in a container of a blender or food processor.
Cover with lid and blend until smooth. Transfer to large bowl.
Stir in lime juice, cinnamon, and remaining orange juice.
Cover, and refrigerate for at least one hour.
Serve chilled.

name: Chimichurri Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050712/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chimichurri-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup flat-leaf parsley, lightly packed and chopped without the stalks

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place all the ingredients in a blender or food processor and pulse until well chopped, but not pureed.
Spoon the sauce over grilled meats, poultry, seafood, or vegetables. This sauce can also be used as a marinade.

name: Chocolate Chip Yogurt Cookies
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041141/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chocolate-chip-yogurt-cookies
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup chocolate chips (miniature, or carob chips)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 375 °F.
In a large bowl combine sugar, brown sugar and margarine; beat until light and fluffy.
Add yogurt and vanilla; blend well. Stir in flour and baking soda; mix well. Stir in chocolate chips.
Drop dough by rounded teaspoonfuls 2 inches apart onto un-greased cookie sheets. Bake at 375 °F for 8 to 12 minutes or until light and golden brown.
Cool 1 minute, remove from cookie sheets.

name: Chocolate Peanut Butter Frozen Bars
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020707/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chocolate-peanut-butter-frozen-bars
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 packages (1.4 ounces each) low calorie chocolate pudding, instant (or cook and serve type)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix pudding according to package directions, except use 3 1/2 cups milk. Beat in peanut butter.
Line a 9x13 inch pan with half the graham crackers.
Spread pudding mixture over graham crackers. Top with remaining crackers.
Freeze for four hours.
Cut into squares and remove from pan.
Store in a plastic bag in the freezer.

name: Chocolate Squash Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215104/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chocolate-squash-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 cup squash, shredded or finely chopped

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Grease and flour a 10-inch tube or bundt pan.
In a large bowl, combine cake mix and cinnamon.
Add eggs, water, and oil. Blend until combined, then beat with an electric mixer for 2 minutes on medium speed.
Fold in squash. Add nuts if you like.
Pour into prepared pan. Bake for 50 minutes to 1 hour, until cake springs back when lightly touched.

notes.text: Other Ideas:

name: Chunky Garbanzo Bean Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041513/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/chunky-garbanzo-bean-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain and rinse the beans and mash in a small bowl with a fork or potato masher until most of the beans have been crushed. If you have a food processor, you can use it for this step.
Stir in oil and onion along with lemon pepper and salt to taste. The mixture will be chunky, not smooth.

notes.text: Suggest serving with vegetables like carrots, pea pods, and celery.

name: Cinnamon Raisin Almond Balls
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040828/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cinnamon-raisin-almond-balls
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse the raisins and almonds with water.
Toss them in the food processor with the cinnamon. When sufficiently mixed, form into balls or bar shapes.

name: Cinnamon-Raisin Breakfast Mix
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041944/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cinnamon-raisin-breakfast-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: In small bowl, mix sugar and cinnamon; set aside.
In large microwavable bowl, microwave butter uncovered on HIGH about 40 seconds, or until melted.
Stir in cereals until evenly coated. Microwave uncovered 2 minutes, stirring after 1 minute.
Sprinkle half of the sugar mixture evenly over cereals; stir. Sprinkle with remaining sugar mixture; stir.
Microwave uncovered 1 minute.
Stir in raisins or dried cranberries. Spread on paper towels to cool.

name: Cinnamon Sugared Pumpkin Pecan Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043323/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cinnamon-sugared-pumpkin-pecan-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F. Spray 12 muffin cups with cooking spray.
Combine 2 tablespoons sugar and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon in a small bowl; set aside.
In a large bowl, combine cereal and milk and set aside for 5 minutes.
Combine remaining sugar and cinnamon, flour, baking powder, and baking soda in a bowl. Whisk pumpkin, egg, and vanilla into cereal.
Fold in dry mixture; being careful not to over mix. Spoon into prepared pan and sprinkle with pecans and sugar-cinnamon mixture.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean.

name: Cinnamon Vanilla Granola
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035114/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cinnamon-vanilla-granola
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 275 °F.
Mix honey, water, vegetable oil, vanilla extract, cinnamon, and salt in a large bowl.
Stir in oats; mix well.
Spread mixture on a cookie sheet, making a thin layer.
Bake for 20 minutes. Remove from oven, stir mixture well and return to oven.
Bake 20 minutes more and stir as before.
Bake 5 to 20 minutes more, until granola is golden brown.
Break into small pieces with spatula.
Cool and then store in a covered container.

notes.text: * Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Citrus Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032247/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/citrus-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Preheat the oven to 425 °F.
To trim the chicken, lay the chicken thighs on the cutting board, skin side up. Press down on the chicken to push out the excess fat. Use a sharp knife to cut excess fat.
Put the chicken, oregano, cumin, lime juice, salt, and pepper in the bowl and mix well. Proceed to the next step or cover and refrigerate up to overnight.
Put the contents of the bowl in the baking pan and transfer to the oven.
Bake about 1 hour until cooked throughout and well browned.
Serve right away.

name: Citrus Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042214/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/citrus-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut fruit into bite size pieces.
Toss with lettuce and onion. Mix remaining ingredients for dressing. Drizzle over salad and toss just before serving.

name: Citrus Salmon Fillets
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042357/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/citrus-salmon-fillets
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 orange or lemon, cut into wedges (optional)

steps: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
In an oven safe skillet, heat oil on medium high heat.
Add onion, carrots (or sweet potato), parsley, and ½ cup of orange juice. Cook 5-8 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix ½ cup orange juice and honey.
In center of skillet, add salmon fillets and season with salt and pepper.
Pour orange juice and honey mixture over top.
Bake entire skillet in oven 16-18 minutes or until fish is flaky.
Garnish with orange or lemon wedges, if using
Wash hands with soap and water.

notes.text: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.

name: Citrus Tuna Melt
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032234/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/citrus-tuna-melt
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup tomatoes, diced (or 2 tablespoons, about 2 ounces, low-sodium diced tomatoes, drained)
6 slices whole grain bread (or homemade bread)
1/4 cup fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped (optional)
1 tablespoon cayenne or jalapeño chilies, diced (optional)
3 slices pasteurized process American cheese, cut into halves

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine tuna, lime juice, onion, tomatoes, apple, celery, and pepper. Mix well.
Toast the bread.
Place 6 slices of toasted bread on a cookie sheet. Put an even amount of tuna mixture on top of each slice. If using parsley and chilies, add these too.
Put 1/2 slice cheese on top of the tuna and bake for about 3 minutes.
Add an extra slice of tomato and lettuce on top if you like.
Serve hot.

name: Citrus Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034137/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/citrus-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 cups mixed vegetables (such as zucchini, corn, and tomatoes)
1/2 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice vegetables and steam in a small amount of water.
Drain, and place in a bowl to cool.
Mix lime juice with oil. Add oregano and combine.
Pour lime juice mixture over cool vegetables and mix well.
Serve.

name: Classic Honey Flan
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021836/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/classic-honey-flan
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees F.
Place saucepan with water on stove over medium-high heat and allow to come to a boil.
Spray four ovenproof custard cups with vegetable oil spray.
Combine the whole egg, egg substitute, milk, 5 tablespoons of honey, grated lemon zest, and vanilla. Beat until mixed but not foamy.
In a separate bowl, combine 2 tablespoons of honey and cinnamon, and mix to blend.

Place the custard cups in a baking dish large enough to accommodate them, plus the water bath. Spoon 1/2 tablespoon of honey and cinnamon into each custard cup. Divide the egg mixture equally into each custard cup.

Place the baking dish on the rack in the middle of the oven and pour the boiling water into the baking dish to a depth of 1 inch, taking care not to let the water splash the flan. Bake for 45 minutes or until the knife blade comes out clean when inserted.
Serve warm or cold. Before serving, loosen the edges with a knife or spatula and invert onto individual dessert plates.

notes.text: * Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Classic Macaroni and Cheese
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041228/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/classic-macaroni-and-cheese
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/4 cups finely shredded low-fat sharp cheddar cheese

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook macaroni according to directions. (Do not add salt to the cooking water.) Drain and set aside.
Spray a casserole dish with nonstick cooking oil spray.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Lightly spray saucepan with nonstick cooking oil spray.
Add onions to saucepan and sauté for about 3 minutes.
In another bowl, combine macaroni, onions, and the remaining ingredients and mix thoroughly.
Transfer mixture into casserole dish.
Bake for 25 minutes or until bubbly. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

name: Cobb Salad with Pears
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215223/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cobb-salad-pears
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: For the dressing, mix pear juice, vinegar, honey, mustard, and salt and pepper and olive oil in a blender.
Put mixed greens in large mixing bowl, drizzle dressing over greens and mix together.
Add remaining chopped pear, walnuts, and grated carrots and toss lightly.
Portion out 1 cup of salad and top with 1/2 tablespoon grated Parmesan cheese.

name: Coffee Cooler
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035340/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/coffee-cooler
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup of coffee, cooled to room temperature (4 fluid ounces)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a blender, combine all ingredients; purée until smooth.
Pour into a chilled glass and sprinkle with cinnamon, cocoa, or nutmeg if you like.

name: Collard Green Gumbo with Ham Hock
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215137/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/collard-green-gumbo-ham-hock
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Put a skillet on the stove and turn the heat to medium. When it is hot, add the oil. Add the onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic, thyme, red pepper flakes, salt, and oregano, and cook until golden, about 20 minutes.
Add the flour in small amounts, sprinkling a little bit at a time and stirring well, until it turns slightly brown, about 10 minutes.
Slowly add the water, stirring constantly. Add the ham hock. Raise the heat to high and when it comes to a boil reduce heat to low.
Add the collard greens and cook until tender, about 45 minutes.
Divide the brown rice between 4 shallow bowls and top each with about 1 cup of gumbo.

notes.text: One medium sized chicken sausage link can be substituted for a ham hock.

name: Colorful Quesadillas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043401/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/colorful-quesadillas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups fresh spinach leaves (or 9 ounces frozen, thawed, and squeezed dry)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, mix the cream cheese and garlic powder.
Spread about 2 tablespoons of the cheese mixture on each tortilla.
Sprinkle about 2 tablespoons bell pepper and 2 tablespoons cheese on one half of each tortilla.
Add spinach: 1/4 cup if using fresh leaves OR 2 tablespoons if using frozen. Fold tortillas in half.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat until hot. Put 2 folded tortillas in skillet and heat for 1 to 2 minutes on each side or until golden brown.
Remove quesadillas from skillet, place on platter and cover with foil to keep warm while cooking the remainder.
Cut each quesadilla into 4 wedges. Serve warm.

name: Confetti Bean Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021541/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/confetti-bean-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15.5 ounces) black or red beans, low-sodium

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain and rinse the beans. Drain the corn.
Combine beans, corn, and salsa in a medium-sized bowl. Mix.

notes.text: Like it hot? Add a few drops of hot sauce or chopped green chilis. Try chopped cilantro, parsley or green pepper, too.

name: Confetti Grain Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021005/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/confetti-grain-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 1/2 cups mixed vegetables, cut into small pieces

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash rice and put into a 2-quart pot with water. Bring to boil, then lower heat to simmer, and cook uncovered until all the water is absorbed (approximately 45 minutes)
Pour into medium sized bowl and allow to cool.
Pour lemon juice over rice and stir. When rice is cooled to lukewarm, add vegetables, salt, pepper, and oil.
Stir and chill at least 1 hour. This dish also can be served warm.

name: Confetti Slaw
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042942/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/confetti-slaw
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice and cut cabbage into thin strips. Place pieces in large mixing bowl.
Peel and grate carrots. Add to mixing bowl.
Add raisins and peanuts to mixing bowl.
Mix all ingredients together.
Combine yogurt and orange juice in small bowl.
Add yogurt mixture to cabbage mixture, stirring to combine ingredients thoroughly.

notes.text: Create-a-Flavor Changes

name: Cooked Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031954/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cooked-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sort: Before soaking beans, pick them over and remove any damaged beans, small stones or dirt.
Soak: Most beans will rehydrate to triple their dry size, so be sure to start with a large enough pot. Choose one of the methods to soak your beans.
Cook: Drain soaking water and rinse beans. Cover beans with fresh water. Simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours until tender.

Soaking Methods: Hot Soak: Hot soaking helps reduce intestinal gas. For each pound (2 cups) of dry beans, add 10 cups hot water; heat to boiling and let boil 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from heat, cover and set aside for up to 4 hours.; Quick Soak: For each pound (2 cups) of dry beans, add 10 cups hot water; heat to boiling and let boil 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from heat, cover and set aside for at least one hour.; Overnight Soak: For each pound (2 cups) of dry beans, add 10 cups cold water and let soak overnight, or at least 8 hours.

name: Cookie Cutter Appetizers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035120/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cookie-cutter-appetizers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup chopped vegetables (choose your favorite vegetables)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Cut out multiple shapes from 1 whole wheat tortilla using cookie cutters.
Spray a cookie sheet with non-stick cooking spray.
Place cut out tortilla shapes onto cookie sheet.
Bake in oven for 12 to 15 minutes or until golden brown.
While tortillas are baking, mix low-fat cream cheese with garlic powder. Set aside.
Wash and chop mixed vegetables.
Once tortilla cut outs are finished baking, let cool.
Spread the cream cheese mixture onto each cut out shape and decorate with mixed vegetables.
serving_size: 1/2 tortilla with cream cheese and vegetables

name: Corn and Bean Medley
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032048/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-and-bean-medley
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain the canned corn, but reserve the liquid from the can.
Heat 3 tablespoons of liquid from canned corn in saucepan.
Cook onion in liquid until soft, about 2 minutes.
Add corn, kidney beans, chili powder, and hot red pepper flakes to onion mixture.
Cook over low heat for about 10 minutes.

name: Corn and Cucumber Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032012/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-and-cucumber-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine ingredients and mix well.
Serve cold.

name: Corn and Green Chili Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021659/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-and-green-chili-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a medium bowl.
Mix well.

name: Corn and Pepper Cups
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021332/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-and-pepper-cups
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 5 medium green peppers (cut in half, lengthwise)
1 can (10 ounces) diced tomatoes with chiles, undrained
1 can (15.2 ounces) low-sodium canned corn, drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Remove seeds from peppers. Cook in boiling water 2 to 3 minutes. Drain. Set aside.
Cook onion and garlic in oil in medium skillet over medium-high heat for 3 minutes.
Combine rice, tomatoes, corn, and onion mixture. Mix well.
Spoon rice mixture into pepper halves. Places on baking sheets coated with cooking spray.
Bake at 350 °F for 10 minutes or until hot. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 5 more minutes until cheese melts.

name: Corn, Blueberry, and Wild Rice Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032251/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-blueberry-and-wild-rice-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 ears sweet corn, husked (or 1 1/2 cups frozen corn or canned corn, drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot, bring salted water to a boil. Add corn. Cook covered for 5 minutes, or until tender. If using corn on the cob, remove corn from the cob after cooking.
In a serving bowl, combine corn, blueberries, cucumber, red onion, cilantro, wild rice, and jalapeno.
For dressing: In a screw-top jar, combine lime juice, oil, honey, cumin, and salt. Cover and shake well to combine. If you do not have a screw-top jar you can whisk ingredients in a small bowl.
Add dressing to salad and toss.
Salad is best enjoyed if covered and refrigerated overnight or up to 24 hours.

notes.text: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.

name: Corn Bread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033905/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-bread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 425 °F. Grease 8x9 inch pan.
Measure cornmeal, flour, sugar, and baking powder into a large mixing bowl. Stir to combine ingredients.
Crack egg into a small bowl and beat with a fork to combine white and yolk.
Add egg, oil, and milk to flour mixture. Mix until ingredients are well blended.
Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until firm to touch or wooden pick inserted in the center comes out clean.

Create-a-Flavor Changes: Buttermilk Corn Bread: Use only 2 teaspoons baking powder and add 1/4 teaspoon baking soda. Substitute 1 cup buttermilk for skim milk.; Whole Wheat Corn Bread: Use 1/2 cup all purpose flour and 1/2 cup whole wheat flour.; Corny Corn Bread: Add 1 cup kernels (fresh, frozen, or canned, well drained) with the milk.; Cheesy Corn Bread: Add 1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese with the milk.; Chili Cheese Corn Bread: Add 1/2 teaspoon chili powder to the flour mixture. Drain one 4-ounce can chopped green chilies. Add chilies and 1/4 cup shredded Monterey jack cheese with the milk.; Blueberry Corn Bread: Fold 1 cup blueberries (fresh, frozen, or canned, well drained) into the batter.; Corn Bread Muffins: Pour batter into prepared muffin cups. Bake 20 minutes at 400 °F.

name: Corn Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231051030/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Beat eggs in a bowl.
Add corn, minced onion, sugar, black pepper, and half the bread crumbs.
Stir and put into a greased 8x8 inch baking dish.
Sprinkle remaining bread crumbs on top of the casserole.
Baked at 350 °F for 30 minutes.

name: Corn Salad with Fat-free Ranch Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042918/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-salad-fat-free-ranch-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups whole kernel corn, fresh or frozen (cooked and drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In bowl, combine vegetables.
Stir in dressing.
Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.

name: Corn Salad with Fresh Basil and Lemon
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214940/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-salad-fresh-basil-and-lemon
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh basil (or 1 tsp dried basil)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook corn in boiling water or in the microwave.
Cut corn from the cob. Add onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice and sugar. Add oil and combine.
Stir the oil/lemon mixture and basil. And salt and pepper to taste (optional).
Refrigerate at least 30 minutes.

notes.text: 3 cups frozen corn can be substituted for fresh.

name: Corn Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215151/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can reduced-sodium whole kernel corn (about 15 ounces)
2 cans no salt added cream style corn (about 30 ounces)

steps: In a large pot, brown ground beef over medium to high heat for 8 to 10 minutes. Drain off fat.
Add water, corn kernels, cream style corn, onion, garlic, chili powder, salt, and pepper to pot. Mix well.
Cook over low heat for about 15 minutes. Serve hot.

notes.text: Tip for cooking ground beef: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef is 160 °F as measured with a food thermometer.

name: Corn Toasties
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050238/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-toasties
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup dry egg mix, mixed with 1/4 cup water (or 1 egg)
2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and baking soda.
In another bowl, combine buttermilk, egg mix, and vegetable oil. Beat until well blended.
Add buttermilk mixture all at once to dry ingredients. Stir until well mixed.
Turn mixture onto a lightly floured board and knead only 10 times.
Roll out to a thickness of 1/4 inch and cut with a 3/4-inch-round cutter.
Cook on a warm ungreased griddle or frying pan for about 10 minutes on each side.

notes.text: Don't have buttermilk on hand? Try using 2 teaspoons vinegar + 3/4 cup milk (made from non-fat dry milk powder).

name: Corn Tortillas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214832/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/corn-tortillas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

Measure the masa harina and salt into a large bowl. Cut the butter into tablespoon-sized pieces and work it into the dry ingredients using the back of a wooden spoon. Add the water and mix with a wooden spoon or with your hands until a soft dough forms. Cover the dough with a clean cloth and let rest for 5 minutes.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each piece into a ball.

To keep the dough from sticking to the tortilla press, put a piece of plastic wrap (or a plastic bag) on the bottom surface of the press. Put a ball of dough in the center of the plastic. Then place another piece of plastic wrap on the top of the dough. Press the dough flat in the press.

Pick up the tortilla with the plastic on both sides. Peel off one piece of plastic (which can be reused). Flip the tortilla off of the plastic onto a hot griddle. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the bottom of the tortilla becomes golden. Flip the tortilla and press lightly with a spatula, which will make the tortilla puff slightly. Cook for one to two minutes more, until the tortilla appears to be done.

name: Cornbread Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043629/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cornbread-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F. Lightly spray an 8-inch square baking pan with vegetable oil spray.

In a large skillet, heat the oil over medium heat, swirling to coat the bottom. Cook the green onions and celery for 4 to 5 minutes, or until tender, stirring occasionally. Stir in the broth, sage, and pepper.
Put the cornbread in a large bowl. Stir in the vegetable mixture, egg substitute, and pecans (the mixture will be moist). Transfer to the baking pan.
Bake for 30 minutes, or until cooked through and golden brown on top. Transfer to a serving bowl.

notes.text: For quick and easy cornbread for this recipe, select a cornbread mix with the lowest amounts of saturated fat, trans fat, and sodium available. Prepare using the package directions, substituting fat-free milk for whole milk and egg substitute for the egg. Omit any butter, margarine, oil, sugar, or salt called for. Bake according to the package directions. Let cool. Crumble 4 cups for the cornbread with your fingers and use as directed in the recipe.

name: Cornmeal Pancakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032039/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cornmeal-pancakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix cornmeal, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar in a bowl.
Add butter (or margarine) to cornmeal mixture.
Bring water to a boil and add to cornmeal mixture. Beat until well mixed.
Mix evaporated milk and vinegar in a small bowl.
Stir milk and vinegar mixture into cornmeal mixture. Beat to mix well. Beat in egg.
Heat griddle or frying pan over medium heat. (If electric frying pan is used, preheat it to 380 °F.) Pan is "hot" when a drop of water "dances." Grease pan lightly.

Pour batter onto griddle or fry pan. Use about 3 tablespoons batter for each pancake. A 1/4 cup measure is handy to use for pouring. Stir the batter up from the bottom now and then to keep it well mixed. Cook until top is covered with bubbles and the bottom is brown. Loosen edges of each pancake all around. Turn pancakes over and brown other side.

name: Country Style Potato Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033706/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/country-style-potato-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash potatoes, leave skin on and cut in bite-sized chunks.
Place in pan and cover with water. Bring to a boil, lower to simmer and cook uncovered until potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain in colander and sprinkle lightly with cold water.
In the mean time, put the rest of the ingredients in a large mixing bowl. Drain potatoes well and add to the bowl.
Mix well and refrigerate until ready to use.
Garnish with fresh lettuce and sliced tomatoes.

name: Couscous with Peas and Onions
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045413/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/couscous-peas-and-onions
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine oil and onions in heavy skillet.
Sauté for 5 to 10 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the peas, sage, water, couscous, and salt if desired.
Cover and cook on medium heat for about 5 minutes or until peas are tender but still bright green and all of the water is absorbed.
Fluff with fork.

notes.text: Serve with lemon wedges or balsamic vinegar.

name: Cowboy Caviar (Bean Salsa)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032502/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cowboy-caviar-bean-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15 ounces) low-sodium black beans, drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix kidney beans, black beans, corn, tomatoes, chilies, and onion in a large bowl.
Add oil and lime juice (if using), toss gently to combine. Taste. Add small amount of salt and pepper if desired.
Serve by itself, with raw vegetables and/or corn chips.

notes.text: Be creative! Add any kind of beans you have. Make it spicier by adding hot sauce.

name: Cran-Apple Crisp
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031944/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cran-apple-crisp
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Wash apples, remove cores and slice thinly, keeping peel on.
In a bowl, combine the cranberries and apples. Pour into an 8x8 inch pan.
Combine melted margarine with oatmeal, brown sugar, and cinnamon until well blended. Sprinkle over apple/cranberry mixture.
Cover and bake for 15 minutes.
Uncover and bake 10 more minutes until the topping is crisp and brown.
Serve warm or cold.

name: Cranberry Ham Slice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041848/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cranberry-ham-slice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine brown sugar, cornstarch, and allspice in a saucepan.
Gradually add the next three ingredients and stir. Cook over medium heat until sauce thickens and boils.
Place one slice of ham in greased baking dish. Pour one half of the sauce over the ham slice. Top with second slice. Add remaining sauce.
Bake, covered in 350 °F oven for 45 minutes.

name: Cranberry Nut Bread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231051035/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cranberry-nut-bread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: powdered sugar, optional (1/3 cup, for glaze)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F. Mix flour, sugar, baking powder and baking soda in a large bowl.
Grate orange peeling, then squeeze juice from orange. Add additional orange juice to make 3/4 cup.
In a separate bowl, blend orange juice, butter, egg, and grated orange peel; add to flour mixture, stirring until just blended. Mix in cranberries and walnuts.
Pour batter into a 9x5 inch loaf pan, greased on bottom only.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Cool in pan for 10 minutes; remove and cool completely on wire rack.
Optional: to make glaze, mix powdered sugar and water; add water as needed to make thin glaze. Drizzle over cooled loaf.

notes.text: *You can substitute 1/2 to 1 cup of the flour with whole wheat flour. All-purpose flour used for nutrition analysis and costing purposes.

name: Cranberry Pumpkin Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214943/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cranberry-pumpkin-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/3 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
2 cups fresh or frozen cranberries ( chopped)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Sift together dry ingredients (flour through allspice) and set aside.
Beat oil, eggs, and pumpkin together until well blended.
Add the wet ingredients (pumpkin mixture) to the dry ingredients all at once. Stir until moistened.
Fold in chopped cranberries.
Spoon into paper lined muffin cups.
Bake at 400 °F for 15 to 30 minutes.

notes.text: Serve with a glass of low-fat milk for a healthy snack.

name: Cranberry Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034907/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cranberry-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 packages strawberry gelatin (3 oz. packages, can also use raspberry)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Make gelatin and refrigerate until partially set.
Beat cranberry sauce.
Grate orange peel into sugar and add to cranberry sauce with rest of ingredients.
Fold mixture into partially set gelatin. Refrigerate until set. Serve.

notes.text: Suggested to serve with a mixture of instant lemon pudding mix and low-fat whipped topping.

name: Cream of Broccoli Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041940/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cream-broccoli-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

In a saucepan combine chicken broth, chopped onion, broccoli, thyme, bay leaf and garlic powder. Bring mixture to boiling. Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 10 minutes or until vegetables are tender. Remove bay leaf.
Place half of the mixture in a blender or food processor, cover and blend 30 to 60 seconds or until smooth. Pour into a bowl; repeat with remaining vegetable mixture, set all aside.

In the same saucepan warm the oil. Stir in flour, salt, and pepper. Add the milk all at once, stirring rapidly with a wire whisk. Cook and stir until mixture is thickened and bubbly. Stir in the blended broccoli mixture. Cook and stir until soup is heated through. Season to taste with additional salt and pepper.

notes.text: Fresh or frozen broccoli can be used. Learn more about:

name: Creamy Chicken Hash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042715/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/creamy-chicken-hash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup green bell pepper, finely chopped
1/4 cup red bell pepper, finely chopped
2 cups skinless cooked chicken breast, diced
1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper (a pinch or to taste)
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste (optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Shred the potato and set aside. (It will darken in color, but this will not affect hash.)

Heat 1 tablespoons butter or oil in a medium/large non-stick skillet. Add onion, bell peppers, celery and garlic. Sauté until lightly browned, 5 minutes. Push vegetables to one side of pan. Add remaining butter or oil. Add potatoes and mix with oil to coat them. Mix and combine well with the vegetables. Cook 3 minutes. If potatoes stick, scrape pan vigorously and move contents around pan to spray the bottom with cooking spray.

Mix in chicken, milk, cayenne, salt and pepper. Spread and flatten out the mixture into a thick cake. Use the edge of a pancake turner to cut it into 4 sections.
