(Or, hash can be broken into rough pieces while cooking.) Cover the pan. Cook until potatoes are tender and hash is lightly browned, 3 to 5 minutes, turning so bottom sides can also brown. (Spray pan with oil spray if necessary while turning hash.)

When hash is done, divide equally among four plates. Serve with barbecue sauce drizzled on top or around each portion. (If desired, sauce can first be thinned, by mixing 4 tablespoons sauce with 4 tablespoons milk.)

name: Creamy Dill Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031818/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/creamy-dill-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put the sour cream, yogurt, and dill in a medium bowl. Stir together.
Store the dip in a covered container if you don’t plan to eat it right away.
Keep the dip in the fridge until you serve it.

notes.text: Serve with cucumber slices. If you want a creamy salad dressing, add a few tablespoons of water to the dip.

name: Creamy Italian Herb Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041658/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/creamy-italian-herb-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, combine all the above ingredients.
Refrigerate in a covered container for at least an hour. Serve chilled.

name: Creamy Peanut Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050306/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/creamy-peanut-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, mix the peanut butter and orange juice until smooth.
Stir in the vanilla yogurt.
Cover and put in the fridge until chilled.

notes.text: Serve with fresh apples, pears, carrot sticks or celery sticks.

name: Creamy Vegetable Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032024/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/creamy-vegetable-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups low-fat plain yogurt (or small curd cottage cheese)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine yogurt (or cottage cheese), pepper, garlic powder, dried onion, dried parsley, salt, and dill (if used). Beat until smooth.
Chill dip in refrigerator until ready to serve. Serve with raw vegetables.

notes.text: Serve with approximately 6 cups of vegetables, such as cauliflower florets, carrot sticks, celery sticks, jicama, sliced bell pepper, or sliced cucumber.

name: Creole Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020925/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/creole-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook celery, green pepper, and onion in vegetable oil in a large saucepan until soft, about 5 minutes.
Break up large pieces of tomatoes. Add tomatoes and seasonings to vegetable mixture.
Bring to a boil. Add beans and return to a boil.
Cover and cook over low heat until flavors are blended and liquid is cooked away, about 30 minutes. Stir once and a while to prevent sticking.

name: Crispy Oven Baked Fries
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041548/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/crispy-oven-baked-fries
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 medium potatoes, cut into strips (great with sweet potatoes!)
2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 450 °F. Lightly oil a 9x13 inch pan.
Wash and cut potatoes. Pat dry on towels.
Spread strips of potatoes in one layer in pan.
Distribute remaining oil evenly over potatoes.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes until potatoes are golden brown and tender. Turn frequently.
Season to taste.

name: Crispy Oven-Fried Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035453/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/crispy-oven-fried-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon vegetable oil (to grease baking pan)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Add 1/2 teaspoon of poultry seasoning to milk.
Combine remaining 1/2 teaspoon of poultry seasoning and all other spices (except paprika) with cornflake crumbs and place in a plastic bag.
Dip chicken into milk, shake to remove excess, then quickly shake in bag with seasoning and crumbs.
Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Remove from refrigerator and sprinkle lightly with paprika for color.
Evenly space chicken on greased baking pan. Cover with aluminum foil and bake for 40 minutes.

Remove foil and continue baking for an additional 30 to 40 minutes or until the meat can be easily pulled away form the bone with a fork. The drumsticks may require less baking time than the breasts. Crumbs will form a crispy "skin." (Do not turn chicken during baking.)
serving_size: 1/2 breast or 2 small drumsticks, 1/6 of recipe

name: Crispy Taquitos
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020835/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/crispy-taquitos
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup canned corn, no salt added (or frozen, thawed)
1/2 cup cheddar cheese, low-fat, shredded (or Monterey jack or queso fresco)
2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 425 °F. In a medium bowl, combine 1 cup Pico de Gallo, chicken, corn, green onion, bell pepper, and cheese.
Soften tortillas on the stovetop or in the microwave oven, and spoon a heaping tablespoon of filling onto the center of each tortilla. Roll up tightly and secure each with a toothpick.
Place rolled tortillas seam side down on a baking sheet and brush each lightly with oil. Bake for 10 to 15 minutes or until crisp and lightly browned.
Place 3 taquitos on each plate and serve with remaining Pico de Gallo.

name: Crispy Walleye Patties
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045728/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/crispy-walleye-patties
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound walleye fillets, minced (fresh or frozen) (2 8-ounce fillets)
1 egg (or 2 tablespoons dried egg mix + 1/4 cup water)
Note: "Minced" means cut up into tiny pieces.

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 °F. Place minced fish in a colander and press firmly to remove as much moisture as possible.
In a medium bowl, mix fish, onion, celery, mayonnaise, crackers, egg, garlic powder, dill, paprika, and salt. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Shape mixture into 8 patties. Spray baking sheet with cooking spray and place patties at least 1 inch apart on the pan.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, flip, and bake for another 10 minutes. Serve warm.

notes.text: Optional: Serve with a lemon wedge or tartar sauce.

name: Crock Pot Vegetable Lentil Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033642/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/crock-pot-vegetable-lentil-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
low-fat plain yogurt (optional, 1 teaspoon per serving)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sauté onion and garlic with olive oil.
Combine sauté mix with the rest of the ingredients in a crock pot.
Cook on low for 8 hours or high for 4 hours.
Spoon stew into bowls to serve and top with a dollop of fat-free or low-fat plain yogurt (optional).

name: Crunchy Berry Parfait
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020527/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/crunchy-berry-parfait
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup blueberries or strawberries (fresh or frozen thawed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spoon yogurt into glass.
Top with fruit and granola.

name: Crunchy Chicken Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021349/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/crunchy-chicken-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 small apple, diced (leave the peel on)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Use leftover cooked chicken, or cook enough chicken to make 2 cups of chicken pieces.
Chop the celery and green pepper into small pieces.
Peel and chop 1/4 of an onion.
Peel and chop half of a cucumber.
Chop the apple into pieces. It’s okay to leave the peel on the apple.
Cut the grapes in half.
Put all the ingredients in a large bowl. Stir together.

notes.text: Serve on lettuce, crackers, or bread.

name: Crunchy Vegetable Wraps
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045436/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/crunchy-vegetable-wraps
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup zucchini, cut into small strips
1/4 cup yellow (summer) squash, cut into small strips
1/8 cup green bell pepper, seeded and diced

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, stir ranch dressing into cream cheese; chill.
Wash and chop vegetables.
Steam broccoli in microwave for 1 minute with 1 tablespoon of water.
Spread cream cheese onto flour tortilla, staying one inch from edge. Sprinkle vegetables over cream cheese. Roll tortilla tightly.
Chill for 1 to 2 hours before serving (the wrap will hold its shape better). With a sharp knife slice into circles and serve.

name: Crustless Pumpkin Pie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045228/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/crustless-pumpkin-pie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup all-purpose baking mix for biscuits (or use Master Mix - see notes for link to recipe)
2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F and lightly grease a 9 or 10 inch pie plate.
Combine all ingredients in a medium mixing bowl or a blender.
Beat 2 minutes with a mixer until smooth, or blend in the blender on high for one minute.
Pour into the pie plate.
Bake until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean, about 50 to 55 minutes.
Cool slightly and keep refrigerated.
Serve with whipped topping or ice cream.

notes.text: *Recipe for Master Mix

name: Crusty Rice with Tofu and Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215321/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/crusty-rice-tofu-and-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups prepared rice (ingredients above, step 1 in directions)
6 scallions (sliced including white and green parts)

steps: To make the rice, cook rice according to the directions on the package. Set aside to cool and dry out.
Put the tofu, corn, scallions, carrot, basil, and salt in the bowl and mix well.
When the rice has fully cooled, add it to the bowl with the tofu and mix well.
Put the skillet over medium high heat and when it is hot, add the oil.

Add the rice and tofu mixture; reduce heat to low and press down the rice mixture with a spatula. Cover and cook 10 minutes. Press down again to help form a crust. Flip portions of the rice so that you get chunks of crispy rice. Cook until crispy, up to 20 minutes.

name: Cuban Beans and Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032354/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cuban-beans-and-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups black beans, canned, low-sodium (or cooked from dry)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the olive oil in a large nonstick skillet. Sauté the garlic, onion, and green bell pepper until golden, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the beans, broth, vinegar, and seasoning; bring to a boil then lower to a simmer. Cook covered for 5 minutes.
Spoon over cooked rice and serve.
serving_size: 1 1/2 cups prepared beans and rice, 1/4 of recipe

name: Cuban Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032334/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cuban-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup fresh lime juice (1 large or 2 small limes)
1 head Romaine lettuce (washed, patted dry with paper towels, and torn into bite-sized pieces)

steps: Put the oil, lime juice, garlic, salt, and pepper in the small bowl and mix well. Lemon juice can be used instead of lime juice.
Put the lettuce, tomatoes, onion, and radishes in the mixing bowl and toss to combine. White onion can be used instead of red onion.
Pour the dressing over the lettuce mixture and toss. Serve right away.
To make the dressing: To make the salad:

notes.text: For protein, add low-sodium canned tuna or salmon on top of the salad.

name: Cucumber Blueberry Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045448/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cucumber-blueberry-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon lime juice, freshly squeezed or bottled
1 medium greenhouse-grown cucumber, cut into small chunks

steps: In a small bowl whisk together vinaigrette ingredients.
In a large bowl mix together all salad ingredients, except bread.
When ready to serve, add vinaigrette to salad and toss.
Toast bread, then cut into four pieces.

name: Cucumber Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041958/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cucumber-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and thinly slice cucumber.
Mix all other ingredients in the mixing bowl.
Add cucumber slices and stir until coated.
Chill until serving.

name: Cucumber Salad with Tomatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041930/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cucumber-salad-tomatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss together the cucumbers, tomatoes, onions, couscous (or rice), dill, and salad dressing.
Chill for 1 hour.
Serve.

name: Cucumber Yogurt and Cream Cheese Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040506/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cucumber-yogurt-and-cream-cheese-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: salt and lemon pepper, to taste (optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Stir yogurt and cream cheese until smooth.
Rinse the cucumber under running water.
Slice the cucumber in half the long way and run a spoon down the middle to remove the seeds.
Chop the cucumber into small pieces.
Stir the cucumber, chopped garlic, and seasonings (optional) into the yogurt mixture.

notes.text: To quickly soften cream cheese, microwave for approximately 20 seconds.

name: Cucumber, Yogurt and Herb Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034321/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cucumber-yogurt-and-herb-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel, seed, and grate one cucumber. Slice other cucumber and set aside.
Mix yogurt, grated cucumber, sour cream, lemon juice, dill, and garlic in a serving bowl. Chill for 1 hour.
Arrange sliced cucumbers, tomatoes, broccoli, and carrots on a colorful platter. Serve with cucumber dip.

notes.text: Watch how to make this kid-friendly recipe on YouTube.

name: Cumin Lime Shrimp over Creamy Cauliflower Risotto
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033054/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/cumin-lime-shrimp-over-creamy-cauliflower-risotto
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 medium shrimp, peeled, deveined and tails removed
1 ripe, fresh avocado, halved, pitted, peeled and diced

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Microwave frozen “riced” cauliflower according to package directions, usually about 5-6 minutes; set aside.

Heat 1 Tbsp. olive oil in a medium nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the shrimp and cook 2 to 3 minutes per side until light pink and opaque. Place shrimp in a small bowl and season with cumin, lime zest, and salt.
Add remaining oil into the pan. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is soft, about 2 minutes. Add garlic and avocado and cook for one minute, until heated through.
Transfer avocado onion mixture into a blender or food processor and add lime juice. Cover and blend until smooth, stirring mixture with a spatula if needed.
Transfer heated “riced” cauliflower into the pan and top with pureed avocado onion mixture. Cook over medium heat, stirring gently until cauliflower has a beautiful green color.
Divide into two bowls and top with cooked shrimp.

notes.text: Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro and additional avocado slices. For more information, visit: https://loveonetoday.com/

name: Curried Brown Rice with Pumpkin Seeds, Apricots and Spinach
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040521/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/curried-brown-rice-pumpkin-seeds-apricots
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup brown rice, short grain, uncooked
1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 medium red onion, peeled and finely chopped
2 cups low-sodium vegetable broth (or low-sodium chicken broth)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse the rice well.
Heat the oil over medium heat in a large heavy saucepan.
Add the onions and garlic and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, then stir in the curry powder.
Add the rice and broth and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 30 to 45 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and stir in the apricots and spinach.
Replace cover and let sit for 10 minutes.
Add the pumpkin seeds, salt, pepper (and more curry if desired) and fluff with a fork.
Serve immediately.

name: Curried Chicken with Raisins and Mushrooms
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020654/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/curried-chicken-raisins-and-mushrooms
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 teaspoons olive oil (extra virgin or virgin)
2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 12 oz, diced into 1 inch cubes)
1/2 medium red bell pepper (cut into 3/4" squares)

steps: Heat olive oil in large sauté pan.
With heat on medium-high, place chicken in pan and cover with lid.
Cook chicken about 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms and peppers to pan and sauté 3 to 4 minutes.
Add chicken broth.
Gently mix in raisins, rice, and curry powder; bring to boil, reduce heat and cover.
Simmer until rice is done; fluff with fork and let sit 3 to 5 minutes before serving.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Add a side salad with light dressing and an 8 oz glass of fat-free milk. Time Saving Ideas: Purchase sliced mushrooms, fresh or frozen bell pepper strips, and pre-cooked, diced chicken.

name: Curried Chicken Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215026/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/curried-chicken-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 cooked cooled chicken thighs (about 3 cups shredded)
1 tablespoon curry powder (or more to taste)
1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro (and/or basil leaves)

steps: Put chicken in a bowl and add remaining ingredients. Mix to combine.
Cover and refrigerate at least one hour and up three days.

notes.text: If you do not have leftover chicken, you can poach chicken. Put 4 boneless, skinless chicken thighs in a pan and cover with cold water (about 4 cups) and bring to a boil over high heat. Lower the heat and cook for 10 minutes. Turn the heat off, turn the chicken pieces over and set aside for 20 minutes. Remove the thighs with a slotted spoon and set aside to cool completely. Shred and prepare recipe as directed. You can also substitute 2 cans of drained light tuna, instead of chicken thighs.

name: Curried Chickpea Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022335/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/curried-chickpea-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cans (15 ounces each) chickpeas, low-sodium, rinsed and drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add the chickpeas to a large bowl and mash with a potato masher. You can mash them to be as smooth or coarse as you desire.
Add all of the remaining ingredients to the bowl and mix until everything is combined.

notes.text: Add the Curried Chickpea Salad to a sandwich and add spinach or lettuce if desired. Also, try topping tossed salad with it instead of salad dressing.

name: Curried Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214948/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/curried-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel the onion, and chop it into small pieces.
Peel the potatoes, and chop them into 1 inch cubes.
Boil the potatoes in a medium saucepan until they are soft. Drain off the hot water.
Add ice cold water to cover the potatoes.
Melt the butter on medium heat in a frying pan or skillet.
Cook the onion in the butter until it turns yellow.
Drain the water from the potatoes and add them to the frying pan. Stir and cook until they absorb the butter.
Add the broth, curry powder, and lemon juice.
Cook until the potatoes have absorbed the broth.

name: Curried Quinoa and Cauliflower
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024747/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/curried-quinoa-and-cauliflower
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 head of cauliflower, trimmed and cut into small florets (about 1 1/2 pounds)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook quinoa until just tender, according to package directions.
Heat oil in saucepan over medium-high heat. Add curry powder and cumin, and cook, about 30 seconds, or until fragrant.
Stir in broth and chopped garlic. Bring to a boil.
Add cauliflower, cover, and return to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and simmer 3 minutes.
Add frozen peas and cook until cauliflower is just tender, stirring occasionally. Remove from heat.
Stir in 2 tablespoons broth from cauliflower mixture into yogurt in small bowl.
Add yogurt mixture to cauliflower. Fold in quinoa, cashews, and cilantro.
Sprinkle with green onion and top with a little fresh lime juice.
Optional: Season with a pinch of salt.

name: Curried Squash Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215036/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/curried-squash-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (14.5 ounce) low-sodium diced tomatoes (including liquid)
1 can (15.5 ounce) low-sodium white beans or chickpeas (drained and rinsed)

steps: Heat a large pot on the stove over medium heat and add oil. Add the onion, garlic and celery and cook about 10 minutes, until the onion is tender.
Add zucchini and curry powder and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the butternut squash, tomatoes and chickpeas and cover. Continue cooking about 10 minutes.
Serve with cooked brown rice.

notes.text: For additional flavor, add 1/2 cup raisins.

name: Curry Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031826/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/curry-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the sour cream, yogurt, and curry powder.
Store the dip in a covered container if you don’t plan to eat it right away.
Keep the dip in the refrigerator until you serve it.

notes.text: Serve with bite-sized raw vegetables, crackers, or pita bread.

name: Curtido Salvadoreño (Cabbage Salad)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032136/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/curtido-salvadoreno-cabbage-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Blanch the cabbage with boiling water for 1 minute. Discard the water.
Place the cabbage in a large bowl and add grated carrots, sliced onion, red pepper, oregano, olive oil, salt, brown sugar, vinegar, and water.
Place in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.

name: Dave’s Herb-Stuffed Mushrooms
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215402/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/daves-herb-stuffed-mushrooms
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3/4 cup canned, drained, no-salt added chickpeas (garbanzo beans)

steps: Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Clean mushrooms with a paper towel or vegetable brush; remove stems to use for the filling.
While oven is warming, put mushroom caps (open side down) in oven for 10 minutes. This will prepare the caps for stuffing.
Chop the garlic and onions and sauté with 1 teaspoon of olive oil. One minute before they are finished, add the four herbs. After 1 minute, remove from heat.
In a large bowl, mash mushroom stems and chickpeas.
Add all other ingredients. Mix well.
Lightly spray a baking sheet and the mushroom caps.
Stuff the mushrooms with the mixture and place on baking sheet.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes or until the stuffing is golden brown.
Remove from oven, sprinkle with an herb of your choice, and enjoy.

name: Deep Dish Apple Cranberry Pie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020738/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/deep-dish-apple-cranberry-pie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 large apples, peeled, cored, and sliced

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Stir all ingredients (except for the pie crust) together in a medium sized mixing bowl and place in a 10-inch deep dish pie pan.
Place one pie crust on top of the fruits. Cut 3 or 4 slits to allow the steam to escape.
Bake at 375 °F for about an hour. Serve warm. Refrigerate any leftovers.

name: Delicious Greens
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032052/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/delicious-greens
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 1/2 cups mustard or collard greens (about 1/2 pound)
1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse greens, remove stems, and tear in small pieces.
In a large saucepan, boil 3 quarts of water.
Add mustard greens, return to a boil and cook 3 minutes. Add cabbage and cook 1 more minute. Drain in colander.
Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium high heat. Add oil and sauté garlic and onion until light brown, about 3 minutes.
Add greens and vinegar and cook briefly, about 3 minutes. Serve hot.

name: Delicious Lentil Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033614/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/delicious-lentil-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups dry lentils, washed (soaking not necessary)
1 can (14.5 ounces) whole tomatoes, low-sodium, cut into pieces (or 3-4 fresh tomatoes cut in wedges)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Melt butter in a large skillet.
Sauté onion until tender.
Add water, lentils, Worcestershire sauce, oregano, and garlic powder.
Cover, bring to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add carrots, celery, and salt.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes more or until the vegetables are tender.
Add tomatoes. Heat thoroughly and serve.

name: Delicious Oven French Fries
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032311/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/delicious-oven-french-fries
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub potatoes and cut into 1/2 inch strips.
Place potato strips into ice water, cover, and chill for 1 hour or longer.
Preheat oven to 475 °F.
Remove potatoes and dry strips thoroughly.
Place garlic powder, onion powder, salt, white pepper, allspice, and pepper flakes in plastic bag.
Toss potatoes in spice mixture.
Brush potatoes with oil.
Place potatoes in nonstick shallow baking pan.
Cover with aluminum foil and place in preheated oven for 15 minutes.
Remove foil and continue baking uncovered for additional 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown. Turn fries occasionally to brown on all sides.

name: Deviled Eggs
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215316/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/deviled-eggs
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Hard boil eggs by placing eggs in a saucepan and covering them with water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to simmer; cook for 15 minutes.
Immediately rinse under cold water to stop cooking and to make it easy to peel off shells. Refrigerate peeled eggs (without shells) until ready for use.
Slice eggs into halves lengthwise. Remove yellow yolks and save whites.
Place yolks in a one-quart zip lock style bag along with the remaining ingredients (except the egg whites). Press out air.

Close bag and knead (mush together) until ingredients are well-blended. (Note: you could also put yolks in a bowl with other ingredients [except the egg whites] and mix together well until they look like a paste).

Push contents toward one corner of the bag. Cut about 1/2 inch off the corner of the bag. Squeezing the bag gently, fill reserved egg white hollows with the yolk mixture. (Note if you used a bowl, spoon the yolk mixture into the egg whites).
Chill to blend flavors.

name: Dilled Fish Fillets
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041524/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/dilled-fish-fillets
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound frozen haddock or cod fillets

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Thaw frozen fish in refrigerator overnight or thaw in microwave oven. Then, separate into 4 fillets or pieces
Place fish in a glass-baking dish. Cover with wax paper.
Cook at "medium" power in the microwave for 3 minutes. Remove cover, turn fish over, and sprinkle with lemon juice and seasonings.
Cover and continue cooking at "medium" power for 3 minutes or until fish flakes with a fork.
Wash hands with soap and water.
Separate into four fillets or pieces.
Place fish in heated fry pan. Sprinkle with lemon juice and seasonings.
Cover and cook over moderate heat until fish flakes when tested with a fork, about 5 minutes.
Microwave Method: Skillet method:
serving_size: 1 4 oz. piece of fish, 1/4 of recipe

name: Dirty Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215233/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/dirty-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 can low-sodium kidney beans, drained (about 8 ounces )

steps: In a small bowl, combine dried egg mix and water. Mix well and set aside.
In a large skillet, cook ground beef, onion, and green pepper in oil over medium heat for about 10 minutes.
Add dried egg mix to skillet. Scramble eggs over medium heat for about 5 minutes.
Add peas and beans to skillet. Cook for about 5 minutes.
Add rice and pepper to skillet. Stir to break up any clumps of rice. Cook for about 5 minutes. Serve hot.

notes.text: Tip for cooking ground beef: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef is 160 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.

name: Dried Bananas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045156/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/dried-bananas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: acidic fruit juice (lemon, lime, orange, pineapple) to reduce browning (optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice bananas into 1/8 to 1/4-inch slices.
(Optional) Dip banana slices into fruit juice to reduce browning. Sprinkle with cinnamon or other flavorings if desired.
Dry until pieces bend like thick leather and no longer feel sticky.

Cool. Store in an airtight container or bag. Oven Instructions: Set oven to lowest temperature possible (175 to 200 °F). Use convection bake if available. Arrange banana slices in a single layer on a wire rack or baking sheet. A wire rack will help the banana dry faster. A baking sheet takes longer and pieces need to be turned part way through drying. Drying takes 1 to 3 hours.; Dehydrator Instructions: Arrange banana slices in a single layer on dehydrator racks. Set dehydrator to 135 °F. Drying takes 6 to 12 hours.

name: Drop Biscuits (from Better Baking Mix)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032823/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/drop-biscuits-better-baking-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F. Lightly grease baking sheet.
Add oil and water to the dry mix. Stir just until all ingredients are wet.
Drop spoonsful 4 inches apart on baking sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes until lightly browned.

notes.text: Try these variations on this recipe: Herb Biscuits - Add to dry ingredients: 1 teaspoon Italian herb mix. Cheese Biscuits - Add to dry ingredients: 1/3 cup grated sharp cheese. Fruit Scones - Add to the dry ingredients: 1/4 cup sugar, 1/2 cup raisins or dried cranberries, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, or the grated rind of an orange or lemon.

name: Dutch Apple Yogurt Dessert
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044416/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/dutch-apple-yogurt-dessert
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon nuts (as topping or crunchy cereal)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a small bowl.
Cover and refrigerate until chilled.
Eat and enjoy as a snack or as a dessert.

name: Dutch Green Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214943/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/dutch-green-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain the beans, and save the liquid from the can in small bowl.
Pour 1/2 cup bean liquid into the saucepan.
Add the cornstarch in the bean liquid. Stir well.
Add the vinegar and brown sugar.
Put on medium heat and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low.
Add the green beans and onions. Heat and serve.

name: Eagle Nest
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020424/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/eagle-nest
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 canned peach halves, packed in juice

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place one peach half, cut side up, in center of plate for nest.
Place 1 tablespoon of cottage cheese in center of nest.
Place raisins on cottage cheese to make eggs.
Enjoy your Eagle Nest.

notes.text: Adults: If preparing with children, use a can opener to open peaches. Drain juice and discard sharp edged lid.

name: Easiest Banana Ice Cream
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045654/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/easiest-banana-ice-cream
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
When bananas have become very ripe, peel and slice them into medium size round pieces. Place on a plastic wrap covered baking sheet and put in freezer overnight.
Place frozen bananas in a food processor or blender with a small splash of milk (not over 1/4 cup total).
Pulse food processor or blender until bananas begin to break up. They will be tiny balls of bananas at this point.

Using a spoon or rubber spatula, scrape down the banana mixture. Continue running the food processor until the mixture is smooth and creamy. This may take a few minutes. The ice cream will look and tasted like soft serve ice cream when finished.
Serve in an ice cream cone or in a small bowl with a small ribbon of chocolate syrup on top (optional).

name: Easy Baked Acorn Squash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021440/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/easy-baked-acorn-squash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 tablespoons maple syrup or honey (can replace with 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper per squash half for a savory flavor)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Cut acorn squash in half and scoop out seeds.
Fill a baking pan with about 1/2 inch of water.
Place the squash in the pan, flesh side up. If they are lopsided, slice the underside horizontally so the bottom sits flat on the pan.
Add 1 tablespoon maple syrup or honey (or ground pepper if you prefer a savory flavor) to each half and spread evenly across the flesh.
Bake for about 1 hour, or until flesh is tender.
Serve as a side with meat or another main dish.

notes.text: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.

name: Easy Beef Supper
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045552/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/easy-beef-supper
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cans (about 30 ounces) no salt added diced tomatoes, drained
1 can (about 15 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans, drained

steps: In a large pan, cook ground beef over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes. Drain fat.
Add onion, green pepper, and tomatoes to ground beef and cook until onion turns light brown.
Turn down the heat to a simmer. Add macaroni, tomato juice, spices, and beans to the pan. Stir well.
Cover the pan and simmer for about 20 minutes.
Remove pan from heat, stir, and serve hot.

notes.text: Tip for cooking ground beef: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef is 160 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.

name: Easy-As-A-Mix Pizza (from Better Baking Mix)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032828/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/easy-mix-pizza-better-baking-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 °F. Grease a 12x15 inch or larger baking sheet, or 12-inch pizza pan.
Measure mix into a bowl. Add oil and water. Stir to form soft dough.
Transfer dough onto baking sheet. Sprinkle with flour. Dip fingers in flour and pat dough into a circle about 11-12 inches across.
Spread pizza crust with tomato sauce. Leave about 1/2 inch around edge with no sauce.
Sprinkle with onion, seasoning and cheese
Bake 10-12 minutes until edges are brown and cheese is melted and starting to brown.
Refrigerate any leftovers within 2 hours.

notes.text: Use leftover tomato sauce from a can within 5 days, or freeze to use later.

name: Easy Oven Fish with Spinach Basil Dipping Sauce & Spiced Apples
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033804/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/easy-oven-fish-spinach-basil-dipping-sauce-spiced-apples
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: For the Spinach Basil Dipping Sauce:
1 cup frozen chopped spinach, thawed and drained
1 pound frozen pollock, or other white fish, such as haddock or cod (partially thawed)

steps: Place rack in center and heat oven to 450 °F. Spray cookie sheet with cooking spray.
To make dipping sauce, place all ingredients in a blender or food processor; blend or process until smooth.
Cut pollock into strips 1-inch wide (easiest when fish is partially, rather than full, thawed) and place on prepared baking sheet.
Mix breading ingredients (bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, and pepper) in a shallow dish or pie pan; place flour and egg whites in separate dishes.
Dip fish sticks in flour, then in egg whites, then breading mix, coating evenly.
Return coated fish sticks to baking sheet, spacing evenly. Cook fish until it is 145 °F, confirmed with a food thermometer, about 10 to 12 minutes, golden brown, turning as needed.
While fish sticks are baking, cut apples in quarters and core them; slice into smaller wedges (about 12 per apple).
Toss with raisins, pecans, and cinnamon.
Heat butter in medium sauce pan. Add fruit mix.
Sauté lightly about 3 to 5 minutes. Apples should still be slightly crisp.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with 100% fruit juice and green beans or asparagus.

name: Easy Oven Packet Caribbean Tilapia with Pears and Carnival Roasted Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020612/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/easy-oven-packet-caribbean-tilapia-pears-and-carnival-roasted-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 yellow bell pepper, cut into 1" chunks
1 cup green beans (fresh, frozen, or canned)
1 pound tilapia fillets, fresh, or frozen (4-4-oz tilapia fillets)
1 tablespoon salt-free Caribbean citrus seasoning blend

steps: Heat oven to 425 °F.
Scrub potatoes under running water, cut into 1-inch chunks.
In a large bowl, toss potatoes with other vegetables, seasonings, and olive oil. Spread mix in a 2-quart baking dish and place in oven.
Roast until potatoes and other vegetables are tender, about 30 to 40 minutes.
About 15 minutes after the potato dish was placed in the oven, put in a baking sheet with fish packets, prepared as follows:
Brush fish with olive oil, coat with seasoning blend.
Place each filet in the center of a square of aluminum foil (or substitute foil with parchment paper).
Cut pears into quarters and core; slice into thin wedges (about 8 to 12 per pear).Top fish with pear wedges.
Bring the foil over the fish and fruit. Fold and pinch the seams.
Place foil packets on a baking sheet. Bake about 20 minutes, until tilapia is cooked to an internal temperature of 145 °F, confirmed with a food thermometer, and fruit is tender.
To serve, carefully open the packet, slide contents onto individual serving plates, and add roasted vegetables.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of non-fat milk.

name: Eating Smart Seasoning Mix
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033121/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/eating-smart-seasoning-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients.
Store in airtight container.
Use in recipes as indicated.

notes.text: Recipe makes about 2.5 cups, one serving size = 1/4 cup. This recipe is used in the Chili Tomato Macaroni and Beef & Potatoes recipes.

name: Egg Foo Young
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045714/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/egg-foo-young
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup cooked chicken, diced (can also use beef)
2 teaspoons cooking oil (or oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Beat eggs with electric mixer (or by hand) until very thick and light, about 5 minutes.
Fold in bean sprouts, chicken or beef, mushrooms, and onion.
Heat oil in frying pan over moderate heat.
Pour egg mixture by half cupsful into the pan. Brown on one side; turn and brown the other side. Keep warm while preparing the sauce.
Mix sauce ingredients in small saucepan until smooth.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Serve sauce over patties.

notes.text: Use only clean eggs with no cracks in shells.

name: Egg Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042147/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/egg-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put the eggs in a pan of cold water. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Cool promptly in cold water, then in refrigerator, so the eggs will be easy to shell.
Remove the shells from eggs, and chop the eggs finely.
Mix all the ingredients together.

name: Eggplant and Pepper Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045339/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/eggplant-and-pepper-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Use a vegetable peeler to remove the peel from the eggplant.
Chop the eggplant into 1-inch cubes.
Chop the red peppers.
Peel and chop the onion.
Put all the ingredients in a large bowl. Stir together.
Spread the ingredients on a baking tray.
Bake at 400 °F for 45 minutes. While vegetables are baking, stir it a few times.
When the eggplant is lightly browned and soft, take the vegetables out of the oven.
Let cool for at least 10 minutes.
Put the dip the blender. Blend until smooth.
Serve the dip cold or at room temperature.

notes.text: Try this low-fat dip with cut vegetables, toast, or as a spread on sandwiches.

name: Eggplant Stir Fry
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025457/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/eggplant-stir-fry
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup green bell pepper, cut into strips
3 tablespoons Italian salad dressing, low fat

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place eggplant, zucchini, green bell pepper, onions and salad dressing into a skillet.
Stir lightly to combine and cook over low heat until tender.
Stir in cherry tomatoes and cook for 3-5 minutes. Serve over cooked brown rice.

name: Eggs over Kale and Sweet Potato Grits
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034019/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/eggs-over-kale-and-sweet-potato-grits
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Coat 4 individual soufflé dishes with 1 tsp vegetable oil.
Make 3 to 4 slits in sweet potatoes; cook in microwave until just soft.
When sweet potatoes are cool enough to handle, peel, cut into chunks, and puree in food processor.
Heat remaining vegetable oil in sauce pan, and sauté kale about 5 minutes.
In a medium sauce pan, boil water and milk, add grits and sweet potatoes; cook for 5 minutes. Remove from heat; stir in sautéed kale.
Divide grits mixture evenly among 4 soufflé dishes (or place all in casserole dish).
Make 4 depressions in the grits mixture with the back of a large spoon. Carefully break one egg into each hollow.
Bake uncovered for 30 minutes until eggs are cooked. Let cool 10 minutes before serving.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with an 8-ounce glass of 100% grapefruit juice.

serving_size: 1/4 of the recipe of Eggs over Kale and Sweet Potato Grits

name: Elaine’s Green-Mash Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035059/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/elaines-green-mash-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Simmer peeled, diced potatoes for about 10 minutes until soft when pierced with a fork.
Cook 1 cup peas in microwave for about 3 minutes; drain and reserve.
Heat milk until hot. Add garlic cloves to milk and let stand for 5 minutes.
Puree peas, 1/4 cup milk, and garlic cloves using a blender.
Drain potatoes and begin to mash.
Slowly add 3/4 cup milk while mashing.
Blend in the puréed peas and garlic, margarine, and white pepper (optional) to the mashed potatoes.
Place mashed potatoes in a serving dish and keep warm.
Just before serving, lightly sprinkle Kosher salt on top of potatoes.

name: Enchilada Bake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043026/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/enchilada-bake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups black beans, cooked (or low-sodium canned)
1 cup kernel corn (1/2 of a 15.2 ounce can, low-sodium, drained and rinsed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet heat oil over medium-high heat; sauté onion and garlic 2 to 3 minutes.
Add beans, corn, cumin and 1/2 cup salsa. Cook 3-4 minutes, coarsely mashing beans with back of spoon.
Spoon 1/3 cup filling onto each tortilla; roll up.
Spoon 1/2 cup salsa into 11x7x2 inch baking dish. Arrange tortillas seam side down; top with remaining 1 cup sauce.
Cover and bake in 350 °F oven for 15 to 20 minutes.
Uncover; top with cheese. Bake 2 minutes longer or until cheese is melted.

name: Enchilada Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042446/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/enchilada-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound 90% lean ground beef (or other ground meat)
1/2 cup onion (chopped, or 1 Tbsp onion powder)
1 can whole corn, low-sodium (15.2 ounce, or any low-sodium canned vegetable, drained)
4 tablespoons taco seasoning mix (dry, or dry enchilada sauce)
mushrooms, olives or any favorite vegetable (1/2 cup sliced, optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook meat and onion until onion juices are clear.
Drain juice and fat from cooked meat and onions.
Add corn, taco seasoning, and rice.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add grated cheese to top; cover and let set for 5 minutes.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: English Muffin Veggie Pizza
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045017/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/english-muffin-veggie-pizza
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese, shredded, part skim

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the broccoli to make 1 cup of chopped broccoli.
Put the broccoli in a saucepan with water. Cook on medium until tender.
Drain the water from the saucepan. Let the broccoli cool.
Cut 4 English muffins in half. Toast the 8 muffin halves.
Shred the mozzarella cheese to make 1/2 cup of shredded cheese.
Peel and shred the carrots to make 3 tablespoons shredded carrots.
Spoon 2 tablespoons pizza sauce over each English muffin half.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon shredded mozzarella cheese on top of each half.
Put 2 tablespoons broccoli and 1 teaspoon shredded carrots on top of each half.
Sprinkle each half with 1 teaspoon grated parmesan cheese.
Toast in the toaster oven for 2 minutes, until the cheese melts.

notes.text: Try making these pizzas with whole wheat muffins.

serving_size: 2 pizzas (each made from 1/2 English muffin), 1/4 of recipe (185g)

name: European Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042432/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/european-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 large yellow bell pepper, cut in strips (about 1 1/2 cups)
1 1/2 cups croutons (whole grain if available, about 24 croutons)

steps: Place all vinaigrette ingredients in a blender, blend until smooth; set aside. (Note: Vinaigrette can be made ahead and refrigerated.)
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet.
Sauté chicken until cooked thoroughly; remove from pan, and let cool.
Slice onions.
Toss cut vegetables with European blend salad greens.
On individual serving plates, top salad with chicken and croutons, drizzle with dressing, and finish with fresh ground pepper, if desired.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with fruit, non-fat milk, and whole grain bread.

name: Eve’s Tasty Turkey Tetrazzini
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020641/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/eves-tasty-turkey-tetrazzini
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 ounces whole-wheat fettuccine, spaghetti, macaroni, or other noodles

steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F. Lightly grease a 9x9 inch baking dish.
Cook pasta in a large pot of boiling water until tender. (Check cooking time for pasta; remove pasta approximately 2 minutes early.)
While pasta is cooking, melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the mushrooms and thyme. Stir and cook until mushrooms are softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in flour until well blended. (Note: Start with 1/3 cup flour and add more, if needed.)
While whisking, slowly add chicken broth and milk. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer until sauce is thickened and smooth, about 5 minutes.
Add turkey, toasted almonds, frozen peas, and cooked pasta. Gently mix together. Pour into the baking dish and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake until the sauce is bubbling and the cheese is golden brown, 25 to 35 minutes. Let cool 15 minutes before serving.
serving_size: 1 Portion of Eve's Tasty Turkey Tetrazzini

name: Fabulous Fruit Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042652/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fabulous-fruit-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup frozen strawberries, unsweetened, coarsely chopped (or other fruit, fresh or frozen)

steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 400 °F. Spray muffin tin with non-stick cooking spray.
In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda. Stir well until all ingredients are blended.
In another bowl, combine buttermilk, margarine, egg, and vanilla. Pour this mixture into the dry ingredients (made in step #3).
Using a large spoon, gently stir ingredients just until moist (do not over-mix). Add fruit and stir gently (do not over-mix).
Spoon batter evenly into 9 muffin cups.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Serve hot or cold. Muffins may be frozen for later use.

name: Falafel with Yogurt Sandwich
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043240/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/falafel-yogurt-sandwich
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup dry garbanzo beans/chickpeas (sorted and rinsed)
1/3 tablespoon parsley (1 sprig or about 1 teaspoon, chopped)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put beans and water in large pot and soak by the overnight or quick-soak method.
Cook until tender, about 2 hours. Add more water if necessary. Drain.
Slowly heat oil and sauté garlic and 1 onion until tender (5 to 7 minutes).
Mash cooked beans, sautéed vegetables, parsley, salt, lemon juice and hot pepper sauce until smooth.
With floured hands, form ovals with bean mixture (about 1/4 cup each). Roll in flour.
Fry falafel, with the remaining oil in skillet, until golden brown. Drain on paper towel.
Combine yogurt with remaining onion.
Serve falafel in pocket bread topped with yogurt.

notes.text: If the batter is too moist, add breadcrumbs to make it thicker. It may take up to a cup of breadcrumbs.

name: Fall Veggie Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044921/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fall-veggie-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Remove the skin from the eggplant. Cut the eggplant into cubes. Chop the tomatoes into small pieces.
Cut the green pepper in half. Remove the seeds and cut it into small pieces.
Chop the onion into small pieces.
Cut the garlic into tiny pieces.
Combine all of the ingredients (except for the cheese) and cook in a large skillet over medium heat until tender.
Top with the Parmesan cheese and serve.

name: French Toast
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032924/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fantastic-french-toast
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the griddle over medium heat, or set an electric frying pan at 375 °F.
Put eggs, milk, and vanilla in a pie pan or shallow bowl and beat with a fork until well mixed.
Grease the griddle or pan with a thin layer of oil or use nonstick spray.
Dip both sides of bread, one slice at a time, in the egg mixture and cook on the hot griddle or frying pan.
Cook on one side until golden brown. Turn the bread over to cook the other side. It will take about 4 minutes on each side.
Optional: serve with syrup, applesauce, fruit slices, or jam.

name: Farmers Market Gazpacho
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033926/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/farmers-market-gazpacho
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 medium cucumbers, diced into 1/4 inch pieces
3 medium red bell peppers, seeded and diced into 1/4 inch pieces
3 medium green peppers, seeded and diced into 1/4 inch pieces
4 medium celery stalks, diced into 1/4 inch pieces
2 medium tomatoes, diced into 1/4 inch pieces
1 medium onion, diced into 1/4 inch pieces

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients except salt, pepper, and lemons in a bowl.
Remove 2 cups of the mixture and reserve.
Using a blender or food processor, puree the remaining mixture in the bowl.
Add 2 cups of reserved mixture to the pureed mixture.
Season with salt, pepper (optional) and the juice from the lemons.
Cover mixture and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
Serve cold, garnished with chopped cilantro.

name: Farmers Market Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035137/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/farmers-market-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15 ounces) low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl. Chill until serving time.
Drain before serving.
Serve with low-fat baked tortilla chips or fresh vegetables.

notes.text: This salsa uses fresh vegetables that are available year-round and add flavor and beautiful color. Kids and grown-ups alike can't resist how good it tastes. If you have a hand-held chopper, this is an easy task for kids in helping with the recipe. Safety Tip: If cutting the corn off the cob, adult supervision is a good idea.

name: Fat-Free Apple Crumb Dessert
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035427/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fat-free-apple-crumb-dessert
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Move the oven rack to the center of the oven. Then preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Spray the bottom and sides of a 9 inch square baking dish with nonstick cooking spray.
Wash and peel the apples. Cut them into thin slices.
Spread the apple slices evenly over the bottom of the baking dish.
In a small bowl, use a fork to mix the oatmeal, brown sugar and cinnamon.
Spread the oatmeal mix evenly over the apples in the baking dish.
Lightly pour the apple juice over the oatmeal mixture.
Cover the dish and bake for 20 to 30 minutes until apples are just starting to soften.
Uncover and bake for another 15 to 20 minutes until apples are soft.

name: Feather Rolls
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035258/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/feather-rolls
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix 2 1/2 cups whole wheat flour, dry yeast, and non-fat dry milk in large mixer bowl. Add water, oil, and sugar (or honey). Mix well 1 to 2 minutes.
Turn off mixer, cover, and let dough sit for 10 minutes.
Add eggs and salt. Turn on mixer. Add remaining flour, 1 cup at a time, until dough begins to form a ball.
Knead for 5 to 6 minutes. Dough should be very soft and manageable. Stiff dough produces heavy, dry rolls. If dough stiffens while mixing, drizzle a little warm water over dough as it kneads.
Dough may be used immediately or covered and stored in the refrigerator for several days.
Lightly oil hands and counter top if needed. Shape immediately into rolls. Let rise until very light.
Bake at 350 °F for 18 to 20 minutes. Do not overbake.

notes.text: * Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Festive Microwave Baked Apples
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214814/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/festive-microwave-baked-apples
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 apple (medium, skinned and cored (not cut into pieces))

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place apple on plate with opening facing up (cored apples should have bottom intact).
Stir sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon in a separate cup, and sprinkle into and onto apple.
Sprinkle raisins on and around apple.
Drop butter alternative spread onto apple and cover with plastic wrap or wax paper.
Microwave on HIGH for 2 1/2 to 3 minutes.
Let sit outside of microwave for at least 30 seconds before eating. It will be HOT.

notes.text: Fruit is naturally sweet so try making this without sugar.

name: Fiesta Hummus
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021559/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fiesta-hummus
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain and mash garbanzo beans in blender, food processor, or with fork. Add remaining ingredients.
Blend until smooth.
Chill one hour or overnight.
Serve on crackers or tortilla chips. Promptly refrigerate leftovers.

name: Fiesta Lettuce Wraps and Pepper Boats
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033821/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fiesta-lettuce-wraps-and-pepper-boats
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound tilapia filets, fresh or frozen (thawed)
1/2 cup yellow corn (frozen or canned, no-salt added)

steps: Slice peppers in half vertically. Arrange lettuce and 8 pepper halves on a serving platter.
Cook brown rice according to package directions.
To make salsa fresca, dice remaining pepper halves, tomato, and onion; mix with corn, garlic, jalapeño pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Sprinkle both sides of tilapia filets with Southwest chipotle seasoning.

Heat 1 1/2 tablespoons canola oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add fish to pan, and cook for 3 minutes on each side (cook fish until it is opaque, 145 ºF). Flake with a fork and place in a serving dish.
When rice is done, stir in remaining 1/2 tablespoon oil, juice from one lime, and ¼ tsp salt. Cut remaining lime into wedges.
To serve, set out pepper-lettuce platter, rice, fish, salsa fresca, sour cream, and lime, and let diners build their own boats and wraps

notes.text: Serving Suggestion: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of fat-free (skim) milk. Substitute brown rice with another quick cooking grain, such as whole-wheat couscous if desired.

name: Party Mix
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214847/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fiesta-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup cereal with fruit (flakes with raisins type)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix cereals together in a large bowl.
Add raisins, peanuts, and coconut; mix well.
Eat it dry or with milk.

name: Fiesta Rice Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031936/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fiesta-rice-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 sweet bell pepper, green, red, or yellow (chopped)
1 can kidney beans, low-sodium (15.5 ounce, drained, rinsed)
2 tablespoons cilantro (or other fresh herbs) (chopped fine)
2 tablespoons red wine vinegar (or white or cider)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and chop vegetables and mix with cooked rice.
In a small bowl, add vinegar, oil, dill, salt and pepper. (Or use your favorite dressing.) Pour over rice mixture.
Add beans and toss well. Serve cold and enjoy!

name: Fiesta Stuffed Avocado
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032614/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fiesta-stuffed-avocado
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tomato sliced and diced (~2 Tbsp tomatoes, diced)
1/2 ripe, fresh avocado, halved, pitted and peeled

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a bowl, combine black beans, tomatoes and onion. Squeeze in fresh lemon juice.
Serve in fresh avocado half.

notes.text: For more information, visit: https://loveonetoday.com/

name: Fig Bars
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043646/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fig-bars
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F. Lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking pan.
Combine figs, walnuts, sugar, orange juice, and hot water in a mixing bowl and set aside.
Mix together margarine or butter and brown sugar until creamy. Add egg and mix until smooth.
Mix flour and baking soda. Stir into egg mixture. Blend in oats to make soft dough.
Reserve 1 cup of dough for topping. With floured fingertips, press the remaining dough into a thin layer on the bottom of the baking pan.
Spread fig mixture evenly over the dough. Crumble reserved dough over top, allowing fig mixture to show.
Bake 30 minutes or until golden brown. Cool completely in baking pan. Cut into 24 bars (about 2 1/2 x 2 inches).

name: Fish with Spinach
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032441/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fish-spinach
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 yellow onion (peeled and chopped into 1/4 inch pieces)
2 cups canned low-sodium diced tomatoes (or fresh tomatoes)
1/4 cup Kalamata olives (or other Greek olives pitted and coarsely chopped)

steps: Put the skillet on the stove over high heat. When it is hot, add 1 1/2 teaspoons oil.
Add fish. Cook about 5 minutes per side, until deeply browned. Remove the fish to the plate and cover.

Reheat the skillet to medium heat. Add the remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons oil, onion, and garlic. Cook about 7 minutes. Add tomatoes and water. Cook about 10 minutes, until the mixture thickens and turns from bright red to an orange color.
Return fish to skillet with the tomato mixture. Cover with spinach and sprinkle with olives. Cover skillet. Cook about 2 minutes over low heat until the spinach is steamed. Serve right away.

notes.text: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.

name: Fish Tacos
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024848/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fish-tacos
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup green cabbage, sliced and chopped
4 (4-ounces each) tilapia fillets (or any white fish)
1 teaspoon chili powder (more or less to taste)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Clean and chop onion, cilantro, and cabbage. Mix in a bowl and set aside.
Coat the baking sheet with cooking spray. Lightly sprinkle fish fillets with chili powder and place on the baking pan.

Place in the oven about 6 inches from the broiler and cook for approximately 3 to 4 minutes, or until fish is fully cooked. You will know the fish is done when it "flakes" or pulls apart easily when separated with a fork.
Lightly fry tortillas on an oiled griddle or skillet, or heat tortillas in the microwave oven for just a few seconds until softened and hot.
Fill tortilla with fish, cabbage, onion, and cilantro and fold in half. Serve with salsa and citrus slices, if desired.

name: Five Happiness Fried Noodles
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024741/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/five-happiness-fried-noodles
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of your choice, divided)
1 cup bamboo shoots (julienned sliced thinly in strips)
2 dried shiitake mushrooms (or about 1/2 cup, soaked, stems removed, and julienned)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot on high heat, bring 10 cups of water to boil. Cook noodles in boiling water until tender or “al dente,” approximately 5 to 7 minutes; drain and set aside.
Heat a non-stick wok or pan over high heat. Add 1/2 tablespoon oil, swirling to coat the pan, add noodles and pan-fry until noodles are golden, about 7 to 10 minutes. Remove noodles from wok.
Add remaining 1/2 tablespoon oil to wok, add vegetables, and stir-fry until just cooked, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Return noodles to the wok, add salt, sugar and soy sauce.
Stir to combine and serve.

name: Fried Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043120/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/flavorful-fried-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons canola oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large frying pan over medium heat, cook rice, minced onion, and carrots in oil, stirring often until lightly browned.
Slowly add water. Reduce heat, cover and simmer until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender, about 20 minutes.
Beat eggs and egg whites in a bowl. Stir in milk, peas, and soy sauce. Pour over hot rice mixture in fry pan.
Cook on medium heat. As mixture begins to thicken, gently draw a spatula across bottom and sides of pan. This allows egg mixture to cook. Continue until eggs are firm.

name: Flour Tortillas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040701/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/flour-tortillas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups all-purpose flour (or 1 1/2 cup all purpose flour and 1/2 cup whole wheat flour)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add oil and mix until crumbly.
Start with 1/2 cup of water and add 1 tablespoon at a time until mixture forms a loose crumbly ball.
Turn onto a lightly floured surface; knead 6 to 8 times or until smooth.
Divide into 10 balls. Roll each piece into an 8 inch circle.
Heat a 12 inch dry skillet over medium-high heat. Place one tortilla at a time into skillet and cook until light brown spots appear on bottom. Turn over and cook on other side until lightly browned.

name: Food Group Funny Face
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043209/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/food-group-funny-face
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 graham cracker (large, or use whole grain or saltine crackers)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spread peanut butter on a cracker in the shape of a face.
Sprinkle grated cheese at top for hair.
Place raisins on cracker for mouth.
Use peas for eyes and 1/2 grape for nose.

notes.text: This snack is intended for children over age two. Do not serve to younger children who may choke.

name: Four Layer Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022119/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/four-layer-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 package frozen mixed vegetables, 10 ounces (or low-sodium canned mixed vegetables)
1/4 cup cheese, low-fat shredded (cheddar or colby jack)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook ground beef in frying pan until brown. Rinse in warm water and drain to remove excess fat.
Scrub potatoes and cut into slices without peeling.
Place potatoes in a large baking or casserole dish. Top with vegetables, ground beef, and cheese.
Pour milk over the casserole. Add salt and pepper as desired.
Cover with a lid or foil. Bake at 350 °F for 1 hour or microwave in non-metal baking or casserole dish for 19 to 23 minutes on high.

name: French Salad Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043932/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/french-salad-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all the ingredients in a jar or bottle with a lid.
Put on the lid. Shake well.
Chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour before serving.

notes.text: Try this dressing on cut vegetables or salad. After serving, keep any leftover dressing in the fridge.

name: French Spinach Frittata
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041459/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/french-spinach-frittata
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups spinach, finely chopped (if frozen spinach is used, thaw and squeeze out excess liquid)
4 scallions (white and green parts chopped into 1/4 inch-pieces)

steps: Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Put the eggs, salt, and pepper in the mixing bowl and stir with a fork until well combined.
Add scallions, spinach, and feta cheese and mix well.
Put an 8-inch ovenproof skillet on the stove over medium heat and when hot, add oil.
Pour the egg mixture into the skillet and carefully transfer to the oven. Bake until the eggs are set and the top is golden, about 30 minutes.
Serve right away or cover and refrigerate overnight.

notes.text: Cheddar, Swiss, or ricotta cheese can be used instead of feta.

name: Fresh Fruit with Cinnamon Yogurt Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041508/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fresh-fruit-cinnamon-yogurt-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Core and slice the apple.
Slice banana into thin circles.
Peel the orange and break it into sections.
Pour the orange juice into a small bowl.
Dip the fruit pieces into the orange juice to prevent browning.
Arrange on a plate.
Mix the yogurt and cinnamon in a small bowl.
Put the bowl of yogurt and cinnamon next to the fruit. Use it as a dip for the fruit.

notes.text: Try making this with other favorite fruits.

name: Fresh Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040959/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fresh-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 jalapeno chiles, finely chopped, seeded if desired

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium bowl, mix all ingredients.
Serve or store salsa in refrigerator for up to three days in a covered plastic or glass container.

name: Fresh Tomato Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031821/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fresh-tomato-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup tomatoes, finely chopped (or 1/2 can, about 8 ounces, low-sodium diced tomatoes)
1/2 cup apple, peeled and finely chopped
1 teaspoon fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped (optional)
1 tablespoon cayenne pepper or jalapeño chilies, chopped (optional)

steps: In a medium-sized bowl, combine tomato, apple, onion, and lime juice (or lemon juice). Mix well.
Add garlic, vegetable oil, and salt to bowl. If using parsley, cilantro, cayenne pepper, or jalapeño chilies, add them too. Mix well.
Cover bowl and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Serve cold.

name: Fresh Tomato Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215154/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fresh-tomato-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
2 teaspoons garlic, minced (or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash the ripe tomatoes. Cut out stem ends. Chop into small pieces and set aside in a large bowl.
In a large pan, heat the oil over medium high heat. Add onion, green pepper, carrots and garlic. Stir-fry until tender, about three minutes.
Add seasonings and tomatoes. Bring to a gentle boil.
