Lower heat and simmer gently, uncovered, until tomatoes turn to a sauce, about 40 minutes. Serve over freshly cooked pasta.

name: Fried Rice with Chicken and Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050532/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fried-rice-chicken-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (Or cooking oil of your choice)
3/4 cup cooked bite-size pieces of chicken

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add rice and stir for 5 minutes.
Stir in carrot, bell pepper, onion, broccoli, soy sauce, black pepper, and garlic powder. Cook until vegetables are tender.
Remove mixture from pan.
Pour eggs into pan and scramble.
Put vegetable mix and rice back in the pan and mix with scrambled eggs.
Add chicken and cook until hot.
Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Frosted Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042736/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/frosted-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 s sprays of cooking spray (for cake pan)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 325 °F.
Grease with small amount of cooking oil or use non-stick cooking oil spray on a 10-inch round pan (at least 2 1/2 inches high). Powder pan with flour. Tap out excess flour.
Sift together flour and baking powder.
In a separate bowl, beat together margarine and sugar until soft and creamy.
Beat in eggs, vanilla, and orange peel.
Gradually add the flour mixture alternating with milk, beginning and ending with flour.
Pour the mixture into the pan. Bake for 40-45 minutes or until done. Let cake cool for 5-10 minutes before removing from the pan. Let cool completely before icing.
Cream together cream cheese and milk until smooth. Add cocoa. Blend well.
Slowly add sugar until icing is smooth. Mix in vanilla.
Smooth icing over top and sides of cooled cake.
Cake: Icing:

name: Frozen Banana Pops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045350/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/frozen-banana-pops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/8 cup orange juice or lemon juice (2 Tablespoons)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel each banana and cut in half (width-wise).
Insert craft stick into bottom of each banana half. Dip each banana half into juice.
Wrap in foil and freeze for two or more hours.

notes.text: Optional Toppings: Dip in chocolate, then roll in chopped nuts, crushed cereal, shredded coconut, or sprinkles.

name: Frozen Fruit Cups
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214759/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/frozen-fruit-cups
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup strawberries, frozen, unsweetened (thawed and undrained)
1 cup crushed pineapple, juice packed (undrained, canned)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Line 18 muffin-tin cups with paper baking cups.
Dice or mash bananas and place in a large mixing bowl.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Spoon into muffin-tin cups and freeze at least 3 hours or until firm. Remove frozen cups and store in a plastic bag in freezer.
Before serving, remove paper cups and let stand 10 minutes.

notes.text: Watch how to make this kid-friendly recipe on YouTube.

name: Frozen Fruit Pops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031620/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/frozen-fruit-pops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup crushed pineapple, canned, juiced packed
6 us fluid ounces orange juice, frozen concentrate (thawed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the ingredients in a medium-size bowl. Divide into 4 paper cups.
Freeze until slushy - about 60 minutes. Insert a wooden stick half way through the center of each fruit pop.
Freeze until hard or at least 4 hours. Peel away the paper cup before you eat the fruit pop.

notes.text: You can mix ingredients and freeze in ice cube tray instead of cups, making great "ice cubes" in fruit juice. Try other fruits or juice concentrates for variety.

name: Frozen Pear Pops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231030904/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/frozen-pear-pops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 ounces frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed
ice cube tray or small paper cups

steps: Cut canned pears into small pieces.
Add yogurt and orange juice to cut pears and mix well to combine.
Divide into 8 ice cubes squares (or 4 small paper cups).
Place in cut straws or popsicle sticks.
Freeze and enjoy!

name: Fruit and Peanut Butter Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022408/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-and-peanut-butter-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare fruit by washing and slicing if necessary.
Arrange fruit on a plate around a small bowl.
To make dip, combine yogurt, vanilla, and peanut butter in a small bowl.
Mix well.
Chill dip in refrigerator until ready to serve.

notes.text: Can use six cups of any washed fruit. Be creative! Spread dip on a tortilla, add banana, and roll up.

name: Fruit and Yogurt Breakfast Shake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033946/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-and-yogurt-breakfast-shake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Blend banana with pineapple juice, yogurt, and strawberries in a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Divide shake between 2 glasses and serve immediately.

name: Fruit Cole Slaw
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041443/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-cole-slaw
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can fruit cocktail (15 ounces, juice packed, drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Shred cabbage.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl.

notes.text: * Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Fruit Compote
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034150/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-compote
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup pineapple chunks (8 ounce can, juice packed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain the juice from the canned pineapple into a small saucepan.
Stir in orange juice and cornstarch. Blend until smooth.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Let the juice mix cool to room temperature.
While the juice mix is cooling, peel and slice the banana. Wash the pear and peaches and cut them into cubes.
Pour the cooled juice mix into a large bowl. Add the pieces of pineapple, banana, pear, and peaches. Stir together.

notes.text: You can serve this compote in serving dishes, or over frozen yogurt or waffles.

name: Fruit Crisp
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025309/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-crisp
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/3 cup canola oil (or unsalted butter, melted)

steps: Preheat the oven to 350 °F. Lightly grease a baking dish with butter or oil.
Combine the apples, flour, and white sugar to make the filling.
To prepare the topping, mix the oats, whole wheat flour, white sugar, brown sugar, and salt. Add the oil (or butter) and stir into the dry ingredients.
Fill the baking pan with the fruit mixture and then cover with the crumble topping.
Transfer to the oven and bake until the fruit is tender and the topping is golden, about 45 minutes.
Serve right away or cover and refrigerate up to 2 days.

notes.text: Frozen unsweetened berries, like blueberries, can be used instead of apples.

name: Fruit Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032622/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 us fluid ounce orange juice, 100% juice, frozen concentrate (thawed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, combine yogurt, orange juice concentrate, lime juice, and brown sugar.
Mix well.
Place bowl containing dip on a large plate and surround with fruit.

name: Fruit Dippers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231051047/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-dippers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups fruit (grapes, banana slices, apple wedges, strawberries)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine yogurt and peanuts. Mix with a spoon.
Place a toothpick in the center of each fruit.
Dip fruit into the yogurt peanut mixture.

name: Fruit & Feta Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032618/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-feta-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup medium red onion, thinly sliced

steps: Whisk together vinaigrette ingredients.
Toss with remaining ingredients and serve.

name: Fruit Juice Slush
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034942/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-juice-slush
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a blender, place juice concentrate, water, and half of ice.
To prevent spillage, do not pass the top line of the blender.
Blend while gradually adding remaining ice. Serve.

notes.text: Use any flavor of juice concentrate. If slush is too thick, add more water.

name: Fruit Kabob
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032129/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-kabob
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Thread the fruit onto the skewers, alternating and arranging the pieces however you like.
Serve right away.

name: Fruit Kabobs with Yogurt Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032111/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-kabobs-yogurt-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 kiwifruits, peeled and cut into quarters

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place fruit chunks on bamboo skewers. Place fruit kabobs on platter.
Place light strawberry yogurt in bowl. Serve kabobs with yogurt on the side.

name: Fruit Milk Shakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035349/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-milk-shakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 ripe bananas (or 1/3 cup orange juice concentrate)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place everything together into a blender.
Blend for 30 seconds to 1 minute.

name: Fruit Pizza
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045020/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-pizza
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 °F.
For crust, cream margarine, sugar, vanilla, and egg until light and fluffy. Add flour and baking powder, mixing well.
Spread mixture about 1/8 inch thick on a pizza pan, baking sheet, or 9x13 inch pan.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned. Cool.
For spread, mix together cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla. Spread on cooled cookie crust.
Arrange fruit on top of pizza. Refrigerate until serving time.

notes.text: Fruit Topping Ideas: Sliced Strawberries, kiwi, bananas, pineapple, mandarin oranges, pears, peaches, blueberries, or grapes.

name: Fruit Pizza To Go
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022404/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-pizza-go
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons whipped fat-free strawberry cream cheese

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toast the English muffin until golden brown. Spread cream cheese on toasted muffin.
Arrange sliced strawberries, grapes, and orange slices on top of the cream cheese.

notes.text: This recipe can be made with any flavor of cream cheese and any fruit you like.

name: Fruit Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041051/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 (8 ounce) container of yogurt, low-fat piña colada

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix fruit in a large bowl.
Add yogurt and mix well.
Chill in refrigerator before serving.
serving_size: 1/2 cup prepared fruit salad, 1/14 of recipe (109g)

name: Fruit Salad with Jicama
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042001/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-salad-jicama
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash, peel, and cut the jicama into thin slices.
Wash, peel, and cut the rest of the fruit (including the lime) into slices or small pieces.
On a large plate, arrange the fruit. Sprinkle the lime or orange juice over the fruit.
In a small bowl, mix the salt and chili powder. Sprinkle over the fruit and serve.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Fruit Salad with Yogurt
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035034/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-salad-yogurt
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Place fruit in a large bowl and mix with pineapple juice. Let stand for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Place 1 cup of fruit salad in a small bowl and top with 1/2 cup of yogurt.
Sprinkle almonds on top of each fruit salad. Serve immediately.

notes.text: Any 100% fruit juice can be used instead of pineapple juice.

name: Fruit Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033912/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine fruits in a medium mixing bowl and add lemon juice.
Stir in sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon. Mix well.
Refrigerate until serving time.

name: Fruit Slush
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040452/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-slush
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups cantaloupe or watermelon, coarsely chopped, seeded, peeled

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a blender, puree fruit and lime juice until smooth. Add sugar if desired.
Combine fruit mixture and water in a large pitcher.
To eliminate the pulp pour through a strainer (optional).
Cover and refrigerate for up to a week.
To serve, stir well and pour into tall glasses over ice.

name: Fruit Smoothie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035419/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-smoothie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all ingredients in a blender.
Blend on high until smooth.
Pour into 2 glasses. Serve right away.

name: Strawberry and Banana Fruit Smoothie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020441/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-smoothie-ii
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups frozen unsweetened strawberries (or other frozen fruit)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Defrost the frozen fruit just enough so that it will blend easily.
Pour the milk into the blender.
Add the pieces of frozen fruit to the milk in the blender.
Add the banana and yogurt.
Blend until smooth, about 30 to 45 seconds.

notes.text: Strawberries, 1% milk, and low-fat vanilla yogurt used in nutrition analysis and costing.

name: Fruit Snake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020429/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-snake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel banana and use butter knife to cut banana in half lengthwise.
Place 2 banana halves on small plate end to end, in an "s" shape.
Add raisins to the top of banana as eyes.
Enjoy your Fruit Snake.

name: Peach Sorbet
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215139/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-sorbet
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cans sliced peaches in 100% juice (15-ounce cans)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Collect all ingredients and freeze cans before starting to prepare the recipe.
Place cans of fruit in freezer for at least 3 hours. Take out when fully frozen.*
Run frozen cans briefly under hot water, or let them sit on counter for 30 minutes to loosen contents. Remove fruit from the cans, and use a sharp knife to cut it into small pieces.
If using a banana, peel, and cut into slices. Banana does not need to be frozen.
Place frozen, chopped fruit (and banana, if using) in the blender, and blend until creamy.
Serve immediately.
Freeze any leftovers in a freezer-safe container or sealable plastic freezer bags.
*It is ok to freeze these cans overnight. They will not explode.

notes.text: Cost and nutrition analysis provided for Peach Sorbet. Try these refreshing flavor combinations, or create your own!

name: Fruit Yogurt Parfait
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031446/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-yogurt-parfait
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup dry crunchy cereal (Grape Nuts or granola cereals are good)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and slice the banana.
Spoon the grapes into a tall plastic cup.
Put 3 spoonsful of yogurt on top of the grapes.
Spoon sliced bananas on top of the yogurt.
Add the rest of the yogurt.
Sprinkle the cereal on top.

name: Fruit Yogurt Pops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215233/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruit-yogurt-pops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 low fat yogurt, fruit flavored (8 ounces)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine ingredients. Pour into 3 ounce paper cups.
Freeze about 30 minutes; then stick a wooden popsicle/ craft stick in the center of each cup.
Freeze overnight until firm. To eat pops, peel off paper cups.
For variety, try other fruit flavored yogurts and frozen fruit or fruit juice concentrates.

name: Fruity Homemade Oatmeal
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035525/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruity-homemade-oatmeal
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Use a vegetable peeler to remove the skin from the apple.
Cut the core out of the apple. Chop the apple into small pieces.
Put the water in the saucepan.
Bring the water to a boil on medium heat.
Stir in oatmeal, raisins, chopped apple, and cinnamon.
Turn heat to low.
Cook 5 minutes, stirring often.

notes.text: To get more fiber, leave the skin on the apple.

name: Fruity Thai Pita Pockets
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032627/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fruity-thai-pita-pockets
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can tropical fruit salad in 100% juice (15 ounces)
3 tablespoons reserved juice from tropical fruit salad
1/2 cup natural peanut butter, crunchy or chunky

steps: In a colander over a bowl, drain fruit salad well; reserve 3 tablespoons juice.
In a small bowl, whisk together reserved juice, peanut butter, cream cheese, and soy sauce.
Place drained fruit, spinach, and cilantro (if desired) in a bowl; mix gently.
Add sauce and toss.
Slice a small portion off each pita. Tuck the slice inside the bottom of the pita.
Fill each pita pocket with the fruit-spinach mixture.
Wrap individually in plastic wrap and refrigerate. Will keep well overnight.

notes.text: Time-saving idea: Purchase pre-opened pita pockets

name: Fudgy Fruit
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041918/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/fudgy-fruit
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/8 cup chocolate chips (or 2 tablespoons semi-sweet chips)
2 large bananas (peeled and cut into quarters)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place chocolate chips in a small microwave safe bowl. Heat on high for 10 seconds and stir. Repeat until chocolate is melted, about 30 seconds.
Place fruit on a small tray covered with a piece of waxed paper. Use a spoon to drizzle the melted chocolate on top of the fruit.
Sprinkle the fruit with chopped nuts.
Cover the fruit and place in the refrigerator for 10 minutes or until the chocolate hardens. Serve chilled.

name: Full of Beans Hot Dish
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031700/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/full-beans-hot-dish
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 can low-sodium great northern beans (15.5 ounce)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat over to 350 °F.
Cook ground beef and onions. Drain fat.
Add remaining ingredients and mix.
Place in casserole dish.
Bake in the oven at 350 °F for 30 minutes.

notes.text: For convenience this recipe includes canned beans. To lower the sodium, feel free to use dried beans that have been prepared according to the package directions.

name: Garden Barley Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050545/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/garden-barley-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 46 us fluid ounces tomato juice, low-sodium
1 can beef broth, reduced sodium (14.5 ounces)
1/2 teaspoon thyme leaves, fresh or dried (crushed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a Dutch oven or stock pot, combine tomato juice, beef broth, barley, sugar, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaf, thyme and salt (if using). Bring to boil; reduce heat.
Cover; simmer 1 hour.
Add zucchini, tomato, and green pepper. Return to boil; reduce heat.
Cover; simmer 15 to 20 minutes or until vegetables and barley are tender.

name: Garden Cannellini Bean Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032417/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/garden-cannellini-bean-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon tomato basil garlic seasoning blend, no-salt
2 15.5 oz cans cannellini (white) beans, low-sodium, drained, and rinsed
Large lettuce leaves (Boston, Bibb, or romaine)

steps: Whisk together dressing ingredients in a small bowl.
In a small sauté pan, toast almond slivers until golden.
Remove from pan and let cool.
In a medium bowl, toss dressing with all ingredients except lettuce.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
To serve, place lettuce leaves on individual plates; top with salad.

notes.text: Serving Suggestion: Serve with a glass of non-fat milk, 1 slice of whole-grain bread, and pear slices.

name: Garden Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231051024/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/garden-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2/3 cup kidney beans, canned, low-sodium (drained and rinsed)

steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.

Place ground beef in a skillet sprayed with non-stick cooking spray. Brown meat over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally to break it into pieces. Drain fat and blot meat with paper towels. Transfer beef into a colander and rinse with very hot water to further remove fat.
Add green pepper, onion, and celery. Cook until softened.
Add beans, corn, tomato sauce, chopped tomatoes, pepper, garlic powder and chili powder.
Cook mixture over low heat for 20 minutes.
Serve hot in bowls. Or serve as a dip with baked tortilla chips or on a bun.
Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Garden Frittata
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041239/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/garden-frittata
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 cups Italian kale, or other kale variety

steps: Beat eggs, pepper, and salt in large bowl; set aside.
Microwave potatoes until slightly soft, but not completely cooked; then cube. (Alternate method without microwave: Cube potatoes and boil 5 minutes until slightly soft; then drain.)
Chop remaining vegetables while potatoes cool. Mix vegetables together.
Heat oil in a 10-inch non-stick skillet. Sauté vegetables for 5 to 8 minutes; add to eggs and mix well.
Pour egg-vegetable mixture into the same skillet. Cook over low to medium heat until eggs are almost set, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Cover and let sit until eggs are completely set, about 5 minutes. Egg dishes should be cooked to 160 ºF.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with 8-oz glass of fat-free (skim) milk and 1/2 sliced orange.

name: Garden Orchard Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045705/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/garden-orchard-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup apple (chopped, cored and diced, not peeled)

steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together in a serving bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours or longer to allow flavors to blend. Serve cold.
Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Garden Pan Bread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043742/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/garden-pan-bread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine cornmeal, flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
In a small bowl, combine bananas, water, and egg mix. Stir until mixed well.
Stir banana mixture into cornmeal mixture. Mix until dry ingredients are moistened. Gently stir in raisins and walnuts.
Lightly spray medium-sized skillet or baking pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Spoon batter into skillet or baking pan.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes or until bread is golden brown and pulls away from the edges. A wooden toothpick or clean fork inserted into the center of the bread should come out clean.
Cut into four equal slices and serve hot or cold.

name: Garden Pasta Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041650/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/garden-pasta-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: In a medium-sized bowl, combine macaroni, onions, cucumbers, and green peppers. Mix well.
In a separate bowl, mix vinegar, vegetable oil, salt, and pepper. If using parsley, add that too.
Pour the prepared dressing over the pasta. Mix well.
Cover bowl and refrigerate for 30 to 45 minutes. Serve cold.

name: Garden Vegetable Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022500/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/garden-vegetable-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder (or 1/2 garlic clove, minced)
3 cups chicken broth, low-sodium (or low-sodium beef or vegetable)
1 can green beans, undrained, low-sodium (14 ounces)
1 can diced tomatoes, undrained, low-sodium (14.5 ounces)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large saucepan sprayed with non-stick cooking spray, sauté the carrots, onion, and garlic over low heat about 5 minutes.
Add broth, cabbage, green beans, tomatoes, and Italian seasoning; bring to a boil.
Cover, lower heat. Simmer about 15 minutes or until carrots are tender.
Stir in zucchini and heat for 3 to 4 minutes. Serve hot.
Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Garlic Bok Choy
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035212/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/garlic-bok-choy
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 5 cloves garlic (use 4-6 cloves, minced or 1 to 1 1/2 teaspoons of garlic powder)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut bok choy crosswise into easy-to-eat pieces.
In a medium skillet over medium-high heat, sauté garlic in oil until fragrant. If using garlic powder, add with salt in the next step.
Add bok choy and stir quickly. Add salt. Stir until greens are wilted and stem pieces are tender-crisp. Serve hot.

name: Garlic Ginger Ramen with Beef
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033304/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/garlic-ginger-ramen-beef
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 pound lean ground beef (15% fat or less)
2 packages instant ramen-style noodles (3 ounces each, broken into small pieces)
1 package (16 ounces) frozen stir-fry vegetables (any type)
1 tablespoon fresh ginger (or 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger)
2 cloves garlic (minced or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat (350 °F in an electric skillet), brown the ground beef. Drain fat from the skillet. Drain fat from the skillet. (See Notes.)
Add water and ONE seasoning packet to cooked beef and mix well.
Add vegetables, green onion, ginger, and garlic. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Add ramen noodles, reduce heat to low, and simmer 3 to 5 minutes until vegetables are tender, stirring occasionally.

name: Garlic Stuffed Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035442/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/garlic-stuffed-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

In a small saucepan, bring water to a boil. Add garlic; cook for 10 minutes. Drain garlic, peel and cut into thin slices. In a small bowl, combine garlic, 1/2 cup of chopped parsley, lemon zest, and seasoning. Mix well.
Loosen skin from each chicken breast to form a pocket. Place about 1 teaspoon of garlic mixture under skin of each breast. Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken skin-side down; cook until golden, about 4 minutes. Turn chicken; reduce heat to medium.
Cover and cook until no longer pink in center, about 10 to 12 minutes. Transfer chicken to a plate. Wipe any fat away from the skillet.
Add remaining chopped parsley, broth, and lemon juice to pan. Bring to a boil; cook for 1 minute. Spoon mixture over chicken.

name: Gazpacho
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042144/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/gazpacho
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 medium tomatoes (ripe, skinned, seeded, and roughly chopped, about 3 3/4 cup or 2 pounds)
1 small cucumber (peeled, seeded, and roughly chopped, about 1 1/2 cup)
1 green pepper (seeded and roughly chopped, about 1 cup)
2 teaspoons minced garlic (or 4 cloves fresh garlic, finely chopped)
1 small tomato (seeded and finely chopped, about 1 cup)
1/2 small red onion (finely chopped, about 1/2 cup)
1/2 green bell pepper (seeded and finely chopped, about 1/2 cup)

steps: Tear bread into small pieces; transfer to medium bowl and cover with 1 cup water.
Soak until bread is saturated, about 15 minutes.
Squeeze water from bread, discarding soaking water.
In bowl of blender or food processor, add bread, tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garlic, and 1/4 cup of water.
Blend until well combined, about 1 minute.
With motor running, add oil in steady stream until well blended.
Stir in vinegar, season with low-sodium adobo.
Strain puréed soup through small-hole strainer, into soup terrine, pressing firmly to pass all liquid through strainer, discard any solids.
Cover terrine; transfer to refrigerator.
Chill at least 1 hour, or up to 48 hours.
To serve, divide soup evenly among serving bowls.
Garnish with tomatoes, onions, peppers, and eggs.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with Spanish Garlic Shrimp, Garlic and Spanish Rice, and a glass of non-fat milk to make the meal complete.

name: Gazpacho Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032043/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/gazpacho-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Chop the tomato, cucumber, and peppers into very small pieces.
Put all the ingredients in a large glass or plastic bowl.
Stir well with a wooden or plastic spoon.
Chill in the fridge for 1 to 2 hours before serving.

name: Ginger Bread Mix
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021200/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/ginger-bread-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl. Mix well.
Store mix in a covered jar until ready to use.

notes.text: Use this mix to make Ginger Orange Muffins.

name: Ginger Orange Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020324/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/ginger-orange-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Combine the Ginger Bread Mix and bran cereal in a bowl.
Beat the egg slightly in another bowl.
Add the egg and other ingredients to the gingerbread and cereal mixture.
Stir only until combined. Let stand for 15 minutes.
Fill 12 muffin cups (well-greased pans or paper liners) 2/3 full.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until done in the center.

notes.text: 2 servings of Ginger Bread Mix = 2 cups

name: Gingery Quinoa with Green Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050359/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/gingery-quinoa-green-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil or cooking oil

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toast quinoa in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring constantly for about 3 minutes.
Transfer toasted quinoa to a medium pot and add water or broth.
Bring to a boil, then let simmer until all of the water is absorbed and quinoa is tender (10 to 15 minutes).
Set aside and leave uncovered to cool.
While quinoa is cooling, place green beans in a microwave-safe dish. Add a small amount of water, cover, and microwave for 4-6 minutes or until just tender.
Rinse green beans in cold water to stop the cooking process.
In a large bowl, combine the quinoa, green beans, olive oil or cooking oil, sesame oil, soy sauce, lemon juice, and ground ginger. Stir well.
Season with salt and pepper, as needed.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Glazed Carrots
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032035/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/glazed-carrots
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel the carrots. Cut in half lengthwise, then cut into 1 inch pieces.
Melt the margarine in a heavy saucepan on low heat.
Add the carrots. Stir to coat them with the margarine.
Add the water, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer for about 15 minutes until tender.
Drain the water.
Add the sugar.
Cover the pan.
Shake the pan back and forth on the burner for 1 minute.
Cook for 1 more minute, until the carrots are glazed but not brown.

name: Glazed Meatloaf
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215357/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/glazed-meatloaf
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 green bell pepper, cored and diced

steps: Preheat the oven to 325 °F. Lightly grease a baking sheet.
Put a skillet over medium heat and when it is hot, add the oil. Add the onion, bell pepper, garlic, and thyme and cook about 10 minutes until golden.
Lower the heat and add the water and tomato paste. Cook about 10 minutes until the onion is soft and most of the liquid has been absorbed. Set aside to cool. Add the mustard, salt and pepper.
While the onion mixture is cool, put the ground beef, 4 tablespoons rolled oats and the egg in the bowl and gently mix, by hand.
Add the cooled onion mixture and gently mix again until everything is thoroughly incorporated. Do not over mix.
Form the mixture into a loaf about 8x4 inches and put on the prepared baking sheet.
To make the glaze: Put the tomato paste and mustard in a small bowl and mix well. Rub on top of the meatloaf and sprinkle with the remaining 2 tablespoons rolled oats.
Put in the oven to cook about 1 hour until deep brown and cooked throughout. Serve right away or cover and refrigerate up to 2 days.

name: Golden Split Pea Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043802/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/golden-split-pea-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
4 potatoes (2 cups diced, with skin on)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place the oil in a large pot or Dutch-oven style pan. Heat over medium-high.
Add the onion and sauté until golden, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix well. Bring to a boil and then lower the heat to a simmer. Cook uncovered until the peas are tender, about 45 minutes. Serve hot.

name: Grandma's Stuffing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032927/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grandmas-stuffing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 slices whole wheat bread, cubed (or white bread or buns, dry)
1 teaspoon parsley, dried (or 1 Tbsp fresh parsley chopped)
2 apples (optional - medium, pared, cored and chopped, or 1/4 cup raisins)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Put cubes in a large bowl. Set aside.
Put water in medium saucepan. Add onion, celery, parsley, salt, and pepper. Cook for 5 minutes. Do not drain. Pour over bread cubes.
Stir in milk and egg. Gently stir in apples, and raisins, if desired.
Spoon into a greased 2-quart baking dish.
Bake at 350 °F for 1 hour.

name: Granola Bars
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045106/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/granola-bars
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Peel and grate the carrots.
Put the honey and peanut butter in a large saucepan. Cook on low heat until they melt.
Remove the pan from the heat. Turn off the burner.
Add oatmeal, raisins, carrots, and coconut to the saucepan. Stir well, and let it cool until you can safely touch it with your hands.
Put the mix into a 9x13 inch baking pan.
Press the mix firmly into the bottom of the pan.
Bake for 25 minutes.
Cut into 24 bars.

name: Granola with Oatmeal, Coconut, and Pecans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042243/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/granola-oatmeal-coconut-pecan
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup pecans, chopped (or try walnuts or peanuts)

steps: Heat oven to 350 ºF. Combine all ingredients in a large bowl, except raisins, mix well.
Bake in 13x9 inch baking pan at 350 ºF for 25 to 30 minutes or until golden brown. Stir every 5 minutes.
Stir in raisins. Cool thoroughly. Store in tightly covered container.
Combine all ingredients except raisins in a large microwave safe bowl; mix well.
Set electric skillet at 300 ºF and stir mixture constantly until lightly browned.
Place in a bowl and stir in raisins. Cool thoroughly.
Store in tightly covered container.
Combine all ingredients, except raisins in a large microwave safe bowl; mix well.
Place in 11x7 glass baking dish.
Cook at HIGH about 8 minutes or until golden brown, stirring after every 2 minutes of cooking; stir in raisins.
Place onto un-greased cookie sheet or aluminum foil to cool. Cool thoroughly. Store in a tightly covered container.
Wash hands with soap and water. Conventional Oven: Electric Skillet: Microwave:

notes.text: Honey should not be fed to children under 1 year of age.

name: Grape and Cashew Salad Sandwich
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032634/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grape-and-cashew-salad-sandwich
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3/4 cup dry roasted unsalted cashews, coarsely chopped

steps: In a medium bowl, mix cottage cheese, grapes, celery, cashews, parsley, and ground black pepper.
Toast bread and build sandwiches following steps 3 and 4.
Spread 1/4 salad mix on 4 of the bread slices.
Add two lettuce leaves to each sandwich; top with 2nd bread slice.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a side of raw baby carrots and 1 cup of sparkling water with a lemon wedge.

name: Grapefruit Spinach Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031623/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grapefruit-spinach-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 1/2 cups fresh spinach, washed and drained
1 can sliced mushrooms, drained (2 ounce cans)
1 cup water chestnuts, diced (5 oz can)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Tear spinach coarsely and place in large salad bowl.
Add mushrooms, water chestnuts, and grapefruit.
Mix together oil, vinegar, grapefruit juice, soy sauce, hot pepper sauce, salt, and dry mustard.
Toss dressing with spinach mixture and serve.

name: Great Northern Bean Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031610/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/great-northern-bean-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 pound chicken, thawed, cut up, and skin removed from each piece
1 cup tomatoes, diced (or 1/2-8 ounce can low-sodium diced tomatoes)

steps: In a medium-sized bowl, soak beans in 3 cups of water overnight.
Drain the water and rinse beans.
In a large pot, brown onion, chicken, and ham in oil over medium to high heat for about 5 minutes.
Add water, beans, and salt to pot. Mix well.
Bring pot to a boil and cook for 5 minutes.
Lower heat and cook for about 1 hour. Stir pot every 15 minutes.
Add tomatoes and vinegar to pot. Keep cooking over low heat for about 20 minutes. Serve hot.

notes.text: Tip for cooking chicken: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for chicken is 165 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.

name: Greek Pork Chops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044134/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/greek-pork-chops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound pork cutlets (or 4 thin-cut, boneless pork chops)

steps: Put the pork, oil, vinegar, oregano, and garlic in the glass or ceramic bowl, or in a sealed plastic bag and mix well. Cover bowl and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Sprinkle the pork with the salt and pepper.
Place a large skillet on the stove over high heat. When hot, add the pork to the dry skillet, waiting about 30 seconds between each addition.
Cook about 7 minutes on each side until crispy. Serve right away.

notes.text: Lemon, lime, or orange juice can be used instead of red wine vinegar.

name: Greek Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214941/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/greek-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 romaine lettuces leaves, torn into 1 1/2-inch pieces (Or more if desired)
1 medium tomato, chopped (Can also use cherry tomatoes)
2 tablespoons olive oil (or oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine lettuce, cucumber, tomato, onion, and cheese in large serving bowl. Whisk together oil, lemon juice, oregano, and salt in small bowl.
Pour over lettuce mixture; toss until coated. Serve immediately.

name: Greek Salad with Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042531/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/greek-salad-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes, cut in half
1/4 cup black olives, cut in half

steps: To make the dressing, add Greek yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper to a small bowl. Mix well to combine.
Cover dressing and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Wash lettuce and tear into bite-sized pieces. Place in large salad bowl and add tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion, olives, and chicken.
Sprinkle with feta cheese.
Top with yogurt dressing and enjoy.

name: Green Bean and Mushroom Medley
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041555/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/green-bean-and-mushroom-medley
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups fresh green beans (cut into 1-inch lengths)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place green beans and carrots in 1 inch of boiling water. Cover, and cook until tender but still firm. Drain.
Add oil to heated skillet. Sauté onions and mushrooms until almost tender. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer 3 minutes.
Stir in green beans, carrots, lemon pepper, garlic salt, and toasted almonds. Cover and cook for 5 minutes over medium heat.

name: Green Bean and Rice Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050110/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/green-bean-and-rice-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can reduced-sodium green beans, drained (about 15 ounces)
1 can diced tomatoes, no salt added (about 15 ounces)

steps: In a medium-sized pan, cook onions in vegetable oil until they start to turn light brown.
Add the rice, green beans, tomatoes, and water.
Bring to a boil.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook over low heat for 10 minutes.

name: Green Bean Sauté
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041033/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/green-bean-saute
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can green beans, low sodium (14.5 ounce, drained, cut)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spray a skillet with non-stick cooking spray.
Sauté onions, mushrooms, and garlic.
Add green beans and heat thoroughly.

name: Green Beans and New Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020912/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/green-beans-and-new-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 1/2 cups frozen green beans (16 oz bag)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add all ingredients to a large stock pot and cover with water.
Bring to a boil and reduce to medium heat.
Cook until green beans and potatoes are tender.

name: Green Beans with Tomatoes and Basil
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035143/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/green-beans-tomatoes-and-basil
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 cups green beans (about 1 pound, ends snipped)
1 can (14.5 ounces) tomatoes, low-sodium (drained and chopped)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook beans in a large saucepan of boiling water for 5 minutes; beans will still be crisp. Drain and rinse under cold running water. Set aside.
In a large frying pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add onion and cook 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add tomatoes, basil, and parsley. Cook 3 minutes to heat and combine flavors.
Stir beans into pan and cook 5-6 minutes. Season with salt and pepper (optional).

name: Green Onion Omelet
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021808/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/green-onion-omelet
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can low-sodium sliced potatoes, drained (about 15 ounces)
1/2 can no salt added tomatoes, drained (about 8 ounces)
1 tablespoon green onion (or wild onion), chopped

steps: Open and drain can of sliced potatoes. Cut sliced potatoes into strips.
In a large skillet over medium heat, lightly brown potatoes in the vegetable oil for 5 to 10 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, add egg, egg whites, milk, and salt. Mix well.
Stir in ham, tomatoes, and green (or wild) onions.
Pour egg mixture over potatoes in the skillet.
Cover skillet and continue to cook eggs over medium heat until firm, not runny (about 8 minutes).
Cut the omelet into four pieces and serve.

name: Green Tea Berry Banana Smoothie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013731/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/green-tea-berry-banana-smoothie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 medium bananas, peeled, cut in half and frozen

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add the water to a small saucepan. Bring the water to a boil over high heat. Remove the pan from the heat.
Add the tea bags. (Be sure the tea bags are submerged.) Let steep for 4 minutes. Discard the tea bags.
Let the tea mixture cool for 30 minutes. Pour into a water pitcher. Refrigerate for 2 hours, or until chilled.
In a food processor or blender, process the tea, berries, bananas, yogurt, gingerroot and vanilla until smooth.
Pour into four glasses. Sprinkle with the chia seeds.

name: Grilled Asparagus and Shrimp Quinoa Salad with Lemon Vinaigrette
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032420/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grilled-asparagus-and-shrimp-quinoa-salad-lemon-vinaigrette
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups fresh asparagus, large spears, cut into 1" pieces
1/2 yellow or red bell pepper, cut into 1/2" pieces
1 14 ounce can quartered artichoke hearts, drained
12 ounces fresh or frozen large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 1/2 cups dry quinoa (cooked according to package directions)
3 tablespoons fresh or bottled lemon juice

steps: Place vinaigrette ingredients in a small bowl and whisk; set aside.
Cut vegetables as directed.
Heat grill and grilling tray.
Place vegetables and shrimp in a large bowl; add about 1/3 of the vinaigrette (about 3 tablespoons) and toss.
Spread shrimp-vegetable mixture over hot grilling tray.
Grill, turning shrimp and vegetables, until the flesh of the shrimp is an opaque color (about 5 to 6 minutes); remove from grill.
Serve grill mixture over cooked quinoa, and drizzle with vinaigrette.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with non-fat milk and grapes.

name: Grilled Cheese with Peaches
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032534/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grilled-cheese-peaches
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 slices whole grain bread, thin slice

steps: Heat the 4 teaspoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Place 4 slices of whole grain bread in the pan.
Layer (in this order) one slice of cheese, a handful of spinach, 4 to 6 peach slices, another slice of cheese, and a slice of bread on top of each original slice of bread.
After 4 to 5 minutes, flip each sandwich and cook another 4 to 5 minutes.

notes.text: Try this recipe with other leafy greens, such as arugula, and other cheeses.

name: Grilled Chicken and Avocado Quinoa Pilaf
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032432/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grilled-chicken-and-avocado-quinoa-pilaf
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons fresh or bottled lemon juice

steps: Heat grill.
Peel and cut avocado into chunks; place in a medium bowl.
Mix lemon juice, basil, an 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. Drizzle over avocado chunks, toss, and set aside.
Cut chicken breasts in half crosswise.
Mix 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and remaining black pepper. Brush mixture on chicken and red bell pepper.
Grill chicken and pepper until done. Set chicken breasts aside. Cut pepper into thin strips.
While chicken and peppers are grilling, heat remaining olive oil in a large pan, add garlic and onion, and cook until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add water, bouillon, and quinoa to pan; bring to boil, cover, reduce heat, and simmer until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is cooked (about 15 to 20 minutes).
Place quinoa pilaf in a large bowl and add chicken, red peppers, and avocado. Toss gently.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with non-fat milk and orange slices.

name: Grilled Fish Tacos with Peach Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021952/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grilled-fish-tacos-peach-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can 15.25 ounces peach halves, drained and chopped (about 1 cup)
1/2 red bell pepper, finely chopped (about 1/2 cup)
1 whole jalapeno pepper, seeded, and finely chopped

steps: In a medium bowl, stir together chopped peaches, bell pepper, onions, jalapenos, cilantro, and lemon juice
Cover and refrigerate until ready to use.
Heat grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. Using paper towels, pat fish dry, transfer to plate.
In a small bowl, stir together chili powder, low-sodium adobo and Sazon packet.
Rub fish with spice mixture to coat completely.
Place fish on hot greased grill grates.
Cook, flipping once until fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork (145 °F), about 8 minutes.
Thinly slice fish.
To serve, fill each tortilla with 1/2 fish fillet and about 1/3 cup of salsa.
Make the salsa: For the fish:

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a Summer Corn Salad, chock full of vegetables, and a quick Mango Banana Shake for your best taco night yet!

name: Grilled Fruit
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022257/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grilled-fruit
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place fruit chunks on a skewer to make kabobs.
Grill or broil on low heat until the fruit is hot and slightly golden.

notes.text: If using wooden skewers, thoroughly soak skewers in water prior to using to prevent burning (approximately 30 minutes). For a twist, try changing the fruit. Other fruits that grill well are apples, figs, pears, plums, cantaloupe, honeydew, and watermelon.

name: Grilled Lamb Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042537/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grilled-lamb-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 12 ounces boneless leg of lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes (if cubed lamb is not available, ask the butcher to prepare it for you)
6 cups shredded Savoy, Napa, or green cabbage
2 tablespoons black or white sesame seeds

steps: Mix marinade/dressing ingredients; divide evenly.
Place lamb cubes in a glass dish; pour half of the marinade/dressing over the lamb.
Cover and refrigerate at least two hours.
In a large bowl, toss cabbage, carrots, jicama (optional), onions, and sesame seeds.
Remove lamb and discard marinade.
Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes; divide lamb among the 4 skewers.
On hot grill, cook the lamb skewers 5 to 6 minutes per side (or to desired degree of doneness).
Remove lamb from skewers, add to salad, and toss.
To serve, divide salad evenly on four plates. Drizzle with remaining dressing.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with nonfat milk and orange slices/wedges. Tips on Cooking Lamb: Cooking temperature: 145 °F (medium-rare); 160 °F (medium); 170 °F (well-done)

name: Grilled Pineapple Ginger Glazed Chicken with Zucchini and Peppers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040530/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grilled-pineapple-ginger-glazed-chicken-zucchini-and-peppers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound chicken breast, boneless, skinless (cut into 4 portions)
1 sweet yellow onion, cut into wedges
8 pineapple spears (2-1/2 x 1-1/4 inch, about 1 ounce each)

steps: To make the glaze, combine pineapple juice, vinegar, brown sugar, soy sauce, ginger and mustard in a medium saucepan set over medium-high heat.
Bring to a boil; boil for about 15 minutes.
Preheat grill to medium heat. Cook couscous according to package directions.
While couscous is cooking, toss chicken breast with oil, salt and pepper.
Grill chicken, for 2 minutes per side or until grill-marked. Continue to grill, basting and turning with Pineapple Ginger Glaze, for 5 to 6 minutes or until cooked.
Grill onion, zucchini, red pepper, orange pepper and pineapple spears, basting with Pineapple Ginger Glaze, for 3 to 5 minutes or until grill-marked and tender.
Serve chicken with vegetables and pineapple over couscous.
Garnish with green onions.

notes.text: Serve with 8 ounces non-fat milk.

name: Grilled Shrimp with Cantaloupe Avocado Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042541/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grilled-shrimp-cantaloupe-avocado-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 lime (divided, half for salsa and half for garnish)
1 cup canned black beans, low sodium, drained and rinsed
1 pound large or jumbo shrimp, uncooked

steps: Preheat grill.
Slice lime in half. In a small bowl, squeeze juice from one half of lime; reserve other half for garnish.
Add remaining salsa ingredients and gently mix.
Peel shrimp, leaving the tails on.
Skewer shrimp on bamboo skewers.
In a small dish mix together canola oil and garlic. Coat shrimp with oil-garlic mix.
Grill 4 to 5 minutes or until cooked.
To serve, top shrimp with salsa, garnish with lime wedges.

notes.text: Serve with 8 ounces non-fat milk and brown rice.

name: Grilled Steak and Peppers Salad with Pears
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040528/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grilled-steak-and-peppers-salad-pears
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups white-wheat rotini pasta, uncooked (about 4 oz)
12 ounces boneless choice beef top sirloin
1/4 cup 100% white grape juice or apple juice

steps: In a small bowl, whisk olive oil, vinegar, grape or apple juice, salt, and herb blend.
Boil water and cook pasta according to package instructions. Drain pasta, rinse in cool water.

Heat grill, rub peppers with 1/2 tsp olive oil. Grill whole peppers, turning as needed, until skin begins to brown and bubble. At the same time, grill beef sirloin to 145 °F, turning once. Remove from grill, let cool slightly.
Slice peppers into strips, discarding seeds and stem. Cut sirloin across the grain into thin slices. Slice pears into thin wedges.
Toss arugula and pasta in large bowl.
To serve, evenly divide pasta-arugula onto four plates, arrange beef, peppers, and pears on top, drizzle with vinaigrette, and sprinkle with crumbled Gorgonzola cheese.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of non-fat milk.

name: Grilled Vegetable Packets
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231030859/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grilled-vegetable-packets
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 small red potatoes (scrubbed well and sliced)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat grill to medium heat or 350 °F.
Wash vegetables and slice.
Toss in a large bowl. Add dressing and toss until all vegetables are coated.

Tear 2 large squares of aluminum foil and place half of the vegetable mixture on each piece. Place an equal piece of foil over the top of vegetable mixture and fold bottom piece with top sheet to form a packet.
Place on heated grill for 20 to 30 minutes or until the potatoes are tender. If you don't have a grill, bake Veggie Packets in the oven at 400 °F for 20 to 30 minutes.
Before you open the packets, poke holes in the foil with a fork. Be very careful opening the foil as the steam will be very hot and could burn you!
Empty vegetables onto serving plate or serve from foil packets.

name: Grilled Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020759/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/grilled-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix oil and garlic in a large bowl. Add vegetables and toss.
Place vegetable on broiler pan or grill. Cook 10 minutes, turning twice until vegetables are tender.
Place vegetables on platter. Serve.

name: Ground Beef Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034804/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/ground-beef-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 pound ground beef, or ground turkey, or venison (lean)
1 can tomato soup, condensed, low-sodium (10 1/2 ounces)
10 1/2 us fluid ounces water (one soup can full)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown meat. Drain fat, if any. Season lightly with salt and pepper (optional).
Add soup and 1 can of water to fry pan. Add vegetables.
Bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, about 25 minutes or until tender. Remove from heat, cover for last 10 minutes to thicken.
Serve. Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Harvest Vegetable Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050300/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/harvest-vegetable-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine romaine lettuce and cilantro, and divide onto four plates.
Place parsnips, carrots, and turnips into 1 quart of boiling water. Return water to a simmer, cook vegetables for 2 minutes. Strain into a colander.
Mix ingredients for the dressing right before use.
Place hot vegetables on top of greens and top with homemade dressing.

name: Healthy Black Bean Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109132709/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/healthy-black-bean-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cans (15.5 ounces each) low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed
2 cups low-sodium chicken broth (or low-sodium vegetable broth)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lightly purée one can of black beans with broth, salsa, and cumin in a blender.
In a medium saucepan, combine puréed bean mixture with remaining beans and heat through.
To serve, ladle soup into 4 bowls.
Top each bowl with one tablespoon of sour cream and garnish with the cilantro.

name: Hearty Beef Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043353/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hearty-beef-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups winter squash, chopped (or 2 cups cabbage, finely chopped)
1 large tomato, chopped (or 15-ounce can low-sodium diced tomatoes)

steps: In a large pot, brown beef in oil over medium to high heat for 8 to 10 minutes. Drain fat.
Add water, squash, onion, celery, garlic, and oregano. If using parsley, add that too. Mix well.
Bring pot to a boil. Lower heat and cook for 20 minutes.
Add macaroni, tomatoes, green pepper, salt, and pepper.
Keep cooking over low heat for 20 minutes. Serve hot.

notes.text: Tip for cooking beef roast: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for beef roast is 145 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.

name: Hearty Mashed Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020947/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hearty-mashed-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 potatoes (baking, peeled and cut in chunks, about 2 pounds)
1 can garbanzo beans, low-sodium (15 ounce, drained)
1/2 cup milk, non-fat (or fortified soy milk)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water
Place the potatoes in a large sauce pan and cover with water. Bring to a boil over high heat then reduce to a simmer.
Add the garbanzo beans 10 minutes after potatoes start cooking. Continue cooking until potatoes are fork tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain water and place the sauce pan back on the stove. Mash the beans and potatoes using a potato masher or hand beaters.
Add the milk, cheese and seasonings.
Reheat if necessary. Serve hot.

name: Hearty Mexican Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034928/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hearty-mexican-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can tomatoes, diced, low-sodium (14.5 ounce can)
2 cans black beans, low-sodium (15 ounce can, low sodium, drained and rinsed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot cook onion, garlic and tomatoes on medium-high heat for 3 minutes. Stir often.
Add beans, potatoes and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to low-medium heat. Cover and continue to cook slowly for 20 minutes.
Add cilantro, cumin and lime. Stir and continue to simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve warm; sprinkle cilantro on top.

name: Hearty Salmon Skewers over Brown Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031532/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hearty-salmon-skewers-over-brown-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: kosher salt, freshly ground pepper, and paprika (to taste)

steps: Cook rice according to package instructions and set aside.
Cut salmon into 24 1/2-inch cubes and coat all sides with topping of kosher salt, freshly ground pepper, paprika, or any desired spice.
Cut fruit into cubes and cut tomatoes in half. Set aside.
Slide piece of salmon onto skewer, then tomato, then fruit. Repeat 3 times on each skewer (or until skewer is full).
Heat 1/2 cup of canola oil in large skillet over medium-high heat for one minute.
Place skewers in pan and turn every 2 minutes per side. Squeeze lemon on skewers as they are cooking.
To serve, place 1/2 cup rice on plates and with 2 skewers on top. Squeeze a hint of lemon, if desired.

name: Hearty Vegetable Beef Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021850/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hearty-vegetable-beef-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3/4 can chicken broth, low-sodium (low sodium, 14.5 oz)
1 can tomatoes, low-sodium (14.5 oz, broken up)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water
Heat broth and water. Add vegetables, meat, and seasonings. Bring to boil. Reduce heat and boil gently, uncovered, for 15 minutes.
Add noodles. Cook until noodles are tender, about 10 minutes
Remove bay leaf. Serve.

name: Hearty Vegetable Salad with Herb Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021800/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hearty-vegetable-salad-herb-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups cauliflower florets (fresh or frozen, thawed)
2 cups broccoli florets (fresh or frozen, thawed)
1 can red kidney beans, low-sodium (15 1/2 ounce, drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In large bowl, combine all salad ingredients.
In a small jar with a tight fitting lid, combine all dressing ingredients and shake well.
Pour dressing over vegetables and stir to coat vegetables. Cover; refrigerate 1 to 4 hours to marinate, tossing occasionally.

name: Heavenly Deviled Eggs
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045949/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/heavenly-deviled-eggs
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put eggs into a saucepan. Cover with cold water.
Bring eggs to a simmer (small bubbles) and cook for 12 minutes.
Remove from the heat and drain.
Crack eggs under cold water and allow to cool. Remove shells.
Split eggs in half lengthwise and remove yolks.
Put yolks, dressing and mustard into a small zipper-lock plastic bag to mix. Cut a small hole in a lower corner of the bag.
Squeeze mixture into egg white halves. Garnish as desired.

notes.text: Garnishes: paprika, cayenne pepper (if you like it hot), pickle relish, sliced scallions, sliced green or black olives. 1/8 teaspoon each of salt and pepper may be substituted for 1 teaspoon of mustard.

name: Herb Broiled Beef
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044137/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/herb-broiled-beef
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound boneless beef chuck shoulder steak, cut 1-inch thick

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix onion, parsley, vinegar, mustard, garlic powder, and basil or thyme.
Place meat in plastic bag and pour in marinade.
Close bag securely, place in a bowl and marinate in refrigerator six to eight hours or overnight, turning at least once.
Pour off marinade and discard. Place meat on rack in broiler.
Broil 15 to 20 minutes or until desired doneness, turning once.
Cut into thin slices to serve.

name: Herb Potato Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034550/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/herb-potato-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub potatoes and cut into cubes.
Place in medium saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 12 minutes or until potatoes are done. Drain.
Mix dressing ingredients.
Combine hot potatoes, dressing, radishes, basil, thyme, and onion powder. Serve hot or cold.

notes.text: The mustard and seasoning make this a tasty potato salad. Try using new red potatoes for added color.

name: Herb Spinach Bake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021239/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/herb-spinach-bake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain canned spinach to remove liquid.
Combine spinach with remaining ingredients in a large bowl.
Add to a 8x8 inch baking dish. You may also use a 9x3 inch baking dish, but the spinach bake will be thinner.
Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes.
Uncover and bake an additional 5 minutes, or until set.

notes.text: Milk can be substituted with 4 tablespoons dry milk + 2/3 cup water.

name: Herbed Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032029/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/herbed-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place all the ingredients in a blender.
Blend all the ingredients thoroughly.
Pour the mixture into a clean container.
Cover and chill.

notes.text: Serve on crackers, or as dip for fresh raw vegetables.

name: Herbed Lentils and Rice Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215250/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/herbed-lentils-and-rice-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat over to 350 °F
In a 2 1/2 quart casserole dish add the chicken broth, lentils, onions, brown rice, water, spices, and 1/4 cup mozzarella cheese.
Stir to combine.
Cover with foil and bake at 350 °F for 2 hours,
Check casserole after 1 hour and add more broth if it seems dry.
Remove foil and top with remaining cheese.
Bake another 2 or 3 minutes until all the cheese is melted.

name: Herbed Spinach Quiche Portabella Caps
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040801/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/herbed-spinach-quiche-portabella-caps
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup frozen chopped spinach, cooked and drained

steps: Place oven rack in center of oven; preheat oven to 375 °F.
Remove portabella stems; wipe clean with damp paper towel.
Spray baking sheet with cooking spray, and place mushroom caps on baking sheet.
In a mixing bowl, whisk together all remaining ingredients, except 1 tbsp Parmesan cheese.
Coat 10-inch non-stick pan with cooking spray and heat over medium flame.
Cook and scramble egg mixture until it just starts to thicken. Remove from heat.
Using a large spoon, scoop partially cooked, hot egg mixture into portabella caps.
Sprinkle tops with remaining Parmesan cheese. Bake about 20 minutes.
Serve immediately.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with strawberries and orange slices (or other fresh, frozen, or canned fruit), water with lime or lemon slice or wedge.

name: Herbed Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042304/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/herbed-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups vegetables (any combination of fresh, frozen, or canned)
1/2 teaspoon Italian herbs, basil, or rosemary (dried, crushed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
If using canned (low-sodium) vegetables, drain, saving 2 tablespoons liquid.
Cook onion, herbs, and garlic in the margarine/ butter in a small saucepan until onion is tender.
Stir in the vegetables and liquid or add water as needed.
Cook and stir until heated through.

name: Hiding Rabbits
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031732/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hiding-rabbits
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 celery stalks (each piece cut in half lengthwise)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place one piece of celery in center of plate with the center facing up.
Use a butter knife to spread peanut butter on top edges.
Place second piece of celery on top, forming a log. Cut log in half.
Repeat steps 1-3 with remaining 2 pieces of celery.
Place cauliflower florets on ends of each log, securing with remaining peanut butter.
Enjoy your Hiding Rabbits.

notes.text: Adults: If this recipe is being prepared by children, use a sharp knife to cut off the ends of celery, cut each celery stalk in half, and cut the cauliflower floret in half. Learn more about:

name: Homemade Bagles
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034309/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/homemade-bagels
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon canola oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a bowl mix sugar, yeast, water, and flours together to make dough.
Rub inside of another bowl with oil. Place dough in bowl and flip to coat with oil. Let rise 30 minutes.
Punch down dough and divide into 16 portions. Shape into a ball and poke a hole through the middle with your fingers.
Place on a well-greased baking sheet and cover with a clean dish towel to rise again for 15 to 20 minutes.
Put 2 inches of water in a pot and heat to boiling.
Using a slotted spoon, gently place each bagel into a rapidly boiling water for 1 minute on each side.
Remove and dry on a towel.
Place back on baking sheet. If desired, sprinkle bagels with cinnamon/sugar or salt.
Bake at 475 °F for 8 to 12 minutes.

name: Homemade Cranberry Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031750/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/homemade-cranberry-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups fresh cranberries (12 ounces, can also use frozen)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel orange and remove seeds.
Place all ingredients in a blender and blend until mixed well.
Heat up and serve over turkey.
