For thicker sauce to do not blend just heat and serve.

notes.text: 1 cup white grape juice concentrate can be substituted for 1 cup sugar.

name: Homemade Mashed Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215057/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/homemade-mashed-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel the potatoes, and cut them into chunks.
Put the potatoes in a medium saucepan with enough water to cover them.
Cook the potatoes on medium heat for 15 minutes or until tender.
Remove the potatoes from the heat. Drain the water off the potatoes.
Mash the potatoes with a fork or potato masher.
Stir in enough milk to make the potatoes smooth and creamy.
Add the butter, salt and pepper.

name: Homemade Pizza Crust
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043318/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/homemade-pizza-crust
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix yeast, water, salt, and oil. Add about 1 cup flour to make a stiff dough. The amount of flour may vary slightly.
Knead the dough until it is very elastic (will stretch and not make a hole).
Use a rolling pin or clean bottle to obtain even thickness.
Lay it on a greased baking sheet to rise while you prepare toppings for pizza.
Bake at 400 °F with desired toppings until crust is browned and top is bubbly.

notes.text: Pizza can be topped with sauce, mozzarella cheese, vegetables, and cooked meats.

name: Homestyle Biscuits
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021550/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/homestyle-biscuits
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 450 °F.
In medium bowl, combine flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar.
In small bowl, stir together buttermilk and oil. Pour over flour mixture and stir until well mixed.

On lightly floured surface, knead dough gently for 10 to 12 strokes. Roll or pat dough to ¾-inch thickness. Cut with a 2-inch round biscuit or cookie cutter, dipping cookie cutter in flour between cuts. Transfer biscuits to an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake for 12 minutes or until golden brown. Serve warm.

name: Honey Baked Lentils
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021125/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/honey-baked-lentils
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine rinsed lentils, bay leaf, and 5 cups water in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil. Cover tightly and reduce heat. Simmer 30 minutes. Do not drain. After cooking, discard bay leaf.
Chop onion. Combine onions and carrots with 1 cup water. Add to lentils and stir into a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Brown ground beef (if using). Drain and discard fat. Add the meat to the lentil mixture.
Pour honey over entire casserole.
Add herbs if desired.
Cover tightly with foil and bake it for one hour at 350 °F.

notes.text: * Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Honey Glazed Turnips
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032517/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/honey-glazed-turnips
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 turnips, medium, about 1 1/2 pounds (sliced or cubed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel turnips.
Slice or cube turnips, 1/2 inch pieces.
In a medium saucepan, combine honey, canola oil and water and bring to a boil.
Add turnips, salt and black pepper, cover and bring to a boil.
Reduce to simmer and cook for about 10 minutes.
Uncover and continue to cook until turnips are golden and glazed, about 10 minutes.

notes.text: * Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Honey Lemon Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021805/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/honey-lemon-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 °F. Line a baking pan with foil for easy clean up. Lightly oil the foil.
Combine flour and salt in a plastic bag. Shake chicken pieces in flour mixture, remove from bag and place on prepared pan.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Combine honey, lemon, and rosemary. Spoon mixture over chicken to glaze chicken pieces. Bake another 15 minutes.

notes.text: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Honey Milk Balls
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044246/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/honey-milk-balls
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix honey and peanut butter.
Gradually add dry milk and mix well.
Chill for easier handling.
With greased hands, form into small balls.
Roll in crushed cereal flakes.
Chill until firm.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

notes.text: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey. View this recipe on our MyPlate Kitchen YouTube channel.

name: Honey Mustard Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042801/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/honey-mustard-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all the ingredients in a jar or bottle with a lid.
Put on the lid. Shake well.
Chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour before serving.

notes.text: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey. Try this dressing on cold cooked pasta and vegetables. After serving, keep any leftover dressing in the fridge.

name: Honey Mustard Pork Chops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251223123747/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/honey-mustard-pork-chops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put the pork chops in the large non-stick skillet.
Cook over medium-high heat to brown one side of the pork chops.
Use the spatula to turn the chops.
Add the rest of the ingredients and stir.
Cover the pan and lower the heat.
Simmer for 6 to 8 minutes until chops are done.

name: Honey of a Pumpkin Bar
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044933/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/honey-pumpkin-bar
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F. Lightly grease or spray with non-stick spray a 12x15 inch baking pan with sides.
In a small bowl, combine dry milk, flour, baking soda, and spices. Set aside.
In a large bowl, thoroughly mix oil, honey, juice, peel, eggs, and pumpkin.
Gradually add flour mixture to pumpkin mixture, stirring until smooth.
Spread batter onto prepared baking pan. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, or until golden brown and cake springs back when lightly touched with your finger. Cool. Cut into squares.

notes.text: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Hooked on Salmon Sticks
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034200/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hooked-salmon-sticks
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large mixing bowl, combine salmon, cracker crumbs, and egg.
Divide mixture into 8 balls and shaped into sticks about 4 inches long.
Lightly coat a skillet with cooking spray. Add oil and preheat the skillet on medium for 1 to 2 minutes. Add fish sticks and cook for 3 minutes.
Flip over and cook about 3 minutes or until golden brown.

name: Hoppin' John (Sausage, Black-Eyed Peas, and Rice)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260101130538/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hoppin-john-sausage-black-eyed-peas-and-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup brown rice, instant uncooked (or white rice)
3 ounces low-fat smoked turkey sausage ring, quartered lengthwise and cut into 1/4-inch pieces (lowest fat and sodium available)
1 jalapeño pepper, medium (seeded and finely chopped)
1 can black eyed peas (low-sodium, rinsed and drained, 15 ounces)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare the rice using the package directions, omitting the salt and butter/margarine.
Meanwhile, in a medium non-stick skillet, heat the oil over medium-high heat, swirling to coat the bottom. Cook the sausage for 3 minutes or until richly browned, stirring frequently.
Stir in the bell pepper and jalapeño pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the peas, water, and salt. Cook for 2 minutes, or until the mixture is thickened slightly but some liquid remains. Remove from the heat.
Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes so the flavors bend. Stir in the rice. Transfer to a serving bowl.

name: Horchata
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022127/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/horchata
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pour the rice and water into the bowl of a blender; blend until the rice just begins to break up, about one minute. Let rice and water stand at room temperature for about three hours.
Strain the rice water into a pitcher and discard the rice. Stir the milk, vanilla, cinnamon, and sugar into the rice water.
Chill and stir before serving over ice.

notes.text: Horchata is a traditional Mexican beverage made with rice and flavored with lime, cinnamon, or sugar.

name: Hot Cornmeal Cereal
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022700/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hot-cornmeal-cereal
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the cornmeal, salt, and cold water.
Pour into the boiling water, stirring occasionally.
Cook until thickened, stirring often.
Cover and cook over low heat about 15 minutes.
Serve hot with milk and sugar.

name: Hot-Wing-Flavored Chicken with Ranch Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033630/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hot-wing-flavored-chicken-ranch-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons hot pepper sauce (or to taste)
4 chicken breast, boneless and skinless, all visible fat discarded (about 4 ounces each) (halved)

steps: Lávese las manos con agua y jabón.
In a large shallow bowl, stir together the hot pepper sauce, lemon juice, and olive oil.
Add the chicken and turn to coat. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 8 hours, turning occasionally if longer than 30 minutes. Discard the marinade.
Preheat the oven to 375 °F. Lightly spray an 8-inch square baking pan with vegetable oil spray.
Put the cornflake crumbs on a plate. Turn the chicken to coat both sides. Transfer to the baking pan.

Lightly spray the top of the chicken with vegetable oil spray. Bake for 30 minutes, or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 °F and the coating is crisp. Transfer to a serving plate.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, whisk together the remaining ingredients. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve. Spoon the sauce over the chicken or use as a dipping sauce.

name: Huevos Motuleños
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032402/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/huevos-motulenos
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup ham, cooked and diced (about 3 ounces)

steps: Soak the pinto beans in 3 cups of water overnight in the refrigerator. Drain. Boil the beans in 3 cups fresh water until they are soft. Drain the water and mash the beans into a paste.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Place tortillas on a cookie sheet and bake for 1 to 2 minutes. Remove cookie sheet from oven and let tortillas cool.
Spoon 1/4 cup of mashed beans on each tortilla. Drain peas and put 1/4 cup of peas on top of beans. Add 2 tablespoons of diced ham on top of peas.
Bake the tortillas for about 8 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, mix egg whites with vegetable oil.
Cook the egg whites in a nonstick pan over medium heat until firm. Cut the egg into 8 pieces.
Place baked tortillas on a plate. Cover ham and mashed beans with a piece of egg.
Add 2 tablespoons of salsa on each tortilla, and serve two tortillas per person.

name: Huevos Rancheros with Fresh Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042545/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/huevos-rancheros-fresh-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 450 °F.
Wash hands with soap and water.
Lightly brush tortillas with oil on both sides and place on a baking sheet.
Bake for 5 to 10 minutes or until tortillas are crisp on the edges and starting to brown.
Remove from oven and set aside.
Spray a large skillet with non-stick cooking spray over medium heat.
Drop 4 egg whites into skillet, then, break whole eggs over whites to make 4 separate servings.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until eggs are cooked.
Place one egg on each tortilla shell and top each with 1 Tablespoon cheese
Place under the broiler for about 2 minutes until cheese is melted.
Spoon fresh salsa around the edge of each shell.

notes.text: Can add fresh lime and peppers as desired.

name: Hummus
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031322/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/hummus
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups garbanzo beans, cooked (also known as chickpeas)
1 tablespoon sesame tahini [sesame paste] (or substitute peanut butter for a sweet taste)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mash the garbanzo beans until smooth (if you have a blender, put the beans and lemon juice into it and blend).
Add the garlic, lemon juice, tahini and oil. Mix well.

name: Instant Chocolate Mousse
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041244/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/instant-chocolate-mousse
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 box of instant chocolate pudding mix (3.9 ounce)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Blend the chocolate pudding mix and the soy milk on medium speed for about 15 seconds until the mixture is very smooth.
Add the silken tofu and blend again. Scrape the mixture down off the sides to be sure it’s all mixed in. Blend and scrape until well mixed and very smooth.
Pour mixture into 4 small serving dishes.
Place in the fridge. Chill for at least 2 hours before serving.

name: Italian Bean Patties
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021752/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/italian-bean-patties
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups low-sodium canned beans, canned (or cooked from dry)
1 cup bread crumbs (dry, or cracker crumbs)
2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, mash beans. Add egg and spices and stir to mix evenly.
Stir in bread crumbs. If mixture seems too wet add more breadcrumbs, 1 tablespoon at a time until mixture resembles meatloaf.
Shape into little sausages or patties. Roll in cornmeal or flour.
Fry slowly in vegetable oil over medium heat until crusty and golden brown.

name: Italian Bean Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031352/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/italian-bean-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15.5 ounces) great northern beans, low-sodium
1 can (15.5 ounces) red kidney beans, low-sodium
46 us fluid ounces tomato juice, low-sodium (or V-8 brand juice)
1 can (14.5 ounces) Italian style or stewed tomatoes, low-sodium

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot, combine all ingredients.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve with Italian or French bread or whole-wheat rolls.

notes.text: Freeze leftovers in plastic sealed containers with 1/2-inch air space under the lid.

name: Italian Broccoli and Pasta
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025007/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/italian-broccoli-and-pasta
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook noodles according to package instructions (do not include oil or salt), and drain.
Spray a medium skillet with non-stick cooking spray; stir-fry onion and broccoli for 3 minutes over medium heat.
Add seasonings (but not the Parmesan cheese) and tomatoes; simmer until heated through.
Spoon vegetable mixture over noodles and top with Parmesan cheese.

name: Italian Inspired Summer Squash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022315/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/italian-inspired-summer-squash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice), divided
6 tablespoons Parmesan cheese or Romano cheese, grated

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Using a large, oven-proof frying pan, heat 1 tablespoon of oil on medium-high.
Arrange squash in pan, add water, and season lightly with salt, pepper, if using, and basil.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, or until tender crisp.
Sprinkle with cheese and drizzle with remaining oil. Place under a preheated broiler and broil until cheese melts and browns slightly.

notes.text: Tip: Add cut up fresh tomatoes, green peppers, green beans, eggplant, onions, or other vegetables in season.

name: Italian Pasta Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032316/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/italian-pasta-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup Italian salad dressing, light or reduced fat (can use more if desired)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together in a large bowl.
Refrigerate for about 30 minutes before serving.

notes.text: For a more hearty salad, add strips of cooked ham, a can of cooked red beans or sprinkle with grated cheese. Learn more about:

name: Italian Style Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045708/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/italian-style-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 head of cabbage (small, sliced thin or shredded)
2 cups corn kernels (or combination of favorite vegetables)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and trim vegetables. Slice zucchini into 1/2 inch pieces; snap beans into pieces; thinly slice or shred cabbage.
Heat oil in frying pan; cook onion over medium heat until soft.
Add vegetables and oregano.
Cook over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes or until tender. Add chopped tomatoes at the last minute of cooking. Stir occasionally.
Serve immediately.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

notes.text: If using fresh green beans, cook for 2 minutes before adding onion.

name: Italian Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044006/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/italian-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound package of pasta, any shape (cooked)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put 1 cup of hot water in a saucepan.
Add vegetables and cook for 5 minutes.
Add tomato sauce, remaining cup of water, basil and salt.
Simmer until heated thoroughly.
Serve with cooked pasta.
Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021231/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/jamaican-jerk-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 pieces of chicken, skinless (4 drumsticks, 4 breasts)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients except chicken in large bowl. Rub seasonings over chicken and marinate in refrigerator for 6 hours or longer.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Space chicken evenly on non-stick or lightly greased baking pan.
Cover with aluminum foil and bake for 40 minutes. Remove foil and continue baking for an additional 30 to 40 minutes or until the meat can easily be pulled away from the bone with a fork.

name: Jean’s Banana Pudding Parfait
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045610/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/jeans-banana-pudding-parfait
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1-oz box instant sugar-free, fat-free vanilla pudding
1 cup fat-free frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the milk and pudding mix; blend well (about 2 minutes).
Add yogurt and vanilla extract; blend until smooth.
Stir the thawed whipped topping into the mixture.
Line the bottom of the parfait cups with a teaspoon of crumbled ginger snaps.
Layer 6 banana slices on top of the cookies; then 2 tablespoons of the yogurt mixture on top. Repeat with another layer of the ginger snaps, bananas, and yogurt mixture.
Top with cinnamon or crushed cookie for garnish.
Cover and chill in refrigerator.
serving_size: 1 glass of Jean's Banana Pudding Parfait

name: Jiffy Oatmeal Crunch
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041127/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/jiffy-oatmeal-crunch
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F and grease a 9x13 inch baking pan.
In large skillet, melt butter and brown sugar.
Remove from heat and stir in remaining ingredients.
Spread into pan and bake for 15 to 20 minutes. Cool; cut into squares.

name: Jollof Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021135/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/jollof-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 pounds cooked meat, cut into 1-inch cubes (use chicken, bacon, shrimp, or smoked pork)
1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
2 cans no-salt added tomato paste (6 ounces each)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sauté cooked meat in oil until slightly brown.
In a large kettle, sauté yellow onion, green pepper, and ginger in vegetable oil until onions are soft.
Add whole tomatoes and simmer for five minutes.
Add tomato paste, 2 quarts water, salt, black pepper, thyme, and red pepper.
Add cooked meat, simmer 20 minutes longer.
In a 2-quart saucepan, cook rice in chicken stock and water until tender.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Pour the rice in a deep bowl and arrange the meat in the center.

name: Julia’s Sautéed & Steamed Collards
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045220/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/julias-sauteed-steamed-collards
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Cut bottom stems from collards.
Wash and cut collards into bite-sized pieces. Place in colander to drain.
Chop garlic cloves into small pieces.
Place olive oil into large skillet. Place on high heat to start.

Place collards in skillet. Keep on high heat, turning collards as they saute, about 1 minute in the uncovered skillet. (You will not need to add water because of the water already on the washed collards.)
Add garlic cloves and red pepper flakes.
Place cover on the skillet to allow collards to steam until they are half their original volume.
Turn heat to low and continue steaming until the collards are tender.

name: Kale and Cranberry Stir-Fry
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032641/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/kale-and-cranberry-stir-fry
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 clove minced garlic or 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder
6 cups kale, chopped (leaf portion, no stems)
1/4 cup freshly squeezed orange juice (1/2 orange)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add oil and onion to large skillet. Stir and sauté over medium-high heat (350 °F in an electric skillet) until onion is clear.
Add cranberries and garlic. Continue to sauté for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add kale. Pour or squeeze orange juice over top of kale. Continue to stir fry for about 5 minutes until kale is wilting and hot.
Serve immediately.

notes.text: 1 bunch fresh kale (about 8 cups, chopped)

name: Kale Chips
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041710/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/kale-chips
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup kale (or chard, spinach, or collards)
1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil (or oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 300 °F.
Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper (optional).
Wash and dry kale. With a knife or kitchen scissors, carefully remove the leaves from the thick stems.
Tear into bite-sized pieces and place kale pieces on cookie sheet.
Drizzle oil over kale and then sprinkle with seasonings of choice.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes or until kale is crisp and edges are brown but not burned.

notes.text: Seasoning suggestions: salt, pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, chili powder, cumin, turmeric, and Parmesan cheese.

name: Kale with Nuts and Raisins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032237/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/kale-nuts-and-raisins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 350 °F.
On a baking sheet, toast nuts for 5 minutes.
Heat oil in frying pan on medium heat.
Add garlic and kale to frying pan and cook for 4 minutes.
Add raisins and nuts and cook for 1 minute more.
Add salt to taste (optional)

notes.text: Walnuts used for costing and nutrition analysis.

name: Kale Salad with Yogurt Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032643/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/kale-salad-yogurt-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or oil of your choice, divided)
1 lemon (zested and juiced - save zest for dressing)
1 lime (zested and juiced - save zest for dressing)
1/2 cup cilantro (chopped or torn, stems included)
1 jalapeño chile pepper (seeds removed and diced, optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and dry kale. Remove stems and tear into bite-sized pieces.
Season kale with salt, pepper, 1 tablespoon of olive oil, lemon juice, and lime juice.
With your hands, massage kale until the leaves just start to wilt.
Make the dressing - in a small bowl, add the salt and pepper to the yogurt.
Add the lemon and lime zest and remaining 1 tablespoon of oil.
Mix in cilantro and jalapeno pepper, if desired.
With a spoon, mix massaged kale with yogurt dressing.
Toss pumpkin seeds over salad.

name: Kibbeh Khamoustah
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021139/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/kibbeh-khamoustah
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound ground beef, 85% lean (coarsely ground, if available)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Fry ground beef in a small amount of oil.
Prepare the dough by mixing matzo meal, semolina, water, and salt.
Wet hands and shape into walnut-sized pieces.
Roll out dough into a small circle and fill with 1 Tablespoon of meat.
Seal the dough. Continue until all the dough and meat is used.
In a large pot, heat a small amount of oil and fry garlic until golden.
Add the scallions and Swiss chard. Mix well.
Cook about 10 minutes.
Cover with water and continue to cook until boiling.
Add lemon juice, to taste (optional).
Add stuffed dough to soup and cook 15 more minutes.

notes.text: Kibbeh Khamoustah is a Kurdish dish. Kibbeh, or dumplings, are stuffed with meat, traditionally lamb or beef, and served with soup.

name: Kid-Friendly Taco Cups
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045701/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/kid-friendly-taco-cups
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 yellow bell pepper, seeded and diced
1/2 green bell pepper, seeded and diced

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

In a large skillet over medium heat, add oil and chopped onion. Stir occasionally until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic, ground pork, peppers and spinach. Stir to crumble meat, cook until no longer pink, about 6 minutes.
Return to heat and add seasonings, stirring to combine. Brown meat 2–3 minutes more and until internal temperature reaches 160 degrees F. Remove from heat and set aside.
In a small bowl, combine tomatoes with lime juice and fresh cilantro. Season with salt if desired.
Arrange 12 serving cups on a platter and fill with cooked pork mixture. Top with your choice of toppings and tomatoes. Serve immediately.

notes.text: Optional ingredients: Avocado, corn, jalapeños, black beans, salsa, nonfat Greek yogurt

name: Layered Black Bean Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031551/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/layered-black-bean-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can black beans, low-sodium (15 ounce, drained and rinsed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mash beans and mix with onion powder, dried oregano, garlic powder, and cayenne pepper. Spread on a serving dish.
Top with salsa, sour cream, green onions, and grated cheese.

notes.text: Serve as a dip for raw vegetables such as celery, carrot sticks, and pepper slices.

name: Leaf Finger Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034852/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/leaf-finger-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lay lettuce leaves on a flat surface. Top each leaf with all ingredients: cucumbers, carrots, beets, and sunflower seeds.
Drizzle each leaf with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Slowly roll the leaf with all ingredients.

name: Leafy Tofu
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215252/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/leafy-tofu
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain tofu.
Dice tofu into 1-inch cubes.
Tear spinach into bite-sized pieces.
In a large pan, heat oil and saute tofu cubes for a few minutes. Move tofu to the center of the pan.
Add spinach, and soy sauce. Mix.
Cover pan and cook until spinach is wilted.
Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds.

notes.text: You may use other dark green leafy vegetables.

name: Leftover Turkey Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040426/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/leftover-turkey-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can reduced-sodium cream of mushroom soup (10.75 ounces)

steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 °F.
Lightly coat a 9x9x2 inch baking dish with vegetable spray. Cut 6 slices of bread (fresh or day-old) into 1-inch cubes and place half into the bottom of a baking dish.
In a bowl, combine turkey, onion, celery, mayonnaise, and pepper. Spoon mixture over bread crumbs.
Place remaining bread cubes over turkey mixture and press down slightly with spoon.
Combine eggs and milk and pour mixture over cubes. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
When ready to bake, preheat oven to 325 °F.
Spoon soup over top of casserole.
Spread one teaspoon margarine on side of each slice of bread. Cut buttered bread into 1/2-inch cubes and sprinkle on top of casserole.
Bake for 60 minutes or until knife inserted in middle comes out clean.
Remove from oven and sprinkle cheese over top. Let stand 15 minutes before cutting and serving.

notes.text: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.

name: Lemon Corn Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031628/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lemon-corn-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Mix first five ingredients together in mixing bowl.
Combine yogurt, lemon peel, oil, egg yolk, and milk together and stir into dry ingredients just until blended.
Whip egg whites with mixer until stiff. Fold into corn meal mixture.
Pour into round 9 inch cake pan coated with nonstick cooking spray.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until corn cake tests done.
For optional lemon glaze: Over low heat blend lemon juice together with powdered sugar. Pierce cake top repeatedly with fork. Slowly pour glaze evenly over the top.

name: Lemon Dill Brussels Sprouts
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035228/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lemon-dill-brussels-sprouts
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup plain Greek yogurt, fat free (or low-fat)
2 cups Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved lengthwise (1 pound)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, mix yogurt, dill weed, lemon juice, and salt. Set aside.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, sauté sprouts (cut side down) in margarine or butter until they begin to brown.
Stir sprouts and add water. Cover the pan and steam until the water is gone and sprouts are tender crisp, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Mix sprouts with lemon dill sauce. Serve warm.

name: Lemon Pepper Salmon Patties
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020530/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lemon-pepper-salmon-patties
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 egg, slightly beaten (can also use dried egg mix)
7 ounces frozen salmon, thawed, drained, and finely chopped (optional to remove the skin)

steps: Mix breadcrumbs, mayonnaise, egg, and lemon pepper in a medium bowl. Add salmon and mix.
Measure 1/3 cup of salmon mixture (packed) and form into a round patty. Repeat until you have five salmon patties.
Spray a skillet with cooking spray and set stove to medium heat.

Place the salmon patties in the skillet and cook until light brown, 5–7 minutes. Flip the patties and cook on the other side until brown. Salmon should reach a final internal cook temperature of 145°F as measured with a food thermometer before serving.

name: Lemon Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024907/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lemon-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Heat the oven to 375 °F.
Combine lemon juice, garlic clove, and oil. Set aside 1 tablespoon.
Peel the potatoes and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Pour the lemon juice mixture in a casserole dish or small baking pan to coat the bottom of the dish.
Place the potatoes in the baking dish and coat with the lemon juice mixture.
Bake about 30 minutes, until potatoes are tender.
After removing from the oven, brush the remaining lemon juice mixture on the potatoes. Serve warm.

name: Lemon Velvet Supreme
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043626/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lemon-velvet-supreme
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup mandarin orange (4 ounce, slices, drained or your favorite fruit)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine vanilla yogurt and pudding mix; gently stir together.
Layer bottom of individual dishes with crushed graham crackers. Reserve a few crumbs to sprinkle on top.
Pour pudding mixture over cracker crumbs.
Top with mandarin orange slices or your favorite fruit. Sprinkle with remaining crumbs.

name: Lemonade
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042237/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lemonade
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut lemon in half crosswise.
Place lemon half on juicer. Push and twist to squeeze out the juice.
Pour juice into glass. Add about 3/4 cup water.
Add sugar, stirring to mix ingredients.

Create-a-Flavor Changes Squeeze one-half each lemon and lime.; Squeeze one-half each lemon and orange.; Add 1/4 cup apple juice concentrate and leave out the sugar.; Use 1/4 cup seltzer water and 1/2 cup water.

name: Lentil Barley Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034648/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lentil-barley-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can 14.5 ounce low-sodium whole peeled tomatoes (coarsely chopped)

steps: Place a large soup pot on the stove and add lentils, scallions, carrots, celery, oregano, barley, and water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for one hour.
Add the tomatoes and continue cooking about 45 minutes. Just before serving, add vinegar.

name: Lentil Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033951/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lentil-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cans tomatoes, low-sodium, diced or crushed (29 ounce or 2 cans 14 1/2 ounce)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large saucepan, brown beef over medium-high heat, breaking it into bite sized pieces. Drain fat.
Add onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Add lentils, tomatoes, chili powder, and cumin. Cook for about 1 hour until flavors are blended.
Serve hot, topped with your favorite chili toppings.

name: Lentil Minestrone
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231030852/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lentil-minestrone
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 sweet potato, peeled and diced into 1/4-inch pieces
1 zucchini, diced into 1/4-inch pieces (or 1 cup of frozen zucchini)
2 cups canned diced tomatoes, no salt added (or fresh tomatoes)

steps: Put a soup pot on the stove over medium-high heat. When the pot is hot, add the oil. Add onion and garlic and cook about 7 minutes until golden.
Add carrots, celery, sweet potato, and zucchini and cook about 10 minutes until slightly tender.
Add tomatoes, lentils, water, and chicken bouillon cube and bring to a boil over high heat. Turn the heat down to low, cover and cook 40 minutes.
Add the kale and cook an additional 20 minutes. Serve right away or cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days.

name: Lentil Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024832/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lentil-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 large red, yellow, or white onion, chopped
8 cups low-sodium chicken broth or vegetable broth

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sauté onions, carrots, red pepper flakes, and garlic in oil until soft.
Add tomatoes, bay leaf, salt and pepper and stir well.
Add rinsed lentils and broth and simmer until lentils are soft, about 30 minutes. Keep checking lentils until they are done.
Season with additional salt and pepper, if desired.

name: Lentil Spaghetti Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035501/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lentil-spaghetti-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 garlic clove (crushed, or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)
28 ounces spaghetti sauce, low-sodium (1 jar, can use 28-32 ounces)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large sauce pan brown meat. Drain.
Add onion and garlic to drained meat. Cook until onions are soft but not brown.
Add cooked lentils and spaghetti sauce and bring to a boil. Lower heat and cook gently for 15 minutes.
Serve sauce over hot cooked spaghetti noodles.

name: Lentil Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031348/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lentil-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cans diced tomatoes, low-sodium (14.5 ounces each)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onion.
Cook for 3 minutes, or until tender.
Stir in garlic powder, carrots, lentils, tomatoes, water, and chili powder.
Simmer, uncovered, for about 20 minutes or until lentils are tender.

name: Lentil Tacos
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033221/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lentil-tacos
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook lentils in 3 cups water for 10 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer for 30 minutes. Add more water if necessary.
Serve with corn tortillas. Can also be served over rice or noodles.

notes.text: Alternate seasoning: 2 tablespoons taco seasoning instead of the other spices.

name: Lentil Vegetable Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024902/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lentil-vegetable-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups potatoes, sliced (15 ounce can, low-sodium)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil 1 cup water in a saucepan.
Add the lentils. Cook for 20 minutes over low heat until tender, then drain.
Cook the peas for 3 minutes in another saucepan. Then remove from heat.
Rinse and drain the peas.
Wash, peel, and shred the carrots.
Put the cooked lentils, sliced potatoes, peas, and shredded carrots in a bowl.
Put the parsley, vinegar, mustard, and olive oil in another bowl. Stir well.
Pour the dressing over the lentil vegetable salad.

name: Lentil Vegetable Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020755/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lentil-vegetable-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sort lentils.
Place lentils in deep pot with water. Bring to a boil and add all ingredients except vinegar.
Reduce heat and cover.
Cook slowly for 1 hour, adding more water if necessary.
Add vinegar.
Remove garlic and bay leaf before serving.

name: Lickety Split Banana Split
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034748/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lickety-split-banana-split
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and cut the banana in half, lengthwise.
Place the banana on a plate.
Top banana with yogurt and sprinkle with cereal and fruit.

name: Light as a Feather Whole Wheat Pancakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035250/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/light-feather-whole-wheat-pancakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat griddle. In medium bowl, stir or sift dry ingredients together.
In a separate bowl, beat egg, buttermilk, brown sugar, and oil together. Stir into dry ingredients just until moistened; batter should be slightly lumpy.
Pour 1/4 cup batter for each pancake onto sprayed or seasoned hot griddle.
Flip the pancake when bubbles appear on surface; turn only once.

name: Lime-Marinated Flank Steak with Stuffed Poblano Peppers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031511/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lime-marinated-flank-steak-stuffed-poblano-peppers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 cans diced tomatoes with green chiles (14 1/2 ounces)
1/3 cup fresh lime juice for marinade
1 can low sodium black beans, drained and rinsed (15 ounces)
6 medium poblano chile peppers (about 4 inches long)
optional toppings: toasted, shelled pepitas (pumpkin seeds), lime wedges, crumbled queso fresco

steps: Drain tomatoes, reserving juice for marinade. Set aside diced tomatoes with green chiles.

Combine reserved tomato juice, 1/2 cup cilantro, lime juice and olive oil in medium bowl. Cover and refrigerate 1/3 cup marinade for rice. Place beef Flank Steak and remaining marinade in food-safe plastic bag; turn steak to coat. Close bag securely and marinate in refrigerator 6 hours or as long as overnight, turning occasionally.

Combine rice, reserved 1/3 cup marinade, diced tomatoes, black beans and remaining 1/4 cup cilantro in medium bowl. Season with salt and pepper, as desired. Set aside. Cook's Tip: Two cups leftover cooked rice or 1 package (8.8 ounces) ready-to-serve whole grain brown rice can be substituted.

Cut slit lengthwise down 1 side of each poblano pepper to create pocket, leaving stem and tip intact. Make another small crosswise cut just below the stem to form T-shaped opening. Remove and discard seeds and membranes, being careful to keep peppers intact. Spoon rice mixture evenly into peppers. Wrap each tightly in aluminum foil to seal.

Remove steak from marinade; discard marinade. Place steak in center grid over medium, ash-covered coals; arrange peppers around steak. Grill steak, covered, 11 to 16 minutes (over medium heat on preheated gas grill 16 to 21 minutes) for medium rare to medium doneness, turning occasionally. Grill peppers, covered, 25 to 30 minutes (20 to 25 minutes on gas grill) or until peppers are tender and filling is heated through, turning occasionally.
Carve steak across grain into thin slices. Remove peppers from foil. Serve peppers with steaks and toppings as desired.

notes.text: Cook's Tip: Two cups leftover cooked rice or 1 package (8.8 ounces) ready-to-serve whole grain brown rice can be substituted. For more information on degree of doneness, safe food handling, and beef safety, visit: https://www.beefitswhatsfordinner.com

name: Lite Fried Okra
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032015/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lite-fried-okra
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3/4 teaspoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a bowl, mix sliced okra, oil, salt, and pepper.
Coat a large fry pan with cooking spray.
Heat over medium heat, and add okra mixture, turning often with a wooden spoon or spatula.
Cook until okra is browned, about 10 minutes.
Serve with hot sauce or favorite relish.

name: Lite Italian Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035933/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/lite-italian-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder (or 1 fresh clove, minced)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a pint sized jar with tight fitting lid.
Shake vigorously to blend ingredients.
Store refrigerated.

name: Louisiana Green Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032210/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/louisiana-green-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cans (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium green beans, drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the onion.
Chop the green pepper and celery.
Drain the liquid from the green beans. Rinse with water.
Put the green beans in a saucepan. Add enough water to cover them
Cook the green beans on low heat until tender. Then drain off the water.
Combine all the ingredients in a skillet.
Cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, until the celery is tender and the food is hot.

name: Low Fat Creamy Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045320/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/low-fat-creamy-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix and stir all ingredients in small container.
Store covered in refrigerator and use within 1 week.

name: Low Fat Ranch Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020320/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/low-fat-ranch-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can great northern beans (15 ounce, rinsed and drained, low sodium)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Blend the beans and garlic in a blender, adding enough water for the desired consistency.
Blend for 2 minutes to make it silky smooth.
Use a spatula to scrape the mixture into a medium bowl.
Stir in the yogurt, cayenne, chives, parsley, and tarragon, salt, and lemon juice. Serve in a bowl.

name: Mac and Beans Medley
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031428/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mac-and-beans-medley
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 bell pepper (green, red, yellow, or orange)
1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium beans, drained and rinsed (black, kidney, pinto or other)
2 cups cooked macaroni, without salt or fat added (or other pasta)

steps: Wash hands with warm water and soap.
Peel and finely chop the garlic. Core, seed, and finely chop the bell pepper.
Heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat. Add garlic and bell pepper. Cook for one minute. Do not let garlic brown. Add diced tomatoes (do not drain) and red pepper flakes.
Cover the skillet and lower heat. Cook for 10 minutes or until sauce is slightly thickened.
Add beans and cooked macaroni to skillet and cook 5 minutes or until heated through.
Serve hot.

name: Macaroni & Cheese with Broccoli
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025054/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/macaroni-cheese-broccoli
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook macaroni, following the instructions on the package.
Drain the cooked macaroni and return to the pan.
While the macaroni is still warm, sprinkle in the flour and stir thoroughly.
Over medium heat, slowly stir the milk into the macaroni.
Add the cheese and pepper.
Stir over medium heat until the milk and cheese thicken into a creamy sauce, approximately 7-10 minutes.
Stir in the broccoli; heat thoroughly.
Taste; add a small amount of salt, if needed.
Refrigerate leftovers.

notes.text: Fresh or frozen broccoli can be used.

name: Macaroni Chick-Pea Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025048/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/macaroni-chick-pea-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15 ounces) low-sodium chickpeas, drained (garbanzo beans)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large saucepan, bring broth and water to a boil. Reduce heat to low.
Add macaroni, celery flakes, and oregano. Simmer 4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add stewed tomatoes, green beans, chickpeas, and garlic powder.
Simmer 5 minutes, or until macaroni and beans are tender.

name: Magic Crust Quiche
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214936/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/magic-crust-quiche
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups vegetables, frozen, no salt added (or use fresh or leftovers)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook onion in oil (or cook with vegetables).
Cook vegetables (or use leftovers). Drain well.
Grease round pie pan or 8x8 inch baking dish.
Spread cooked vegetables in pan. Spread cheese on top of vegetables.
Mix milk, eggs, and baking mix. Pour over vegetables and cheese.
Bake at 350 °F for 35 minutes, until a safe internal temperature has been reached and a knife inserted into the middle comes out clean.

notes.text: Suggest preparing with frozen broccoli (shown) or spinach.

name: Magic Mix
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035705/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/magic-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine dry milk, flour, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut in margarine with two knives until the mixture looks like cornmeal.
Store in a dry, closed container in the refrigerator for up to 6 weeks.

name: Magical Fruit Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042756/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/magical-fruit-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (20 ounces) pineapple chunks, juice packed
1 cup seedless grapes, red or green
1 package (3.5 ounces) instant pudding mix, lemon or vanilla

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain off the juice from the canned pineapples. Put chunks in a large bowl.
Rinse the grapes and drain. Add the grapes to the bowl.
Peel the bananas and cut into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl.
Pour the milk over the fruit. While slowly stirring the fruit mixture, sprinkle in the pudding mix.
Let the mixture stand for 5 minutes and serve.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Mango Berry Rotini Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034657/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mango-berry-rotini-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup (4 oz) whole-wheat rotini pasta, uncooked

steps: In a small bowl, whisk vinaigrette ingredients; set aside.
Boil water and cook rotini according to package instructions. Drain cooked rotini and rinse in cool water.
While rotini is cooking, cut mango into chunks, removing peel and pit.
Place salad ingredients in a large bowl; drizzle with vinaigrette. Toss gently.

notes.text: Serving Suggestion: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of non-fat milk.

name: Mango Cucumber Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021519/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mango-cucumber-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Cut all but one half of mango into chunks, removing peel and pit; chill remaining mango half for use with garnish.
Slice off 1/4 of the cucumber and chill for use with garnish. Coarsely chop remaining 3/4 of the cucumber.
Place chopped mango, cucumber, onion, and pepper (optional) in blender or food processor with lime juice and water. Purée until smooth.
Blend in yogurt. Chill until ready to serve.

About 15 to 30 minutes before serving, prepare garnish. Dice chilled mango half, removing peel and pit; dice remaining cucumber. Mix mango and cucumber dices with cilantro. To serve, top bowls of soup with garnish.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of 100% apple juice.

name: Mango Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032521/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mango-salsa1
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the mango, be sure to remove the seed.
Cut the pepper and onion into small pieces.
Mix all the ingredients together.

name: Mango Shake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031725/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mango-shake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 fresh pitted mango (or 4 Tablespoons of frozen mango juice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all ingredients into a blender.
Blend until foamy.
Serve immediately.

name: Manhattan Clam Chowder
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034242/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/manhattan-clam-chowder
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cans (6.5 ounces each) clams, chopped and drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub potatoes well to remove any eyes or blemishes.
In a slow cooker, combine all ingredients; stir.
Cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or until the vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaf and peppercorns before serving.

name: Maple Sweet Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231013751/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/maple-sweet-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prick potato skins with a fork. Microwave on high for 3 to 4 minute until soft and easily pierced with a knife.
Scoop out the pulp into a medium bowl.
Mash the pulp and stir in the yogurt, maple syrup, and orange juice.
Transfer to a microwave safe serving bowl and microwave for 1 to 2 minutes to heat through.

name: Marinara Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041702/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/marinara-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
4 cans (14.5 ounce) crushed tomatoes, low sodium

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash the vegetables.
Collect, dice, and measure all ingredients before starting to prepare the recipe.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic powder. Cook for about 10 minutes or until the onion is clear.
Add the carrots and celery and cook for 5 minutes until slightly soft.
Add the tomatoes and Italian seasoning. Stir until all ingredients are mixed together. Taste, and add a little bit of salt and pepper if desired.
Turn the heat to medium-high and bring sauce to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low. Simmer uncovered for at least 30 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 2 minutes until spinach wilts.*
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Eat within 3 to 5 days.
* For a smoother sauce, blend in a blender or food processor.

notes.text: This recipe freezes well. Defrost in the refrigerator overnight, then reheat and eat!

name: Marinated Beef
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050526/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/marinated-beef
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 tablespoons vegetable oil, divided (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Using a cutting board and sharp knife, cut round steak across the grain into thin strips about 1/2 inch wide and 2 to 3 inches long.
In a medium glass mixing bowl, combine garlic, lemon juice, 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil, salt, and pepper.
Add beef strips and stir to coat with the oil mixture (marinade sauce). Cover bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for about 2 hours.
In a medium skillet over medium-high heat, heat 2 tablespoons of the oil for 1-2 minutes until hot.
Drain marinade from beef. Put beef in skillet, stir and cook for 5 to 7 minutes or until meat is thoroughly browned.

name: Marinated Three-Bean Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031230/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/marinated-three-bean-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 can low-sodium cannellini (white) beans (15.5 ounce can)
1/2 can low-sodium cut green beans (14.5 ounce can)
1/2 can low-sodium red kidney beans (15.5 ounce can)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain the canned beans. To reduce the sodium rinse the beans under running water
Peel and chop the onion.
In a large bowl, combine the cannellini beans, green beans, kidney beans, onion, and celery.
Pour the Italian dressing over the vegetables and toss lightly.
Cover the bowl and marinate in the refrigerator for at least one hour. The salad can be left in the refrigerator over night.
Drain before serving.

notes.text: Double the recipe to use the entire can of beans. Garnish with parsley if desired.

name: Mashed Parsnips and Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031235/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mashed-parsnips-and-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub parsnips and potatoes under running water and peel.
Cut into similar size pieces.
In a medium saucepan, cover the vegetables pieces with cold water. Bring the water to a boil and simmer until vegetables are soft, 15 to 20 minutes.
Drain the vegetables and mash. Stir in milk, salt, pepper, garlic powder and margarine. Serve hot.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

notes.text: Try other seasonings such as parsley, thyme or nutmeg.

name: Mashed Sweet Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044946/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mashed-sweet-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and peel the potatoes. Cut them into slices that are 3/4 inch thick.
Put them in a saucepan with enough water to cover the potatoes.
Bring the water to a boil on medium heat.
Cook the potatoes for 20 to 25 minutes until they’re soft.
Drain the water. Put the potatoes in a medium bowl.
Use a fork or potato masher to mash the potatoes.
Mix in the thyme, salt, and pepper.

name: Red Lentils with Onion | Masoor Dal
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043853/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/masoor-dal-red-lentils-onion
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse the lentils in a strainer under running water two to three times.
In a bowl, combine the washed lentils, 1 teaspoon oil, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Boil lentils in 1 1/2 cups water until they turn yellow and soft. Add turmeric powder, cumin powder, and sugar to the boiled lentils and mix them well.
In a separate pan, add rest of the oil and allow it to heat.
Split the chili peppers in half and add to the heated oil.
Add onion to the oil and stir until it starts to turn light brown.
Add 2 tablespoons boiled lentils (mixed with spices) into the fried onion and stir well for 1 minute.
Add the rest of the boiled lentil mix and stir.
Add 1 cup of water and allow it to boil for two minutes. Serve over white rice. Add parsley garnish if desired.

notes.text: This is a very common food item in Bengali as well as in Pakistani and Indian communities. Generally, lunch or dinner is started with this item followed by two to three main courses. On special occasions, or when preparing this for someone special, one may garnish it with coconut flakes or cilantro leaves.

name: Master Mix Oregon
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050351/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/master-mix-oregon
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl combine all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour, dry milk, baking powder, and salt.
Mix thoroughly.
Cut in shortening with pastry blender or two knives until mixture looks like course cornmeal.
Store in covered containers in the refrigerator.

notes.text: The final product of this recipe is intended to be used as an ingredient in other recipes. It is not intended as a ready-to-eat product.

name: Matzo Meal Kugel (Pudding)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214805/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/matzo-meal-kugel-pudding
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine eggs and sugar; beat well.
Add milk and melted butter; mix well.
Stir in matzo meal and salt.
Pour into buttered 11x13 inch pan.
Bake at 350 °F for 1 hour (don't over bake).
Cut into slices. Can be served hot or cold.

name: Meatball Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033604/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/meatball-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 low-sodium beef or chicken bouillon cubes (or 1 tablespoon low-sodium bouillon powder)
8 ounces 90% lean ground beef (or turkey or chicken)
1/2 medium onion, peeled and finely chopped
2 cups fresh vegetable mix, chopped (carrots, celery, and spinach)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot, combine water, rice, bouillon cubes, and oregano. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Stir to dissolve bouillon. Reduce heat to low and simmer.
Meanwhile, in a large bowl, mix ground meat, tomato, onion, egg, and salt. Form into 12 meatballs.
Add meatballs to broth mixture and simmer 30 minutes.
Add vegetables. Cook 10 to 15 minutes or until meatballs are cooked and rice and vegetables are tender.
Serve hot.
serving_size: 1/2 cup broth mixture and 3 large meatballs

name: Meatloaf in a Mug
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215207/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/meatloaf-mug
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients and stir to mix.
Spray microwave-safe mug with cooking spray.
Pat beef mixture into mug. Make a small hold in center, all the way to the bottom.
Microwave on HIGH (100%) for 3 minutes or until done.

notes.text: Food Safety Note: Cook until the internal temperature is 160 °F when measured with a meat thermometer.

name: Meaty Stuffed Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022052/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/meaty-stuffed-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 ounces turkey, diced and cooked (or use cooked chicken, beef, or pork)

steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Scrub potatoes. Remove any bad spots. Do not peel. Cut each in half, lengthwise.

In a covered saucepan, boil potatoes in just enough water to cover the pieces. When they are fork-tender (about 15 to 20 minutes), remove from heat and drain. Set aside. (Note: you can also pierce whole potatoes with a knife or fork in several places and cook in microwave without water until fork tender, then cut each in half, lengthwise).
Meanwhile, in a large skillet sprayed with non-stick cooking spray, combine cooked meat, broccoli, onion, carrots and water.
Boil until vegetables are fork tender - about 5 minutes. Reduce heat to low.
In a jar with a tight fitting lid, combine milk, flour and pepper. Shake well.
Stir flour mixture into meat mixture until well blended.
Stir in cheese. Cook over low heat about 5 minutes longer or until sauce thickens, stirring frequently.
To serve, place 2 potato halves on each plate and mash the middle somewhat. Spoon about one third cup of the meat mixture over each potato half
Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Mediterranean Chicken and White Bean Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025501/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mediterranean-chicken-and-white-bean-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup skinless chicken, cooked and diced into 1/2 inch pieces
1 15.5 ounce can low-sodium white beans, drained and rinsed
1 cucumber, peeled and diced into 1/2 inch pieces
1/4 red or white onion, chopped into 1/2 inch pieces
1 tablespoon dried basil or parsley leaves

steps: Put everything in the bowl and gently toss.
Serve right away, or cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days.

name: Mediterranean Roasted Eggplant with Tomato Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034432/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mediterranean-roasted-eggplant-tomato-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup low-sodium pizza or spaghetti sauce

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Wash and remove the stem end, and slice the eggplants into 1/2-inch slices.
Spray a baking pan with vegetable oil spray and lay the eggplant in the pan in a single layer.
Spoon low-sodium pizza or spaghetti sauce on each slice.
Bake 30 minutes in the preheated oven.
Stir the yogurt and garlic together.
Drizzle the sauce in thin lines on each of the eggplant slices before serving. You can do this easily by putting the sauce in a plastic squirt bottle or using a spoon.
Serve immediately as an entrée or side dish.

name: Mediterranean Tuna Antipasti Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032647/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mediterranean-tuna-antipasti-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 15.5-ounce can garbanzo beans, low sodium, drained and rinsed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place walnuts, onion, bell pepper, parsley, tuna, and garbanzo beans in a large bowl and mix lightly.
Whisk together lemon juice and olive oil and drizzle over salad; stir lightly to coat ingredients with dressing. Season with salt and pepper, if desired.
Place lettuce on a platter or divide between 8 salad bowls. Top with equal amounts of salad.

name: Melissa’s Slow Cooker Stuffing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045540/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/melissas-slow-cooker-stuffing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Melt butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add onion, celery, mushrooms, and parsley to pan. Stir often until veggies are tender.
Combine bread cubes, cranberries, and apple in a large bowl. Pour veggies over bread cubes and mix gently.
Season with poultry seasoning, sage, thyme, garlic powder, and pepper. Pour in broth (just enough to moisten) and gently mix in eggs.
Transfer mixture to slow cooker and cover.
Set slow cooker to High for 45 minutes; then reduce heat to Low and cook for 4 to 8 hours.

name: Melon and Mint
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032651/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/melon-and-mint
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Blend lime juice, mint leaves, and brown sugar together in a small food processor.
Place melon cubes in a bowl. Drizzle dressing over melon and toss gently.

name: Vegetable Pinwheels
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034109/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mexican-pinwheels
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain the corn and green chilis. Collect, chop, and measure all ingredients before starting to prepare the recipe.
Mix cream cheese, corn, green chilies, onions, and salsa together in a bowl.
Spread mixture on tortillas, roll up tightly, and wrap in plastic wrap.
Cut in 1-inch slices, and serve immediately, or store in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

notes.text: Be creative! Add washed, chopped fresh cilantro or spices like cumin and chili powder in step #2.

name: Microwave Baked Apple
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024937/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/microwave-baked-apple
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash apples and remove core.
Cut a thin slice off bottom of each apple to form a flat surface. Place apples in a microwave-safe baking dish.
Mix brown sugar and cinnamon in a small dish. Spoon mixture into center of apples.
Cover wax paper and microwave on high power 6 to 10 minutes or until apples are soft.

name: Microwave Cauliflower and Peas in Cream Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042301/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/microwave-cauliflower-and-peas-cream-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine cauliflower, peas, and water in a 1-quart casserole. Cover. Microwave at High 6 to 8 minutes, or until fork-tender, stirring after half the time. Let stand, covered.
Place onion and butter or margarine in 2-cup measure. Microwave at High 1 to 1 1/2 minutes, or until onion is tender.
Stir in flour. Microwave a few seconds until flour mixture starts to bubble.
Add remaining ingredients. Microwave at High 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, or until thickened, stirring every minute.
Drain vegetables. (Freeze drained liquid for use in soups later.) Pour sauce over vegetables and stir to coat.

notes.text: Options: Vegetables may be boiled or steamed and sauce prepared on top of a range if a microwave is not available. Variations: Use other combinations of vegetables, such as green beans and cauliflower; broccoli and carrots; or peas and carrots. Add lime as a garnish if desired.

name: Microwave Denver Scramble Slider
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020519/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/microwave-denver-scramble-slider
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons red or green bell peppers, chopped
1 slider-sized bun or whole wheat English muffin, split and toasted

steps: Place peppers and onions in 8 ounce ramekin or custard cup, or in a small bowl. Microwave on high 30 seconds; stir. Add egg, ham, and water, beat until egg is blended.
Microwave on high 30 seconds; stir. Microwave until egg is almost set, 30 to 45 seconds longer. Season with salt and pepper, if desired.
Serve in bun.

name: Microwave Potato Corn Chowder
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042526/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/microwave-potato-corn-chowder
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Melt margarine in glass bowl on HIGH for 30 to 50 seconds.
Stir in flour, salt and pepper until smooth.
Blend milk into flour-margarine mixture.
Cook on HIGH for 6 to 8 minutes, until thickened, stirring well each minute. Set aside.
In a separate microwave safe bowl, cook 2 potatoes in 1 cup water. When potatoes are done add potatoes and cooking water to white sauce.
Stir in one 16 ounce can of corn. Cook 2 to 3 minutes or until steaming hot.

notes.text: Shredded cheese, crumbled bacon, chopped ham, or onion may be added. Add clams for clam chowder.

name: Migas "Crumbs"
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034013/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/migas-crumbs
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Tear tortillas into small pieces.
Heat oil in a medium-sized pan.
Add tortillas and stir until pieces begin to brown.
Add peppers and onion; sauté until soft.
Add eggs; stir until the eggs are cooked.
Remove from heat and sprinkle on the grated cheese.
Cover the pan and let cheese melt.
Serve immediately.

name: Minestrone Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031244/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/minestrone-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 package (10 ounces) frozen vegetables, any type
2 cans (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium stewed tomatoes
2 cans (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium broth, any flavor
1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium beans, any type

steps: Adult and child: Wash hands with soap and water.
Child: In a large pot, combine frozen vegetables, tomatoes, broth and beans.
Adult: Bring the soup to a boil and add the pasta. Then reduce to low heat. Let simmer for 6 to 8 minutes or until the pasta and vegetables are tender.
This recipe is developed for a child to help an adult in the kitchen. Directions are written to different audiences.

name: Mini Caprese Bites
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041623/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mini-caprese-bites
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon olive oil, or cooking oil of choice

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice string cheese into 4 equal parts.
On a toothpick, skewer one cherry tomato, 2 basil leaves, and 1 piece string cheese.
Drizzle finished kebabs evenly with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.

name: Mixed Fruit Salad
