attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024933/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mixed-fruit-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can mandarin oranges in light syrup (11 ounce can - drained)
1 can fruit cocktail (15 ounce can - drained)
1 can pineapple chunks (20 ounce can - drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together.
Cover and chill until ready to serve.
Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Mixed Grain Bread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042034/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mixed-grain-bread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix cornmeal, brown sugar, salt and oil with boiling water, cool to lukewarm (105 to 115 degrees F).
Dissolve yeast in 1/4 cup warm water; stir into cornmeal mixture. Add whole wheat and rye flours and mix well. Stir in enough all purpose flour to make dough stiff enough to knead.
Turn dough onto lightly floured surface. Knead until smooth and elastic, about 5 to 10 minutes.
Place dough in lightly oiled bowl, turning oil top. Cover with clean towel; let rise in warm place until double, about 1 hour.

Punch dough down; turn onto clean surface. Cover with clean towel; let rest 10 minutes. Shape dough and place in greased 9x5-inch pan. Cover with clean towel; let rise until almost double, about 1 hour.

Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Bake 35 to 45 minutes or until bread sounds hollow when tapped. Cover with aluminum foil during baking if bread is browning too quickly. Remove bread from pan and cool on wire rack.

name: Mock Southern Sweet Potato Pie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021207/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mock-southern-sweet-potato-pie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups cooked sweet potatoes, skin removed and mashed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Combine the flour and sugar in a bowl.
Add milk and oil to the flour mixture.
Stir with fork until well mixed and then form pastry into a smooth ball with your hands.
Roll the ball between two 12-inch squares of waxed paper using short, brisk strokes until pastry reaches edge of paper.
Peel off top paper and invert crust into pie plate.
Combine sugars, salt, spices, and eggs.
Add milk and vanilla. Stir.
Add sweet potatoes and mix well.
Pour mixture into pie shell.
Bake in preheated oven for 60 minutes or until crust is golden brown.
Cool and cut into 16 slices.
Crust: Filling:

name: Mousse a la Banana
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022300/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mousse-la-banana
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place milk, sugar, vanilla, and banana in blender. Process 15 seconds at high speed until smooth.
Pour mixture into a small bowl; fold in yogurt. Chill. Spoon into four dessert dishes; garnish each with two banana slices just before serving.

name: Mouth-Watering Oven-Fried Fish
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021406/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mouth-watering-oven-fried-fish
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 pounds cod fish fillets (or other white fish)
1/2 cup corn flakes, crumbled (or regular breadcrumbs)
1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 475 degrees F.
Clean and rinse fish. Wipe fillets with lemon juice and pat dry.
Combine buttermilk, garlic, and hot sauce in a medium bowl.
Combine pepper, salt, and onion powder with crumbs and place on plate.
Let fillets sit briefly in milk. Remove and coat fillets on both sides with seasoned crumbs. Let stand briefly until coating sticks to each side of fish.
Arrange on lightly oiled shallow baking dish.
Bake for 20 minutes on middle rack without turning.
Cut into 6 pieces. Serve with fresh lemon wedges.

name: Mozz Totz
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042936/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mozz-totz
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Line a baking sheet with foil and spray lightly with cooking spray.
Remove cheese from package and cut into bite size pieces.
In a small non-stick skillet mix oregano and basil with breadcrumbs.
Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally until crumbs are lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Dip each piece of cheese in milk and then into toasted bread crumbs, coating completely.
Place on baking sheet about 1 1/2-inches apart.
Spray string cheese lightly with non-stick cooking spray.
Bake 5 to 6 minutes or until heated through. (Cheese may melt slightly and lose shape. Simply press it back into place).
Dip in warmed marinara sauce and enjoy.

name: Mozzarella Chicken with Garlic Spinach
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040018/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mozzarella-chicken-garlic-spinach
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 small chicken breast halves, skin and bone removed
8 ounces part skim mozzarella cheese, shredded
1 tablespoon canola oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Place chicken between 2 sheets of plastic wrap; pound chicken to 1/4 inch thick.
Coat chicken with breadcrumbs and place on foil-covered baking sheet. Discard remaining breadcrumbs. Bake 10 minutes.
Top chicken with cheese; bake 4 to 5 minutes until cheese is melted and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 °F.
Meanwhile, heat oil in a large skillet on medium heat. Add garlic and stir 1 minute.
Add half the spinach and cook 1 minute.
Add remaining spinach. Cook until wilted, turning occasionally. Serve with chicken.

name: Muffins (from Better Baking Mix)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032327/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/muffins-better-baking-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Grease 12-cup muffin pan.
Mix the Better Baking Mix and sugar in a bowl.
Beat the egg with a fork.
Add egg, oil, and water to dry ingredients. Stir just until all ingredients are wet.
Spoon into the prepared muffin pan.

name: Mushroom Barley Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042729/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mushroom-barley-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
2 medium carrots, peeled and sliced thin

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in large soup pot over high heat. Sauté onion, celery, carrots, and mushrooms until golden, about 4 minutes.
Add the rest of the ingredients except for the parsley and bring to a boil.
Lower heat to a simmer and cook until the barley is tender, about 20 minutes.
Sprinkle parsley on top of soup and serve hot.

name: Mushroom Beef Sloppy Joes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034828/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mushroom-beef-sloppy-joes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Chop mushrooms to approximate size and texture of cooked ground beef.
Heat a sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef and mushrooms, and cook.
Sauté until ground beef is done.
Remove mushroom-beef mixture from pan.
Add onions and garlic to pan; cook until golden.
Return mushroom-beef mixture to pan, along with remaining ingredients.
Simmer about 10 minutes; remove from heat.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of non-fat milk and a slice of watermelon.

name: Mushroom Steak Fajitas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042321/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/mushroom-steak-fajitas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 12 ounces sirloin or other boneless steak (about 3/4-inch thick)
1 cup green bell pepper, sliced into strips
1 medium red bell pepper, sliced into strips
1 medium yellow bell pepper, sliced into strips

steps: Slice beef across the grain into 1/4-inch strips. Place in a medium bowl with 1/2 tablespoon fiesta lime seasoning; toss to coat.
Place mushrooms, peppers, and onion and remaining fiesta lime seasoning in a large bowl; toss to coat.
Heat oil in large, non-stick skillet. Add beef strips; cook about 3 to 4 minutes. Remove from skillet.
Place coated vegetables in skillet and sauté until vegetables are slightly tender, about 5 to 8 minutes.
Add beef back to skillet and sauté mixture 1 to 2 more minutes.
Assemble fajitas by dividing beef-vegetable mixture evenly on each tortilla, top with remaining ingredients and roll up.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of non-fat milk and side of mango chunks.

name: Naan
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035219/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/naan
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 packet of active dry yeast (1/4 ounce)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, dissolve yeast in warm water and let stand about 10 minutes, or until frothy.
Stir in sugar, milk, egg, salt, and enough flour to make a soft dough.
Knead for 6 - 8 minutes on a lightly floured surface or until smooth.
Let it rise 1 hour until the dough has doubled in volume.
Punch down dough and knead in garlic.
Pinch off small handfuls of dough about the size of a golf ball.
Roll into balls and place on a tray.
Cover with a towel and allow to rise until doubled in size, about 30 minutes.
During the second rising, preheat grill to high heat.
At grill side, roll one ball of dough out into a thin circle.
Lightly oil grill. Place dough on grill and cook for 2 - 3 minutes or until puffy and lightly browned.
Brush uncooked side with butter and turn over.
Brush cooked side with butter and cook until browned, another 2 to 4 minutes.
Remove from grill and continue the process until all the naan has been prepared.

name: Neopolitan Tuna Fettuccine
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031526/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/neopolitan-tuna-fettuccine
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can no salt added diced tomatoes (14.5 oz. can)
5 ounces canned tuna packed in water, drained
1/4 cup sliced ripe olives, drained (or 1 2.2-ounce can)
Salt and ground pepper to taste

steps: Cook fettuccine as label directs. Reserve 1 cup cooking liquid; drain.

Meanwhile, in 10-inch skillet over medium heat, in hot oil, cook onion and garlic, about 5 minutes until just softened. Add diced tomatoes and capers; simmer 5 minutes. Add tuna, olives, salt, and pepper to taste.
Toss fettuccine with tuna mixture to mix well. Serve immediately. If necessary, add reserved cooking liquid.

name: New Orleans Red Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033250/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/new-orleans-red-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pick through beans to remove bad beans; rinse thoroughly.

In a large pot combine beans, water, onion, celery, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil; reduce heat. Cover and cook over low heat for about 1-1/2 hours until beans are tender. Stir. Mash beans against side of pan.
Add green pepper, garlic, parsley, thyme, salt, and black pepper. Cook, uncovered, over low heat until creamy (about 30 minutes). Remove bay leaves.
Serve with hot cooked brown rice, if desired.

name: No Bake Breakfast Cookies
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040610/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/no-bake-breakfast-cookies
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat honey and peanut butter in a medium saucepan over low heat. Stir until blended.
Remove from heat. Stir in dry milk.
Fold in cereal and raisins. Drop by heaping tablespoons onto waxed paper to form mounds.
Cool to room temperature. Store in refrigerator.

notes.text: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: No-Bake Cookies
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040612/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/no-bake-cookies
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In large sauce pan, bring the first six ingredients to a full, rolling boil for 1 minute, stirring as needed.
Remove from heat. Add oats, dry milk, raisins, and vanilla to boiled mixture.
Mix well.
Drop by tablespoons onto waxed paper and let stand until cool, about 15 to 20 minutes.

name: Oat Bran Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050450/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/oat-bran-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons raisins, dates, or other dried fruit

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 degrees F.
In a large bowl, mix the first four dry ingredients. Set aside.
In another bowl, mix the egg with orange juice, milk, and oil.
In small bowl, mix fruit and blend with dry ingredients.
Add the liquid ingredients to the dry until it is moist.
Spray muffin tin with a non-stick coating. Pour batter into muffin tins.
Bake for 15 to 17 minutes. Remove muffins from pan after 10 minutes. Cool on a rack. Freeze muffins for later use.

name: Oat Snack Cakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043834/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/oat-snack-cakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Mix together oatmeal, flour, sugar, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon in a large bowl.
Cut in margarine until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Combine oil, vanilla, egg whites, and water. Stir into dry ingredients and add raisins, mixing only until it holds together.
Wash hands thoroughly, then dip in cornmeal or flour. Pinch off pieces of dough and form into balls about 1 inch in diameter.
Place balls on baking pan (sprayed with non-stick cooking spray) and press out slightly to about 1/4-inch in thickness.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until lightly browned. Cool, then store in an airtight container.

name: Oatmeal Bread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032916/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/oatmeal-bread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup warm water (105 to 115 degrees F)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine rolled oats and salt in a large mixing bowl. Stir in boiling water; cool to lukewarm (105 to 115 degrees F).
Dissolve yeast in 1/4 cup warm water in small bowl.
Add yeast water, molasses, and oil to cooled oatmeal mixture. Stir in whole wheat flour and 1 cup all-purpose flour. Add additional all-purpose flour to make a dough stiff enough to knead.
Knead dough on lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic, about 5 minutes.
Place dough in lightly oiled bowl, turning to oil top. Cover with clean towel; let rise in warm place until double, about 1 hour.
Punch dough down; turn onto clean surface. Shape dough and place in greased 9x5 inch pan. Cover with clean towel; let rise in a warm place until almost double, about 1 hour.

Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Bake 50 minutes or until bread sounds hollow when tapped. Cover with aluminum foil during baking if bread is browning too quickly. Remove bread from pan and cool on wire rack.

name: Oatmeal Raisin Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032231/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/oatmeal-raisin-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon margarine or butter, to grease the muffin cups

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
Put the milk, egg, and oil in a small mixing bowl. Slowly stir them together.
In a large mixing bowl, mix the flour, oatmeal, sugar, baking powder, salt, and raisins. Stir until they are mixed.
Pour the milk-egg-oil mix into the large bowl with the dry ingredients.
Stir until the dry ingredients are barely moistened. Do not over-mix (the batter should be lumpy).
Grease each cup in the muffin pans with some margarine or butter.
Spoon the batter into the cups in each muffin pan, until each cup is half-full with batter.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, or until the muffins are golden brown.

name: Okra and Greens
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034313/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/okra-and-greens
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons corn oil (or cooking oil of choice)
4 chili peppers, finely chopped and crushed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large heavy pan sauté onions in oil until golden brown.
Add remaining ingredients, except for lemon juice. Simmer over low heat, covered, until greens are tender.
Squeeze on lemon juice before serving.

notes.text: You can substitute about 2 cups of cut/frozen okra in place of whole okra.

name: Old Fashioned Bread Pudding
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021029/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/old-fashioned-bread-pudding
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spread one side of bread with margarine or butter. Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Cut into 1-inch cubes.
In lightly sprayed casserole dish, combine bread, sugar, and raisins. Then follow microwave or oven method below.
In bowl, blend eggs, milk, salt and vanilla. Pour liquid over bread mixture; lightly blend.
Cover, microwave on HIGH for 5 minutes. Turn dish 1/4 turn. Microwave on HIGH for 3-5 minutes longer (pudding is done when edges are firm and center is almost set).
Let sit covered for 10 minutes before serving. Serve warm or cold. Refrigerate leftovers.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. In bowl, blend eggs, 2 cups milk (instead of 1 1/2 cups for microwaving), salt, and vanilla. Pour liquid over bread mixture; lightly blend.
Bake uncovered for 1 hour (pudding is done when a table knife inserted in the pudding comes out clean).
Serve warm or cold. Refrigerate leftovers.
Microwave method: Oven method:

name: Old Fashioned Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032931/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/old-fashioned-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toast bread cubes and set aside for later use.
Melt margarine or butter in medium size fry pan.
Add celery and onion; cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add parsley, mushrooms, seasonings, and broth. Cook for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and add the toasted bread cubes. Cover and let stand 10 minutes. Serve immediately.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: One-Dish Roasted Potatoes and Apples with Chicken Sausage
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021936/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/one-dish-roasted-potatoes-and-apples-chicken-sausage
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 red potatoes or your favorite potato variety (about 1 pound)
2 red apples (Fuji, Pink Lady, Honeycrisp, Gala, etc.)

steps: Preheat oven to 425 °F.
Cut potatoes into chunks, place in 2-quart baking dish.
Drizzle with canola oil. Toss to coat.
Roast potatoes in oven for about 20 minutes.
While potatoes are roasting, cut apples and onions into chunks, and sausage into 1/2-inch slices.
Remove baking dish from oven and reduce heat to 375 °F. Add all remaining ingredients to baking dish and toss.
Return baking dish to oven and roast an additional 30 minutes until apples and potatoes are tender.

name: One Pan Potatoes & Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021122/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/one-pan-potatoes-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 16 ounces chicken breasts, boned and skinned
2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 can (15.2 ounces) low-sodium whole kernel corn, drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut potatoes into 3/4 in cubes.

Microwave potatoes for 8-10 minutes until tender OR cook potatoes on the stovetop. To cook on the stovetop, place potatoes in water, bring to a boil and then reduce heat to a simmer until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes. Drain potatoes.
Cut chicken into 3/4-inch cubes
In a large skillet, brown chicken in oil on high for 5 minutes.
Add potatoes; cook until potatoes are lightly browned.
Add salsa and corn. Cook until heated through.

name: One Pan Spaghetti
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020830/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/one-pan-spaghetti
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown meat and onions in a large skillet over medium-high heat (300 degrees F in an electric skillet). Drain fat.
Stir in water, tomato sauce, sugar, and spices; bring to a boil.
Add spaghetti, cover pan, and simmer 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often to prevent sticking.
When spaghetti is tender, top with grated cheese.
Refrigerate leftovers with in 2 hours.

notes.text: For 16 ounces of broken spaghetti noodles, use about 1/3 of a one pound box.

name: One Pan Taco Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031454/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/one-pan-taco-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound 85% lean ground turkey (or lean ground beef)
2 cans (10 ounces each) tomatoes and green chiles

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet or pot, brown ground turkey and cook onion. When done, use paper towel to soak up any grease.
Add remaining ingredients, except cheese, and mix together.
Heat until very hot.
Top with cheese before serving.

notes.text: Low-fat cheddar cheese used for nutritional analysis and costing.

name: Orange and Honey Glazed Brussel Sprouts
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032323/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/orange-and-honey-glazed-brussel-sprouts
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 5 cups Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved (about 1 pound)
2 tablespoons olive oil or oil of choice

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 450ºF with a large, rimmed baking sheet placed on the middle rack.
Add Brussels sprouts to a large bowl, and toss with oil, salt and pepper.
Remove baking sheet from oven, and carefully arrange Brussels sprouts cut side down on the sheet. Return to oven, and roast until golden, about 20 minutes, flipping halfway through.
While the sprouts are baking, in a small saucepan over medium-high heat, combine orange juice, apple cider vinegar, honey and chili paste.
Bring to a boil and cook for 5 to 10 minutes, until reduced and syrupy. Remove from heat and allow to cool slightly.
Place sauce in a large bowl and add roasted Brussels sprouts. Toss to combine. Transfer to a serving plate and top with lemon zest.

notes.text: You may substitute 1/2 teaspoon chili powder for 1 teaspoon chili paste.

name: Orange Banana Frosty
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021109/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/orange-banana-frosty
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all ingredients in a blender and mix well.
Add more liquid if you want the drink thinner.

name: Orange Cow
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043347/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/orange-cow
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place all ingredients in blender or food processor.
Secure lid and blend until smooth. Serve immediately.

notes.text: Substitute 1 cup milk and 1 cup water for 2 cups water and 1/3 cup nonfat dry milk.

name: Orange Delight Juice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034006/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/orange-delight-juice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water
Blend at high speed in blender until frothy.

notes.text: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Orange Glazed Skinless Chicken Wings
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214846/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/orange-glazed-skinless-chicken-wings
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse chicken wings and dry on paper toweling. Tuck the wing tip under the larger joint to form a triangle.
Heat butter in skillet (200 degrees F on temperature-controlled gas burner).
Sprinkle wings with seasoned salt and place in heated butter. Sauté on temperature-controlled gas burner (325 degrees F) until evenly brown on both sides, about 20 minutes.
Spread with orange marmalade, continuing to sauté while basting frequently for another 20 minutes.
Remove from skillet. Serve hot.
Hold at serving temperature on automatic burner or in 'Keep-Warm' oven set at 170 degrees F. They will be glazed and "sticky" good.

notes.text: Leg pieces or whole chicken may be prepared this way and served as an entrée.

name: Orange Honeyed Acorn Squash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032956/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/orange-honeyed-acorn-squash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Cut squash in half. Remove seeds and place halves in shallow baking pan.
Combine orange juice and honey. Mix well. Put some of the orange juice/honey mixture in each squash cavity.
Add 1 tablespoon of the margarine to each squash half. Sprinkle with nutmeg, if desired.
Cover pan with aluminum foil to keep steam in and speed cooking.
Bake 30 minutes. Remove foil and continue baking 30 minutes more, or until squash is tender.

notes.text: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Orange Pork Chops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033136/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/orange-pork-chops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
In a medium skillet, brown pork chops in a small amount of oil.
Cut sweet potato into 1/2-inch slices.
Place meat and sweet potato slices in a baking dish and top with orange slices; sprinkle with seasonings if desired.
Cover and bake for 1 hour until meat is tender.
Cook pork to 145 degrees F.

name: Oven-Baked Potato Pancakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035253/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/oven-baked-potato-pancakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
3 tablespoons whole wheat flour (or all-purpose flour)
2 large russet potatoes (or Yukon Gold potatoes)
applesauce and yogurt (plain low-fat or Greek) (optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 425 °F. Lightly oil the baking sheets by spreading the oil around with your clean hand or a paper towel.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt in a small bowl.
Use the large holes on your grater to grate the potato, then grate the onion too.
Put the potato and onion mixture in the colander inside the sink. Using a paper towel, press the potato mixture down to squeeze out and blot up some of the extra moisture. Stir it and blot again.
Put the potato mixture in the large bowl, add the egg, and stir well. Add the flour mixture and stir it very well.

Use a spoon or your fingers to pluck a clump of the potato mixture from the bowl and spread it into a round, flat nest on the oiled baking sheet: it should make a circle that's about 3 inches wide and 1/4 inch thick. Repeat to fill the sheet. (You don't need to leave space between them.)
Bake until the bottoms are deeply golden, 15 to 20 minutes, then turn the pancakes over and put them back in the over for 10 more minutes.
Serve the latkes with applesauce and yogurt (optional).

notes.text: These Hanukkah favorites are traditionally fried in oil to celebrate the oil of the eight nights of lights (like a menorah, which is a special Hanukkah candle holder, does). Our potato pancakes are actually oven-baked, which makes them easier, crunchier, and healthier.

name: Oven Baked Sweet Potato Fries
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045652/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/oven-baked-sweet-potato-fries
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and peel sweet potatoes. Cut into 1/4-inch slices.
In a large bowl, toss slices in olive oil until coated. Sprinkle with salt and pepper if desired.
Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Bake at 425 degrees F until tender and golden brown (about 20 minutes), turning occasionally to brown evenly.

name: Oven Fried Fish
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031858/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/oven-fried-fish
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound tilapia fillets, fresh or thawed (4 fillets)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
In a small bowl, add egg, salt (if desired), and pepper and beat together.
Place the bread crumbs in a separate bowl. Dip fish fillets in the egg mixture, then dip in the bread crumbs to coat.
Melt butter in a shallow 9x13 inch baking pan for 1 minute in the oven. Tilt pan to coat with butter.
Arrange fish fillets in the pan.
Bake uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, until fish flakes easily with a fork. Serve topped with lime or lemon slices (optional).

notes.text: Instead of bread crumbs, 1/2 cup crushed, unsweetened cereal or 1/2 cup crushed saltine crackers can be used.

name: Oven-Fried Yucca
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215125/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/oven-fried-yucca
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound yucca (cassava) peeled and cut into 3-inch sections (or 1 pound peeled frozen yucca)
1 spray non-stick cooking spray, as needed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot, combine the yucca with enough cold water to cover it by 1 inch. Bring the water to a boil and slowly simmer the yucca for 20 to 30 minutes, or until it is tender.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Transfer the yucca with a slotted spoon to a cutting board. Let it cool and cut it lengthwise into 3/4-inch wide wedges, discarding the thin woody core.

Spray cookie sheet with the nonstick cooking oil spray. Spread yucca wedges on cookie sheet and spray wedges with cooking oil spray. Cover with foil paper and bake for 8 minutes. Uncover and return to oven to bake for an additional 7 minutes.

name: Oven Roasted Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041909/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/oven-roasted-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons Italian dressing, low-fat (or olive oil)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
If chicken is frozen, thaw in the refrigerator 24 hours before cooking.
Place chicken on a pan or plate while thawing in the refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Remove necks and giblets from chicken cavity, if present before cooking. Reserve for another use.
Place chicken, breast side up, in a roasting pan.
Brush chicken skin with Italian dressing and sprinkle with garlic salt.
Stuff lemon or orange into chicken cavity.
Roast 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours or until meat thermometer inserted into chicken thigh registers 165 degrees F.
Let chicken set for 15 minutes after removing from the oven before carving.

name: Oven-Roasted Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031958/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/oven-roasted-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
3 cups fresh vegetables (potatoes, broccoli, carrots, cauliflower, or red peppers)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F.
In a small bowl, mix the oil, lemon juice, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Wash, peel, and cut the fresh vegetables to get 3 cups cut-up vegetables.
Spread vegetables on baking sheet pan.
Pour the oil mixture over the vegetables and mix together.
Bake for 20 minutes. Stir after the first 10 minutes of baking.
Serve the vegetables while they are still hot.

name: Overnight Oatmeal
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032904/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/overnight-oatmeal
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup dried fruit (raisins, cranberries, or apricots)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all ingredients in a cooking pot and cover. Let sit overnight in refrigerator.

In the morning, put on a stove burner and cook on medium heat until simmering, then turn on low and heat for 10 to 15 minutes more or less depending on type of oats -- quick (5 minutes), regular, or steel cut.
Serve warm with a little milk (or milk alternative), a drizzle of maple syrup, and a side of fresh fruit, if desired.

notes.text: 1/2 cup raisins and 1/4 cup walnuts used in nutrient analysis and costing.

name: Overnight Oatmeal with Berries
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032656/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/overnight-oatmeal-berries
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup low-fat milk (or less for thicker oatmeal)

steps: Combine milk, Greek yogurt, honey, cinnamon, and vanilla extract in a container or jar with a lid.
Add oats and mix well.
Top with raspberries or gently fold into oat mixture.
Cover and refrigerate 8 hours to overnight.
Enjoy cold, or heat as desired.

notes.text: Frozen blueberries or strawberries may be used in place of raspberries.

name: Pan Roasted Tilapia with Tomatillo Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031849/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pan-roasted-tilapia-tomatillo-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 serrano or other chiles, finely chopped
4 - 4oz tilapia fillets (patted dry with a paper towel)

steps: Preheat the oven to 450 °F.
To prepare the tomatillos, peel back the husk from the smooth green tomatillo skin. Rinse the tomatillos with warm water and cut into quarters.

Place the husked tomatillos, onion, chilies, garlic, and 1 teaspoon oil in the baking pan, stir well and transfer to the oven. Roast about 20 minutes until the tomatillos are soft and dark green. Set aside to cool.
Transfer the mixture to the blender; add the salt, lime juice, and cilantro. Purée.
Place the skillet on the stove over high heat and when it is hot, carefully add 2 teaspoons oil.
Put the tilapia fillets in the pan, waiting about 30 seconds between additions. Cook about 5 to 6 minutes, until golden brown on both sides.
Transfer the tilapia to the serving plate and top with generous amounts of salsa. Serve right away.
To make the tomatillo salsa: To cook the tilapia:

notes.text: Canned tomatillo salsa can be used instead of fresh. Tilapia can be substituted with any inexpensive white fish.

name: Pancakes (from Better Baking Mix)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032834/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pancakes-better-baking-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all the ingredients in a bowl.
Stir just enough to moisten dry ingredients.

Preheat skillet on medium-high heat. The skillet is ready when drops of water "dance" on the dry surface. Add a teaspoon of vegetable oil or use cooking oil spray. For each pancake, pour 3 to 4 tablespoons of batter onto hot skillet.
Cook slowly until the surface is covered with bubbles. Turn and cook until second side is lightly browned.

notes.text: Try applesauce or other fruit on pancakes instead of syrup.

name: Parmesan Chive Biscuits
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050010/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/parmesan-chive-biscuits
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl.
Stir together to mix well. Do not over mix.
Turn out onto a floured board. Roll to a 1-inch thick square.
Cut into 12 squares. Bake on a cookie sheet, spaced slightly apart, in a 400 degrees F oven for 12 to 15 minutes.

name: Parmesan Peas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022322/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/parmesan-peas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 teaspoons unsalted butter (or cooking oil of your choice)
2 cans of reduced-sodium peas, drained and rinsed (15 ounce cans or 16 ounces frozen peas)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat butter in a medium skillet over medium heat.
Add peas and cook 2 to 3 minutes or until peas are heated through.
Add lemon juice and pepper and mix well. Sprinkle with parmesan cheese and serve warm.

name: Parsley, Almond, and Lemon Pesto
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215033/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/parsley-almond-and-lemon-pesto
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a food processor, combine the almonds, cheese, parsley, and lemon juice.
Slowly pour in oil and mix it into the rest of the ingredients.
Season with salt and pepper, if using.

name: Parsnip Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214857/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/parsnip-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cloves garlic, chopped (or 3/4 teaspoon garlic powder)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, salt, and pepper; cook for1 minute.
Stir in the parsnips, potato, broth, and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer for 20 minutes or until the parsnips and potatoes are soft.
Stir in the margarine or butter and let the soup sit uncovered for 5 minutes.
Purée the soup in batches in a blender, using the manufacturer's directions for puréeing hot liquids.
Heat the soup before serving, stirring in water if it seems too thick.

name: Party-Time Pasta
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033206/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/party-time-pasta
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups frozen vegetables such as carrots, broccoli, and cauliflower, thawed
1/2 cup fresh parsley, chopped (or 2 tablespoons dried parsley)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat a large nonstick pan over medium heat. Add ground turkey and paprika. Cook and stir until meat is brown and no longer pink, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomatoes, chicken broth and pasta. Bring mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer until pasta is almost tender, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Remove lid. Place vegetables on top of pasta. Replace lid. Cook until vegetables are tender, about 5 minutes.
Prepare the Tasty Topping. Mix parsley, bread crumbs and Parmesan cheese. Sprinkle over vegetables in skillet. Cover and let sit for 3 minutes before serving.

name: Passover Rhubarb Cobbler
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214848/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/passover-rhubarb-cobbler
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a shallow 2-quart baking dish, combine 1 1/4 cups sugar and cornstarch*. Add rhubarb, raspberries, and lemon juice - mixing gently but thoroughly.
Meanwhile, in a food processor or a bowl, whirl or rub together with your fingers the matzo meal, the remaining 1/2 cup sugar, margarine, and nutmeg to create fine crumbs.
Squeeze matzo mixture to compact into lumps, then crumble over rhubarb mixture.
Baked in oven at 375 degrees F until cobbler is bubbling in center and top is golden brown, about 1 hour. Let cool 15 minutes.
Spoon cobbler into bowls and top with sorbet or whipped cream (optional).
*If you do not wish to eat cornstarch feel free to substitute instant tapioca pudding in equal amounts.

name: Pasta Bolognese
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033829/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pasta-bolognese
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 yellow onion, chopped into 1/4 inch pieces
2 14.5-ounce cans no salt added crushed or diced tomatoes (including liquid)
1/4 cup no salt added tomato paste

steps: Put skillet on the stove over medium heat and when it is hot, add oil.
Add carrot, celery, and onion and cook about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables begin to brown.

Raise the heat to high. Pinch off tablespoon-sized pieces of the beef and add a few at a time, stirring well between additions. Cook, breaking the meat apart until it is no longer raw, starts to give off liquid, and no longer clumps together, about 10 minutes.
Add the water, tomatoes, and tomato paste, stirring well. Cook about 10 minutes until the sauce begins to thicken.
Slowly stir in the milk, a little bit at a time. Turn the heat down to low and cook 45 minutes until all the liquid has been absorbed.
Fill a large pot halfway with water. Bring it to a boil over high heat.
Add the pasta and about 12 minutes cook until just tender.
Drain the pasta and divide into 4 bowls.
Top each bowl with about 3/4 cup Bolognese and sprinkle with 1 tablespoon Parmesan cheese.
Serve right away.
To make the Bolognese sauce: To make the pasta:

name: Pasta with Chickpeas, Tomato, and Spinach
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044332/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pasta-chickpeas-tomato-and-spinach
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 small yellow onion, chopped into 1/4 pieces
8 ounces whole wheat pasta (such as rotini or shells)
1 16-ounce can low sodium chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1 14.5-ounce can no salt added diced tomatoes (including the liquid)

steps: To cook the pasta, fill a pot with water and bring to a boil over high heat. When the water is boiling, add the pasta and cook until just tender, about 12 minutes. Just before draining, reserve 1 1/2 cups of the pasta water. Drain the pasta and set aside.

While the pasta is cooking, prepare the sauce: Put a skillet on the stove over medium-low heat and when it is hot, add the oil. Add the garlic, onion, carrots, celery, and rosemary and cook until the garlic is golden, about 10 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and using a fork, lightly mash half of them. Add the reserved pasta water and tomatoes and cook 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and spinach to the skillet mixture and cook until the spinach is tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed by the pasta, about 10 minutes. Add the red pepper flakes, if desired.
Mix well and serve immediately, garnished with Parmesan cheese.

notes.text: Kale can be used instead of spinach.

name: Pasta Frittata with Peas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215109/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pasta-frittata-peas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 ounces whole grain spaghetti, regular or thin
1 cup frozen peas, thawed (or 1 cup chopped tomatoes)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain and place in a 9-inch pie plate that has been sprayed with nonstick cooking spray.
Combine eggs, seasonings, cheese, and peas. Spread the egg mixture over the top of the spaghetti so the mixture covers the frittata and some of it sinks between the spaghetti strands.
Bake for 20 minutes or until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean. Let frittata stand 5 minutes before serving.
Tomato Variation: Instead of mixing 1 cup of peas with the egg, seasonings, and cheese mixture, sprinkle the chopped tomatoes evenly over the top of the frittata before putting it in the oven.

notes.text: Salt omitted from nutrition analysis.

name: Pasta with Greens, Beans, and Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033844/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pasta-greens-beans-and-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
2 cups cooked chicken cubes (or 3 chicken sausages, chopped)
6 cups spinach, chopped (or 1 bunch Swiss chard)
1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium cannellini beans, rinsed and drained (can also use great northern or navy beans)
2 cups low-sodium chicken broth (or vegetable broth)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook the pasta according to directions on box, and drain.
On medium heat, add vegetable oil and onion to a large pan.
Cook for 5 minutes, add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Stir in chopped chicken and cook until heated through.
Add spinach (or chard), beans, chicken or vegetable stock, and Italian seasoning.
Add in cooked pasta and stir to combine.
Cook for 5 minutes, until pasta is heated through.
Add salt and pepper, to taste (optional), and garnish with Parmesan cheese before serving (optional).

name: Pasta Primavera
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033047/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pasta-primavera
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook noodles according to package directions.
While noodles are cooking, heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add vegetables and sauté until tender; stir constantly.
Add tomato and sauté 2 more minutes.
Toss vegetables with noodles and margarine.
Add seasonings; sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.

name: Pasta Primavera Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042624/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pasta-primavera-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Rinse in cold water to stop cooking and prevent sticking. Drain.
Cook vegetables until just tender. Drain and cool.
Combine cold pasta, vegetables, and salad dressing.
Top with sliced eggs and cheese.
Refrigerate until time to serve.

notes.text: Low-fat cheddar cheese used for nutrition analysis and costing.

name: Pasta Primavera in Spaghetti Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041412/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pasta-primavera-spaghetti-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare pasta according to package directions. Add frozen vegetables during the last 5 minutes of cooking time.
Drain pasta and vegetables and set aside.
Bring the spaghetti sauce to a boil over medium heat.
Stir in the pasta and vegetables.
Top with grated Parmesan cheese.

notes.text: May substitute any type of pasta for the rotini. Do not overcook the pasta and vegetables. Maybe substitute other types of canned or bottled Italian sauces.

name: Pasta Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043616/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pasta-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Drain and place in large bowl or pan.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix well.
Cool in refrigerator before serving.

name: Pasta Salad with Herb Vinaigrette
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025450/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pasta-salad-herb-vinaigrette
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 ounces uncooked whole wheat pasta, cooked, drained

steps: Whisk dressing ingredients in a small bowl until blended.
Combine pasta, broccoli, tomato, and carrot in a large bowl; toss. Pour dressing over pasta mixture; toss until evenly coated. Add eggs; toss briefly.
Refrigerate, covered, at least 4 hours to blend flavors.

notes.text: For a different flavor or to reduce cost, use any other vinegar you have on hand for the dressing.

name: Pasta Vegetable Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045434/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pasta-vegetable-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients in a medium-sized bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Mix again before serving.
Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Pasta with Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214905/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pasta-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Chop tomatoes and mix with all the remaining ingredients in a large bowl.
Let the mixture stand at room temperature for about 20 minutes. Toss with cooked pasta and top with grated cheese.

notes.text: Add a can of white or black beans, drained, for extra protein before tossing with pasta. Feel free to add other vegetables that you have on hand. Salt and pepper not included in analysis.

name: Pea Guacamole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032009/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pea-guacamole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (4 ounces) diced green chilies, drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mash peas until smooth.
Add the lime juice, tomato, onion, green chilies, cilantro, garlic, salt (if using), and black pepper. Mix well.
Serve with an assortment of raw vegetables and whole-grain tortilla chips.

name: Pea Pesto
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043440/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pea-pesto
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup frozen peas (can also use fresh or canned)
1 cup fresh spinach (or can use frozen or canned)
1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
For the pesto, add peas, Parmesan cheese, basil, spinach, walnuts and garlic into a food processor or blender.
Add in water, oil, salt and pepper. Blend until the ingredients are combined to form a thick sauce.
Place pesto in an airtight container.
Refrigerate until needed.

name: Peach Apple Crisp
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021745/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peach-apple-crisp
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/3 cans (20 ounces total) peaches, in light syrup, drained and sliced
2 medium tart apples, peeled and sliced

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Lightly grease 9x9x2-inch casserole dish.
Combine peaches, apples, vanilla, and cinnamon in a bowl. Toss well and spread evenly in greased casserole dish.
Combine flour and sugar in small bowl. Cut in margarine with two knives until the mixture resembles coarse meal.
Sprinkle flour mixture evenly over fruit.
Bake until lightly browned and bubbly, about 20 minutes.

name: Peach Cooler
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034507/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peach-cooler
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup canned peaches packed in juice, drained (or1 cup of sliced fresh peaches)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put the ingredients in a blender. Blend well.
Sprinkle with nutmeg if you like.
Serve cold.

name: Peach Crisp
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033314/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peach-crisp
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Slice the peaches.
Spread the peach slices on the bottom of a 9x9-inch baking pan.
Melt the margarine in a saucepan.
In a small bowl, mix everything but the peaches. Stir until the mix is well blended.
Sprinkle the oat mix on top of the peaches.
Bake for 20 minutes.

notes.text: Serve the peach crisp either hot or cold. To remove the peach fuzz, you can rub the washed peach gently with a paper towel.

name: Peach Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042031/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peach-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 15-ounce cans of peaches, juice packed (with liquid)

steps: Drain peaches and reserve liquid. Pour peaches into a medium saucepan with cinnamon.
Cook on low to medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes.
Mash to desired consistency with either a potato masher or wooden spoon. Add reserved peach liquid as needed.

name: Peachy Peanut Butter Pita Pockets
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033229/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peachy-peanut-butter-pita-pockets
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup low-fat peanut butter (smooth or chunky)
1/2 medium apple, cored and thinly sliced

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut pitas in half to make 4 pockets and warm in the microwave for about 10 seconds to make them more flexible.
Carefully open each pocket and spread a thin layer of peanut butter on the inside walls.
Fill with a combination of apple, banana, and peach slices. Serve at room temperature.

name: Peachy Pops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043351/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peachy-pops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Use a knife to remove the skin and chop the peaches.
Spoon peaches into each of the 6 paper cups.
Place yogurt in a medium mixing bowl.
Slowly pour and stir the orange juice into the yogurt. Mix well.
Pour some of the juice and yogurt mix into each cup to cover the peaches.
Place a spoon in the center of each cup.
Cut 6 squares of aluminum foil big enough to cover the tops of cups. Stab each spoon handle through each piece of foil. The foil will hold the spoon in the center of the cup.
Place cups in the freezer for at least 4 hours.
Just before serving, peel the paper cups away from the pops to eat.

name: Peanut Butter and Apple Wraps
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033736/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peanut-butter-and-apple-wraps
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 medium apple, sliced (suggest Red Delicious apple)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lay tortilla flat and spread peanut butter over 2/3 of the tortilla leaving edges at sides
Sprinkle 2 tablespoons granola over peanut butter.
Cut apple slices into small chunks and place them on top of the granola.
Fold over the edges of the tortilla and roll up "burrito style."
Eat and Enjoy.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Breakfast Shake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035354/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peanut-butter-banana-breakfast-shake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth and creamy.
Pour into a tall glass and garnish with a sprinkle of cocoa powder, if desired.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Smoothie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041819/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peanut-butter-banana-smoothie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Peel bananas, chop into small pieces and place in freezer until hard.
Gather all ingredients and put all ingredients in a blender.
Blend on high until smooth.
Pour into 2 glasses. Serve right away.

notes.text: Watch how to make this kid-friendly recipe on YouTube.

name: Peanut Butter Bananas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045717/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peanut-butter-bananas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel bananas. Spread the entire outside of each banana with peanut butter.
Roll the bananas in crushed nuts, sprinkles or other items.
Cut the bananas in one inch slices.
Store in the refrigerator or freezer until ready to serve.

notes.text: Walnuts used in nutrition analysis and for costing purposes. A cheaper option would be to use peanuts.

name: Peanut Butter Bread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040037/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peanut-butter-bread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Lightly grease or spray with non-stick spray, a loaf pan.
In large bowl, beat eggs. Add milk, sugar, and peanut butter. Mix well.
In a separate bowl combine flour, baking powder, and salt. Mix thoroughly.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix only enough to moisten all ingredients.
Pour into prepared pan. Pan will be half full. Bake for 1 hour.

name: Peanut Butter Cereal Bars
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040856/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peanut-butter-cereal-bars
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup raisins or other dried fruit

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large saucepan, bring honey to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and stir in peanut butter.
Add cereal, oats and raisins; mix well. Remove from heat
Lightly grease an 8x8 inch baking pan. Press mixture into pan. When cool, cut into 16 bars.
Store in an airtight container for up to a week.

notes.text: * Honey is not recommended for children under 1 year old.

name: Peanut Butter Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040848/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peanut-butter-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
Line 12 muffin cups with paper baking cups (or grease the bottom of each cup with butter or margarine).
Put the peanut butter and honey in a mixing bowl. Beat until well blended.
Add the eggs 1 at a time, beating well after each egg.
Add the milk, and mix well.
Add the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Stir just until they are moistened. Don’t stir them too much.
Fill each muffin cup 2/3 full.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown.
Put on a wire rack.
Cool for at least 10 minutes before serving.

name: Peanut Butter 'n Fruit-wich
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021924/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peanut-butter-n-fruit-wich
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spread 2 tablespoons peanut butter on bread.
Place fruit slices on top.
Optional: Top with grated carrot.

notes.text: Instead of whole wheat bread try crunchy graham crackers or roll up the filling in a soft tortilla. Instead of fresh fruit use canned, drained pineapple.

name: Peanut, Peach, N Pineapple Wrap
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032710/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peanut-peach-n-pineapple-wrap
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup red or green bell pepper (chopped)

steps: In a medium bowl, combine peaches, pineapple, bell pepper, and cinnamon.
Warm the tortillas.
Spread 2 tablespoons of peanut butter on one side of each tortilla, leaving room on the edges.
Spoon equal portions of the peach mixture over peanut butter, then top with lettuce.
Fold the side and bottom edges of each tortilla toward the middle over the filling, then roll so the tortilla covers the filling.

name: Peanut Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022027/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peanut-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 pounds whole yellow or red potatoes, peeled, halved, and cut into quarters (about 6 potatoes)

steps: Heat oil over medium heat in a pot and add onions. Cook for a few minutes.
Add ginger and garlic. Cook for 1-2 minutes. Add cumin and salt.
Add peanut butter, tomato paste, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil and add potatoes.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes or until potatoes are fork-tender and cooked through.
Add kale, and continue to cook for 1-2 minutes,
Serve garnished with lime zest, lime juice, and crushed peanuts; drizzle with Sriracha for a spicy kick (optional)

notes.text: Yellow and red potatoes will stay fork tender in this stew. Russet potatoes may fall apart and get mushy.

name: Peanutty Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021019/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peanutty-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and diced (about 2 cups)
1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium tomatoes, not drained
green onion (optional, thinly sliced for garnish)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine first 9 ingredients in a soup pot. Bring to boil, then turn down to medium low, cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in peanut butter and milk. Return to gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 5 minutes.
Stir in spinach and cook until wilted, 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from heat.
Ladle stew into bowls and top with peanuts and green onion, if desired.

name: Pear Kabobs with Strawberry Dipping Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024819/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pear-kabobs-strawberry-dipping-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 medium pears, cored and cut into 1-inch cubes

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, combine the vanilla yogurt and strawberry preserves. Set aside.
Thread the fruits by alternating the pears, strawberries, bananas, and pineapple onto the skewers.
Serve the fruit skewers with a dollop of the strawberry sauce on the side.

notes.text: Other materials needed:

name: Pear in Orange Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231030855/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pear-orange-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel the pears and cook in a double boiler for 15 minutes.
Mix sugar and orange juice and cook over low flame for 5 minutes. Cool for 5 minutes.
Place steamed pears on individual plates. Pour 1/4 of the juice mixture over each and serve.

name: Pear Party Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020731/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pear-party-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 medium pear, cored and finely chopped
1 medium apple, cored and finely chopped
1 medium orange, peeled and finely chopped

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine pear, apple, kiwifruit, and orange in a medium-sized bowl.
Pour honey and lemon juice over fruit and gently toss.
Scoop up bites of fruit salsa using bites of cinnamon graham crackers (optional).

notes.text: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey. Other materials needed:

name: Pear PB&J Bouquet
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021258/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pear-pbj-bouquet
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Use a flower-shaped cookie cutter to cut each slide of bread. If bread sticks to cutter, gently push the petals out with your fingers.

Wash the pear and dry it with a paper towel. Cut the pear in half, and remove the core. Cut each pear half into four slices, then cut each slice into five pieces. You will only use the center three pieces of each slice, so go ahead and eat the end pieces.

Spread 1 teaspoon of peanut butter in a circle in the center of each of the flowers. Place 3 pieces of pear on the peanut butter on each flower. Arrange the pears so the skin is facing out and the white centers are touching in the middle.
Drizzle 1/2 teaspoon of strawberry preserves in the center of each flower and over the pears.

notes.text: Other materials needed:

name: Pear Quesadillas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045735/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pear-quesadillas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Sprinkle cheeses, basil, and onion on half of each tortilla.
Place pear slices on top of other ingredients in each tortilla.
Fold over filled tortilla and brush each side with olive oil.
Heat the filled tortillas in a non-stick skillet until cheese melts, about 2 to 3 minutes on each side.
Cut quesadilla into four pieces and serve immediately.

name: Pear Rabbit
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020744/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pear-rabbit
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place 2 pear halves, flat side down, on a small plate to make the body.
Use butter knife to cut a tail, ears and feet from another pear half. Add each part to the body.
Use butter knife to cut one raisin in half and place on small end for eyes.
Enjoy your pear rabbit!

notes.text: Adults: If cooking with kids, use can opener, open pear halves and discard sharp-edged lid.

name: Pear Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041952/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pear-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup green beans, sliced into bite size pieces
1 cup canned pears, drained and chopped

steps: Place salad greens, sliced vegetables, pears, walnuts, and raisins in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together vinegar, yogurt, and orange juice to prepare dressing.
Top salad with dressing and mix gently. Serve.

name: Pears in a Pod
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050542/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pears-pod
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 medium celery stalks, cleaned and cut into 3-inch long pieces
2 medium pears, cored and cut into chunks

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spread the peanut butter into the center of the celery pieces.
Place the pear chunks on top of the peanut butter.
Serve on a plate and enjoy with your friends.

notes.text: Other materials needed: Learn more about:

name: Peppers Stuffed with Rice and Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044330/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peppers-stuffed-rice-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can low-sodium black beans (15 ounce can)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 °F.
Cook brown rice according to package directions.
Wash the peppers under running water.
Cut the tops off the peppers and spoon out the seeds.
Cut up two peppers and leave four to fill with the rice mixture.
Drain and rinse the black beans.
Combine the chopped up peppers, beans, rice, salsa, tomato and salt (optional).
Spoon about 3 tablespoons of the mixture into the bottom of each pepper.
Sprinkle with 2 tablespoons of cheese.
Repeat steps 8 and 9 to fill the pepper completely, but do not top with cheese.
Bake peppers for 30 minutes.
Top each pepper with 2 tablespoons of cheese and continue baking for 15 minutes more.

notes.text: Green bell peppers used for nutritional analysis. Use homemade salsa to lower the sodium of this recipe.

name: The Perfect "Pear" and Brussels Sprout Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020916/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/perfect-pear-and-brussels-sprout-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large mixing bowl, add the pear, Brussels sprouts, and all other ingredients and mix until well incorporated.
Serve and enjoy!

name: Perfect Pumpkin Pancakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021720/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/perfect-pumpkin-pancakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine flour, brown sugar, baking powder, pumpkin pie spice, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
In a medium bowl, combine egg, canned pumpkin, milk, and vegetable oil; mix well.
Add wet ingredients to flour mixture, stirring just until moist. Batter may be lumpy. (For thinner batter, add more milk.)
Lightly coat a griddle or skillet with cooking spray and heat on medium.

Using a 1/4 cup measure, pour batter onto hot griddle. Cook until bubbles begin to burst, then flip pancakes and cook until golden brown, 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 minutes. Repeat with remaining batter. Makes about 1 dozen 3 1/2 inch pancakes.

notes.text: If you don't have pumpkin spice on hand, don't worry -- it's just a combination of cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and cloves. In this recipe, you can substitute 3/4 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg, and 1/8 teaspoon each of ginger and cloves for the pumpkin pie spice. Safety Tip: You can be sure your skillet or griddle is hot enough for pancakes without burning your hand. Just sprinkle a few (3 or 4) drops of water on the surface. If they dance and sizzle, you are ready to cook. Be sure handles of skillets and pans are always turned toward the center or back of the stove, to prevent the pan from catching on hands or clothes and causing burns. Learn more about:

name: Peter Pumpkin Squares
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043411/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/peter-pumpkin-squares
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon margarine or butter (to grease the pan)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a medium bowl, stir together the pumpkin, brown sugar, eggs, and oil. Mix well.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, oats, cinnamon, baking powder, and baking soda.
Add the pumpkin mix to the flour mix. Stir well.
Grease a 9x13-inch baking pan with butter or margarine.
Pour the batter into the greased baking pan.
Bake for 30 minutes.

name: Picadillo
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022208/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/picadillo
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground turkey in a non-stick frying pan.
Add onions, carrots, zucchini, potatoes, salt, pepper, and cumin. Sauté for about 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes and just enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer, uncovered, until vegetables are tender.
Dissolve cornstarch in about 1 tablespoon of cold water, add to mixture, bring back to a boil until gravy thickens. Serve.

name: Pico de Gallo
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033200/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pico-de-gallo
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a medium bowl.
Serve immediately or cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days.

notes.text: Use to season your family meals or serve with tortilla chips.

name: Pineapple Angel Food Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044403/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pineapple-angel-food-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup crushed pineapple in 100% juice (do not drain)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a large mixing bowl, beat the egg whites until they are foamy.
Add the cream of tartar and beat until stiff, but not dry. Gradually beat in the sugar.
Add the vanilla and salt and then gently fold in the flour.
Add the pineapple to the cake mix.
Pour into an ungreased 13x9-inch pan.
Bake for 25 to 35 minutes, until golden brown or an inserted toothpick comes out clean.
Let cool and serve with whipped topping (optional).

name: Pineapple Avocado Chicken Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021939/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pineapple-avocado-chicken-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups cooked, cubed chicken breast (about 8 oz.)
4 6 1/2-inch whole wheat pita pockets (or 8 4-inch pita pockets)

steps: Mash 1/2 avocado in a small dish; add yogurt, rice vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Cut remaining avocado into small chunks and mix together with pineapple, bell pepper, carrots, cabbage, green onion, and chicken.
Add dressing; mix gently.
Fill pita pockets and serve.

notes.text: Serve with 8 ounce non-fat milk.

name: Pineapple Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040029/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pineapple-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (20 ounces) pineapple, crushed or chunks

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Coat frying pan with nonstick cooking spray and set heat to low.
Once pan heats up, add chicken. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Cook uncovered until chicken begins to brown, then add crushed pineapple and water.
Cover chicken until chicken is tender.
May serve over rice.

name: Pineapple Orange Frozen Yogurt
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021617/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pineapple-orange-frozen-yogurt
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup pineapple chunks, fresh or canned

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place yogurt and pineapple in large plastic bag and flatten. Freeze overnight.
Combine yogurt, pineapple, and juice in food processor or blender and blend until smooth.
Serve immediately or place back in the freezer to harden until ready to serve, up to 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Stir before serving.

name: Pineapple Pork
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020823/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pineapple-pork
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
1 cup canned pineapple chunks, undrained (8 ounces)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
