Cut the green pepper into strips.
Heat the oil in a large skillet.
Place pork chops on the heated skillet. Sprinkle the salt on top.
Cook the pork chops for 5 minutes on low heat on each side.
Cook pork chops until they reache an internal temperature of 145 degrees F.
Remove the cooked pork from the skillet. Place it in a serving dish and keep warm.
Put the green pepper slices in the skillet.
Stir in the pineapple chunks with their juice.
Add the ginger and cinnamon.
Simmer for about 3 to 5 minutes.
Spoon the pineapple mixture over cooked pork.

notes.text: Serve with cooked rice.

name: Pineapple Rice Bake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050052/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pineapple-rice-bake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup pineapple, crushed, undrained (8 ounce can)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F. Lightly coat an oven safe 2 quart casserole dish with nonstick spray or oil.
In a large mixing bowl, beat together eggs, milk, and sugar.
Add undrained crushed pineapple, cinnamon, nutmeg, and vanilla.
Stir in cooked rice. Pour into prepared casserole dish.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes or until a knife inserted in center of pudding comes out clean.

name: Pineapple Zucchini Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042323/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pineapple-zucchini-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F. Grease or lightly spray with non-stick cooking spray, a 9x13 inch pan.
In a large bowl, beat eggs, sugar, vanilla, and oil. Add zucchini.
In a separate bowl, combine baking powder salt, baking soda, and flour. Add dry ingredients to creamed mixture.
Stir in fruit and nuts, if using.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, or until cake springs back when lightly pressed with your finger.
serving_size: 1 3x3.25 inch piece of cake, 1/12 of recipe (135g)

name: Pink Party Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022122/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pink-party-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup peas, green, fresh or frozen

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil the potatoes in 2 cups of water in a deep kettle. Cover and cook over moderate heat for about 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
When thoroughly cool, dice potatoes and place in a big bowl.
Add diced beets and mix with the potatoes.
Set aside 1/4 cup of peas for garnishing and add the rest to the bowl.
Save 1 egg to use as a garnish. Chop the rest and add to the bowl.
Peel the skin off the apple and remove the core. Cut the apple into small pieces, place in a small bowl, and sprinkle with lemon juice. Add apple to the salad.
Add the vinegar, olive oil, and sugar.
Mix thoroughly. Chill and serve.

notes.text: The skin can be left on the apple to increase fiber and save time.

name: Pizza Eggburger
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021010/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pizza-eggburger
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spray a small non-stick skillet with non-stick cooking spray.
Over medium heat, break egg into pan; break yolk.
When egg is done turn over sprinkle with cheese and top with pepperoni (optional). Cook until cheese is melted.
Open bun, spread with pizza sauce and top with cooked egg.

name: Pizza Meat Loaf
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215302/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pizza-meat-loaf
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lightly grease 9 inch pie plate with vegetable oil. Pat turkey into pie plate.

Cover turkey with waxed paper. Cook in microwave on high; rotate plate 1/4 turn after 3 minutes. Cook until turkey reaches an internal temperature of 160 °F, about 5 more minutes. Drain excess liquid. OR - Place turkey in 350 °F oven; bake until turkey reaches an internal temperature of 160 °F, about 30 to 35 minutes. Drain any excess liquid.
Top cooked turkey with vegetables, spaghetti sauce, and cheese.
Return turkey to either the microwave or oven and heat until cheese is melted, about 1 to 2 minutes.

name: Plantain Cups with Shredded Chicken | Mofonguitos
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022143/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/plantain-cups-shredded-chicken-mofonguitos
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 small can chicken (10 ounces, drained or 1 cup cooked diced chicken)
1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
2 tablespoons olive oil (Or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a skillet, heat oil over medium heat. Add shredded chicken and onions. Cook for about 1-2 minutes.
Add spices to the mixture and cook, stirring often, for about 5 minutes. Set aside for later.
Wash and scrub plantains. Cut off each end and make 3 vertical cuts along the side of the plantain. Using your thumb, peel the skin away from the flesh of the plantain and cut into 1-inch chunks.

Heat the oil over medium heat in a skillet for about 1 minute. Add the plantain chunks and sprinkle the salt on top. Cook on all sides of the chunks (about 5-6 minutes on each side). Using tongs, be sure to turn the plantain pieces on their sides so the insides cook throughout, and they turn a golden color.
Turn the heat down to low and remove the plantain chunks from the pan.
Take 2 plantain chunks at a time and shape them into a cup using either your hands, a small pestle and mortar, or a lemon squeezer.
Fill the plantain cups with the chicken mixture and top with a low-fat yogurt dip (optional).
Serve immediately.

name: Pocket Fruit Pies
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042045/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pocket-fruit-pies
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Warm tortillas in microwave or oven to make them easier to handle.
Peel and chop fruit into pieces.
Place 1/4 of the fruit on half of each tortilla.
In a small bowl, stir together brown sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Sprinkle over fruit.
Roll up the tortillas, starting at the end with the fruit.
Place on an greased baking sheet and make small slashes to allow steam to escape. Brush with milk and sprinkle with additional sugar, if desired.
Back at 350 °F in oven for 8 to 12 minutes or until lightly brown.
Serve warm or cool.

name: Polenta with Pepper and Cheese
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032222/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/polenta-pepper-and-cheese
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can whole kernel corn mixed with green and red peppers (11 ounces, drained)
6 ounces cheese, cheddar, reduced fat, shredded
1 can black or pinto beans, low-sodium (15 ounces, rinsed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium sauce pan, bring the water to a boil. Gradually add the cornmeal or polenta. Reduce heat to low.
Continue stirring, add the corn, chilies, and the salt. Cook 6 to 8 minutes or until mixture thickens, stirring occasionally.
Gently stir in the margarine, cheese, and beans.
Remove from the heat and transfer to a serving dish.
Garnish with red bell pepper rings and cilantro.

name: Popcorn Treats
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043231/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/popcorn-treats
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pop popcorn.
Mix popped corn, raisins, and cereal in a large bowl.
Mix sugar and cinnamon in small dish.
Drizzle melted margarine or butter over mixture.
Add sugar and cinnamon mixture.
Shake or stir until all ingredients are evenly distributed.

name: Pork Loin Roast with Veggies
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025507/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pork-loin-roast-veggies
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups onions, cut in wedges (about 1/2 pound or 2 medium )
2 cups potatoes, diced (about 12 ounces or medium)
2 cups baby carrots (or 3/4 pound regular carrots, sliced)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
In a bowl mix veggies with 1 tablespoon oil, salt, and pepper.
Lay veggies around the edge of a 9x13 inch pan and put in oven.
Use a small bowl to make the rub. Mix the brown sugar, garlic, 1/2 teaspoon pepper, and 1/4 teaspoon salt in the bowl.
Sprinkle the rub over the loin. Press gently so the rub sticks to the roast. Wash your hands after handling the raw meat.
Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium high heat. Add the loin. Brown the sides of meat. Turn after about 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Transfer the pork to the center of the pan with veggies. Bake for about 40 minutes. A meat thermometer should read 145 °F. Check the temperature after 30 minutes in the oven.
Remove from oven. Let set for 5 minutes. Slice and serve.
serving_size: Approx. 3 oz. meat and 1 cup veggies, 1/6 of recipe

name: Pork Power Bowl
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033814/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pork-power-bowl
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 medium purple or orange carrots, ribbon peeled
1/4 teaspoon salt (or ½ tsp. kosher salt)
1 pound pork tenderloin, cut into 1½ inch cubes
1 15.5 oz can low sodium black beans, drained and rinsed
1 red bell pepper, cut into strips
1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro, plus more for garnish

steps: In a large mason jar add the carrots, radish, rice wine vinegar, garlic, salt, honey and water, shake to combine. Let sit for 30 minutes.
In a medium bowl toss the pork, 2 Tbsp. lime juice, 1 Tbsp. olive oil, paprika and cumin. Cover and marinate for 15 minutes. Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.

Place the quinoa, stock and kale in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and let sit for 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Thread the pork onto skewers and grill over medium-high heat, turning frequently, until pork reaches an internal temperature of 145 degrees F. Let pork rest for 3 minutes.

Divide the quinoa between four bowls. Arrange the beans, peppers, avocado, carrots and radishes on top of the quinoa. Remove the pork from the skewers and place it on top of the bowls. Drizzle with dressing and garnish with additional cilantro, if desired.

In a food processor, add yogurt, 3 Tbsp. olive oil, 1 Tbsp. lime juice, ½ an avocado, green onion and cilantro. Puree until smooth, season with salt and pepper. Thin dressing with cold water, if desired.
Dressing (optional):

notes.text: Dressing nutrition not included.

name: Pot Roasted Beef
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025427/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pot-roasted-beef
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 red potatoes, peeled and quartered (or 2 cans, low-sodium sliced potatoes, drained)
2 turnips, peeled and quartered (or 1 can low-sodium sweet potatoes, drained)

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Season the roast with salt and pepper.
In a large pan, brown the roast in the oil over medium to high heat for 10 to 12 minutes. Drain fat.
Use a large iron skillet or roasting pan. Put the roast in the middle of the pan. Add the potatoes, turnips, onions, and carrots around the roast.
Pour the tomato juice over the roast and vegetables.
Cover the pan with a lid or foil and bake for 1 hour or until potatoes are cooked.
If desired, cut roast into one inch chunks. Mix and serve.

notes.text: Tip for cooking beef roast: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for beef roast is 145 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.

name: Potato Beef Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231014704/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/potato-beef-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can cream of mushroom soup, reduced sodium (10.75 ounces)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel onion and dice into 1/4-inch pieces.
Cook ground beef and onions in a skillet until the meat is browned. Drain of fat.
Add mushroom soup and 1/2 can water.
Use a brush to scrub potatoes under cold running water. Slice potatoes into 1/2-inch thick pieces and places in the bottom of a casserole dish.
Spread meat and soup mixture over potatoes.
Bake at 350 °F for 45 minutes until potatoes are tender and casserole is bubbly and browned.

name: Potato, Black Bean, & Kale Skillet
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034718/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/potato-black-bean-kale-skillet
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 1/2 cups kale (curly Italian or other variety, approx. 6 oz.)
1 15 oz. can low sodium black beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Dice potatoes into 1/4 inch pieces.
Chop kale.
Heat oil, in large skillet over medium heat, Add garlic and onions; cook 2 to 3 minutes until just starting to brown.
Add diced potatoes, chili, salt, and pepper to skillet, cover with lid and cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add chopped kale and black beans. Cook about 3 to 5 more minutes, stirring gently.
Serve with Greek yogurt.

notes.text: Serve with 8 ounce glass of non-fat milk, chicken breast, and orange slices.

name: Potato Cakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020722/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/potato-cakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups potatoes (cold, mashed, made from instant potato flakes)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare potatoes according to package.
Put mashed potatoes into a bowl.
Add flour and onion. Mix well.
Pat potato mixture on a lightly floured board until 1/2 inch thick.
Cut with a 3-inch round cutter.
Place on a baking sheet, cover and refrigerate until just before cooking.
Heat oil in a frying pan or griddle.
Fry cakes over medium heat, turning to brown on both sides. Serve immediately.

name: Potato Nachos
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031436/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/potato-nachos
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 small red potatoes, skins on (1 pound)
2 teaspoons vegetable oil or cooking spray
8 ounces lean ground turkey (15% fat or less)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice potatoes into small circles about 1/4 inch thick.
Lightly coat the potato slices with oil (or spray for 3 seconds with cooking spray).
Arrange slices on a baking sheet in a single layer. Bake in the oven at 450 °F for 25 to 30 minutes, depending on desired darkness.
Meanwhile, add ground turkey and chili powder to a skillet. Cook, stirring over medium heat (300 °F in an electric skillet) for 8 to10 minutes or until turkey browns.
Remove potatoes from the oven.
Transfer baked potatoes to an oven-safe dish. Top with turkey and sprinkle with cheese. Put back in the oven to melt the cheese, about 2 minutes.
Remove from oven and top with lettuce, tomato, cucumber, cilantro, and salsa.

notes.text: Try other toppings, such as guacamole or reduced-fat sour cream or plain yogurt.

name: Potato Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043419/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/potato-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub the potatoes, and peel them.
Cut the potatoes into 1-inch cubes.
Put the potatoes into a saucepan. Cover with water.
Bring the potatoes to a boil on medium heat.
Let the potatoes simmer for 15 minutes until they’re soft.
Drain the hot water, and let the potatoes cool.
While the potatoes are cooling, peel and chop some onions until you have 1 cup of chopped onions.
Chop the celery until you have 1/2 cup of chopped celery.
Put the chopped onion and celery in a medium mixing bowl.
Add the mayonnaise and pickle relish. Stir together.
Add the cooled potatoes. Stir again.
Cover the bowl. Put in the fridge for at least 2 hours before serving.

notes.text: Leave on the potato peels for more fiber and other nutrients.

name: Potato Skins with Buffalo Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041425/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/potato-skins-buffalo-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Center oven rack and preheat oven to 425 °F.
Place chicken in a sauté pan, add water, and cover. Simmer for 20 minutes and remove from pan; let cool slightly. When chicken is cool enough to handle, shred using two forks, one in each hand.
While chicken is simmering, wash and scrub potatoes with a clean vegetable brush under running water and slit each one lengthwise about 1-inch deep.
Place potatoes in a microwave-safe dish and microwave on high, uncovered, for about 10 minutes. Let cool slightly.

Slice each potato in half length-wise, scoop out potato, leaving a 1/4 inch shell. Mash potato together with hot pepper sauce, sour cream, margarine, and milk. Fold in blue cheese and shredded chicken.
Spoon mixture into potato skins slightly denting center (to hold fresh toppings after baking).
Place filled potato skins on a 9x13 inch baking sheet and bake about 15 to 20 minutes until tops are golden brown.
Dice tomatoes and green onions. Cut celery stalks into four inch sticks.
To serve, top potatoes with onions and tomatoes. Serve celery sticks on the side for scooping potato contents.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of non-fat milk and apple slices.

name: Potato Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022230/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/potato-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the onion.
Chop the celery.
Peel the potatoes, and cut them into small cubes.
Melt the margarine in a large saucepan on low heat.
Add the onion and celery. Cook for a few minutes.
Add the potatoes, salt, pepper, and 1 1/2 cups water.
Cook for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
In a small bowl, stir together the dry milk and flour.
Add 1 1/2 cups water slowly, stirring as you add it.
Add the milk mix to the potatoes.
Cook until the soup is heated and slightly thickened.
Adjust the seasonings.

name: Potato Spinach Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231051113/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/potato-spinach-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 2/3 cups frozen hash browns, country style (about 12 ounces, thawed)
6 egg whites from large eggs (3/4 cup)
1/2 cup cheese, reduced-fat sharp cheddar, shredded
1/2 cup cheese, reduced fat Monterey Jack, shredded

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 °F.
Wash your hands and work area.
In large bowl, combine hash browns, green pepper, 1/4 cup onion, salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
Spray a 8x8 inch baking dish with non-stick cooking spray. Press potato mixture into bottom.
Bake until lightly browned around edges, 20 to 25 minutes.
In large bowl, stir together evaporated milk, egg whites, 1/4 teaspoon pepper, cheeses, spinach, remaining 1/4 cup onion, and tomatoes.
Reduce oven temperature to 350 °F.
Pour mixture over potato crust. Bake uncovered until center is set, 40 to 45 minutes.
Cover and let stand for 10 minutes. Cut into 6 pieces. Serve hot. Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Potato Spinach Lasagna
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045623/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/potato-spinach-lasagna
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3/4 cup non-fat ricotta cheese (or cottage cheese)
1 1/2 cups no salt added pasta sauce (about 1/2 of 24-oz jar)

steps: Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Bring water to a boil in large sauce pan.
Thinly slice potatoes, add to boiling water and cook 5 minutes, drain and rinse with cool water; drain again.
Heat olive oil in medium skillet, add onions and garlic; sauté about 2 to 3 minutes until just starting to brown.
Add spinach, sauté 1 more minute.
Remove from heat and drain off liquid.
In a medium bowl, mix cheese with egg until well blended.
Add layers to 8 inch square baking dish as follows, using about 1/4 of each: pasta sauce, potato slices, sautéed spinach mixture and cheese mixture.
Repeat layers until all ingredients are used.
Cover with foil.
Bake about 35 to 40 minutes.
Remove foil and bake an additional 10 minutes until cheese is melted.

notes.text: Serve with sparkling water, lemon slice, and a slice of rustic grain bread.

name: Pretzel Shapes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042256/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pretzel-shapes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 °F.
In a small bowl, dissolve yeast in warm water, add honey and let set for a few minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, measure flour and salt.
Add yeast mixture to flour mixture and stir until it forms a smooth ball. Add a little more flour if the dough is sticky.
Knead dough on countertop or dough board until it forms a smooth ball. Add a little flour if the dough is sticky.
Divide dough into 12 pieces about the size of a walnut. Roll each ball into a snake and then twist to make a pretzel, letter, or other fun shape.
Place pretzels on a baking sheet lightly coated with cooking spray. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until golden brown.

notes.text: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Pulled Pork Sandwich with Red Cabbage and Carrot Slaw
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033146/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pulled-pork-sandwich-red-cabbage-and-carrot-slaw
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 pound boneless pork roast (or half pork shoulder)
1 1/2 cups cider or white vinegar (or a combination of both)
8 whole wheat dinner rolls or slider buns

steps: Put everything in the slow cooker and turn the heat to medium. Cook, undisturbed, for 8 hours or until it is fork-tender (about 190 °F with a meat thermometer).
Remove the pork from the slow cooker but keep the liquid. While still hot, use two forks to shred the meat. Remove any fat found between the shreds.
Skim as much fat as possible from the liquid in the slow cooker. Add about 1 cup of the cooking liquid to the shredded pork.
Put the shredded cabbage and carrots in a bowl.
Mix the canola oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a small bowl and stir well.
Add the dressing to the cabbage mixture and coat thoroughly.
Add 1/2 cup of pulled pork to each roll or bun and top with 1/2 cup cabbage and carrot slaw. Serve right away.
Pulled Pork: Red Cabbage and Carrot Slaw:

name: Pumpkin and Bean Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022332/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pumpkin-and-bean-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Blend white beans, onion, and water with a potato masher or blender till smooth.
In a large pot, add the pumpkin, juice, cinnamon, nutmeg, black pepper, and salt. Stir.
Add the blended bean mix to the pot.
Cook over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, until warmed through.

name: Pumpkin Angel Food Cake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040619/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pumpkin-angel-food-cake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a large mixing bowl, beat the egg whites until they are foamy.
Add the cream of tartar and beat until stiff, but not dry. Gradually beat in the sugar
Add the vanilla and salt and then gently fold in the sifted flour (1 cup).
Add the remaining ingredients (1 Tablespoon of flour - water) and beat with an electric mixer on low speed for 30 seconds. Then, beat on medium speed for 1 minute.
Pour into an ungreased 10-inch angel food cake pan.
Bake 37 to 47 minutes or until golden brown and cracks are dry.
Remove from oven and immediately turn pan upside down until cooled.

notes.text: Angel food cake pan can be turned upside down onto a glass bottle. Suggest serving with whipped topping.

name: Pumpkin Bread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043843/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pumpkin-bread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a large mixing bowl, beat together pumpkin, sugar, oil, and yogurt.
In a medium bowl, combine the flours, baking powder, soda, cinnamon, and salt. Add to pumpkin mixture, stirring until just moistened.
Stir in raisins.
Pour into 2 greased 9x5x3 inch loaf pans and bake for about 1 hour.
Cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes; remove from pan and cool completely.

notes.text: Substituting yogurt for eggs and oil reduces fat and cholesterol.

name: Pumpkin Cheese Pie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050745/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pumpkin-cheese-pie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Place the cream cheeses, eggs, and sugar in a large mixing bowl. Mix at medium speed until creamed. Add the remaining ingredients and mix at medium speed until ingredients are well mixed.
Spoon the mixture evenly in each pie crust and place both in the oven for approximately 50 minutes until pies look firm in the middle.

name: Pumpkin Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035516/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pumpkin-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 green bell pepper (cored, seeded and chopped )
2 cloves garlic (finely chopped or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder )
1 can diced tomatoes with juice, low-sodium
1 can kidney beans, low-sodium (or other beans if desired)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium high heat.
Add onion, bell pepper, jalapenos and garlic and cook, stirring frequently until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add turkey and cook until browned.
Add tomatoes, pumpkin, water, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium low then add beans.
Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 30 minutes more.
Ladle chili into bowls and serve.

name: Pumpkin Chocolate Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042744/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pumpkin-chocolate-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Whisk all the dry ingredients together. Add pumpkin and water.
Fold the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients until just combined. Fold in chocolate chips.
Place batter into 24 prepared muffin tins and bake at 350 °F for 10 to 12 minutes.

name: Pumpkin Cookies
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035007/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pumpkin-cookies
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Mix pumpkin, brown sugar, eggs, and oil thoroughly.
Blend dry ingredients and add to pumpkin mixture.
Add raisins and nuts.
Drop by teaspoonfuls on greased cookie sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes until golden brown.

name: Pumpkin Mac & Cheese for One
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215052/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pumpkin-mac-cheese-one
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Stir the "wet" ingredients (soup, pumpkin purée, milk, and mustard), and heat in microwave for 45 to 60 seconds; stir again until creamy.
Add cooked pasta to cream and sprinkle cheese on top. Heat another 30 to 45 seconds or until cheese melts.

name: Pumpkin Pudding
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031728/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pumpkin-pudding
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can pumpkin, 15 ounces (or 2 cups cooked mashed squash such as Hubbard)
2 teaspoons pumpkin pie spice (or 1 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon ginger, 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg and 1/4 teaspoon cloves)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl mix pumpkin, salt and pumpkin spice together.
Slowly stir in milk and mix well. Add instant pudding mix and stir for 2 minutes until it thickens. Refrigerate until serving time.

name: Pumpkin Ricotta Stuffed Shells
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215152/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pumpkin-ricotta-stuffed-shells
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 ounces jumbo pasta shells (about 12 jumbo pasta shells)
1/2 teaspoon garlic powder (or 2 cloves garlic, minced)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Cook pasta shells according to package directions. Drain and place each on a baking sheet to cool.
In a medium bowl, stir together ricotta, pumpkin, spices, and all but 1 tablespoon of the cheese. Reserve the 1 tablespoon cheese for topping.

Spread pasta sauce in the bottom of a baking dish that holds all the shells in a single layer. Fill each shell with about 3 tablespoons of pumpkin mixture and place shells close together on top of the sauce.
Cover pan with foil and bake for 30 minutes. Remove foil, sprinkle with remaining cheese, and bake for 15 minutes more.

notes.text: Freeze unused pumpkin and add to soup, chili or pancake recipes.

name: Pumpkin Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033431/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pumpkin-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can white beans (15 ounce, rinsed and drained)
1 can vegetable or chicken broth, low-sodium (14.5 ounces)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Blend white beans, onion, and water.
In a soup pot, mix bean puree with pumpkin, broth, and spices.
Cover and cook over low heat about 15 to 20 minutes until warmed through.

name: Pupusas Revueltas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215112/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/pupusas-revueltas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a non-stick skillet over low heat, sauté chicken in oil until chicken turns white. Constantly stir the chicken to keep it from sticking.
Add onion, garlic, green pepper, and tomato. Cook until chicken mixture is cooked through. Remove skillet from stove and let mixture cool in the refrigerator.
While the chicken mixture is cooling, place the flour in a large mixing bowl and stir in enough water to make a stiff tortilla-like dough.
When the chicken mixture has cooled, mix in the cheese.

Divide the dough into 24 portions. With your hands, roll the dough into balls and flatten each ball into a 1/2 ich thick circle. Put a spoonful of the chicken mixture in the middle of each circle of dough and bring the edges to the center. Flatten the ball of dough again until it is 1/2 inch thick.
In a very hot, iron skillet, cook the pupusas on each side until golden brown.
Serve hot.

name: Purple Cow
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022634/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/purple-cow
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place all ingredients in blender or food processor.
Secure lid and blend until smooth. Serve immediately.

notes.text: Substitute 1 cup milk and 1 cup water for 2 cups water and 1/3 cup nonfat dry milk

name: Quesadilla con Huevos
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050702/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quesadilla-con-huevos
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup cheddar or colby jack cheese (grated - cojack)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put 2 tablespoons cheese and 1/4 of the scrambled eggs on each tortilla.
Heat 2 quesadillas at a time in microwave on high for 30 to 45 seconds or until cheese melts.
Top with salsa and fold tortilla in half to serve.
Add parsley if desired.
serving_size: 1 Quesadilla con Huevos, 1/4 of the recipe (85g)

name: Quick and Easy Baked Potato Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042101/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-and-easy-baked-potato-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 tablespoons real bacon bits or pieces

steps: Place whole potatoes (do not poke holes) into microwave-safe dish.
Cover dish. (If covering dish with plastic wrap, poke small holes in plastic.)
Microwave on high for 10 to 12 minutes depending on strength of microwave.
Use oven mitts or a towel to remove dish from microwave. Carefully remove cover from dish due to steam build up and let cool.
Cut potatoes into bite-sized pieces and place in a large bowl with remaining ingredients. Stir and mix well.

notes.text: This salad may be served right away, but is best if refrigerated for at least one hour to allow flavors to blend.

name: Quick and Easy Pizza
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045644/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-and-easy-pizza
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 ounces part-skim mozzarella cheese, shredded (1 1/2 cups)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Collect, shred, and measure all ingredients before starting to prepare the recipe.
In a medium bowl, mix 1 cup flour, yeast, sugar, and water with a spoon.
Gradually stir in the other cup of flour until the mixture forms a ball.
Dust a cutting board or clean countertop surface with flour. Put the ball of dough on the surface, then use your clean hands to knead the dough on the surface for about 5 minutes.

Spray a bowl with nonstick cooking spray. Put the dough in the bowl, and cover it with a clean dishtowel. Put the bowl on the oven while it is preheating (but not on a burner that is turned on), and let it sit for 10 to 15 minutes (preheating the oven will cause the stovetop to be slightly warm and will help the dough rise).

Spray a 12-inch x 16-inch baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray. Spread the dough into an even layer on the baking sheet. Spread the dough into an even layer on the baking sheet. For a thicker crust, use a smaller baking sheet.
Add a thin layer of the Easy Marinara Sauce from the Eating Smart, Being Active Let's Cook! Cookbook, leaving a 1/2 inch crust on all edges.
Add the shredded cheese and pizza toppings. Be careful not to put too many toppings on the pizza, or it will be soggy.
Bake for approximately 15 minutes until the crust is brown and the cheese melts and is slightly browned in spots.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Eat within 3 to 5 days.

notes.text: *Make it whole grain! To make whole grain pizza crust, substitute 1 cup of 100% whole wheat flour for 1 cup of the all-purpose flour. Increase the water to 1 cup, and increase the baking time to 20 minutes.

name: Quick and Easy Potato Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042132/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-and-easy-potato-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 1/2 Yukon Gold potatoes, very thinly sliced
1 cup onion, quartered and thinly sliced
1 cup shredded reduced-fat sharp cheddar cheese

steps: Spray an 8-inch microwave-safe baking dish with nonstick cooking spray. Place 1/3 of the potatoes and 1/2 of the onions on the bottom of the dish and sprinkle with 1/3 the cheese and 1/2 the herbs.
Repeat layers, then top with the last 1/3 of the potatoes, layering potatoes so that there is a solid layer of potatoes with no gaps; sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Stir together stock, Dijon mustard, and garlic salt, and pour over the potatoes.
Cover with plastic wrap and microwave on HIGH until internal temperature registers 165 °F on a food thermometer, about 20 minutes.
Use oven mitts or a towel to remove dish from microwave; carefully remove cover due to steam build-up and serve.

name: Quick Black Bean Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021358/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-black-bean-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Leave frozen corn in the fridge overnight to defrost. If you forget to do this ahead of time, defrost it in the microwave.
Drain and rinse the black beans.
Combine all ingredients together and serve as a side dish.

name: Quick Black-Eyed Peas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050910/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-black-eyed-peas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Over medium high heat cook bacon and onions for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the rest of the ingredients and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to simmer and allow to cook until the peas are tender, about 30 minutes.
Serve hot.

name: Quick Chicken & Vegetable Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041339/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-chicken-vegetable-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cans low-sodium chicken broth (14.5 ounce cans)
1 package mixed vegetables (10 ounce frozen or vegetables of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put the tomatoes, potatoes and broth in the pot. Cook on medium heat until they boil.
Add the onion. Turn the heat to low, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the remaining ingredients.
Cover the pan.
Cook for at least 5 more minutes over low heat until vegetables are tender.

name: Quick Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020841/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can kidney beans, low-sodium (15 1/2 ounces, with liquid)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

Thoroughly cook ground beef in skillet until browned (internal temperature of 160 °F). Do not undercook ground beef. Carefully wash your hands and any surfaces that have come in contact with raw meat.
Drain off fat into container.
Stir in kidney beans with liquid, tomato sauce, onion, and chili powder.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Refrigerate or freeze leftovers within 2 hours of cooking. Use refrigerated leftovers within 4 days.

name: Quick and Easy Bean Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041517/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-easy-bean-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/3 cup beans, low-sodium canned or cooked (pinto beans work great)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place beans in a small, resealable plastic bag. Squeeze out extra air and seal. Mash beans with fingers.
Add yogurt and salsa. Seal bag and mix with fingers.
Open bag or cut off corner of bag and squeeze out dip.

name: Quick 'N Cool Summer Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032841/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-n-cool-summer-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can green beans, low-sodium (14.5 ounce, drained, or other vegetable)
1 can tuna packed in water (6.5 ounces, drained and flaked)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare elbow macaroni according to package directions and drain.
Add vegetables, tuna, onions, cheese, and pickles.
Mix yogurt, salad dressing, lemon juice, salt, and seasoned pepper.
Toss with macaroni mixture.
Chill before serving.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly.
* Add chopped carrots if desired.

name: Quick Peach Cobbler
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041755/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-peach-cobbler
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can sliced peaches, packed in juice (15 ounce)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 375 °F.
Open the can of peaches. Pour the peaches and their juice into the casserole dish. Heat them on the stovetop until they bubble.
Slightly beat 1 egg.
In a mixing bowl, mix the egg, sugar, flour, baking powder, salt, and margarine.
Drop spoonsful of this mixture on top of the hot, bubbling peaches.
Use pot holders to carefully remove the casserole dish from the stove.
Put the casserole dish in the oven. Bake for about 30 to 40 minutes.

name: Quick Skillet Lasagna
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034535/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-skillet-lasagna
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Chop onion. Cook beef and onion, in a large frying pan until beef is brown and onion is tender. Drain off excess fat.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, parsley, water, and garlic powder to the beef mixture. Bring to a boil and simmer until sauce is thick, about 25 minutes.
Cook noodles in a separate saucepan according to package directions. Drain.
Add cooked, drained noodles to the beef mixture. Stir to prevent sticking.
Mix cheeses and drop by spoonfuls into the frying pan.
Cover and heat over low heat about 5 minutes.
Refrigerate leftovers.

notes.text: To decrease fat and cholesterol, omit the beef and add vegetables such as broccoli or zucchini to the sauce.

name: Quick Tuna Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044112/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quick-tuna-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can cream of mushroom soup, low-sodium (10.75 ounce)
1 can tuna (6.5 ounces, packed in water, drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Bring 1 quart of water to a boil in a large pot and cook the egg noodles in the water for 2 minutes.
Cover the pot, remove from heat, and let stand for 10 minutes.
In the meantime, mix the water, soup, and milk together in a bowl.
Combine tuna and peas with the mixture and pour into a 1-quart casserole dish.
Drain the noodles well and combine with the tuna mixture.
Sprinkle the top with bread crumbs if desired.
Bake for 30 minutes.

notes.text: To lower sodium content, use reduced-sodium cream of mushroom soup.

name: Quinoa and Black Bean Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033018/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/quinoa-and-black-bean-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can black beans, low-sodium (15.5 ounce can, rinsed and drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse the quinoa in cold water. Boil water in a saucepan, and then add the quinoa.
Return to boil, and then simmer until the water is absorbed, 10 to 15 minutes. Cool for 15 minutes.
While quinoa is cooking, mix olive oil, lime juice, cumin, coriander, chopped cilantro, and scallions in a small bowl, and set aside.
Combine chopped vegetables with the black beans in a large bowl, and set aside.
Once quinoa has cooled, combine all ingredients and mix well.
Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.

name: Rainbow Bell Pepper Boats with Garbanzo Beans and Kale
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031708/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/rainbow-bell-pepper-boats-garbanzo-beans-and-kale
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 medium bell peppers (red, yellow, and orange)

steps: Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Cook rice according to package directions.
Slice bell peppers in half vertically and remove seeds.
Reserve about half of garbanzo beans; mash remaining portion with a fork.
Mix rice with kale, garbanzo beans (mashed and whole), nuts, salt, and pepper.
Fill peppers with mix; place in baking dish and cover.
Bake about 30 minutes.
Remove lid and bake more 5 more minutes.

name: Rainbow Veggie Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034250/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/rainbow-veggie-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15.5 ounces) red kidney beans, low-sodium (drained and rinsed)
1 can (15.5 ounces) black beans, low-sodium (drained and rinsed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all the vegetables together in a large bowl.
Pour dressing over vegetables.
Sprinkle with pepper.
Stir gently, coating all vegetables.
Cover and refrigerate at least 8 hours.

name: Ratatouille
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041055/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/ratatouille
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 eggplant (peeled and cut into 1 inch cubes)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large saucepan and sauté onion, garlic, bell peppers, and eggplant until tender, about 15 minutes.
Add tomatoes and basil, cook about 10 minutes. Add pepper and parsley before serving.
Serve hot. Cover and refrigerate within 2 hours.

notes.text: Optional: Use a bag of frozen vegetables. It will be more economical than fresh vegetables and contain less sodium than canned vegetables.

name: Red Bean Quesadilla
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034735/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/red-bean-quesadilla
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup frozen spinach (thawed and squeezed to remove excess liquid)
1/2 cup shredded Monterey Jack or Cheddar cheese
1 can 15.5 ounce low-sodium red kidney beans (drained and rinsed with cold water)

steps: Using a fork, mash beans in a bowl until slightly chunky. Add no-salt seasonings such as garlic powder and dried or fresh herbs, if desired.
Place 1 tortilla on a plate and top with half the mashed beans.
Top the beans with 1/2 cup of the spinach.
Top the spinach with half the cheese.
Top the cheese with half the avocado. (optional)
Put the other tortilla on top of the avocado, gently pressing it down so the top half sticks.
Repeat with the remaining 2 tortillas.

Place a nonstick skillet on the stove over medium and heat until warm, then place 1 quesadilla in the dry skillet. Cook until golden brown, about 1 to 2 minutes on each side. (Or put the plate in the microwave and heat until the cheese melts, about 45 seconds.)
Repeat with the remaining quesadilla.
Cut each quesadilla into quarters. Serve warm.

notes.text: Black beans or white cannellini beans can be used instead of kidney beans.

name: Red Beans and Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031926/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/red-beans-and-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup red bell pepper (chopped - could also use green pepper)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pick through beans to remove shriveled or broken beans. Rinse beans thoroughly.
In a 5-quart pot, mix beans, water, onion, celery, and bay leaves. Bring to boiling; reduce heat.
Cover and cook over low heat for about 1 to 1/2 hours or until beans are tender. Stir and mash beans against side of pan.
Add garlic, parsley, thyme, salt, black pepper, and red or green pepper.
Cook uncovered, over low heat, until creamy, about 30 minutes. Remove bay leaves. Serve over hot cooked rice.

notes.text: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.

name: Red Chile Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035604/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/red-chile-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 dried red chiles (more or less depending on taste)
2 pounds pork top loin (cut into pieces)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash chilies, removing stems and seeds. Place in blender with 1 cup water and blend into paste
Brown pork lightly in non-stick skillet. Add the chili paste and mix well, adding water if mixture is too thick. Add oregano and garlic powder. Cover and simmer slowly for one hour.

name: Red Hot Fusilli
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020813/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/red-hot-fusilli
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 tablespoon fresh basil, chopped (1 tsp dried basil)
1 tablespoon oregano leaves, crushed (1 tsp dried oregano)
ground red pepper (or cayenne, to taste)
cooked chicken breast (1/2 pound diced into 1/2-inch pieces, optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a medium saucepan. Saute garlic and parsley until golden.

Add tomatoes and spices. Cook uncovered over low heat 15 minutes or until thickened, stirring frequently. If desired, add chicken and continue cooking for 15 minutes until chicken is heated through and sauce is thick.
Cook pasta firm in unsalted water.
To serve, spoon sauce over pasta and sprinkle with coarsely chopped parsley. Serve hot as a main dish and cold for the next day's lunch.
*Cost estimate and nutritional analysis does not include chicken.

notes.text: If pre-cooked chicken is not available, cook 3/4 pound raw chicken and chop into 1/2 inch pieces when cooled down.

name: Red Lentil Latkes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035446/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/red-lentil-latkes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 medium potato, grated (about 1/2 pound, peeling is optional)
Parmesan cheese, grated (optional, 2 tablespoons, or other cheese)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add the lentils to a medium saucepan and add water to cover by about an inch. Bring to a boil, then lower heat to a simmer and cook until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Meanwhile, remove the excess water from the potato: you can either squeeze it by the handful, or put the entire pile on a clean tea towel and wring it out.

Crack the egg in a medium bowl and beat it lightly. Add the potato, cooked lentils, garlic, and green onion. Add cheese and hot sauce if you're using them. Add the salt and a good grinding of black pepper and stir until combined.

Heat a large skillet over medium heat, then add a generous drizzle of oil (1-2 tablespoons). Working in batches, so as not to crowd the pan, add clumps of the potato-lentil mixture (about the size of a golf ball or slightly larger works well), and flatten each as soon as it's in the pan, making them about a half inch thick.

Cook for about 4 to 5 minutes per side, until the latkes are deeply golden brown and cooked through. Add a little more oil to the pan for each additional batch. Serve immediately or keep the latkes warm in a 200 °F oven for up to an hour.

name: Red Monster Smoothie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044450/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/red-monster-smoothie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup water (optional almond milk or coconut milk)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Using a blender, mix the greens and the liquid of your choice.
Gradually add in the rest of the ingredients, blending after each addition.
Separate into two cups and reserve one serving for later.

name: Red Potato and Cabbage (Colcannon)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045354/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/red-potato-and-cabbage-colcannon
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 cups green cabbage, thinly sliced (about 1/2 head)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub potatoes, but do not peel. Cut into quarters. Cook in boiling water or steam until tender, about 15 to 20 minutes.
While potatoes cook, heat butter or margarine in a large skillet over medium high heat. Add onion and cook until it becomes clear, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Add cabbage and cook, stirring occasionally, until cabbage begins to brown, about 4 to 6 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Add milk, salt, and pepper. Cover and cook until cabbage is tender, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Drain potatoes. Add cabbage mixture to potatoes. Mash with a potato masher or large fork to reach desired texture. Serve warm.

name: Red Potato Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025015/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/red-potato-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: To prepare sauce, combine yogurt, mayonnaise and mustard in a small bowl. Mix well and refrigerate.
Wash potatoes and place in pot. Cover with water about 1 inch above potatoes.
Bring water and potatoes to a boil and simmer until potatoes are fork tender.
Drain potatoes and set aside to cool.
When potatoes are cooled, cut into bite-sized cubes. Place cut potatoes into large bowl.
Add celery, onions, salt, and pepper to potatoes. Top with sauce and mix well.
Garnish with parsley and enjoy.

name: Refried Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022339/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/refried-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 cups dry pinto beans (sorted and rinsed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook beans and reserve some of the cooking liquid before draining.
Sauté onions and garlic in oil until onions become clear. Add a little water if vegetables stick.
Mash half of the beans, and add to onion and garlic. Continue to sauté for 10 minutes, stirring frequently. Allow some of the mashed beans to brown.
Add cumin. Add remaining beans and continue cooking until they are warmed through.
Water or liquid from beans may be added to keep the beans soft and mushy.

name: Rhubarb Blueberry Crisp
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035049/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/rhubarb-blueberry-crisp
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a medium bowl, stir together brown sugar, flour and oats.
Stir in the butter and set aside.
Spread the rhubarb and blueberries in an 8x8 inch baking dish and set aside.
In a medium saucepan, mix cornstarch and sugar and stir in the juice. Cook over medium heat, stirring all the time, until the mixture has thickened. Turn off the heat.
Stir in vanilla and pour the mixture over the rhubarb and blueberries.
Crumble oat mixture on top of the fruit.
Bake for 45 minutes or until topping is browned and fruit is bubbling at edges. Serve warm or cold.

name: Rice Bowl Breakfast with Fruit and Nuts
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021024/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/rice-bowl-breakfast-fruit-and-nuts
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup chopped fruit (try a mixture - apples, bananas, raisins, berries, peaches)
2 tablespoons chopped nuts (try walnuts or almonds)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine cooked rice, milk and cinnamon in a microwave-safe bowl. Microwave on HIGH for 45 seconds. Stir and heat for another 45 to 60 seconds, or until rice mixture is heated through.
Divide rice mixture between two bowls. Top with fruit and nuts. Serve warm.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Rice with Chicken | Arroz con Pollo
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041435/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/rice-chicken-arroz-con-pollo
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (14.5 oz) low-sodium diced tomatoes (including liquid)

steps: To trim, lay chicken thighs on the cutting board, skin side up. Push the chicken down so the excess fat is on the cutting board (the excess is the part that isn’t right on top of the chicken). Using kitchen scissors or a sharp knife, cut off excess fat and discard. Pat chicken dry with paper towels, and discard towels.
Place the skillet over medium high heat and when it is hot, add the chicken thighs, skin side down and cook until browned, then flip, about 5 minutes on each side.
Turn the heat off, carefully remove the chicken from the skillet and transfer to the plate. Pour off all but 1 tablespoon fat.
Reheat the skillet over low heat and add the onion, pepper, garlic, cumin, and oregano and cook until the onion is softened, about 10 minutes.
Add the uncooked rice and tomatoes and stir well.
Add the water and bouillon cube and bring to a boil over high heat. Return chicken to pan, skin side down, turn the heat down to low and cover.
Cook chicken for 20 minutes and then carefully flip so that the skin side is up.
Cover and cook for an additional 20 minutes. Serve right away.

name: Rice-Crusted Pizza
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045537/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/rice-crusted-pizza
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 350 °F. Grease a 12-inch pizza pan or baking sheet.
Cook rice following directions on the package; set aside.
Grate cheese; set aside.
Crack egg and place in mixing bowl, stirring to blend. Measure and add 2 cups cooked rice, 1 cup grated cheese, and salt. Mix well to combine ingredients.
Spread rice mixture in prepared pan, pressing firmly and making outer edge slightly raised.
Spread tomato purée evenly over rice mixture.
Place pan in oven. Bake for 25 minutes.
Remove pan from oven sprinkle pizza with remaining cheese. Bake 5 minutes longer or until cheese melts.
Remove pizza from oven. Cut into 12 slices.
Create-a-Flavor Changes: Try different kinds of rice.; Try different kinds of cheese.; Use sliced or chopped green peppers, onions, mushrooms, or other vegetables as toppings.

name: Rice Dessert
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020725/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/rice-dessert
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup crushed pineapple in juice (8 ounce can)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put aside 1/4 cup of drained pineapple.
Mix all other ingredients together in a medium-sized bowl.
Serve in small dishes.
Top with the remaining crushed pineapple.

name: Rice Pudding
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045601/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/rice-pudding
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In sauce pan, heat milk and water.
Add rice, bring to boil, lower heat to simmer; stir mixture every 10 minutes. Cook uncovered until rice is tender, about 30 minutes.
In large bowl, mix eggs, 3/4 cup evaporated milk, vanilla, and sugar. Set aside.
Add remaining 1/4 cup evaporated milk to rice mixture.
Spoon 1 cup of rice mixture into egg mixture and stir. Pour egg-rice mixture into remaining rice.
Heat pudding until it boils, stirring continuously. Remove from heat, and sprinkle with cinnamon.

name: Rice Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042141/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/rice-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix rice, vegetables, and raisins in a medium-sized bowl.
Mix mayonnaise, dressing and salt in a small bowl. Stir into rice/vegetable mixture.
Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Rise and Shine Cobbler
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040932/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/rise-and-shine-cobbler
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup pear halves (canned, drained and sliced)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large microwave-safe bowl, mix peaches, pears, prunes, and vanilla extract.
Rub an orange against a grater to remove 1 teaspoon of the orange peel. Then, cut the orange in half and squeeze 1/4 cup orange juice. Add orange peel and juice to fruit mixture. Stir.
Top with granola.
Microwave on high for 5 minutes. Let stand for 2 minutes.
Spoon into 4 bowls and serve warm.

name: Roast Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050612/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roast-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Combine Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt, and pepper (optional).
Rub chicken with oil, then rub with spice mixture.
Place chicken, breast side down, in roasting pan or Dutch oven.
Bake, uncovered, until internal temperature reaches at least 165 °F.
Let chicken rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

name: Roast Turkey Breast with Rosemary, Sage, and Thyme
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033740/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roast-turkey-breast-rosemary-sage-and-thyme
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 pounds turkey breast half (with skin and bones)
chicken broth, low sodium (or margarine, for basting, optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Place turkey breast in roasting pan along with onion and carrot.
Mix spices with olive oil. Rub turkey with olive oil.
Roast turkey at 400 °F for 15 minutes. Baste with margarine and chicken broth (optional).

Reduce turkey temperature to 350 °F and roast turkey, basting every 20 minutes with pan juices (or margarine and chicken broth), about 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until meat thermometer inserted in thick part of meat registers 165 °F.
Remove to carving board and let rest for 10 minutes.

name: Roasted Bell Peppers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042308/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-bell-peppers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 450 degrees F.
Wash bell peppers and remove tops and seeds. Cut peppers in half and rub with vegetable oil.
Place cut side up on a rimmed baking sheet and sprinkle with Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Roast until peppers are tender and blistered in spots, about 30 to 35 minutes.

notes.text: No Italian seasoning? Use 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 1 teaspoon dried basil, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder.

name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045746/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-brussels-sprouts
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Wash and trim Brussels sprouts. Cut large Brussels sprouts in half from top to bottom; leave small Brussels sprouts whole.
In a large bowl, toss Brussels sprouts with the oil, salt, and pepper.
Place Brussels sprouts in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Lining the baking sheet with foil or baking parchment will help with clean-up.
Roast for 20 to 30 minutes, stirring once after 10 to 15 minutes. Sprouts should be tender and browned.
Remove from oven and drizzle with lemon juice.

notes.text: Try adding other seasonings with the lemon juice such as red pepper flakes or parmesan cheese.

name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts, Potatoes, and Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034024/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-brussels-sprouts-potatoes-and-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups Brussels sprouts (fresh or frozen halved vertically, about 3/4 pound)
1/2 cup non-fat ricotta cheese (or cottage cheese)

steps: Preheat oven to 325 °F.
In a 2 quart baking dish coated with cooking spray, toss Brussels sprouts, potatoes, onion, and garlic with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper.
In a small bowl, mix cheese with milk.
Coat chicken breasts with remaining olive oil.
Nest among vegetables in baking dish.
Top with cheese mix.
Cover with foil and bake for 40 to 45 minutes or until chicken is done.

notes.text: Serve with 8 ounce non-fat milk and orange slices.

name: Roasted Cauliflower
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215251/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-cauliflower
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Remove outer leaves of cauliflower. Cut florets off the stem. Wash and drain.
Combine oil, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Toss the cauliflower florets in the oil mixture.
Spread cauliflower on a large rimmed baking sheet.
Roast in the oven at 450 degrees F for 15 to 20 minutes until the cauliflower starts to soften and begins to brown.
Sprinkle with cheese. Continue to roast for 5 to 10 minutes.

name: Roasted Cauliflower Steaks
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044226/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-cauliflower-steaks
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Lightly grease a large baking sheet.
Slice cauliflower from top to bottom through the core into 1- to 1 1/2- inch thick steaks. Put steaks on the baking sheet along with end pieces, flat side down.
In a small bowl, mix the rest of the ingredients, except cheese.
Spoon on and spread or brush the cauliflower with half the mixture. Roast for 20 minutes.
Remove baking sheet from the oven, carefully turn the steaks and spread the rest of the mixture. Roast for 15 to 20 minutes or until the cauliflower is browned and tender.
Sprinkle with cheese, if desired, and serve.

name: Roasted Chickpeas (Garbanzo Beans)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021353/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-chickpeas-garbanzo-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15 ounces) low-sodium garbanzo beans, drained and rinsed
1 tablespoon canola oil (or cooking oil of choice)
spices of your choice, optional (try garlic, paprika, sage, etc.)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Drain and rinse the beans until there is no foamy residue. Pick out the skins and discard. Wrap the drained beans in a clean towel to dry thoroughly.
Measure oil into a 9x13-inch baking dish or foil lined pan. Pour beans into dish, sprinkle with salt and spices. Mix oil and spices well to coat all the beans.
Bake for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring or shaking every 15 minutes. Longer makes more crunch, but watch to prevent burning!

name: Roasted Herb Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035236/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-herb-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound potatoes (3 medium or 3 cups cubed)
2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F.
Coat a baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray.
Wash and peel the potatoes.
Cut the potatoes into 1/2-inch cubes, and put them in a large bowl.
Put the oil, rosemary, and salt in a small bowl. Stir together.
Pour the oil mix over the potatoes. Stir to coat the potatoes evenly.
Spread the potatoes on the baking sheet.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until lightly browned.

name: Roasted Pork Tacos with Pico de Gallo
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034031/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-pork-tacos-pico-de-gallo
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup red onion, cut into small cubes

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pico de gallo: In a bowl, mix all the ingredients. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Seasoning: In a small bowl, mix the paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Remove the silver skin from the pork tenderloin, rub it with oil and coat the entire loin with the seasoning.
Place the pork tenderloin on the grill at medium/high heat (400˚F), over indirect heat, for approximately 6 minutes on each side, 18 minutes total.
Cook until it reaches internal temperature of 145˚F with a 3-minute rest. Then chop it into small pieces.
To make the tacos, heat the tortillas and place some pork tenderloin and pico de gallo on top.

name: Roasted Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043940/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup green pepper, chopped into 1-inch cubes

steps: In a medium-sized bowl, mix potatoes, onions, green peppers, and garlic.
Add vegetable oil, salt, and pepper to bowl. If using parsley and paprika, add that too. Mix well.
Cover bowl and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Spread potato mixture evenly on a cookie sheet. Bake for about 35 minutes. Serve hot.

name: Roasted Pumpkin Seed Snack Mix
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043311/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-pumpkin-seed-snack-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups crispy rice or wheat cereal squares

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together and serve.

name: Roasted Root Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034627/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-root-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 root vegetables (choose a variety from potatoes, rutabagas, turnips, parsnips, beets, sweet potatoes, etc.) (medium)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Cut vegetables into large chunks.
Place in a medium-sized bowl and pour oil over top. Add seasonings or Parmesan and mix well.
Spread an even layer on a baking sheet or pan.
Bake for 1 hour or until tender. Check a few vegetables to see if they are tender.

name: Roasted Tomatoes with Herbs
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035242/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/roasted-tomatoes-herbs
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 degrees F.
Spray a large baking sheet with cooking oil spray.
Cut each tomato in half. Place tomatoes on the sheet, cut side up.
Drizzle tomatoes with 1 tablespoon of oil and season with pepper.
Cook for 30 minutes, or until tomatoes are beginning to brown on the bottom.
Mix the remaining oil, parsley, garlic, and cheese in a small bowl.
Remove tomatoes from the oven and sprinkle the herb mixture over the tomatoes.
Return to oven for another 10 minutes, or until spices begin to brown.

name: Round Steak Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034924/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/round-steak-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 pounds round steak, cut 1/2 inch thick
1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium French-style green beans, drained
1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium tomatoes, peeled and whole

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Season round steak lightly with garlic salt, salt and pepper.
Cut into serving pieces and place in crock pot with sliced onion, which has been separated into rings.
Add potatoes and green beans.
Top with tomato soup and tomatoes.
Cover and cook on Low for 8 hours.
Remove cover during last half-hour if there is too much liquid.
To cook in 2-quart crock pot, reduce ingredients slightly.

notes.text: Menu Idea: round steak casserole, canned pears, lowfat milk

name: Salad with Pineapple, Nuts, and Raisins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034302/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/salad-pineapple-nuts-and-raisins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup vegetables, chopped (tomatoes, cucumbers, carrots, green beans)
1 cup canned pineapple chunks (in juice), drained (or fresh orange segments)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put mixed salad greens on a large platter or in a salad bowl.
In a large bowl, mix chopped vegetables and pineapple or orange segments. Spoon onto the mixed greens.
Mix vinegar, orange juice, and yogurt in a small bowl and pour dressing over salad greens and vegetables.
Top with nuts and raisins. Serve.

notes.text: Tomatoes used in nutrition and cost analysis for vegetables.

name: Salata Ma Jibna (Salad with Parmesan Cheese)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050715/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/salata-ma-jibna-salad-parmesan-cheese
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup onions, cut into slivers or thin slices
1 cup cabbage, cut into slivers or thin slices
1/2 cup carrots, cut into very thin slices

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a salad bowl, combine onions, cabbage, carrots, and tomatoes.
Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Sprinkle garlic and Parmesan over salad.

notes.text: Salata Ma Jibna is a Sudanese dish.

name: Salmon Burgers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031853/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/salmon-burgers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (16 ounces) salmon (OR two 5 oz cans of tuna in water, drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, mix all ingredients together. Mixture will be moist.
Spray a large skillet with non-stick cooking spray. Heat skillet.
Drop fish mixture onto the skillet using a 1/3 or 1/2 cup measuring cup. Brown on both sides.

notes.text: *Dry bread crumbs, crushed unsweetened cereal, or uncooked oatmeal can be used instead of cracker crumbs.

name: Salmon Burgers and Sweet Potato Oven Fries
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042328/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/salmon-burgers-and-sweet-potato-oven-fries
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: For the Sweet Potato Oven Fries:
1 tablespoon lemon pepper seasoning blend (low sodium)

steps: Place oven rack in center, heat oven to 425 °F.
Wash and scrub sweet potatoes, slice into wedges, length-wise.
In a large bowl, toss potato wedges with canola oil and seasoning.
Spread on cookie sheet. Roast in the oven, turning occasionally, until tender and golden brown, about 30 to 40 minutes.
While sweet potatoes are roasting, prepare salmon burgers. Drain salmon; place in a medium mixing bowl and flake.
Fold in green onions and red pepper, crushed crackers, lemon juice, egg whites, and yogurt.
Shape into 4 patties.
Coat large nonstick skillet lightly with cooking spray; heat.
Cook salmon burgers until golden brown, turn, and continue cooking until other side is golden brown.
Serve burgers with sliced tomatoes and lettuce, and sweet potato oven fries.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of 100% berry juice blend.

name: Salmon Loaf
