attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215100/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/salmon-loaf
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees F.
Drain salmon and remove skin if desired. Mash bones with meat.
Add the other ingredients.
Add enough milk so that the mixture is moist but not runny.
Place in a lightly oiled 9x5 inch loaf pan.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Serve.

name: Salmon Patties
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031907/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/salmon-patties
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/3 cup bread crumbs or cracker crumbs

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash fresh vegetables (if using).
Collect, mince, and measure all ingredients before starting to prepare the recipe.
Open salmon, and drain liquid into a liquid measuring cup. Add lemon juice and cold water to the salmon liquid to make 1/2 cup liquid total, and set aside.
Put the salmon in a separate mixing bowl. Mix in the celery (if using), green pepper (if using), and onion.
In another small bowl, beat the eggs. Then, add them to the salmon mixture.
Add the bread or cracker crumbs, flour, pepper, and the salmon liquid mixture to the salmon mixture, and stir until all ingredients are mixed together.
Use 1/3 cup measuring cup to measure salmon mixture. Shape into a 1/2 inch thick patty, and place on a plate. Repeat to make 6 patties.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat, then add 3 patties.
Cook for about 2 to 3 minutes (or until golden brown) on each side.
Remove patties from skillet, and place on a clean paper towel-lined plate to drain. Cook remaining 3 patties, then serve immediately. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Eat within 3 to 5 days.

name: Salmon Spread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031333/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/salmon-spread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 green onion, chopped (or 1/4 cup onion, or onion powder to taste)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain salmon and flake with a fork into a bowl.
Mix in all other ingredients.
Serve on bread, crackers, or a rice cake.
Sprinkle chopped parsley to garnish.

name: Salsa Pinto Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021403/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/salsa-pinto-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 clove garlic, minced (or 1/8 teaspoon garlic powder)
2 cans (15 ounces each) low-sodium pinto beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until tender.
Stir in the beans and salsa.
Cook for 10 minutes.
Serve over rice, pasta, or baked potato.

name: Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032524/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/salsa1
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cans (14.5 ounces) low-sodium diced tomatoes, drained
1 can (4.5 ounces) diced green chiles, drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, stir together all the ingredients until well mixed. Cover and chill at least 4 hours.
Serve with Baked Tortilla Chips or raw vegetables.

name: Sanchico Tuna Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031340/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sanchico-tuna-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can chunk light tuna (in water, 6.5 ounce can)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain tuna. Transfer to a mixing bowl and mix well with avocado for texture.
Add tomatoes, onion, lime juice, crushed red pepper, salt, and mango.

name: Sarah’s Green Bean Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034945/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sarahs-green-bean-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Blanch the green beans in boiling water for about 4 minutes for crisper beans or longer for a softer texture. Then plunge in ice water. Drain and set aside.
Place diced onions and mushrooms in a microwaveable bowl and microwave for about 2 1/2 minutes on high to soften. Set aside.
Melt the butter over medium heat. Once melted, stir in flour with a whisk and cook for about 1 minute (continuously whisking).
Whisk in the milk and cook over low heat until you have a thick white sauce.
Stir in Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, black pepper, and salt.
Stir the drained green beans, onions, and mushrooms into the white sauce (including any liquid with the onions and mushrooms).
Pour into a casserole dish sprayed with nonstick spray. Crush the crackers and toss cracker crumbs with olive oil and onion powder. Sprinkle over the top of the casserole.
Bake at 350 °F for about 30 minutes or until crackers are golden brown.
serving_size: 1 portion of Sarah's Green Bean Casserole

name: Sarah’s Spicy Curry Turkey Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231014715/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sarahs-spicy-curry-turkey-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Heat the olive oil and butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook for about 7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in flour, curry powder, and cinnamon and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth and scrape up any brown bits at the bottom of the pan.
Bring to a simmer. Then add carrots, spinach, potatoes, and turkey.
Bring to a boil. Then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer (covered) for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve in bowls and garnish with a spoonful of cranberry sauce.
serving_size: 1 cup of Sarah's Spicy Curry Turkey Soup

name: Sardine, Cucumber, and Tomato Sandwich
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021912/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sardine-cucumber-and-tomato-sandwich
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cans sardines, water packed (4 oz cans, drained)
1 red or white onion (peeled and thinly sliced)

steps: Put 4 slices toasted bread on the cutting board. Arrange cucumber slices on top of each slice.
Distribute the sardines evenly on top of the cucumber and using the fork, gently mash them. Spread the mashed sardines to cover the cucumber. Squeeze the lemon juice over the sardines.
Put the tomato slices on top of the sardines. Add the red onion. Top with the remaining slices of toast and press down gently to hold the sandwich together.
Cut the sandwich in half and serve right away.

notes.text: Canned tuna or salmon can be used instead of sardines

name: Sautéed Beet Greens
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040457/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sauteed-beet-greens
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
4 cups chopped beet greens (2 bunches with stems removed)
2 cloves garlic, minced (or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a medium-sized pan over medium heat.
Add the beet greens and garlic to the pan. Stir until just wilted, then reduce the heat to low and stir occasionally until soft, about 5 to 8 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice, red pepper flakes, and salt. Serve right away or use in another recipe.

notes.text: No beet greens? Use other leafy greens such as mustard greens or chard.

name: Sautéed Cabbage and Onion
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032140/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sauteed-cabbage-and-onion
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large sauté pan.
Sauté onion over medium heat, until light brown, about 5 to 6 minutes.
Add sliced cabbage, salt, black pepper, and caraway seeds.
Stir and cook for 30 minutes.
Serve immediately.

name: Sautéed Cauliflower Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041835/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sauteed-cauliflower-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 clove garlic, minced (or 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder)
1 medium cauliflower (grated or finely chopped, 4 to 5 cups)
1 tablespoon lemon juice or lime juice (optional)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley or cilantro (optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large skillet or saucepan on medium heat. Add onion and cook until soft, 3 to 5 minutes.
Add garlic, cauliflower, salt, and pepper. Stir until cauliflower is tender, 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice and sprinkle with parsley, if desired. Serve warm.

name: Sautéed Walleye with Tarragon
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020437/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sauteed-walleye-tarragon
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 walleye fillets (4–6 ounces each), thawed and patted dry
1 teaspoon chopped fresh tarragon or parsley (or 1/2 teaspoon dried)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Season walleye on the flesh side with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with tarragon or parsley and press lightly into the flesh to help it stick.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium high heat.
Place the fillets seasoned side down in the pan, tilting the pan to make sure the butter surrounds the fillets, and cook for about 3 minutes.
Gently flip the fillets and cook on the second side, about 2 minutes. Walleye should reach a final internal cook temperature of 145 °F as measured with a food thermometer before serving.
Plate and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

notes.text: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.

name: Savory Bread Pudding with Kale and Butternut Squash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021908/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/savory-bread-pudding-kale-and-butternut-squash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup shredded low-sodium mozzarella or cheddar cheese

steps: Preheat the oven to 375 °F. Lightly grease a 2-quart baking pan.
Put a skillet over medium heat and when it is hot, add the oil. Add the onion and cook about 10 minutes, until tender.
While the onion is cooking, put eggs and milk in a bowl and mix until combined.
Add the cheese, bread, kale, squash, and salt and mix well. Let the mixture stand at least 15 minutes until the bread absorbs most of the milk.
When the onion has finished cooking, add it to the bread mixture and mix well.
Pour the mixture into the prepared pan and transfer to the oven.
Bake uncovered for 50 to 60 minutes until lightly browned and set. Let stand 15 minutes before serving.

notes.text: It is important to use stale bread that has dried out. If you don’t have stale bread, put fresh bread in a preheated 250 °F oven and bake until dried, usually about 15 minutes.

name: Savory Meatloaf Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041800/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/savory-meatloaf-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Spoon mixture and divide evenly into 12 greased muffin cups.
Bake for 1 hour, or until temperature in center of meatloaf is 160 °F.
Cool slightly before removing from muffin cups.

name: Savory and Spicy Ground Beef & Succotash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021341/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/savory-spicy-ground-beef-succotash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup frozen lima beans, cooked and drained
1 3/4 cups low-sodium corn (15 1/2 ounce can, drained)
1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium tomatoes, broken up

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef in 9-inch skillet. Drain excess liquid.
Stir in remaining ingredients except nutmeg. Cover and simmer 5 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Sprinkle with nutmeg before serving.

name: Scallion Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031940/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/scallion-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 1/2 cups brown rice, cooked in unsalted water

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook rice according to directions on the package.
Combine the cooked rice, bouillon granules, and scallions and mix well.
Measure 1-cup portions and serve.

name: Scalloped Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020807/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/scalloped-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash potatoes; peel and slice into thin slices.
Melt 1 tablespoon of margarine in heavy, deep skillet. Remove skillet from heat; spread half of potato slices in skillet.
Cover potatoes with onions. Sprinkle half of flour and pepper over potato mixture.
Add remaining potato slices, flour, and pepper. Cut 1 tablespoon of margarine into small pieces and place on top of potato mixture.
Pour milk over potato mixture; bring to boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium low, cover, and cook until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.

notes.text: Leave potato skins on for more nutrition!

name: Scalloped Potatoes and Chicken with Fennel
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032850/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/scalloped-potatoes-and-chicken-fennel
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Place rack in center of oven and preheat to 350 °F.
Leaving skin on, thinly slice potatoes.
Cut stalks and fronds from fennel bulb. Discard stalk. Thinly slice fennel bulb. Chop fennel fronts and set aside.

Place potato and fennel slices in 2-quart covered baking dish, and add water to cover vegetables. Cover with lid and microwave on high for about 5 minutes. Let cool slightly and drain vegetables into a colander.
Wipe baking dish dry and spray with cooking spray. Add vegetables back to dish and sprinkle with minced garlic.
Cut chicken breasts in half (total of four pieces). Place atop the potato-fennel mix.

In a bowl, mix melted margarine and flour into a smooth paste. Add 1 1/4 cups skim milk, salt, and pepper, stir until smooth. Pour over chicken, potatoes, and fennel. Cover baking dish and place in oven. Bake about 30 minutes.

Mix remaining milk with sour cream. Increases oven temperature to 425 °F. Remove dish from oven. Spread with sour cream mixture and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and fennel fronds. Return to oven uncovered and bake an additional 10 minutes until top is golden and bubbling. Internal temperature of chicken should be 165 °F.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serving with 8 ounce glass of sparkling water and 1/2 orange, sliced.

name: Scalloped Potatoes II
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041317/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/scalloped-potatoes-ii
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 russet potatoes, medium, 3 to 4 inch (peeled and sliced into 1/4 inch slices)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare a large casserole baking pan by coating lightly with oil or cooking oil spray.
Place a layer of potatoes in pan, using approximately 1/4 of potatoes.
Sprinkle layer with 1/4 cup chopped raw onion, 1/2 tablespoon margarine, 1 tablespoon flour, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and sprinkling of black pepper.
Repeat layers, making a total of 4.
Meanwhile heat milk over low heat.
Pour warm milk over all ingredients in casserole dish.
Bake at 350 °F for 1 hour.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare a large casserole baking pan by coating lightly with oil or cooking oil spray.
Make a white sauce by melting margarine in a small pan. Stir in flour. Gradually add milk, stirring constantly.
Cook, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened. Remove from heat.
Add salt and pepper.
Place a layer of potatoes and onion in a prepared casserole pan, using approximately 1/4 of the potatoes and 1/4 cup onion.
Spread with 1/2 cup of the sauce prepared in steps 2 and 3.
Repeat layers, making a total of 4.
Bake at 350 °F for 1 hour.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Quickest Method: Creamiest Method:

notes.text: Leave potato skins on for more nutrition!

name: Scrambled Eggs and Zucchini
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034040/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/scrambled-eggs-zucchini
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon garlic and herb seasoning mix
1/4 cup cheese, low-fat shredded (use your favorite)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and chop zucchini, measure out about 2 cups.
Dice the onion and pepper, set aside along with the zucchini.
Stir the egg and milk together and set aside.
Sauté the vegetables in oil on medium heat. Remove from the pan.
Scramble the egg mixture until cooked thoroughly. Stir in the vegetable mixture and fold together.
Cook together until temperature reaches 145 °F.
Sprinkle the seasoning and cheese on top. When the cheese is melted, serve warm.
Add fresh or other dried herbs as desired.

name: Scrambled Tofu
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021739/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/scrambled-tofu
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain tofu.
In small bowl, dice or mash tofu. For optional ingredients, crush garlic and/or slice watercress, mushrooms, cheese, bell peppers, and green onions.
In a pan, melt butter. Add tofu. Add bean sprouts and optional ingredients. Saute over medium heat until lightly browned.
Beat eggs and add to tofu mixture. Cook until firm.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir and cook until firm.

notes.text: Optional ingredients: garlic, watercress, mushrooms, cheese, bell peppers, green onions, and chop suey mix.

name: Seared Greens
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045331/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/seared-greens
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 cups kale or collard greens (1 1/2 pounds)
2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Clean the greens thoroughly and cut stems away. Dry well and tear into salad pieces or slice across leaf into 1/2 inch pieces.
In a large deep pot or skillet with a cover, sauté garlic in oil over medium heat.
Add greens in pan with 1 cup water.
Cover pan and steam for 4 minutes.
Uncover, stir constantly until greens shrink. Add salt and pepper and continue to stir on high until mixture is thoroughly wet.
Sprinkle cider vinegar on mixture. Cover.
Turn off heat. Let stand until ready to serve.

notes.text: You can also try this recipe using turnip greens, mustard greens, spinach, swiss chard, or beet greens.

name: Seasoned Roasted Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033955/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/seasoned-roasted-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 medium yellow squashes, washed and sliced
1/2 medium bell pepper (green or red), washed, seeded, and sliced
1/4 cup fat free Italian salad dressing

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Stir vegetables and dressing in large bowl.
Spread vegetables in the center sheet of aluminum foil on top of baking sheet.
Bring together and seal to make packet.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes.

name: Sesame Turnips and Carrots
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044955/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sesame-turnips-and-carrots
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
4 cloves garlic, minced (or 1 teaspoon garlic powder)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet on medium-high heat, add oil and sauté turnips, carrots, and salt until vegetables begin to soften.
Stir in garlic and sesame seeds and cook until vegetables begin to brown.
Stir in honey. Serve warm.

notes.text: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Shake-A-Pudding
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034405/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/shake-pudding
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 carton (3.4 ounces) instant vanilla pudding mix
2 bananas, peeled and sliced (or other sliced fruit)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place 2 cups of milk in a quart jar with tight-fitting lid.
Add one small package of instant vanilla pudding mix to the jar; screw lid on jar.
Shake until mixture is smooth.
Place pieces of fruit in a serving bowl or paper cups.
Pour pudding over fruit and chill.

name: Shepherd's Pie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035403/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/shepherds-pie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place diced potatoes in saucepan. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer (about 15 minutes).
Drain potatoes and mash. Stir in milk and set aside.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Brown turkey in a large skillet. Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add vegetables and broth. Bring to a slow boil.
Spoon vegetable-meat mixture into an 8-inch square baking dish. Spread potatoes over mixture. Bake 25 minutes.
Serve hot. Garnish with shredded cheese (optional).

name: Shirini
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034836/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/shirini
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 winter squash (1 1/4 pounds of butternut, acorn, or pumpkin)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil the sugar and water until it forms a thick syrup in a medium saucepan.
Wash the pumpkin, peel it, remove the seeds, cut into pieces, and cook in the syrup until it is very thick and almost all absorbed.
Arrange the pumpkin on a plate and decorate with walnuts and cinnamon (optional).

name: Shorba (Lamb and Peanut Soup)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022129/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/shorba-lamb-and-peanut-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 pounds lamb bones (or lean beef ribs)
1/2 pound carrots, peeled and cut into chunks (3-4 medium carrots or 12 baby carrots)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a 6-quart saucepan, simmer bones in 2 quarts of water and 2 teaspoons of salt (optional) for one hour.
Add onions, carrots, cabbage, string beans, and garlic.
Simmer for one hour until vegetables are thoroughly cooked.
Remove lamb bones and purée the mixture.
Add 4 tablespoons peanut butter thinned with lemon juice.
Add cooked rice (optional).
Add salt and pepper to taste.

notes.text: Shorba is a Sudanese dish based around lamb. In Sudan, lamb bones commonly are used to flavor the soup-like dish.

name: Short Cut Lasagna
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214814/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/short-cut-lasagna
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 (15 ounce) container part-skim ricotta cheese (or cottage cheese)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spready 1/2 the sauce on the bottom of a 2-quart baking dish or pan.
Layer half the dry noodles, ricotta, and Parmesan.
Top with 1 cup sauce and layer rest of the noodles, ricotta, and mozzarella.
Top with remaining spaghetti sauce.
Bake 60 minutes at 350 °F. Remove and let is set for 20 minutes. Top with Parmesan cheese.

notes.text: Add browned, drained meat or cooked vegetables if desired. Mix with middle layer of sauce. Spinach would make a fantastic addition.

name: Shrimp Confetti Salad Sandwich with Grapes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041737/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/shrimp-confetti-salad-sandwich-grapes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 pound frozen cooked cocktail shrimp (thawed, peeled, and deveined)
1 8-oz can yellow corn kernels (reduced sodium, drained)
1 cup canned black beans (low sodium, drained and rinsed)
4 leaves Bibb lettuce or other leaf lettuce

steps: Chop shrimp coarsely.
Mix together shrimp salad ingredients (everything except for the bread, tomato slices, and lettuce).
Divide salad evenly among 4 slices of bread; spread to edges of bread.
Top with tomato slices, lettuce, and second bread slice.

name: Simmered Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031328/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/simmered-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups dried beans, rinsed (pinto, black, or pink)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place beans, water, onion, and bay leaf in a large pot.
Cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1 to 1 1/2 hours or until beans are tender.
Remove bay leaf and stir in salt. Cook 15 minutes longer.
Top each serving of simmered beans with 1/2 cup fresh salsa, or store beans in refrigerator for up to 3 days in a covered plastic or glass container.

name: Simple Fish Tacos
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034847/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/simple-fish-tacos
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound cod or white fish fillets, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
2 cups red and green cabbage, shredded

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, combine sour cream, mayonnaise, cilantro, and 2 tablespoons seasoning mix.

In a medium bowl, combine cod, oil, lemon juice, and remaining seasoning mix; pour into large skillet. Cook stirring constantly, over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes or until cod flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Fill warm tortillas with fish mixture.
Top with cabbage, tomato, sour cream mixture, lime wedges, and taco sauce.

name: Simple Green Smoothie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021133/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/simple-green-smoothie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup low-fat milk (or fortified soy, coconut, or almond milk)
1 cup frozen fruit (all one fruit or a combination of mixed frozen fruit)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add the kale or spinach and the liquid of your choice to a blender. Blend.
Add in the rest of the ingredients, blending after each item.
Serve and enjoy, cold.
Reserve the leftover smoothie in the refrigerator for later in the day or the next day.

notes.text: Consume within 24 hours.

name: Simply Satisfying Kale and Tuna Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031912/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/simply-satisfying-kale-and-tuna-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash kale. Set aside to drain water off.
Cut tomatoes in half and lightly toss in bowl with balsamic vinegar, oil, and pinch of salt and pepper. Set aside.
In a salad bowl, mix tuna and juice from the can gently with the squeeze of 1/2 lemon and a pinch of pepper.
Massage kale for about 3 minutes to soften it.
Add the kale and 1/2 the tomatoes to the tuna. Gently toss until all is coated with dressing.
Add remaining tomatoes.
Squeeze remaining lemon all over and serve.

name: Skillet-Braised Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033031/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/skillet-braised-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 medium chicken breast, about 1-inch thick, skinless
1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
seasoning, such as salt, pepper, seasoning salt, onion powder or garlic powder (optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Season the chicken. In a lightly oiled medium skillet over medium-high heat, sauté the chicken for one minute on each side until lightly browned.
Cover the skillet with a tight-fitting lid. Reduce the heat to low. Cook for 10 minutes. Do not lift the lid.
Turn off the heat. Let the chicken rest for 10 minutes. Do not remove the lid.

The chicken is safely cooked when the internal temperature is at least 165 degrees F. Check in the thickest part with a food thermometer. If not done, cover and return to low heat for 3 to 5 minutes and check for doneness.

name: Skillet Catfish
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024927/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/skillet-catfish
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Make the spice rub. Put the cornmeal, oregano, cayenne pepper, thyme, paprika, salt, and pepper on a plate and combine well.
Dredge both sides of the catfish in the spice mixture.
Put the skillet on the stove and turn the heat to high.
When the skillet is hot, add the oil. Add the fish and cook about 4 minutes on each side, until browned and cooked throughout.
Serve right away garnished with lemon or lime wedges.

notes.text: Use cod or tilapia instead of catfish.

name: Skillet Lasagna
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045407/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/skillet-lasagna
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 ounces lasagna noodles (or 4 cups of any other type of pasta, uncooked)
1 container of ricotta cheese, part-skim, 15 ounces (or cottage cheese)
1 package frozen spinach, thawed & squeezed dry (10 ounces, or chopped broccoli)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook the noodles as directed on the package. Drain and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix the ricotta cheese (or cottage cheese), 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese, and Italian seasoning.
Spray a large skillet well with cooking spray. Do NOT place skillet on heat until all ingredients are in skillet.
Spread half of the jar of sauce in skillet. Top with half the cooked noodles (4 lasagna noodles).
Spread half of the cheese mixture over the noodles. Top with half the spinach or broccoli.
Sprinkle half the mozzarella cheese over the vegetables.
Repeat with the remaining noodles, the remaining cheese mixture, the remaining vegetables, the remaining sauce, and the remaining mozzarella cheese.
Sprinkle with the rest of the Parmesan cheese. Cover.
Turn on the stove top to medium-low until the cheese is melted (approximately 20 minutes). Allow to stand for 5 minutes before serving.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Eat within 3 to 5 days.

notes.text: Thaw spinach in the refrigerator overnight or in the microwave on low power. Once thawed, wrap the spinach in a clean towel, and twist to wring out the water.

name: Skillet Meals
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031413/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/skillet-meals
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 package broccoli (10 ounce, frozen, can also use mustard greens, collard greens or spinach)
2 cans stewed tomatoes, low sodium (about 30 oz)
1 can white beans (15 ounces, rinsed and drained)
oregano, basil, or hot pepper (other spices to taste, optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Steam greens in the stewed tomatoes using a small pan, pot, or electric skillet on medium-high heat.
Cook greens 10 to 20 minutes, until they are as soft as you like them. Stir gently.
Add the rice, canned beans, and seasonings.
Cook until heated through.

notes.text: Learn morre about:

name: Skillet Noodles and Beef
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035622/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/skillet-noodles-and-beef
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef in a large skillet. Drain and rinse to remove fat.
Add onion, tomato sauce, water, and spices. Cover and bring to a boil.
Add noodles. Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Defrost spinach in the microwave. Stir spinach into skillet mixture. Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir mixture. Spoon cottage cheese on top and sprinkle with shredded mozzarella. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes. Add water if mixture gets too dry.

name: Skillet Pasta Dinner
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042456/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/skillet-pasta-dinner
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 pound 85% lean ground turkey (or ground sausage or beef)
8 ounces uncooked tube pasta (ziti, penne, or macaroni)
2 cups fresh or frozen vegetables (try zucchini and carrots)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown the ground meat, onion, and garlic in a large skillet or heavy saucepan. Drain off any grease.
Add the tomato sauce, water, and uncooked pasta.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the fresh or frozen vegetables. Stir and continue cooking until the pasta and vegetables are tender, about 10 more minutes.

notes.text: Frozen vegetables used for nutritional analysis and costing purposes. Learn more about:

name: Skinny Pizza
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042549/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/skinny-pizza
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups sliced mushrooms (white button or baby portobello)
1 green bell pepper, thinly sliced (about 1 cup)
1/2 cup tomato sauce, no salt added

steps: Heat oven to 400°F.
Place tortillas on 2 large baking sheets.
Cook, flipping once, until crisp (about 10 minutes). Set aside.
Meanwhile, heat oil in large skillet over medium heat. Add mushrooms, peppers, onions, and garlic.
Cook until all vegetables are soft and tender (about 10 minutes). Set aside.

Spread tortilla crust with 2 tablespoons tomato sauce, 1/4 cup vegetable mixture, 2 tablespoons mozzarella cheese, and 1/2 teaspoon of Parmesan cheese. Repeat with remaining crusts and topping ingredients.
Transfer pizzas to same baking sheets.
Cook until cheese is melted and edges of tortillas are golden brown (about 10 minutes).

name: Sloppy Garden Joes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034602/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sloppy-garden-joes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 whole wheat buns, split in half to make 12

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sauté onions, carrots, green pepper, and ground turkey or chicken in a large pan over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add tomato sauce, crushed tomatoes, mushrooms, barbecue sauce, and bring to boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and cook for an additional 3 minutes or until thick.
Serve open-faced on toasted or plain whole-wheat buns.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

notes.text: You can also use 8 ounce of fresh mushrooms instead of canned.

name: Slow-Cook Barbecue
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231004802/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/slow-cook-barbecue
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 pounds boneless chuck steak, boneless, 1 1/2-inches thick
1/4 cup ketchup (add more ketchup if desired)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the beef on a diagonal, across the grain into slices 1 inch wide and place in a slow cooker.
Combine the remaining ingredients and pour over the meat.
Mix the meat and sauce together.
Cover and cook on low for 3 to 5 hours.
Serve on toasted hamburger buns with a mixed green salad.

name: Slow Cooker Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020604/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/slow-cooker-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound pinto beans (16 ounce dried, rinsed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix beans, water, onion, and chili powder in slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 7 hours or until tender. Drain.
Stir in barbecue sauce, ketchup, mustard, and pepper sauce.
Cook on high for 15 minutes or until hot through.

name: Slow Cooker Beef Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040405/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/slow-cooker-beef-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 pounds stew meat, cut into 1-inch cubes
add herbs as desired (bay leaf, basil, oregano, etc.) (optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place meat in slow cooker.
Mix flour, salt, and pepper in a medium bowl, and pour over meat; stir to coat.
Add remaining ingredients and stir to mix.
Cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or high for 4 to 6 hours.
Stir stew thoroughly before serving. If using bay leaf, discard before serving.

name: Slow Cooker Cheesy Swiss Steak
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031301/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/slow-cooker-cheesy-swiss-steak
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the beef roast into 4 pieces.
In a small bowl, mix the flour and salt.
Dip each piece of meat into the mix of flour and salt. Coat it on all sides with the mix.
Put the meat in the crock pot.
Add the chopped carrots and onion.
Add the Worcestershire sauce and tomato sauce.
Cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours, OR on high for 4-5 hours.
Just before serving, sprinkle the cheese on top.

name: Slow Cooker Hamburger Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260106050827/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/slow-cooker-hamburger-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: oregano, basil, or other herbs (1/2 teaspoon, optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef in a medium fry pan. Drain fat.
Place beef, chopped vegetables, tomatoes, and water in slow cooker.
Cook on low 8 to 10 hours or on high for 4 to 6 hours.

name: Slow Cooker Lentil Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041248/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/slow-cooker-lentil-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped (or 2 tablespoons dried)
2 teaspoons beef bouillon (or 2 cubes beef bouillon)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together in slow cooker.
Cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or high for 4 to 5 hours.
Serve hot with crackers or bread.

name: Slow Cooker Pork Stew over Brown Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041409/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/slow-cooker-pork-stew-over-brown-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 cups complete bran and wheat flakes ready-to-eat cereal (crushed to 3/4 cup)
3/4 cup 100% apple juice or apple cider

steps: Trim fat from pork.
Spray large pan with non-stick cooking spray. Cook half of the pork at a time until browned.
In a 4 to 6 quart crockery cooker, layer carrots, onion, thyme, pepper, salt, and garlic. Sprinkle with cereal and cherries.
Top with pork and pour apple juice or cider over contents in the cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours or on high for 3 1/2 to 4 hours.
Prepare the brown rice according to package directions toward the end of the stew cooking time. (Brown rice typically takes about 40 to 45 minutes to cook.)
Stir pork mixture and serve over 1/2 cup brown rice.

name: Smoked Ham Hocks with Lima Beans
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215243/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/smoked-ham-hocks-lima-beans
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Peel, rinse, and chop onion. Peel and mince garlic.

In a large pot over high heat, add ham hocks and water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer. Add onion and garlic. Cover and cook until meat is tender and internal temperature registers 145°F on a food thermometer, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Transfer ham hocks to a clean cutting board. Let cool.
Add lima beans to pot. Cook according to package directions.
When ham hocks are cool, shred meat from the bone, removing any fat. Return to pot. Stir in pepper. If using salt, stir in now.

name: Smoky Mustard-Maple Salmon
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040810/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/smoky-mustard-maple-salmon
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 teaspoon smoked paprika or ground chipotle pepper

steps: Preheat oven to 450 °F.
Line a baking sheet with foil and coat with cooking spray.
Combine mustard, maple syrup, paprika (or chipotle), pepper, and salt in a small bowl.
Place salmon fillets on the prepared baking sheet.
Spread the mustard mixture evenly on the salmon.
Roast until just cooked through (approximately 8 to 12 minutes).

name: Smothered Greens
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035150/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/smothered-greens
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 14 cups mustard greens, or turnip, collard, kale, or mixture (about 2 pounds)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare greens by washing thoroughly and removing stems.
Tear or slice leaves into bite-sized pieces.
To make the turkey stock, place all ingredients except greens into large saucepan and bring to a boil.
Add greens to turkey stock. Cook 20 to 30 minutes until tender.

name: Snappy Cole Slaw
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044318/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/snappy-cole-slaw
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and shred the cabbage with a knife or grater. Put in a mixing bowl.
Bring the vinegar and water to a boil in the saucepan. Remove from heat and add the sugar, mustard, and black pepper to the saucepan.
Continue to cook this mixture in the saucepan until the sugar is dissolved and hot, then pour over the shredded cabbage.
Toss. Refrigerate until chilled to blend flavors.

notes.text: Refrigeration is needed before serving. Learn more about:

name: Snappy Rice Dish
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025407/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/snappy-rice-dish
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup vegetables, frozen or fresh, cut into bite-sized pieces
1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth (or use water)
1/2 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans (or other canned beans)
dill weed, optional (fresh snipped or dry, to taste)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook the vegetables in the chicken broth (or water) using a small pan, pot, or electric skillet, on medium-high heat.*
Cook the vegetables the way you like them (firm or soft), stirring gently. Add more broth as needed to keep the vegetables moist.
Add the rice, canned beans, and seasonings. Cook until heated through.

* Microwave version: Follow the same steps above. Use a microwave-safe, covered dish. Stir the vegetables every 2 to 3 minutes. Just before they are cooked, add the rice, beans, and herbs. Cook until heated. Rotate the dish and stir gently.

notes.text: Try this recipe with peas, corn, carrots, or whatever veggies you like!

name: Soft Chicken Taco
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033959/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/soft-chicken-taco
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 chicken breasts, thawed, skin and bone removed from each piece
2/3 tablespoon taco seasoning or chili powder (optional)

steps: In a large bowl, mix chicken, vegetable oil, garlic, salt, and pepper.
If using taco seasoning or chili powder, add that too.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap, and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
While the chicken is in the refrigerator, cook the pepper and onion on a stovetop over medium heat until done (about 12 minutes).
Cook the chicken over medium heat. Cook each side about 10 to 15 minutes.
Place chicken on a plate. Let it cool for 5 minutes. Cut the chicken into strips.
To make the tacos, put chicken on the tortilla first. Add peppers and onion strips next. Top with lettuce, tomato, and salsa. If using parsley or cilantro, add that too.

notes.text: Tip for cooking chicken: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for chicken is 165°F, as measured by a food thermometer.

name: Soft Pretzels
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041355/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/soft-pretzels
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 degrees F. Lightly grease 2 baking sheets.
In large bowl, sprinkle yeast over warm water (if water is too hot, it will kill the yeast). Stir until well blended.
Combine white and wheat flour in a separate bowl.
Stir in sugar, salt and 2 1/2 to 3 cups flour to make a soft, sticky dough. Turn dough onto well-floured surface.

To knead, fold dough in half and push dough flat with heels of hands. Turn dough 1/4 turn. Repeat for 5 to 7 minutes. If needed, add more flour until dough is smooth and elastic. Dough should not stick to hands or counter.
Cut dough into 12 even pieces (about golf-ball sized).
Roll one piece of dough into 15 inch long rope.
Cross left side over middle, creating loop.
Fold right side of rope up and over first loop to form pretzel shape.
Place pretzels 3 inches apart on baking sheet. Enlarge holes in pretzels by inserting finger into holes. This will prevent them from closing during baking.
In small bowl, mix egg and 1 tablespoon water together. Brush on pretzels. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown. Best if eaten warm.
To Form Pretzels: To Bake:

name: Somali Summer Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050500/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/somali-summer-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 tablespoons olive oil (or oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine oil and lemon juice.
Dice all the fruits and vegetables and then add to the bowl.
Add salt and pepper to taste (optional).
Serve chilled.
Best served within 24 hours.

name: Soul-Healthy Cornbread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021253/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/soul-healthy-cornbread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F. Lightly spray and 8 inch square pan with vegetable oil cooking spray.
Mix dry ingredients in an medium-sized mixing bowl.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix well by hand.
Pour the batter into the sprayed pan and shake to make it level.
Bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, about 25 minutes.
Allow to cool, then cut into 12 squares.

name: South of the Border Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040720/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/south-border
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the sour cream, yogurt, and salsa.
Store the dip in a covered container if you don’t plan to eat it right away.
Keep the dip in the fridge until you serve it.

notes.text: Serve with baked tortilla chips, crackers, or bite-sized vegetables.

name: South of the Border Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042114/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/south-border-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups low-sodium canned corn (15.25 ounces each - drained and rinsed)
2 cans low-sodium black beans (15.5 ounces each - drained and rinsed)
1 can diced tomatoes with green chilies (10 ounces)
3 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
1/3 cup fresh squeezed lemon juice (can also use lime juice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the salad ingredients in a large bowl.
Mix the dressing ingredients in a small bowl.
Pour dressing over corn mixture and mix well.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

name: Southern Banana Pudding
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042051/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/southern-banana-pudding
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 (3.4 ounces each) boxes instant vanilla pudding and pie-filling mix

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix 3 1/2 cups of the milk with the pudding mixes. Beat the pudding mixture with a wire whisk for 2 minutes until it is well blended. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Fold 1 cup of the whipped topping into the pudding mix.

Arrange a layer of wafers on the bottom and sides of a 2-quart serving bowl. Drizzle 2 tablespoons of the remaining milk over the wafers. Add a layer of banana slices and top with one-third of the pudding.
Repeat layers, drizzling each wafer layer with remaining milk and ending with pudding. Spread the remaining whipped topping over the pudding.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours before serving.

name: Southwestern Pepper Cups
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021214/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/southwestern-pepper-cups
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 5 medium green bell pepper, halved and seeded (or use red or yellow peppers)
1 can (10.5 ounces) tomatoes with chilies, diced and undrained
1/2 can (15.2 ounces) low-sodium whole kernel corn, drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Blanch peppers in boiling water 2 to 3 minutes. Drain. Set aside.
Cook onion and garlic in oil in medium skillet over medium-high heat for 3 minutes.
Combine rice, tomatoes with chilies, corn, and onion mixture. Mix well.
Spoon into pepper halves, place on baking sheet coated with cooking spray.
Bake at 350 degrees F for 10 minutes or until hot. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake again at 350 degrees F for 5 to 10 minutes or until hot and cheese melts.

name: Soy Marinated Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040839/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/soy-marinated-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Slice the orange to make round slices and set aside.
Place 4 chicken breasts in a 1-gallon sized plastic zipper bag.
Add the liquid to the bag with the chicken.
Zipper the bag closed and gently massage to mix the liquids and evenly cover the chicken inside the bag.
Let the chicken marinate in the bag in the refrigerator for 4 or more hours.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Spray shallow oven-proof baking dish with non-stick spray large enough to place chicken in single layer in the baking dish.
Remove the chicken from the bag, place in a single layer in the baking dish. Throw away the zipper bag from the chicken.
Bake chicken uncovered for 20 minutes.
Turn the chicken over, cover with orange slices that were set aside, and bake 15 more minutes (total of 35 minutes).
Check with a food thermometer. Temperature should reach 165 °F.
Serve chicken topped with an orange slice from the baking dish if desired.

name: Spaghetti and Spinach Pesto
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031443/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spaghetti-and-spinach-pesto
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound whole wheat spaghetti, uncooked (or your favorite pasta shape)
1 package 10-ounce frozen spinach, thawed, well drained

steps: In a blender (or food processor), combine spinach, oil, Parmesan cheese, parsley, garlic, salt, and basil. Mix at medium speed until finely chopped.
Melt margarine in water. With blender or processor running, gradually pour in melted margarine mixture until blended.
Cook pasta according to package directions.
Toss pesto with cooked pasta.
Sprinkle feta on top and serve.

notes.text: Serving Suggestion: Serve with grilled chicken, side salad, skim milk, and apple slices.

name: Spaghetti with Quick Meat Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032751/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spaghetti-quick-meat-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound lean ground beef (90% or leaner)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain.
Meanwhile, heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion, carrot, and celery and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is beginning to brown, 5 to 8 minutes.
Stir in garlic and Italian seasoning; cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add beef and cook, stirring and breaking up with a spoon, until no longer pink, 3 to 5 minutes.
Increase heat to high. Stir in tomatoes and cook until thickened, 4 to 6 minutes.
Stir in parsley and salt. Serve the sauce over the pasta, sprinkled with cheese.

name: Spaghetti Squash with Tomatoes, Basil, and Parmesan
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041551/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spaghetti-squash-tomatoes-basil-and-parmesan
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons dried basil (or 1/2 cup fresh basil, chopped)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

Place the 2 squash halves, cut side down, in glass baking dish. Add about 1/4 cup water and cover with plastic wrap. Microwave on high 12 minutes or until soft when pressed. Let stand covered for 3 minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk oil, basil, oregano and 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese. Stir in tomatoes and season lightly with salt and pepper to taste.
Scrape squash out with a fork, add strands to tomato mixture, and toss until combined. Sprinkle with remaining 1 tablespoon Parmesan cheese.

name: Spanish Baked Fish
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034128/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spanish-baked-fish
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound perch fillets, fresh or frozen

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Lightly grease baking dish (9 x 13-inch) with butter or margarine.
Separate the fish into 4 fillets or pieces.
Put the fish pieces in the baking dish.
Peel the onion and cut it into slices.
Stir the onion, tomato sauce, and spices together in a small bowl.
Pour the onion-spice mix evenly over the fish pieces.
Bake about 10 to 20 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork.

name: Spanish Frittata
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040913/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spanish-frittata
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 °F.
Put the potatoes in a non-stick skillet on the stove and cover with cold water. Turn the heat to medium-high and cook about 15 minutes until the potatoes are easily pierced with a knife.
Drain the potatoes well and set aside to cool. Then peel and cut into 1-inch cubes.
Put the eggs, salt, and pepper in the bowl and mix well with a whisk.
Return the skillet on the stove and turn the heat to medium-high. Add the oil. Add onion and cook about 5 minutes until soft. Add the cubed potatoes.
Pour the egg mixture over the potatoes and onions. Press down with a spatula to make an even layer and shake gently to prevent sticking. Lower to medium heat and cook about 7 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and cook until the frittata is completely set, about 5 minutes.
Gently loosen frittata from the pan. Place a serving plate over the skillet and carefully invert the frittata onto the plate.
Slice into 4 wedges. Serve warm.

name: Spanish Omelet
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040015/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spanish-omelet
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice, or non-stick cooking spray)
black pepper and garlic salt with herbs (to taste)
3 ounces part skim mozzarella cheese, shredded

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Cook potatoes in boiling water until tender.
In a nonstick pan, add oil or vegetable spray and warm at medium heat.
Add the onion and sauté until brown. Add vegetables and sauté until tender but not brown.
In a medium mixing bowl, slightly beat the eggs and egg whites, pepper, garlic salt, and mozzarella cheese. Stir egg cheese mixture into the cooked vegetables.
Oil or spray a 10-inch pie pan or ovenproof skillet. Transfer potatoes and eggs mixture to pan. Spread with parmesan cheese and bake omelet until firm and brown on top, about 20 to 30 minutes.

name: Spanish Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032302/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spanish-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium chopped tomatoes, undrained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet cook green pepper and onion in oil until tender over medium heat.
Stir in the spices, rice, tomatoes with juice, and water.
Cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes or until rice is done.

name: Spiced Baked Squash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021604/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spiced-baked-squash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
Coat the baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray.
Wash the squash. Cut it in half lengthwise. Remove the seeds. Cut the squash into 1/2 inch slices.
Place the squash on the baking sheet. Sprinkle with salt.
Melt the margarine on low heat in a small saucepan.
Add the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger to the saucepan.
Spread the margarine mix on the squash.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, or until tender.

name: Spicy Carrots and Squash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041616/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spicy-carrots-and-squash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/8 cup low-sodium vegetable broth (or low-sodium chicken broth)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash, peel, and cut carrots. Wash and cut up squash.
Combine carrots and broth in a large saucepan. Cover and cook over medium heat about 5 minutes.
Add squash and cook 5 more minutes or until vegetables are just tender. Add more broth, if necessary, to keep from burning.
Stir vinegar, brown sugar, and mustard into vegetables.
Cook for a few minutes over medium heat until most of the liquid cooks off.

notes.text: Try this recipe without brown sugar.

name: Spicy Chicken and Potato Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022223/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spicy-chicken-and-potato-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1/4 pound chicken, thawed, cut up, and skin removed
6 small red potatoes, chopped (or 1 can, about 15 ounces, low-sodium sliced potatoes)
1/4 cup white rice, uncooked (or brown rice)
1 cup fresh peas (or 1/2 can, about 8 ounces, low-sodium green peas)
cayenne or jalapeño chilies, diced (1/2 teaspoon, optional)
parsley or cilantro, chopped (1/2 cup, optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot, brown onion and garlic in oil over medium to high heat for 5 minutes.
Add chicken to pot and brown for about 5 minutes.
Add water, potatoes, rice, and chili powder to pot.
Bring pot to a boil, and cook for 15 minutes.
Lower heat and cook for about 15 to 20 minutes. Stir pot every 10 minutes.
Add peas and cook for about 8 minutes. If using cayenne or jalapeño chilies, add that too. Mix well.
Remove pot from heat. If using parsley or cilantro, add that now.
Mix well and cover for 5 minutes. Serve hot.

notes.text: Tip for cooking chicken: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for chicken is 165 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.

name: Spicy Cucumber & Orange Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032147/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spicy-cucumber-orange-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash the cucumbers, oranges and lemon or lime under cold running water.
Slice the cucumbers. Peel and cut the oranges into small pieces.
Place cucumber slices and orange pieces in a medium size bowl. Add chili powder, lemon or lime juice and salt.

name: Spicy Fruit Cup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043342/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spicy-fruit-cup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup pineapple chunks, in its own juice

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the strawberries in half.
Open the can of mandarin oranges. Drain off the syrup.
Open the can of pears. Drain off the juice. Slice the pears.
Open the can of pineapple, but don’t drain off the juice.
Put the undrained pineapple, orange juice, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a mixing bowl. Stir together.
Carefully stir in the mandarin oranges, pears, and strawberries.
Refrigerate for 1 to 4 hours before serving.

name: Spicy Okra
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044234/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spicy-okra
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 packages (10 ounces each) frozen cut okra
1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 fresh jalapeño pepper, pierced 3 times with fork (or habanero pepper)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse okra in a colander under hot water.
Heat oil in a 10-inch heavy skillet over moderately high heat. Sauté onion for about 3 minutes.
Add tomatoes (including juice) and jalapeño (or habanero) pepper, and boil. Stir the mixture for 8 minutes.
Add okra and cook, gently stirring, until okra is tender, about 5 minutes.
Stir in salt and pepper and discard the jalapeño (or habanero) pepper.

name: Spicy Oven-Baked Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043413/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spicy-oven-baked-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Put chicken thighs, hot sauce, mustard, thyme, and garlic in the bowl and mix well.
Cover and refrigerate at least one hour or up to 24 hours.
Heat the oven to 450°F.
Put the chicken on a baking sheet and sprinkle with the salt and pepper.
Place in the oven and bake about 50 minutes until crispy and crackling. Serve right away.

name: Spicy Southern Barbecued Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022241/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spicy-southern-barbecued-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients except chicken in saucepan.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Place chicken on large platter and brush with half the sauce mixture.
Cover with plastic wrap and marinate in refrigerator for 1 hour.
Remove plastic wrap from chicken. Place chicken on baking sheet lined with aluminum foil and broil for 10 minutes on each side to seal in juices.
Remove from broiler and add remaining sauce to chicken. Cover with aluminum foil and bake at 350 °F for 30 minutes.
* Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Spinach and Meat Cakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033545/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spinach-and-meat-cakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound 93% lean ground beef (or lean turkey)
2 cups frozen spinach, chopped (may substitute with 2 bunches of fresh spinach)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat large frying pan (no oil).
Combine all ingredients except brown rice in a large mixing bowl. Mix well.
Form mixture into 12 small balls. Place in frying pan and flatten into patties using a spatula.
Cook over medium heat until cooked on both sides.
Serve over brown rice.

name: Spinach and Mushroom Enchilada Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215111/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spinach-and-mushroom-enchilada-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons olive oil (or oil of your choice)
3 yellow banana peppers (seeded, deveined, and minced)
1 cup green enchilada sauce (approximately one 10 oz can)
8 corn tortillas (6 inch, cut in half)
2 packages frozen chopped spinach (10 ounce box, thawed)
6 1/2 ounces reduced fat Monterey jack cheese (grated)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

Heat oil in a very large non-stick skillet. Add onion, garlic, and peppers and stir. Add mushrooms and cook about 15 to 20 minutes, until liquid evaporates. (If pan is not large enough, cook mushrooms in batches.)
Pour half of the enchilada sauce into a 13x9 inch baking dish.

Arrange 8 tortilla halves over the sauce in the baking dish. Preheat the oven to 350 °F. When mushrooms are cooked, stir in the salt and crumble in the oregano leaves. Drain the spinach, squeeze it dry, and mix it thoroughly with the mushroom mixture. Spoon half the mushroom mixture into the baking dish, carefully covering tortillas.

Set aside 1/4 cup (about 1 ounce) of grated cheese. Sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top of the mushroom mixture. Layer with the remaining 8 tortilla halves, then the remaining mushroom mixture and enchilada sauce. Sprinkle top of casserole with the remaining 1/4 cup cheese. Cover baking dish with aluminum foil and bake for 30 minutes, or until casserole is steaming hot in the center.

notes.text: Allow casserole to stand at room temperature 5 minutes before serving. Serve with pinto or black beans and salad.

name: Spinach Black Bean Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042041/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spinach-black-bean-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 1/2 cups canned low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine vinegar, oil, mustard, garlic, oregano, basil, and nutmeg.
Wash, drain, and chop spinach.
Add spinach, black beans, tomatoes, and onions to vinegar and oil. Toss well and serve.

name: Spinach Potato Pancakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031950/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spinach-potato-pancakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 cups spinach leaves, chopped and steamed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine the first eight ingredients in a bowl.
Stir in egg and mix well.
Drop batter in 1/4 cup sizes onto a well-greased hot griddle and flatten to form patties.
Fry until golden brown; turn and cook until the second side is lightly browned. Drain on paper towels and serve with applesauce, if desired.

name: Spinach Rice Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033557/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spinach-rice-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2/3 cup fresh spinach, washed and cut into thin strips
1/2 cup green onion, thinly sliced (including tops)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine dressing, soy sauce, and sugar. Stir into chilled rice.
Cover and chill salad.
Add spinach, celery, and onion before serving.
Shake on bacon bits if desired.

name: Spinach Salad with Apples and Eggs
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022103/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spinach-salad-apples-and-eggs
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup dried figs (about 16 figs or one 7-ounce package)
1/2 cup light honey mustard or poppy seed dressing

steps: To hard boil eggs: Place eggs in saucepan large enough to hold them in a single layer. Add cold water to cover eggs by 1 inch. Heat over high heat just to boiling. Remove from heat and cover. Let eggs stand in hot water about 12 minutes. Drain and fill pan with cold water; let sit 10 to 15 minutes. Peel and slice. (If making ahead, refrigerate cooked unpeeled eggs.)
Prepare other ingredients while eggs are cooking and cooling.
Wash, slice, and core apples.
Cut apples and dried figs into bite-sized chunks.
Wash and drain spinach.
To plate, divide ingredients evenly among four plates, top spinach with apples, eggs, dried figs, and croutons. Drizzle with dressing.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of 100% grape juice together with vanilla or lemon low-fat yogurt.

name: Spinach Salad with Apples and Raisins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022214/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spinach-salad-apples-and-raisins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 package (10 ounces) baby spinach, washed (or kale or other greens)
1/4 cup canola oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine spinach, apples, and raisins.
Mix all dressing ingredients and pour over salad just prior to serving.

notes.text: Granny Smith apples are recommended for salad, but any apple on hand will work. Try decreasing or cutting out the sugar if you like your salad less sweet. Learn more about:

name: Spinach Stuffed Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035631/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spinach-stuffed-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 package (10 ounces) frozen spinach, thawed and drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Thaw the spinach before you cook this recipe! After it thaws, drain any extra water from the spinach.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Wash and scrub the potatoes.
Bake the potatoes in for 1 hour till they’re tender and you can pierce them with a fork.
Wash and chop the green onion until you get 1/4 cup onion.
Put the sour cream, tofu, spinach, onion, pepper, and cheese in a mixing bowl. Mix well.
When the potatoes are baked, let them cool. Then use a spoon to scoop out the inside of the potato. Add the inside of the potato to the sour cream mix. Stir together.
Stuff the potato skin shells with the mixture. Sprinkle the potatoes with the seasoning.
Bake the potatoes for 20 to 25 minutes until they’re a little brown. Add extra cheese on top if desired.

notes.text: You can use part-skim mozzarella cheese in place of low-fat cheddar cheese.

name: Spinach, Tomatoes, and Corn
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042749/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spinach-tomatoes-and-corn
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place all ingredients in a large saucepan. Cover.
Heat thoroughly over medium-high heat, about 10 minutes. Add seasonings to taste.

name: Split Pea Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031249/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/split-pea-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook chopped onions in margarine in a large pan until tender over medium heat.
Wash and drain split peas.
Add water, split peas, and salt to onion. Bring to boiling.
Lower heat and cover pan. Simmer about 2 hours, until thickened.

notes.text: Optional: Cook a ham bone or pieces of ham in the soup. Remove bone and serve meat in soup.

name: Spring Vegetable Sauté
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033922/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spring-vegetable-saute
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
3/4 cup sugar snap peas, or green beans

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 2 minutes, then add the garlic and cook another minute
Stir in the potatoes and carrots. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook until almost tender, about 4 minutes.
If the vegetables start to brown, add a tablespoon or two of water.
Now add the asparagus, peas, radishes, salt, pepper, and dill. Cook, stirring often, until just tender -- about 4 minutes more.
Serve immediately.

name: Spring Vegetable Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034145/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/spring-vegetable-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1/4 head of red cabbage, finely shredded (about 2 cups)
2 medium ripe tomatoes, seeded and chopped
1/2 cup canned artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
1 cup green peas, frozen or fresh
salt and pepper (freshly ground black pepper, optional, to taste)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In large soup pot, heat oil over medium heat. Sauté cabbage, tomatoes, artichoke hearts, and peas for 10 minutes.
Add vegetable juice and water. Bring to boil. Reduce heat, add basil, and simmer for 10 minutes, or until all vegetables are tender and soup is piping hot.
Serve in individual serving bowls. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

name: Springtime Cereal
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031715/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/springtime-cereal
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3/4 cup wheat and barley nugget cereal
2/3 tablespoon (2 teaspoons) almonds, sliced and toasted

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the wheat and barley nugget cereal, bran cereal, sunflower seeds, and almonds in a medium bowl.
Add the raisins, the bananas, and half of the strawberries.
Gently stir in the yogurt and divide between two bowls.
Scatter the remaining strawberries over the top and enjoy!

name: Squash Salsa
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032151/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/squash-salsa
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15 ounces) low-sodium black beans, rinsed
1/2 medium green pepper, seeded and diced
1 medium summer squash, peeled, seeds removed, diced
1 teaspoon Adobo seasoning (combination or garlic, coriander, salt, and cumin)
lemon or lime juice (2 tablespoons, optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients except cheese in a large bowl. Let sit for 30 minutes.
Spoon over tortilla chips, cooked rice, or noodles.
Top with grated, part-skim mozzarella cheese and cilantro (optional). Serve hot or cold!

name: Squash Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021413/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/squash-soup
