conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 cup no salt added canned tomato sauce
5 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large saucepan, heat oil over medium heat.
Stir in onions, carrots, and garlic.
Cook for about 5 minutes, covered.
Stir in the tomato sauce, chicken broth, cooked squash, and herbs.
Bring soup to a simmer and cook, covered, for 30 minutes.

name: Stewed Cauliflower, Tomatoes, and Onions
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041136/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stewed-cauliflower-tomatoes-onions
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Chop the cauliflower into 2-inch pieces.
Peel the onion and chop it into small pieces.
Chop the tomatoes into small pieces.
Put the cauliflower in a medium saucepan and add 1 inch of water. Cook over medium heat, and let it boil for 3 minutes. Drain cauliflower.
In a large pan, heat the oil, and add the onion. Cook over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cauliflower. Cook while stirring for 3 minutes, until lightly browned.
Add the tomatoes and pepper. Cook for 5 more minutes.
Serve with a sprinkle of parsley and cheese.

name: Stir Fried Beef
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021155/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stir-fried-beef
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Trim fat from steak and cut steak into small, thin pieces.
In a large skillet, heat oil and sauté garlic until garlic is golden.
Add steak, vinegar, salt, and pepper. Cook for 6 minutes, stirring beef until brown.
Add onion and tomato. Cook until onion is transparent. Serve with boiled potatoes.

name: Stir-Fry with Chicken and Noodles
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042136/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stir-fry-chicken-noodles
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
2 chicken breasts, boneless, skinless, cut into strips
1 teaspoon fresh ginger, finely chopped (or 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger)
1/2 medium head of cabbage, thinly sliced (about 6 cups)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Bring 4 cups water to boil in a 2 to 3 quart saucepan. Add noodles, cover, and remove from heat (do not add flavor packets). Wait one minute. Drain noodles and set aside.
In a small saucepan, combine peanut butter, soy sauce and 1/2 cup water. Heat over low heat, stirring until smooth. Remove from heat.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat (350 degrees F in an electric skillet). Add chicken and cook until no longer pink when cut, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Add red pepper, ginger, and carrots and cook for 2 to 3 minutes. Add cabbage and cook 3 to 4 minutes or until cabbage is crisp-tender.
Stir in green onion, cooked noodles, and peanut sauce. Toss and serve right away.

notes.text: To avoid peanuts or peanut butter, try this stir-fry with sunflower seeds or sunflower seed butter.

name: Stir Fry Vegetables and Beef
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042555/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stir-fry-vegetables-and-beef
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 medium red or yellow bell pepper (sliced)
2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix spices, soy sauce, and water; set aside.
Wash vegetables. Shred carrots and slice mushrooms. Chop broccoli, peppers, and onions.
Heat oil in large frying pan and add meat when oil is hot; stir until brown.
Push meat to the side and in the middle of the pan add carrots, onions, and peppers. Cook them for one minute.
Add mushrooms and broccoli. Cook until they are tender.
Add liquid mixture and cook until bubbly.
Reduce heat, cover pan, and cook for two more minutes.
Serve over whole wheat pasta or brown rice.

name: Stove Top Green Chile Chicken Enchiladas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031704/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stove-top-green-chile-chicken-enchiladas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 1/2 cups extra-sharp cheddar cheese, finely shredded

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the oil in a medium saucepan.
Saute the chopped onion in the oil. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chilies, chicken broth, chicken and garlic powder. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Mix the cornstarch into about 1/4 cup of cold water until all the lumps are gone. Add to the chile and chicken mixture. Cook for 2 more minutes.
Tear the tortillas into strips and divide into thirds. Add them to the pan and cook until they are hot, stirring with a spoon from time to time.
Sprinkle the cheese over the enchiladas. Cover the pan and cook until the cheese has melted. Serve immediately.

name: Stove Top Potato and Cabbage Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042521/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stove-top-potato-and-cabbage-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
4 medium potatoes, peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in large skillet or Dutch oven. Add onions and stir over medium heat until golden.
Add potatoes and chicken stock. Cover tightly, reduce heat to low and simmer until potatoes are almost tender.
Add cabbage, cover and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Remove cover, sprinkle with cheese and nuts.
Let stand just until cheese is melted, about 2 minutes.

name: Stovetop Tamale Pie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033108/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stovetop-tamale-pie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans, drain and save liquid
1 can (15.2 ounces) whole kernel corn, not drained

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook beef in large, hot skillet until lightly browned. Drain off fat.
Stir in remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in corn.
Place chili in a 10-inch skillet. Heat thoroughly.
As chili heats, mix cornmeal and salt with water in a medium sauce pan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened, about 2 minutes.
Spread cornmeal mixture over hot chili to form a crust. Sprinkle with chili powder.
Cover and cook over low heat, with lid slightly ajar, until topping is set, about 10 minutes.
Prepare Chili: Prepare Tamale Pie: Optional - Top with light sour cream or low-fat yogurt.

notes.text: *Bean liquid is not included in the nutrition or cost analysis.

name: Strawberries, Watermelon, and Pineapple Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042334/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/strawberries-watermelon-pineapple-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup fresh pineapple chunks, or canned packed in natural juice (do not drain)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Stir fruit together in a medium-sized bowl.
Cover and chill. Serve as soon as possible.

notes.text: Refrigerate leftovers (or try freezing for a slush).

name: Strawberries, White Bean, and Edamame Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032722/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/strawberries-white-bean-and-edamame-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 15-ounce can low sodium white beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Cook edamame according to package directions, while preparing remaining ingredients.
Rinse under cool water and drain.
In a small bowl, whisk vinaigrette ingredients.
In a medium bowl, toss all ingredients except spinach and vinaigrette.
Serve on individual plates by nesting strawberry, white bean and edamame mix atop spinach.
Drizzle with dressing.

name: Strawberry Banana Parfait
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020444/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/strawberry-banana-parfait
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup bran and wheat flakes ready-to-eat cereal

steps: Stir banana and vanilla into yogurt and combine well.
In a 10 to 12 ounce glass, alternately layer the yogurt-banana mixture, strawberries, and cereal.
Serve immediately and enjoy.

name: Strawberry Kiwi Yogurt Pops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042338/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/strawberry-kiwi-yogurt-pops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: ice cube tray or small paper cups

steps: Cut kiwi and strawberries into small pieces.
Add yogurt to chopped fruit and mix well to combine.
Divide into 8 ice cube squares (or 4 small paper cups).
Place in cut paper straws or popsicle sticks.
Freeze and enjoy!

notes.text: Create your own yogurt pops and experiment with different flavors or try out one of these recipes:

name: Strawberry Mango Feta Toast Points
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045451/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/strawberry-mango-feta-toast-points
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup basil leaves (plus 2 tablespoons for topping)

steps: Peel and pit mango. Dice 3/4 of mango and 3/4 of strawberries; place in large bowl with feta cheese. Put remaining fruit, 1/4 cup basil, vinegar, and oil in a blender and blend.
Pour blended vinaigrette over fruit-feta mix and toss gently.
Chop remaining basil leaves.
Toast bread slices and cut each slice diagonally.
Top toast points with dressed fruit-feta mix and chopped basil.

name: Strawberry S'Mores
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020447/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/strawberry-smores
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse the strawberries in water.
Slice the strawberries.
Add the yogurt and strawberries to 1/2 of graham cracker.
Top with the other 1/2 of graham cracker.
Enjoy immediately.

name: Strawberry Yogurt Pops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042341/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/strawberry-yogurt-pops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: ice cube tray or small paper cups

steps: Cut strawberries into small pieces.
Place strawberries and yogurt into blender and mix until smooth.
Pour into 8 ice cube squares (or 4 small paper cups) and place in cut paper straws or popsicle sticks.
Freeze and enjoy!

notes.text: Create your own yogurt pops and experiment with different flavors or try out one of these recipes:

name: Stuffed Baked Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042644/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stuffed-baked-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 teaspoon hot pepper sauce (or to taste)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prick potatoes with fork. Bake at 425 degrees F for 60 minutes or until fork is easily inserted.
Cut potatoes in half lengthwise. Carefully scoop out potato, leaving about 1/2 inch of pulp inside shell. Mash pulp in large bowl.
Mix remaining ingredients with the mashed potato, except Parmesan cheese. Spoon mixture into potato shells.
Sprinkle top of each stuffed potato with Parmesan cheese.
Place on baking sheet and return to oven. Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until tops are golden brown.

name: Stuffed Bell Peppers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022117/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stuffed-bell-peppers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 5 bell peppers (red, orange, yellow, or green)

steps: Wash hands with soap and watr.
Cut a circular hole in the tops of the bell peppers. Remove seeds and membrane and set aside.
In a large bowl, combine remaining ingredients and stir until completely mixed. Fill the bell peppers with meat mixture.
Place the stuffed bell peppers in large stock pot on stove, with the tops facing up. Add 1-inch water to bottom of pot and cover.
Place heat on medium, keeping covered for 30 to 40 minutes until rice is done. Serve.

notes.text: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.

name: Stuffed Pasta Shells
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214948/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stuffed-pasta-shells
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 package (10 ounces) frozen chopped spinach, thawed
1 1/2 cups part skim mozzarella cheese, shredded, divided

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Lightly coat a 13x9x2-inch baking dish with cooking spray. Set aside.

Drain spinach by placing in a sieve or colander over the sink, or in a bowl and pressing with a spool to remove as much liquid as possible or squeeze out liquid with clean hands. Place spinach in medium bowl.
Add the cottage cheese, 1 cup of the mozzarella cheese, oregano, and pepper to the spinach. Stir to mix thoroughly.
Pour half of the spaghetti sauce into prepared baking dish. Add water and stir into the mix.
Spoon about 3 tablespoons cheese mixture into each uncooked pasta shell. Arrange in a single layer over top.
Pour remaining sauce over top.
Sprinkle with remaining 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese evenly over sauce.
Cover tightly with foil. Bake for 1 hour or until shells are tender. Let stand 10 minutes before serving.

name: Stuffed Summer Squash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031401/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stuffed-summer-squash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup white beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Wash and cut both squash in half, lengthwise. Remove the large seeds.
Steam the squash, skin side down, in a small amount of water in a fry pan or skillet until slightly tender (but not mushy).
Scoop out a good amount of pulp (1 cup), place in a bowl and mix with other ingredients (brown rice through Parmesan cheese).
Place the squash shells in a baking dish. Stuff the squash with the stuffing mixture.
Top with grated Parmesan cheese. Bake in preheated oven for about 30 minutes.

notes.text: Other Stuffing Options:

name: Stuffed Tomatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031740/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/stuffed-tomatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1/4 cup water, or more as needed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
Peel the onion. Chop it into small pieces.
Cut each tomato in half. Remove the part with the stem.
Gently squeeze each tomato half over the sink to remove the seeds.
Put the breadcrumbs into medium bowl. Add the spices and oil.
Mix well, slowly adding water to moisten the crumbs.
Use a spoon to press the crumb mixture into the tomato halves.
Lightly oil a baking pan. Place the tomatoes on the pan, with the cut side up.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the crumbs are browned and the tomatoes are soft.

notes.text: If you don’t have a box of breadcrumbs, make your own. Toast 4 slices of bread. Crush with a rolling pin or the side of a jar to make breadcrumbs. If you don’t have breadcrumbs or bread, crush 3 cups of a flaked cereal instead.

name: Sugar and Spice Cookies (from Better Baking Mix)
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032102/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sugar-and-spice-cookies-better-baking-mix
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup brown sugar, packed (or white sugar)
1/4 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Lightly grease baking sheet.
In a mixing bowl, combine baking mix, sugar, cinnamon, and raisins (optional). Stir to mix.
Put oil, egg, and vanilla in a small bowl. Beat with a fork to mix.
Add oil and egg mix to the dry ingredients.
Stir to combine. Dough will be thick.
Measure level tablespoons of dough. Drop on cookie sheet about 2 inches apart. Dough will spread 2 1/2 to 3-inch wide cookies as it bakes.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until edges start to turn brown. Be careful not to overbake.
Remove cookies from baking sheet while still warm.

name: Summer Breeze Smoothie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020728/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/summer-breeze-smoothie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup crushed pineapple, canned in juice

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place all ingredients in blender and purée until smooth.
Serve in frosted glass.

name: Summer Italian Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045203/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/summer-italian-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Combine onion, squash, tomato, and green pepper in a baking dish.
Sprinkle with oregano.
Pour the tomato sauce over the vegetables.
Bake, uncovered at 350 degrees F for 20 to 30 minutes.
Top with cheese and bake another 4 to 5 minutes until cheese is melted.
Refrigerate leftovers.

name: Summer Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042933/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/summer-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Wash and dry greens. Tear into bite-sized pieces and place in large salad bowl.
Add onion, mushrooms, walnuts, and parsley. Just before serving, toss with dressing.

name: Summer Squash Medley
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045908/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/summer-squash-medley
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In large skillet, heat oil.
To heated oil, add yellow squash, zucchini, and onion. Cook on medium heat until tender, about 10 minutes, stirring often.
Add tomatoes and simmer 5 minutes.
Season with garlic powder to taste. Add salt and pepper (optional), if desired.
Serve warm, topped with Parmesan cheese.

name: Summer Squash Squares
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044834/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/summer-squash-squares
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
3 cups thinly sliced zucchini (or yellow squash)
1 teaspoon dried parsley (or 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly and pour into a greased 13x9-inch baking dish.
Bake in preheated oven for 25 minutes, or until bubbly and brown.
Cut into 8 squares and serve while warm.

notes.text: Learn more about:

name: Summer Squash Stir Fry
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042928/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/summer-squash-stir-fry
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
2 cups summer squash, washed and sliced
seasonings, to taste, optional (suggested seasonings: garlic powder, pepper, cumin, thyme, basil, or oregano)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet, heat oil on medium-high heat.
Add onion and stir fry until onion is clear and begins to brown.
Add carrots and stir until carrots are tender and crisp. Add squash and cook for about 2 minutes. Lower heat.
Add seasonings of choice. Cook for 2 more minutes. Serve as a side dish.

name: Summer Vegetable Spaghetti
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042507/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/summer-vegetable-spaghetti
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups fresh tomatoes, peeled and chopped (about 1 pound)
2 cups summer squash, thinly sliced (about 1 pound)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

Combine first 10 ingredients (onions - black pepper) in large saucepan. Cook for 10 minutes over medium heat, then stir in tomato paste. Cover and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally until vegetables are tender.
Cook spaghetti in unsalted water according to package directions.
Spoon sauce over drained hot spaghetti and sprinkle Parmesan cheese over top.
Garnish with basil if desired.

name: Sunshine Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021901/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sunshine-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 1/4 cups celery, finely chopped, with leaves

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in medium saucepan. Add celery and onions and saute until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add water, orange and lemon juice, and hot sauce. Bring to a boil. Stir in rice and bring back to a boil. Let stand covered until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in almonds. Serve immediately as a side dish for a fish entree.

name: Sunshine Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042013/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sunshine-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 5 cups spinach leaves, packed, washed, and dried well
2 medium oranges, peeled and chopped into bite-sized pieces
1/3 cup "lite" vinaigrette dressing (around 15 calories per tablespoon or less)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss all ingredients together in a large bowl. Add dressing and toss again.
Serve immediately.

name: Sweet Acorn Squash
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043550/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-acorn-squash
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put each squash in the microwave. Heat for 1 1/2 minutes on high. This will soften the squash and make it easier to cut.
Cut each squash in half. Remove the seeds and loosen fibers in the middle.
Place the squash on an ungreased baking pan. The cut side of the squash should be face-up, and the uncut part of the squash should touch the pan.
Pour 2 tablespoons of juice into each half of the squash. Spread it evenly on the inside of each squash.
Bake at 400 degrees F for 30 to 45 minutes, until tender.
Season with cinnamon and nutmeg and serve.
serving_size: 1/2 of one prepared squash, 1/4 of recipe

name: Sweet and Juicy Raisin Tapenade
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032530/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-and-juicy-raisin-tapenade
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 large whole grain pita bread (approximately 16 wedges or melba rounds)

steps: Place tapenade ingredients in food processor.
Run until raisins, olives, and walnuts are finely chopped.
Can be made ahead and refrigerated.
Serve with melba rounds or pita wedges.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of 100% apple juice and hummus with cucumber slices and carrot or celery sticks. Notes on Raisins:

name: Sweet and Sour Cabbage
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041008/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-and-sour-cabbage
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 medium head of cabbage (about 4 cups when chopped)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the cabbage in half and rinse it with water.
Chop the cabbage into very thin bit-sized slices.
In a large bowl, combine ingredients and mix well.
Cover the bowl.
Chill in the fridge for several hours before serving.

name: Sweet and Sour Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031735/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-and-sour-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small saucepan, combine sugar and cornstarch.
Stir in vinegar.
Cook over medium heat until slightly thickened and clear.
Chill before serving. Store refrigerated.

name: Sweet and Sour Vegetables
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215341/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-and-sour-vegetables
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients except vegetables into bowl; mix and set aside.
Heat 2 teaspoons of oil in large skillet and add frozen vegetables. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes or until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Add sweet and sour sauce and cook for another 2 minutes or until mixture comes to a boil. Add water if it seems too thick.
Serve immediately.

notes.text: Infants and children under the age of 1 should not eat honey or recipes with honey in them.

name: Sweet Cornmeal Pudding with Ginger and Cinnamon
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031801/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-cornmeal-pudding-ginger-cinnamon
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 °F. Lightly grease 1-quart baking pan.
In a saucepan, heat 2 1/2 cups of milk to a simmer.
In a bowl, mix together the other 1/2 cup cold milk with cornmeal.
Add cornmeal mixture to warm milk, stir well.
Cook 20 minutes over low-medium heat. Stir often to prevent scorching. Cook until thickened.
Remove pudding from heat. Stir in margarine, molasses, ginger and cinnamon.
Pour into the greased baking pan.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes. When a knife is inserted and comes out clean, the pudding is done.
Cut into 8 squares before serving. Serve warm.

name: Sweet Potato and Apple Bake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050754/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-potato-and-apple-bake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 1/2 cups canned sweet potatoes, drained (save 2 tablespoons of the liquid)
2 cups apples, peeled, cored, and cut into bite-sized pieces
1/3 cup chopped nuts (pecans, walnuts or any other type)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Put sweet potatoes and apples in baking dish.
Pour the reserved, 2 tablespoons of the sweet potato liquid over the mixture.
Mix brown sugar, nuts, flour, and melted butter together in a small bowl.
Sprinkle over the top of the sweet potato and apple mix.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until the top is golden brown and bubbly.

notes.text: Granny Smith apples tend to work best in this recipe.

name: Sweet Potato Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040704/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-potato-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse sweet potatoes in cold running water and pierce with a fork.
Microwave sweet potatoes on full power until tender, about 15 minutes. Turn them half way during baking.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Remove skin from sweet potatoes and mash with hand beaters or food processor. Add the rest of the ingredients and mix until smooth.
Pour mixture in an 8 inch baking dish. Bake until casserole is firm in the center, about 40 minutes.
Remove pan from oven. Allow to stand for 5 minutes then cut into 10 squares.
Serve hot. Refrigerate leftovers.

notes.text: You may want to experiment with using canned sweet potatoes.

name: Sweet Potato Cheesecake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041926/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-potato-cheesecake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup gingersnaps, finely crumbed (or graham crackers)
1 cup sweet potatoes, peeled, cooked, and mashed

steps: Combine crumbs and butter.
Press mixture into bottom and 1 inch up sides of an 8-inch spring form pan. Set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, beat cream cheese, sweet potatoes, egg white, sugar, pumpkin pie spice, orange peel, and the vanilla until combined. DO NOT OVER BEAT.
Stir in milk. Carefully pour into prepared pan.
Bake at 350 degrees F for 60 to 70 minutes until center appears set.
Cool on wire rack for 45 minutes. Cover and chill thoroughly.
Remove sides of pan and serve.
Wash hands with soap and water. Crust: Filling:

name: Sweet Potato Harvest Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033333/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-potato-harvest-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 cups sweet potatoes, diced (about 2-3 sweet potatoes)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Drizzle diced sweet potatoes with 1 teaspoon of olive oil and roast in the oven on a baking sheet for 10 minutes.
Once sweet potatoes are cooked, remove from the oven and allow them to cool.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the sweet potato, apples, pomegranate seeds, and pepitas.
Whisk the remaining 1/2 tablespoon of olive oil, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper in a separate bowl.
Once mixed, add to sweet potato mixture and toss until the salad is lightly coated.

notes.text: Learn more about:

name: Sweet Potato Hash with Egg
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042906/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-potato-hash-egg
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 large sweet potatoes (cut into cubes, about 4 cups)
1 small yellow onion, peeled and diced

steps: Put sweet potatoes and water in a skillet and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low and cook about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the water has been absorbed by the sweet potatoes.

Add oil, sausage, onion, bell pepper and garlic to the skillet with the sweet potatoes. Cook about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion is lightly browned and the sweet potatoes are tender.
Divide the hash between 4 plates and return the skillet to the stove.
Reheat the skillet over medium high heat and when it is hot, add the remaining 1 teaspoon oil.
Add the eggs, one at a time, and cook about 3 to 5 minutes until the whites are solid and the yolks begin to thicken but are not hard. Flip the egg and cook for one more minute.
Top sweet potato hash with an egg and serve right away.

notes.text: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.

name: Sweet Potato Pancakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043510/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-potato-pancakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup complete pancake and waffle mix (or 1 8-ounce package)
1/2 cup mashed sweet potatoes, baked or canned (or winter squash or pumpkin)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients and stir just until large lumps disappear. Note: Over-stirring will result in tough pancakes.
Pour slightly less than 1/4 cup batter for each pancake onto skillet or electric griddle heated to 350 to 375 degrees F.
When pancakes bubble around edges and towards center, sprinkle with chopped nuts (if you choose). Then, flip pancakes.
Pancake is done when bottoms are golden brown.
Serve with applesauce or syrup.

name: Sweet Potato Pancakes with Balsamic Maple Mushrooms
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032407/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-potato-pancakes-balsamic-maple-mushrooms
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 medium sweet potatoes or yams (orange flesh)
1 pound cremini and/or white button mushrooms, quartered

steps: Microwave sweet potatoes until soft; let cool. Peel and mash potatoes, using an electric mixer.
Add milk, egg, and vegetable oil to potatoes; mix. Sift together dry ingredients and add to potato mixture. Mix on low until just blended.
Heat non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat; coat skillet with cooking spray.
Use 1/4 cup of batter per pancake, ladling into hot skillet. Wait until pancake bubbles and looks slightly dry on top before flipping over.
While pancakes are cooking, heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in another skillet (do not use non-stick) over medium flame.
Add quartered mushrooms and toss coat with oil. Let simmer, stirring occasionally, until juices run.
Add maple syrup and balsamic vinegar to pan. Let simmer until sauce reduces and thickens.
To serve, stack 2 or 3 pancakes, alternating with balsamic maple mushrooms.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with 8 ounces non-fat milk and 1 cup of field greens dressed with olive oil and vinegar.

name: Sweet Potato Patties
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033934/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-potato-patties
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash the sweet potatoes.
Bake the sweet potatoes in a microwave until they are soft.
Remove the peels from the sweet potatoes.
Put the sweet potatoes in a medium bowl. Mash them with a fork.
Crush the breadcrumbs on a cutting board with a rolling pin or jar.
Put the crushed breadcrumbs in a small bowl.
Shape sweet potato into 6 small patties.
Roll each patty in the crushed crumbs.
Heat the oil in a medium frying pan on medium heat.
Brown each patty on both sides in the oil.

notes.text: For variety, add some finely chopped apple.

name: Sweet Potato Pie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043739/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-potato-pie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups canned sweet potatoes, mashed (not canned in syrup)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Beat egg whites well.
Add orange juice, spices, brown sugar, orange zest, non-fat milk, butter, and salt.
Add mashed sweet potatoes and mix thoroughly.
Pour into pie shell and bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until firm.

notes.text: Use extra egg yolks in this recipe Sweet Potato Custard.

name: Sweet Potato Pone
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031310/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-potato-pone
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees F.
Combine all ingredients in a 3-quart saucepan.
Simmer slowly, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes.
Pour into well-greased 9-inch baking pan.
Bake for 30 minutes, stirring every five minutes for the first 20 minutes.
Smooth down the top and allow to brown.
Cut into squares and serve hot or cold.

notes.text: Sweet Potato Pone is a Liberian dish often served as a dessert following a family meal.

name: Sweet and Savory Peanut Butter Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215359/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-savory-peanut-butter-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon reduced sodium soy sauce (reduced sodium)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine peanut butter, apple butter, milk, soy sauce, and lime juice in a small bowl.
Whisk together until very smooth.
Store tightly, sealed in refrigerator.
Serve with celery or other crunchy fruits and vegetables.

name: Sweet and Sour Salad Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042923/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweet-sour-salad-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients and stir or shake well.
Chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour before serving. Store in the fridge in a bottle or container.

notes.text: Try this dressing on cut vegetables or salad. After serving, keep any leftover dressing in the fridge. Learn more about:

name: Sweetened Condensed Milk
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035345/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/sweetened-condensed-milk
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In order listed, put ingredients into a blender and blend until smooth.
Store in the refrigerator for up to one week.

name: Swiss Chard and Cranberries
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044423/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/swiss-chard-and-cranberries
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
6 cups swiss chard (1 pound stems chopped and leaves sliced)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a skillet, heat oil over medium heat. Add onions and cook until softened.
Add the Swiss chard stems and continue to sauté until beginning to soften.
Increase the heat to high and add the Swiss chard leaves and dried cranberries.
Once the chard is wilted, turn off the heat and cover the skillet, letting it rest for a few minutes before serving.
For softer greens, let them rest a little longer.

name: Taco Flavored Potatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044032/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/taco-flavored-potatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Wash and scrub potatoes well. Cut the potatoes in half, lengthwise and then into wedges.
Place potatoes in large mixing bowl, toss with the olive oil until potatoes are well coated.
Sprinkle the seasonings and corn meal over potatoes, toss again until coated.
Arrange the potatoes on a baking sheet.
Bake for approximately 30 minutes until potatoes are golden brown.

name: Taco Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041734/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/taco-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup kidney or pinto beans (dry-cooked or canned, drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef and drain any fat.
Add beans, cumin, and chili powder and heat through.
Toss lettuce, tomatoes, onion, and cheese in large bowl.
Spoon on meat and bean mixture and top with broken tortilla chips.
Prepare dressing by mixing yogurt and salsa. Serve on the side of the salad
Refrigerate leftovers within two hours.

name: Taco Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035037/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/taco-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups corn (2-15.5 oz low-sodium cans, rinsed and drained)
2 cans red kidney beans, low-sodium (15.5 oz each, rinsed and drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown meat in a pot over medium heat.
Put meat in a strainer to drain fat. Rinse with hot water.
Mix all the ingredients in the same pot and cook on low for an hour.

name: Tangy Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031833/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tangy
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 us fluid ounces juice concentrate (frozen orange/pineapple, thawed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix milk, concentrate, and nutmeg.
Shake well before using.

notes.text: Use this dressing on your favorite salad, as a dip, or as an ingredient in this Summer Salad!

name: Tangy Crisp Vegetable and Pasta Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042204/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tangy-crisp-vegetable-and-pasta-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup pasta (such as bowties, shells, macaroni, etc.)
1/2 red pepper (sliced, could use green or yellow)
1 tablespoon dried parsley (can use fresh if available)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions, but do not add salt to cooking water.
Drain, rinse with cool water, and drain again.
In a small saucepan, combine vinegar, sugar, garlic powder, and black pepper.
Stir over medium heat until sugar is dissolved, but do not boil. Let cool.
Rinse, drain, and chop remaining ingredients. Combine in a shallow container.
Add cooked pasta and vinegar mixture. Mix gently.
Cover and refrigerate overnight to allow flavors to blend.
Top with parsley and serve cold.
Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

name: Tangy Jicama Slaw
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041040/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tangy-jicama-slaw
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup canned Mandarin oranges (in light syrup)
1 1/2 tablespoons lime juice (juice of one lime)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut the jicama in half so you have a flat side for stability.
Peel the jicama using a small sharp knife.
Cut the jicama in small strips or grate it using a large hand grater.
Stir all the ingredients together in a bowl and enjoy.

name: Tartar Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020452/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tartar-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup low-fat plain yogurt (or low-fat sour cream)
1 tablespoon onion, minced (or 2 teaspoons dried minced onion)
1 teaspoon dried parsley (or 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, combine all the ingredients.
Serve immediately or cover and refrigerate until used.

notes.text: Try making with plain Greek yogurt.

name: Tastee Burgers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032844/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tastee-burgers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place lentils in a colander, rinse in cold water, and drain.
In a medium saucepan, bring water to a boil. Add lentils, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes.
Add onion and carrots. Cook 15 minutes more or until lentils are tender.
Remove from heat and cool slightly.
Stir in bread crumbs, egg, garlic powder, oregano, and salt.
Melt margarine or butter in large skillet. Drop lentil mixture by rounded 1/2 cupsful into hot margarine. Flatten mounds into patties and cook until firm and golden brown on both sides.
Top each patty with a thin slice of cheese.
Serve immediately.
Refrigerate leftovers within two hours.

name: Tasty Chicken and Veggie Packets
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022200/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tasty-chicken-and-veggie-packets
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons olive oil (or oil of your choice - divided)
4 teaspoons lemon juice (freshly squeezed (1 tablespoon + 1 teaspoon, divided))

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Cut four large rectangles of parchment paper or aluminum foil and fold in half to create a crease. Unfold.
Place each chicken breast in the middle of the foil or parchment paper and season with salt and pepper (if desired).
Top chicken with your choice of vegetables and seasonings.
Drizzle each packet with 1/2 teaspoon oil and 1 teaspoon lemon juice.
Fold the parchment paper or foil in half and then crimp around the edges tightly in 1/4-inch folds to create a half moon shape.
Using a spatula, transfer the packets to a baking sheet. Bake until the chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 165 °F, about 20 minutes, depending the thickness of the chicken breast.

notes.text: For a video demonstration of the preparation of this recipe, see Nutrition.gov. Optional ingredients are not included in the nutrient or cost analysis.

name: Tasty Fish and Veggie Packets
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020330/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tasty-fish-and-veggie-packets
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 cod fillets (4 ounces each, can also use tilapia, sole, hake, flounder, or other white fish)
2 teaspoons olive oil (or oil of your choice, divided)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Cut four large rectangles of parchment paper or aluminum foil and fold in half to crease. Unfold.
Put each fish fillet on the foil or parchment paper and season with salt and pepper.
Top fish with your choice of vegetables and seasonings.
Drizzle each packet with 1/2 teaspoon oil and 1 teaspoon lemon juice.
Fold the parchment paper or foil in half and then crimp around the edges tightly in 1/4-inch folds to create a half moon shape.
Using a spatula, transfer the packets to a baking sheet. Bake until the fish is cooked to an internal temperature of 145 °F, about 10 to 12 minutes, depending the thickness of the fish.

notes.text: See a video demonstration of the preparation of this recipe on Youtube. Optional ingredients are not included in the nutrient or cost analysis.

name: Tasty Low-Fat Cream Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251223170339/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tasty-low-fat-cream-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the onion.
Chop the celery into small pieces.
Put the celery and onion in a saucepan.
Add 1/2 cup chicken broth (save the other cup of chicken broth for later).
Cook these ingredients on low heat. Let the broth simmer for 2 to 3 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the dry milk, flour, and pepper. Add them into the 1 cup of chicken broth that hasn't been cooked yet. Beat till smooth.
Add this mix to the celery, onion, and broth.
Cook over medium heat till the soup thickens.

name: Tasty Veggie Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044255/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tasty-veggie-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix together ingredients.
Keep this simple dip in the fridge.

notes.text: A tasty addition to fresh veggies or a good sauce for tacos.

name: Ten Minute Corn Chowder
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024810/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/ten-minute-corn-chowder
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon vegetable oil (or oil of your choice)
4 tablespoons cheddar cheese (shredded, reduced fat - divided)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the oil and sauté the onion and garlic until golden, about 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, place the flour, milk, mustard, and seasonings in a small bowl and mix well.
Add the milk mixture to the skillet followed by the corn; mix well until the mixture comes to a boil and thickens, for about 3 minutes. Stir frequently to keep the mixture from burning.
Divide into four bowls and top each with 1 tablespoon of shredded cheese.

name: Teriyaki Lettuce Wraps
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041746/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/teriyaki-lettuce-wraps
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the water, cornstarch, and teriyaki sauce.
Add meat and water chestnuts.
Heat oil in a skillet or heavy saucepan and add meat and sauce mixture; stir until cooked through.
Serve in a lettuce leaf.

notes.text: Ground or thinly sliced beef or pork can be substituted for turkey.

name: Terrific Bean Taco
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050552/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/terrific-bean-taco
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook until soft.
Add refried beans to skillet. Heat thoroughly.
Spread refried bean mixture in taco shells or on tortillas.
Sprinkle with shredded cheese, lettuce, chopped tomatoes, and taco sauce, as desired.

name: Tex-Mex Skillet
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020810/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tex-mex-skillet
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound lean ground beef (or ground turkey or chicken)

steps: Rinse lettuce, bell pepper, tomato, and jalapeño. Rinse and peel onion. Peel garlic.
Chop or shred lettuce into bite-sized pieces. Mince garlic. Cut the jalapeño and bell peppers in half. Remove seeds with the tip of a knife. Dice peppers.
Over a small bowl, grate tomato and onion using the coarse side of a box grater. Collect all pulp and juices.
Grate cheddar cheese.
In a colander, drain and rinse beans.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook meat, bell pepper, and garlic until meat is lightly browned. Drain to remove fat.
Stir in frozen corn, beans, water, and spices. Bring mixture to a boil. Lower heat and cover. Simmer for 10 minutes, or until most liquid is gone.
While meat mixture is simmering, make a salsa. Add jalapeño and a pinch of salt to the grated tomato and onion. Stir and set aside.
Divide the meat mixture evenly among the 8 tortillas. Top each with grated cheese, salsa, and lettuce. Roll up and serve.

name: Thai Pineapple and Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050821/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/thai-pineapple-and-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 cups cooked brown rice (regular or instant)
2 tablespoons canola or peanut oil, divided
1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 1" cubes
1 red bell pepper, cut into chunks
2 cups cut broccoli florets and stems

steps: Cook rice according to package directions.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet. Add cubed chicken, stir fry 4 to 5 minutes until chicken is done. Remove from skillet.
Heat remaining oil. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add bell pepper, onion, and broccoli; cook 5 minutes.
Add pineapple; cook an additional 3 to 4 minutes.
Return chicken to skillet and stir in juice from 1/2 lime, fish sauce, chili sauce, and cilantro. Cook 1 more minute.
Serve over brown rice with lime wedges.

notes.text: Serve with 8 ounces non-fat milk.

name: Thousand Island Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215035/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/thousand-island-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 sweet pickle relish packets (2/3 tablespoon packets each)

steps: Wash hands with soap and warm water.
Mix ingredients together.
Chill and serve over vegetables or on a salad.

name: Three Bean Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022350/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/three-bean-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup green beans, cut (canned or fresh cooked)
2 cups yellow wax beans (canned or fresh cooked)
1/4 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix beans, vegetables and garlic cloves in a large bowl.
Mix vinegar, oil, and sugar in a saucepan. Heat until sugar dissolves. Cool slightly.
Stir seasonings into vinegar mixture. Pour over vegetables. Toss lightly. Chill overnight.
Remove garlic before serving.

name: Three-Grain Peanut Bread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034459/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/three-grain-peanut-bread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 °F.
Combine dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Using two knives, cut peanut butter into dry ingredients until it appears coarse and crumbly.
In a small bowl, beat together egg white and milk. Add to dry ingredients and mix well.
Spread mixture into a greased loaf pan. Bake at 325 °F for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Cool for 10 minutes and remove from pan.

name: Three Sisters Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021538/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/three-sisters-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
4 cloves garlic (minced or 1 teaspoon garlic powder)
2 cups summer or winter squash (diced - fresh or frozen)
1 1/2 cups corn (fresh or frozen or a 15-oz can (drained and rinsed))
1 1/2 cups cooked beans (any type or a 15-oz can (low-sodium, drained and rinsed))
1 can low-sodium diced tomatoes (14.5 ounces or 2 cups diced fresh)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large pan on medium heat. Add carrot and onion and sauté until onions have begun to turn slightly brown, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Add garlic, squash, and corn and continue to stir for another 3 to 4 minutes.
Add beans, tomatoes, broth, cumin, and pepper.
Allow soup to come to a boil and then turn heat down to a simmer until all vegetables are tender to taste (15 to 30 minutes, depending on the vegetables used).

notes.text: Try This: Change the vegetables and beans based on what you have on hand. Instead of cumin, try 2 to 3 teaspoons of Italian seasoning or 1 tablespoon of curry powder.

name: Three Sisters Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050652/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/three-sisters-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups red potatoes, cubed (or 1 1/2 cans, about 24 ounces, low-sodium sliced potatoes, drained)
2 tomatoes, diced (or 1 can, about 15 ounces, low-sodium diced tomatoes, drained)
1 can (15 ounces) tomato sauce, no salt added
1/2 cup frozen corn kernels (or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium whole kernel corn, drained)
1/2 cup yellow squash, diced (or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium sweet potatoes, drained and diced)
1/2 cup green squash, diced (or 1/4 can, about 4 ounces, low-sodium carrots, drained)
1/2 can low-sodium kidney beans, drained (about 8 ounces)

steps: In a small skillet, brown ground beef and onions over medium to high heat for 8 to 10 minutes. Drain fat.
In a large pot, combine cooked ground beef, water, and red potatoes.
Bring the pot to a boil and cook for 15 minutes.
Add all the other ingredients to the pot and bring to a boil. Lower heat and simmer for about 25 minutes.

notes.text: Tip for cooking ground beef: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef is 160 °F, as measured with a food thermometer. See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.

name: Tic Tac Toe Veggie Pizza
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025315/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tic-tac-toe-veggie-pizza
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3/4 cup pasta sauce, no salt added
4 sticks part skim mozzarella string cheese

steps: Place rack in middle of oven and pre-heat to 400 °F.
For Xs, cut carrot and bell pepper into small sticks about 2 inches long. For Os, cut summer squash into 12 slices. For grid, pull apart each cheese stick to make 4 strips.
Place pita rounds on baking sheet and spread pasta sauce on each.
Let kids build tic tac toe pizzas with cheese and vegetables.
Bake about 10 minutes or until cheese is bubbling.

name: Tofu with Broccoli
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024839/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tofu-broccoli
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro (or basil leaves)

steps: Put the tofu on a cutting board and cut it in half and then cut each half into 4 equal pieces.
Put 2 layers of paper towel on a cutting board and put the tofu on top. Let drain at least 20 minutes (and up to 2 hours).
Place a skillet over medium heat and when hot, add 2 teaspoons oil. Add the tofu, one piece at a time, and cook until golden, about 3 minutes per side. Remove the tofu to a plate and set aside.

Reheat the skillet and when hot, add remaining 2 teaspoons oil. Add garlic and scallions and cook until just golden, about 2 minutes. Add the broccoli and water and raise the heat to high. Cook until the broccoli is tender, about 4 minutes.
Return the tofu to the pan and add the remaining ingredients. Stir well.
Serve with a side of brown rice.

name: Tofu Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034446/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tofu-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

Prepare tofu by draining the water from the package and placing tofu between two plates. Put a heavy object on top and let stand for 10 to 15 minutes. Drain the water that collects on the bottom plate every few minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the mayonnaise, mustard, and soy sauce.
In a medium bowl, combine the diced tofu, celery, onion, pepper, and parley; stir in the mayonnaise mixture and toss gently to coat.
Refrigerate covered until the flavors are blended -- at least one hour.
Use as a sandwich filling or on top of whole grain crackers.

notes.text: You may substitute yellow mustard for brown mustard.

name: Tofu, Tomato, and Spinach Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034229/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tofu-tomato-and-spinach-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 package tofu, silken, firm or extra firm (14 ounce - patted dry and cut into ½ inch cubes)
4 cups spinach leaves, fresh (washed and dried, or 1- 10 ounce box frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat a 3 quart saucepan over medium heat; add oil and chopped onion. Cook onion until softened, but not brown. Stir in garlic and cook just until fragrant.
Add chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Add tomatoes and tofu. Lower heat and simmer until tomatoes are soft but not mushy (this takes just a couple of minutes).
Stir in green onions (optional), spinach, ground pepper and cilantro. Cook just until spinach is wilted.
Remove from heat. Taste for seasoning. Serve hot.

notes.text: Add extra vegetables that you have on hand, such as peppers, spinach, avocado, kale, etc. for more flavor and nutrients!

name: Tomato and Cucumber Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042957/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tomato-and-cucumber-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, combine the salad ingredients.
In a small bowl, mix the dressing ingredients together.
Pour the dressing over the salad. Mix well.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

name: Tomato and Garlic Omelet
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031502/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tomato-and-garlic-omelet
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 teaspoon olive oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 300 °F.

Cut the bread into cubes; toss with oil and garlic in a small bowl. Spread the cubes in a single layer on a baking sheet and toast in the oven for 15 to 25 minutes, or until golden brown, tossing once or twice. Transfer to a plate to cool.
Spray a medium pan with nonstick cooking spray and heat over medium-high heat. Pour in egg substitute.
When the egg begins to set, spread evenly across the bottom of the pan and reduce the heat to low.

Once the top layer of egg is almost cooked, sprinkle the cheese and basil on top and scatter the tomatoes and bread over half of the omelet; fold the unfilled omelet half over the filling. Slide the omelet on a plate and serve.

name: Tomato Basil and Bean Pasta Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045243/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tomato-basil-and-bean-pasta-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound pasta (ziti, bow tie or other shaped pasta)
2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
1 cup kidney beans (cooked or low-sodium canned drained, or try garbanzo beans or black beans)
mozzarella cheese, fat-free (cubed or shredded cheese, optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain and cool.
In a small mixing bowl, whisk together vegetable oil, vinegar, Dijon-style mustard, and pepper to make vinaigrette.
In a large mixing bowl, combine pasta, beans, basil, and tomatoes. Pour vinaigrette over top and toss together. Cover and chill at least 1 hour.
If desired, add nuts and cheese just before serving, tossing again to combine.

name: Tomato Basil Bruschetta
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021631/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tomato-basil-bruschetta
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
2 French bread baguette (or Italian, cut into 1/2 inch diagonal slices)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Combine tomatoes, garlic, onion, basil, and olive oil in a bowl. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste (optional). Set aside.
Arrange bread on a baking sheet in a single layer. Bake about 5 to 7 minutes until it begins to brown slightly.
Remove bread from oven and transfer to a serving platter.

Serve the tomato mixture in a bowl with a serving spoon and let everyone help themselves. Or place some on each slice of bread before serving. If adding the tomato mixture yourself, add it at the last minute or the bread may become soggy.

name: Tomato Basil Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050116/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tomato-basil-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
2 garlic cloves (crushed, or 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder)
2/3 cup non-fat dry milk (+ 2 cups water or substitute 2 cups non-fat milk)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium saucepan, cook onion in oil over medium heat, stirring frequently until golden brown, about 4 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute longer. Add chopped tomatoes.
Cook uncovered over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Spoon 3/4 of mixture into food processor or blender container; puree until smooth. Return to saucepan.
Add red pepper, basil, and reconstituted milk to the soup.
Heat until hot, but do not boil.
Season to taste with salt and pepper (optional).
Serve immediately.

name: Tomato N' Cheese Pasta
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034714/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tomato-n-cheese-pasta
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup whole grain pasta (shell, penne, or ziti)
1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions; drain.
In a small saucepan, cook onion and garlic in oil until tender.
Stir in tomatoes, basil, oregano, sugar, and pepper.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes. Add pasta to sauce.
Transfer to a greased 1-quart baking dish.
Top with cheeses.
Bake, uncovered at 375 °F for 10 to 15 minutes or until cheese is melted.

name: Tortellini Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231051106/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tortellini-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse beans. Put into a 4 or 5 quart heavy pot with 8 cups of water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium, cover, and simmer until the beans are tender (1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours).
Add 4 cups water and remaining ingredients to beans. Return to boil. Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer 1/2 hour, until tortellini and vegetables are tender.

name: Tortilla Chips and Bean Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042058/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tortilla
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Place tortillas in a stack on cutting board. With a sharp knife, cut stack into eight pieces, forming triangles or wedges.
Lay tortillas pieces out in single layer on baking sheet. Set aside while making dip.
Open canned beans. Pour beans in colander; rinse and drain. Place beans in a small mixing bowl and mash with a potato masher. Spread beans over bottom of baking dish.
Measure salsa and spread over beans.
Measure sour cream and spread over beans.
Grate and measure cheese; sprinkle over bean mixture.
Place lettuce wedge on cutting board. Slice into thin strips; set aside.

Place both the baking sheet with tortilla pieces and the dip in preheated oven. Bake about 8 minutes or until tortilla pieces are crisp and dip is bubbly. Sprinkle lettuce over dip and serve with tortilla chips.

notes.text: Flavor Change Options:

name: Tortilla Pizzas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035409/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tortilla-pizzas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 teaspoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice or margarine)
1 can (16 ounces) low-sodium, fat-free refried beans
2 ounces fresh or canned green chili peppers, diced
3 cups vegetables, chopped (try broccoli, mushrooms, spinach, and red bell pepper, or use your favorite veggies)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brush one side of two tortillas with water. Press the wet sides of the tortillas together to form a thick crust for the pizza.
Brush the outside of the tortillas with a small amount of oil or margarine. Evenly brown both sides in a heated frying pan. Repeat with the rest of the tortillas. Set aside.
Heat refried beans, onion, and half of the chili peppers together in a medium saucepan, stirring occasionally. Remove from heat.

Spread about 1/3 cup of the bean mixture on each tortilla pizza. Sprinkle with 1/2 tablespoon taco sauce, then top with 1/2 cup of the chopped vegetables, 1 teaspoon chili peppers, and 1 tablespoon cheese for each pizza.
Return to frying pan and heat until cheese melts. Top with cilantro, if desired. Serve immediately.

notes.text: Corn tortillas used for nutrient analysis. Using flour tortillas will change nutrition information.

name: Tostadas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041222/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tostadas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
On a baking sheet, arrange tortillas in a single layer. Spray both sides with non-stick cooking spray and bake for 4 minutes or until crisp.
If desired mix chili powder into refried beans.
Spoon 1/3 cup of refried beans on each tostada. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 10 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Top each one with lettuce and tomato.
Serve with salsa and sour cream (optional).

name: Tostadas Delgadas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042353/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tostadas-delgadas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Turn on oven to 350 °F.
Place tortillas on a cookie sheet and put in oven for 10 minutes or until crispy.
Wash lettuce and tomatoes. Shred lettuce and dice tomatoes
Spread two large tablespoons of refried beans on each tortilla.
Top with lettuce, tomatoes, and cheese. Add green onions if desired.
Serve immediately and refrigerate leftovers.

name: Trail Mix Bars
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033648/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/trail-mix-bars
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine dry ingredients in bowl.
Combine honey and sugar in pan and bring to a boil.
Add peanut butter and vanilla, stir until peanut butter melts.
Pour mixture over cereal and mix well.
Press into a 13x9 inch pan and cool.

notes.text: * Children under one year of age should not consume honey.

name: Trail Treat
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042649/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/trail-treat
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: square corn, rice, or wheat cereal (1 cup)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Choose the ingredients you want to use.
Measure the suggested amounts of chosen ingredients and add to mixing bowl.
Mix ingredients using stirring spoon and divide evenly into 4 storage bags.
Enjoy your Trail Treat!

notes.text: Ingredients used for costing and nutritional analysis:

name: Tropical Morning Treat
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044940/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tropical-morning-treat
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place orange juice in bowl.
Wash apple and dry. Remove the seeds and dice. Coat apple surfaces with orange juice to prevent browning.
Peel orange and break into sections. Cut sections into small pieces.
Peel and slice banana into 1/4 inch circles.
Combine all fruit and orange juice lightly in a bowl and mix together. Chill or serve immediately.

name: Tropical Overnight Oatmeal
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020341/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tropical-overnight-oatmeal
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Mix oats, milk, yogurt, and allspice in two bowls or glass jars.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Just before serving, add pineapple, banana, and almonds.

name: Tropical Yogurt Pops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042348/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tropical-yogurt-pops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup mango pieces, fresh or frozen
1/2 cup pineapple pieces, fresh, canned, or frozen
ice cube tray or small paper cups

steps: Place all ingredients into blender.
Blend on high until smooth.
Pour into 8 ice cube squares (or 4 small paper cups) and place in cut paper straws or popsicle sticks.
Freeze and enjoy!

notes.text: Create your own yogurt pops and experiment with different flavors or try out one of these recipes:

name: Tuna Apple Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031419/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuna-apple-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can tuna, packed in water (12 ounces)
2 pita bread, whole wheat (cut in half)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, stir together tuna, onion, apple, celery, raisins, and 2 tablespoons of dressing.
In another bowl, toss together salad greens with remaining dressing.
Carefully open pita breads and fill with equal amounts of greens and tuna salad.

notes.text: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.

name: Tuna Apple Salad Sandwich
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040551/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuna-apple-salad-sandwich
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 apple (such as Fuji or Pink Lady Washington)
8 leaves lettuce (Bibb, Romaine, green, or red leaf)

steps: Cut apple in quarters; remove core and chop.
In a medium-sized bowl, mix all salad ingredients, except tuna.
Gently fold in tuna.
Make sandwiches using lettuce and whole-grain bread (toasted, if desired), and fill with tuna apple salad.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of 100% orange juice.

name: Tuna Melt Burger
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231025416/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuna-melt-burger
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Drain tuna and break the meat apart with a fork.
Wash and chop the celery and shred the cheese.
Mix tuna, celery, cheese, light mayonnaise, dried onion, salt, and pepper into a medium mixing bowl with a wooden spoon.
Divide tuna mixture into six portions, place one portion on six slices of whole wheat bread. Then place a single slice of bread on top of each. (you will make a total of 6 sandwiches).
Wrap each sandwich on a square of aluminum foil, folding edges securely.
Bake about 20 minutes or until hot in the middle. Cool slightly before serving.
Remove from oven. Pierce foil to release steam before serving.

name: Tuna Pasta
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022059/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuna-pasta
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can water packed tuna (5 ounces, drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook spaghetti according to package; drain.
Heat oil in a large skillet or pan over medium heat. Add onion and broccoli (or zucchini). Cook until softened.
Stir in tomato-based pasta sauce. Bring to a boil. Turn heat to low and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add drained tuna into the sauce mixture. Stir just enough to heat the tuna.
Add salt and pepper to taste (optional). Add cooked spaghetti to the sauce. Stir the pasta and sauce mixture until mixed together uniformly.
Optional: Add 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese to cooked mixture of pasta and sauce.
Serve hot.

name: Tuna Pasta Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034638/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuna-pasta-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 12 ounces pasta shells, or other pasta
1 can cream of mushroom soup, reduced sodium (10.75 ounces, or cream of celery, or chicken)
2 cans water packed tuna (5 ounces each)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to package directions and drain.
In a large skillet or pot, cook onion and pepper in oil.
Add cream soup, diced tomatoes and tuna to onion and pepper.
Mix with pasta. Put in baking dish.
Cook at 350 °F for 25 minutes until bubbly.
Top with cheese and parsley if desired and return to oven for 5 minutes to melt.

name: Tuna Quesadillas
