attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044859/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuna-quesadillas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can tuna fish, packed in water (5 ounces, drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix tuna with mayonnaise.

Microwave Spoon filing onto half of each tortilla. Top filling with cheese and fold tortilla in half. Microwave on high for 60 seconds. Turn the plate halfway through cooking time. OR Stovetop Divide mixture onto two tortillas. Top with cheese and the remaining two tortillas. Spray a skillet with non-stick cooking spray. Brown quesadillas on both sides. Cut before serving.

name: Tuna Salad with Grapes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041104/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuna-salad-grapes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cans water packed tuna (5 ounce cans, drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine drained tuna, celery, mayonnaise and yogurt and stir.
Add grapes to mixture and stir gently.
Cover and chill until ready to serve.
Serve over lettuce leaves.

notes.text: Optional:

name: Tuna Salad on Greens
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022153/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuna-salad-greens
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toss lettuce, vegetables, oil, vinegar and herbs in a large salad bowl.
Mix ingredients for tuna salad in another medium sized mixing bowl.
Assemble salad by placing greens on a large plate. Top with a scoop of tuna salad.
Serve crackers on the side.

name: Tuna Slider with Green Chiles
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035746/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuna-slider-green-chiles
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 5 ounces canned tuna, packed in water (drained and flaked)
1 can chopped green chilies (4 oz. can)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro or parsley

steps: In large bowl, combine tuna, green chilies, celery, red onion, mayonnaise, and chopped cilantro; toss to mix well.
Add lettuce leaves to the bottom half of each roll.
Top with some tuna mixture.
Add top half of roll and enjoy!

name: Tuna Veggie Antipasto
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041311/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuna-veggie-antipasto
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup red onion (raw, chopped or any of your favorite raw veggies)
2 1/2 cups celery (raw, chopped or any of your favorite raw veggies)
1 can tuna, in water (5 ounce light, drained and flaked)
1 can white beans (15 ounces, or your favorite beans)
1/2 teaspoon dried dill (or 1 tablespoon fresh dill)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and trim vegetables. Chop into bite-sized pieces. Place in large bowl.
Combine vinegar, dill (or other herbs), garlic, and oil. Pour over vegetables.
Drain and rinse beans. Break up tuna into smaller chunks.
Combine vegetables, beans, and tuna; toss gently.
Marinate salad overnight to combine flavors.
Chill and serve as a light summer lunch or as a picnic side dish.

name: Tuna Veggie Picnic Sandwich
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231014648/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuna-veggie-picnic-sandwich
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup red bell peppers, thinly sliced
6 romaine lettuce leaves, torn in half

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, mix together tuna, mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and lemon juice.
Stir in carrots, red bell peppers, and celery. Place 6 torn leaves of romaine lettuce on half of the slices of whole wheat bread.
Spoon tuna mixture on top of the lettuce slices.
Place another torn lettuce slice on each tuna sandwich and cover with another slice of bread.
Wrap sandwiches in colorful plastic wrap or wax paper and keep chilled.
Your sandwiches are now picnic ready!

name: Turkey and Cucumber Sandwich
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231014631/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turkey-and-cucumber-sandwich
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 ounces turkey breast, thinly sliced (or fat free, low-sodium deli turkey)

steps: Mix the yogurt, dill, onion, pepper, and chopped cucumbers.
Divide the yogurt/ cucumber mixture on all 8 slices of bread.
Top the whole wheat bread with turkey and cucumber slices.
Cover with the white bread slices.

name: Turkey Burgers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050513/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turkey-burgers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine onions, turkey, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and parsley. Mix well.
Shape mixture into four patties.
Fry in a pan on medium heat or grill until internal temperature reaches 165 °F.

name: Turkey Gravy
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214806/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turkey-gravy
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/2 cups chicken or turkey broth, low-sodium
2 1/2 ounces giblets (cooked and chopped, approximately 1/2 cup)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Melt margarine in skillet over low heat. Mix in flour and salt. Stir and heat until bubbly.
Add broth slowly, stirring constantly. Cook over low heat for 5 to 10 minutes.
Add the cooked giblets. Heat a few minutes to blend flavors.
Store leftovers in refrigerator within 2 hours.

name: Turkey Meatloaf
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050529/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turkey-meatloaf
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon onion (dehydrated, or one small onion, minced)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Bake in 9x5 loaf pan for 25 minutes or until it reaches an internal temperature of 165 °F. Check the temperature with a meat thermometer.
Cut into five slices and serve.

name: Turkey Patties
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231023733/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turkey-patties
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix ground turkey, bread crumbs, egg, onions, and mustard in a large bowl. Shape into 4 patties, about 1/2 inch thick.
Spray a large skillet with cooking spray. Add patties and cook, turning once to brown other side. Cook until golden brown outside and white inside, about 10 minutes. Remove.

name: Turkey Pinwheel Appetizers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231051007/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turkey-pinwheel-appetizers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 8 ounces cream cheese, low-fat (garlic and herb)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place tortillas on microwaveable plate or paper towel; microwave uncovered on HIGH 10 to 15 seconds to soften.
Spread about 2 tablespoons cream cheese over each tortilla. Top with a slice of turkey, chopped tomatoes, and spinach.
Roll up lightly; then wrap in plastic wrap. Refrigerate 2 to 3 hours to blend flavors.
Cut each roll into eight 1-inch slices. Arrange with cut side down on serving plate.

name: Turkey Potato Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041212/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turkey-potato-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix turkey, celery, potato, onion, and green pepper.
Mix mayonnaise, mustard and salt. Stir lightly into turkey mixture.
Chill.

name: Turkey Salad with Orange Vinaigrette
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021218/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turkey-salad-orange-vinaigrette
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

In a jar with tight-fitting lid, combine all vinaigrette ingredients; shake well. If you don't have a container with a tight-fitting lid, place ingredients in a small mixing bowl and mix together with a whisk.
In large bowl, combine all salad ingredients; toss gently.
Serve with vinaigrette.

name: Turkey Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034918/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turkey-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or oil of your choice)
1 clove garlic (finely chopped, or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)
Italian seasoning ( or fresh herbs as desired)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in medium saucepan. Add onion, garlic, carrots, and celery and stir for 2 minutes.
Add potatoes, tomatoes, and water to pan. Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer 30 minutes or until vegetables are tender. Add turkey and cook another five minutes or until heated.
Season to taste before serving.

name: Turkey Stuffed Cabbage
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022110/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turkey-stuffed-cabbage
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse and core cabbage. Carefully remove 10 outer leaves, place in saucepan, and cover with boiling water. Simmer 5 minutes. Remove and drain cooked cabbage leaves on paper towels.
Shred 1/2 cup of raw cabbage and set aside.
Brown ground beef and turkey and minced onion in skillet. Drain fat.
Place cooked and drained meat mixture, bread crumbs, water, and pepper into mixing bowl.

Drain tomatoes, reserving liquid, and add 1/2 cup of tomato juice from can to meat mixture. Mix well; then place 1/4 cup of filling on each parboiled, drained cabbage leaf. Place folded side down in large skillet.
In skillet top cabbages with tomatoes, sliced onion, water, shredded cabbage, and carrot. Cover and simmer about 1 hour (or until cabbage is tender), basting occasionally.
Remove cabbage rolls to serving platter; keep warm.
Mix lemon juice, brown sugar, and cornstarch together in small bowl. Add to vegetables and liquid in skillet, and cook, stirring occasionally, until thickened and clear. Serve over cabbage rolls.

name: Turkey Tostadas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040831/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turkey-tostadas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups cooked turkey (cut into bite-sized pieces, or 2 cups ground turkey, browned in a skillet and drained)
1/4 cup cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese (shredded, low-fat)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375° F.
Wash and prepare vegetables.
In a large skillet over medium heat, combine turkey, taco seasoning, and water.
Bring mixture to boil, reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Place tortillas on a baking sheet. Bake at 375° for 4 to 7 minutes or until tortillas are crispy.
Spread tortillas with a tablespoon of beans. Top with 1/4 meat mixture and cheese.
Return tortillas to oven to cook for 2 to 3 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Top with tomatoes, lettuce, onions, and taco sauce. Garnish with yogurt and guacamole, if desired.

notes.text: Recipe analysis includes light meat turkey without skin.

name: Turnip Pancakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031616/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turnip-pancakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, mix flour, pepper, egg, garlic, soy sauce, and water in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in the turnip, carrot, and green onion
Heat half of oil in a large skillet over medium heat (350 °F in an electric skillet). Pour about 1/4 cup of batter for each pancake into skillet. Flatten with a fork into a 3-inch circle.

Cook until edges look dry and bottom is golden, about 3 to 4 minutes. Turn once. Cook until bottom is golden and crispy. Repeat with remaining batter, adding remaining oil as needed. Pancakes will be moist in the center.
Combine dipping sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Serve with warm pancakes.

notes.text: No rice vinegar? Try apple cider vinegar instead.

name: Turtle Apple
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020500/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/turtle-apple
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash apple. Cut in half (see notes).
Place apple half in center of small plate.
Put mandarin oranges next to apple for arms, legs, and head.
Enjoy your Turtle Apple.

notes.text: Adults: Make sure you use sharp knife to cut apple in half, remove core, and discard. Then, using a can opener, open mandarin oranges, and discard sharp-edged lid.

name: Tuscan Potato Skillet
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043705/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/tuscan-potato-skillet
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (or 1 teaspoon dried rosemary)
2 1/2 cups frozen green beans, thawed (12 oz. bag)

steps: Cut each potato into 4 wedges. Place in a large microwave-safe bowl and season with salt and pepper. Microwave on HIGH for 4 minutes. Stir and microwave for 4 minutes more.
While potatoes are cooking, cut each chicken tenderloin into 4 equal pieces.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook for 5 minutes or until nicely browned, stirring frequently.
Add remaining oil and potatoes; cook and stir for 5 minutes more to brown potatoes and fully cook chicken.
Stir in rosemary, garlic, green beans, lemon zest and juice. Cook for a few minutes more to heat through. Season to taste with salt and pepper.

notes.text: Use whatever type of potatoes you have on hand, are on sale, or offer the best price.

name: Two Bean Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040845/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/two-bean-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 can (about 8 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans, drained

steps: In a medium-sized pot, brown ground beef over medium to high heat for 8 to 10 minutes. Drain fat.
Add kidney beans, vegetarian beans, onions, chili powder, tomato juice, and pepper.
Cook over low heat for about 40 minutes. Serve hot.

notes.text: Tip for cooking with ground beef: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for ground beef is 160 °F, as measured with a food thermometer. Tip: USDA Foods macaroni products such as spaghetti, rotini, and macaroni are great additions to chili.

name: Vegetable and Rice Skillet Meal
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021830/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-and-rice-skillet-meal
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 teaspoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)
2 cups mixed vegetables (chopped cauliflower, peppers, carrots, or peas)
1 can low-sodium kidney beans (15.5 ounces, drained, rinsed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add onion, ginger, turmeric, and cumin, stir while cooking for 1 minute.
Add remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil, cover, and reduce heat.
Simmer 20 to 25 minutes. Serve hot.
Refrigerate leftovers with in 2 to 3 hours.

name: Vegetable and Turkey Stir Fry
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040034/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-and-turkey-stir-fry
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
2 thin slices of ginger root, minced
16 ounces cooked turkey, cut into 1/2 inch cubes
2 packages (10 ounces each) frozen vegetables, chopped (or fresh)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large frying pan on high heat.
Add ginger, garlic, turkey, vegetables, and salt. Stir fry about 1 minute to coat with oil.
Adjust heat to prevent scorching. Add sugar. If vegetables are tender, stop cooking at this time.
If the vegetables are firm, add 1 to 2 tablespoons of water, cover and cook for 2 minutes or until tender.
Serve at once, or if you wish to add a gravy, mix the gravy ingredients well, pour over vegetables and turkey, cook for 30 seconds.

name: Vegetable Cheese Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109214912/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-cheese-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 cups mixed vegetables, frozen or fresh, chopped
1/2 cup Swiss cheese, cut into small pieces

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Bring 2 cups water to a boil. Add vegetables, onions, salt, and curry powder, if using. Reduce heat, cover and cook until almost tender.
Mix remaining 1 cup water, dry milk, and cornstarch together in a small bowl. Add to partially cooked vegetables.
Cook over medium heat, stirring often, until thickened.
Add cheese and stir until melted. Add more water if too thick.
Top with green onions if desired.

notes.text: Store leftovers covered in the refrigerator.

name: Vegetable Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044339/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 yellow onions, peeled and coarsely chopped
3 16-ounce cans low-sodium dark red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
2 14.5-ounce cans no salt added diced tomatoes

steps: Put the pot over medium heat and when it is hot, add the oil. Add the onions, zucchini, sweet potatoes, garlic, and spices and cook, stirring from time to time, for 20 minutes.
Add the kidney beans and tomatoes. Stir and cook, covered, until the squash is tender, about 30 minutes.
Add the corn and cook until warmed throughout.
Serve right away or transfer to a container once cooled. Refrigerate up to 5 days.

name: Vegetable Dipping Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231044251/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-dipping-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix together all ingredients in a bowl.
Serve with your favorite vegetables.

notes.text: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey. Serving suggestion: Good with carrot sticks, broccoli, cauliflower, tomatoes, or any of your favorite vegetables.

name: Vegetable Fried Rice
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045442/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-fried-rice
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Make 2 cups of cooked white rice. Use the package directions to make the rice.
Chop 1/2 cup of celery and 1/4 cup of onion.
Heat the oil in a skillet or large frying pan.
Add the celery and onion. Stir fry for 2 minutes.
Add the vegetables to the pan. Keep stirring the vegetables until they are tender-crisp.
Add the cooked rice.
Sprinkle with soy sauce and pepper.
Stir fry for 2 minutes until the rice is heated and the flavors are blended.

name: Vegetable Medley with Salsa Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022251/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-medley-salsa-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 medium celery stalks, cut into 3-inch sticks
1 cup green bell pepper (or other color)
3 jalapeno chiles, finely chopped, seeded if desired

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Arrange vegetables on a platter.
In a small bowl, mix sour cream and salsa. Serve.
In a medium bowl, mix lime juice, tomatoes, onions, jalapeño chiles, cilantro, and salt.
Store salsa in refrigerator for up to three days in a covered plastic or glass container.
Fresh Salsa Preparation:

notes.text: Feel free to serve with whatever vegetables you have on hand. Could also be served with crackers.

serving_size: 1 cup vegetables and 1/2 cup salsa dip, 1/4 of recipe

name: Vegetable Pizza
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024942/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-pizza
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 cup green bell pepper, sliced (or red bell pepper)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F.
Spoon pizza sauce on pizza shell.
Put pizza shell on a cookie sheet. Arrange vegetables over sauce. Sprinkle on the cheese.
Bake for 10 minutes.
When baked, cool pizza for 3 minutes before slicing. Cut into 8 wedges.

name: Vegetable Rice with Tomatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045827/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-rice-tomatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium Mexican or Italian style tomatoes
green bell pepper, optional (if using: seeded and chopped)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in medium-sized saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the rice until just golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup of chicken broth if moisture is needed.
Add onions and garlic and cook for a minute or two.
Stir in the tomatoes and their juice, the rest of the chicken broth, salt, and bell pepper (if using). Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for about 20 to 25 minutes, or until the broth is absorbed.

name: Vegetable Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031754/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (15 ounces) whole kernel corn, drained
1 can (15 ounces) low-sodium chickpeas, drained (garbanzo beans)
1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium diced tomatoes (reserve 1/3 cup liquid)
1/4 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain corn, carrots, and chickpeas. Throw away liquid. Rinse vegetables and drain again.
Drain tomatoes but save 1/3 cup of the liquid.
Mix corn, carrots, chickpeas, tomatoes, onion, and red pepper in a large bowl.
Mix together all other ingredients in a separate bowl.
Pour over vegetables.
Cover and set aside for at least 3 hours in the refrigerator.

notes.text: Feel free to add other vegetables like green beans to the recipe. Instead of canned vegetables you could also use a 16 ounce bag of frozen vegetables. However, analysis was done with ingredients as specified in the recipe.

name: Vegetable Snake
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020508/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-snake
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash ingredients.
Put cucumber slices (see notes) on a small plate to form a snake.
Add 2 slices of tomatoes for eyes.
Enjoy your Vegetable Snake.

notes.text: Adults: Use a sharp knife to slice the cucumber and tomato into thin slices crosswise.

name: Vegetable Soup with Chicken
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040414/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-soup-chicken
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 ears corn (or 1 can low-sodium whole kernel corn)
1 pound fresh carrots, peeled and diced (or 1 can low-sodium carrots, about 15 ounces)
2 pounds potatoes, peeled and diced (or 2 cans low-sodium sliced potatoes, about 15 ounces each)

steps: In a large pot, heat the chicken and water over medium to high heat until hot.
Cut the kernels off the ears of corn.
Add the corn kernels and all other ingredients to the pot and boil for 10 seconds.
Lower the heat and simmer for about 30 minutes.

notes.text: Tip for cooking chicken: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for chicken is 165 degrees F, as measured with a food thermometer.

name: Vegetable Stew
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034950/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-stew
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups white potatoes, cut into 2-inch strips
4 cups summer squash, cut into 1-inch chunks
1 cup summer squash, cut into 4 chunks
1 3/4 cups canned low-sodium sweet corn, rinsed and drained (or 2 ears of fresh corn, cut off the cob)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put water and bouillon in large pot and bring to a boil.
Add potatoes and carrots and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients, except for tomatoes, and continue cooking for 15 minutes over medium heat.
Remove 4 chunks of squash and purée in blender.
Return puréed mixture to pot and let cook for 10 minutes more.
Add tomatoes and cook for another 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and let sit for 10 minutes to allow stew to thicken.

name: Vegetable Stroganoff
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034706/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-stroganoff
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 pound medium shaped whole wheat pasta (cooked)
1 14.5-ounce can diced tomatoes, no salt added (including the liquid)
2 tablespoons tomato paste, no salt added
1/2 cup plain low-fat yogurt (or light or heavy cream)

steps: To cook the pasta, fill a pot halfway with water. Bring it to a boil over high heat. When it has boiled, add the pasta and cook until just tender, about 12 minutes. Drain the pasta and set aside.

While the pasta is cooking, cook the stroganoff: Put a skillet over medium heat and when it is hot, add the oil. Add the onion, garlic, carrots, zucchini, peppers, and dried basil and cook until soft and golden, about 20 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook until the sauce comes together, about 20 minutes.
Put the yogurt and tomato paste in the bowl, stirring until smooth.

Turn the heat off and move the vegetables in the skillet to one side. Gradually add the tomato paste mixture to the other side of the skillet, stirring all the while. Turn the heat to low and cook about 5 minutes, until heated through.
Add the cooked pasta and stir until mixed.

name: Vegetable Tacos
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050317/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetable-tacos
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sauté onion, garlic and jalapeno, add cumin, salt, and black pepper. When everything is soft, add red pepper and mushrooms. Sauté for 2 more minutes.
Serve over tortilla and garnish with cut tomatoes and cilantro or cilantro sauce.

name: Vegetarian Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231014712/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetarian-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 medium green bell pepper, cut into 1/4-inch pieces
2 cans (14.5 ounces each) low-sodium whole tomatoes, cut into 1/4-inch pieces (or 8 medium fresh tomatoes)
2 medium summer squash, cut in to 1/4-inch pieces
1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans, rinsed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add oil to a large pot and sauté onions, bell pepper, garlic, and jalapeno over medium-high heat for about 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add chili powder, cumin, half of the chopped cilantro, salt, and pepper, and continue cooking for another 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the tomatoes, zucchini, and squash. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add beans, and continue to simmer for another 5 minutes.
Serve the mixture hot. Put remaining cilantro on top.

name: Vegetarian Collard Greens
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042159/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetarian-collard-greens
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes (increase to 1 teaspoon if you like food spicy)
2 1/2 cups collard greens, stems removed and chopped*
2 medium tomatoes, seeds removed and chopped**

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash all vegetables,* and remove seeds from the tomatoes.**
Collect, chop, and measure all ingredients before starting to prepare the recipe.
Heat the oil and butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, and cook for about 2 minutes until slightly soft.
Add the red pepper flakes and garlic, and cook for 1 minute. Add the chopped collard greens, and cook for another minute.
Add the broth, cover, and bring to a simmer. Cook for about 40 minutes until the greens are tender.
Add tomatoes.
Taste, and add a small amount of salt and black pepper if desired.
Serve hot.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Eat within 3 to 5 days.

notes.text: * Preparing collard greens: First, remove any damaged outer leaves. Fill a large bowl with cold water, and dunk the greens. Swish them around for a few minutes to help loosen any dirt on the leaves. Pour out the dirty water and fill the bowl with clean water. Swish the leaves under the clean water again to remove any additional dirt. Continue this process until the water in the bowl remains clear. To cut collard greens, fold each leaf in half with the stem at the fold crease. Either cut or tear the stem off. Stack several leaves on top of each other and roll the leaves up. Cut the roll of leaves into 1-inch thick pieces. ** Removing tomato seeds: Turn the tomato on its side so the stem faces to the right. Cut the tomato down the center and use a 1/4 teaspoon to spoon out the seeds.

name: Vegetarian Matzo Ball Soup
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045110/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetarian-matzo-ball-soup
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Stir together eggs, oil, and vegetable stock in a small bowl. Add matzo meal, dill, and salt. Stir until evenly combined. Cover and refrigerate 15 minutes to 8 hours.
Bring large pot of water to a boil; add a dash of salt. Using oiled hands, form dough into 12 1-inch balls.
Drop the balls one at a time into the boiling water. Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
While matzo balls are simmering, make soup by adding all broth ingredients and bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
To serve, spoon 2 cooked matzo balls into a bowl and ladle 1 cup of soup over them.
Wash hands with soap and water. To Make Matzo Balls: To Make Broth:

notes.text: Recipe cost can be reduced by substituting dried dill for fresh dill.

serving_size: 2 cooked matzo balls with 1 cup soup, 1/6 of recipe

name: Vegetarian Spaghetti Sauce
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041558/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetarian-spaghetti-sauce
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium skillet, heat oil. Cook onions, garlic, and zucchini in oil for 5 minutes on medium heat.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer covered for 45 minutes. Serve over pasta.

name: Vegetarian Stuffed Peppers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040513/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vegetarian-stuffed-peppers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 medium red, yellow, or green bell peppers
2 teaspoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 degrees F. Lightly oil a large shallow baking pan.
Cut peppers in half lengthwise and remove seeds. Arrange peppers cut sides up in baking pan and lightly oil cut edges of stems.
Halve cherry tomatoes and chop onion and basil. Finely chop garlic.
In a bowl, toss tomatoes, onion, basil, garlic, and olive oil. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Spoon equal portions of mixture into peppers and roast in upper third of oven until peppers are tender, about 20 minutes.

notes.text: Add any type of beans to add protein to this recipe.

name: Veggie Bean Wrap
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033838/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/veggie-bean-wrap
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 medium green or red bell peppers, seeded and chopped
1 can (15 ounces) low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a nonstick pan, sauté bell peppers and onion for 5 minutes over medium heat. Add beans, stir well. Reduce heat to low and simmer about 5 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine mangoes, lime juice, cilantro, and avocado. Set aside 1/2 of this mango mixture for topping.
Fill warmed tortillas with 1/4 bean mixture and 1/4 mango mixture.
Fold ends of the tortillas over. Roll up to make wraps. Top veggie bean wraps with remaining mango mixture.

name: Veggie Burgers
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045613/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/veggie-burgers
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can (about 15 ounces) low-sodium whole kernel corn, finely chopped
1 teaspoon cayenne or jalapeño chilies, seeds removed and finely chopped, (optional)

steps: In a large bowl, combine corn and cornmeal.
Add onions, green pepper, rice, chili powder, and pepper. If using cayenne and jalapeño chilies, add them too. Mix well.
Form the burger mixture into 6 equal patties about 1/2 inch thick, and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Spray both sides of the patties with nonstick cooking spray.
In a large pan, brown both sides of the patties over medium to high heat for 5 to 8 minutes.
Bake the patties in the oven for 10 minutes.
Toast the flour tortillas in the oven for 8 minutes.
Place patty on half of tortilla and fold tortilla over to serve like a taco.

name: Veggie Chow Mein
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020908/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/veggie-chow-mein
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 ounces spaghetti noodles (or thin flat egg noodles)
1 cup broccoli, cut into small pieces
1 cup green or red bell peppers, finely chopped

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare noodles according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
Cook onion and garlic with oil in a large frying pan for 1 minute over medium/high heat.
Add carrot, chicken bouillon, and pepper sauce. Stir.
Add broccoli, celery, and bell pepper and continue to stir.
Reduce heat to low and add noodles and soy sauce. Mix well over low heat for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add salt and pepper to taste.

notes.text: Add other vegetables as desired. Top with chives.

name: Veggie Dip
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215014/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/veggie-dip
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Measure cottage cheese and put in bowl or blender.
Beat with a fork or mixer, or in a blender, until cottage cheese is smooth.
Add the other ingredients. Stir together.
Store the dip in the fridge for 1 to 2 hours to let the flavors blend.

name: Veggie Loaded Mashed Potato Bowl
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032747/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/veggie-loaded-mashed-potato-bowl
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 7.5-ounce can chickpeas, low sodium, drained and rinsed
1/2 large tomato, diced (or 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.

Wash and scrub the potato with a vegetable brush. Cut into 2-inch pieces and place in a small pot. Cover the diced potatoes with cold water. Place the pot on the stove and turn the heat to high. Once the water comes to a boil, reduce the heat to a simmer. Cook the potato pieces until they are fork-tender but not falling apart, about 15 to 20 minutes. Remove from heat and drain the potatoes. Return the potatoes to the stove for about 30 seconds to ensure all the water is removed from the pan and the potatoes are dry.

While the potatoes are boiling, roast the chickpeas and broccoli in the air fryer. Toss the chickpeas with 1 tablespoon olive oil and the curry powder, lay them out on a baking tray in an even layer, and place in a 400 °F air fryer for 10 minutes, until crispy. Toss the broccoli with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and the paprika, and roast in an air fryer at 400 °F for 10 minutes. This can be done simultaneously if your air fryer has the space for both.

Remove the potatoes from the heat and add the Greek yogurt, olive oil, and granulated garlic. Mash the potatoes using a potato masher or a sturdy wire whisk. Do not over mix the potatoes, or they can become gluey. Adjust the seasoning with the salt and pepper.
While everything is roasting, prepare the cucumber-tomato salad. Dice 1/2 of a large cucumber and 1 large tomato. Combine in a bowl and toss.
To serve, add the mashed potatoes on the bottom, followed by the roasted chickpeas, broccoli, and cucumber-tomato salad. Top with optional garnishes and enjoy!

notes.text: Learn more about:

name: Veggie Noodles
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215414/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/veggie-noodles
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups vegetables (fresh, frozen or canned, drained*)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil water in a cooking pot. Add the pasta. Turn down the heat to medium-low; cook according to box directions. Pour pasta and water into colander to drain.
Add vegetables and spaghetti sauce to cooking pot. Cook over medium-low heat just until the vegetables are hot.
Return cooked, drained pasta back to cooking pot and mix together.
Sprinkle with cheese just before serving.

notes.text: * Fresh or frozen vegetables can be used. Just cook them before tossing with pasta.

name: Veggie Omelet in a Mug
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032538/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/veggie-omelet-mug
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup finely chopped mushrooms (or your favorite vegetables)
2 tablespoons low-fat cheddar cheese, shredded (or your favorite cheese)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lightly grease the inside of a 12-ounce microwave-safe mug.
Use a fork to combine the eggs, milk, salt and pepper in the mug and stir well. Mix in the vegetables and cheese.

Microwave on HIGH for 45 seconds. Stir. Return to the microwave and cook on HIGH until the mixture has puffed and set, 60 to 90 seconds. The omelet may look wet on the top but it will dry as it cools.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

notes.text: To make a meal, serve with a slice of whole grain toast and fruit.

name: Veggie Pizza Pita Pockets
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231031929/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/veggie-pizza-pita-pockets
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pita, whole wheat (cut around the sides, into flats)
Pick two from the following vegetables:
green and red bell peppers, sliced

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place one pita round on a plate.
Spread 2 tablespoons of tomato sauce on pizza.
Sprinkle various chopped vegetable over sauce.
Layer one slice of cheese on top of sauce.
Cover with the other half of pita round.
Microwave 35 to 45 seconds, or until cheese melts.
Slice in half, let cool, and enjoy!

notes.text: 1 tablespoon each of broccoli and red onion used for costing and nutrition analysis. Tips:

name: Veggie Quesadillas
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045549/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/veggie-quesadillas
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 medium green bell pepper, seeded and chopped

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash vegetables.
Spray pan with cooking oil spray.
Cook vegetables on medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring frequently. Remove from pan.
Spray pan with cooking spray. Place tortilla in the pan. Sprinkle with half the vegetables and half of the cheese.
Place the other tortilla on top. Cook on medium heat for 4 to 6 minutes or until the cheese starts to melt and the bottom tortilla starts to brown.
Flip quesadilla. Cook for 4 minutes or until tortilla browns.
Repeat steps 4 - 5.
Cut each quesadilla in half. Serve with salsa.

notes.text: Other Ideas

name: Veggie Stir-Fry with Turkey
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041752/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/veggie-stir-fry-turkey
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 3/4 cups low-sodium canned corn (or frozen, or cut from cob)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large frying pan over medium heat, cook ground turkey until no longer pink.
Add red peppers, onions, corn, okra, and squash and cook for 5 minutes until tender.

name: Veggie Stuffed Pita
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050246/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/veggie-stuffed-pita
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons vegetable oil (or oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash vegetables.
Remove the broccoli flowers from stems, cut the flowers into small florets, and put into mixing bowl.
Chop carrots into bite size pieces, add to into mixing bowl.
Slice the zucchini into thin slices. Cut each slice into quarters and put into bowl.
Grate the cheese and put into a separate bowl.
Measure oregano, pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder; mix together.

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Put the spices in the heated oil and then add the mixture of vegetables to the pan. Stir vegetables with a wooden spoon and sauté about 5 minutes. When the vegetables are slightly tender, remove from heat.
Spoon vegetable mixture into the pita. Top the hot vegetables with 1-ounce grated cheese.

notes.text: Substitute green pepper, mushrooms, or onions in place of listed vegetables.

name: Very Berry Muesli
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040935/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/very-berry-muesli
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 cup old fashioned rolled oats, uncooked
1/2 cup dried fruit (try raisins, apricots, dates)
1/2 cup apples, chopped (about 1/3 of a medium apple)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In medium bowl, mix oats, yogurt, and milk.
Cover and refrigerate for 6 to 12 hours.
Add dried and fresh fruit, and mix gently.
Serve scoops of muesli in small dishes. Sprinkle each serving with chopped nuts.

name: Very Berry Smoothie
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035423/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/very-berry-smoothie
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Peel and slice the banana.
Gather all ingredients and combine in a blender.
Cover and blend until smooth.
Serve right away or pour into ice cube trays and freeze. During the week, pop out the cubes for a quick on-the-go breakfast.

notes.text: Get an additional food group in your smoothie by adding 1 cup of spinach or kale.

name: Vidalia Onion and Tomato Salad with Grilled Tuna
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021346/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vidalia-onion-and-tomato-salad-grilled-tuna
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 pound ahi (yellowfin) tuna steak (fresh or frozen)
1 large head lettuce (Boston, Romaine or Bibb) (washed, dried, and torn into bite-sized pieces)
1/4 cup lemon juice, fresh or bottled

steps: Heat grill.
Whisk together dressing ingredients in a small bowl.
Cut tuna into 1-inch chunks and skewer and place on two or three 3-inch skewers; brush lightly with olive oil. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Grill skewered tuna until fish is opaque and flakes with a fork (145 °F); remove from grill.
In a large bowl, toss dressing with all vegetable ingredients. To serve, divide salad on four individual plates; top with tuna.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of non-fat milk and a slice of whole-grain bread.

name: Vinaigrette Salad Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043613/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/vinaigrette-salad-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 tablespoons vegetable oil (olive, canola, avacado, or cooking oil of choice)
4 tablespoons vinegar (cider, balsamic, or red wine vinegar)
1/4 teaspoon mustard (yellow, dijon, or brown mustard)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together.
Serve.

notes.text: Variations Sweet Vinaigrette (Basic Vinaigrette recipe plus) Italian Vinaigrette (Basic Vinaigrette plus) Honey Mustard Vinaigrette (Basic Vinaigrette plus) *Children under the age of one should not consume honey.

name: Waldorf Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215000/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/waldorf-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Place chopped walnuts on a baking sheet and bake for 12 to 15 minutes. Stir occasionally until they are evenly toasted.
Combine nuts, apples, celery, and raisins.
Stir together yogurt, sugar, and lemon juice. Pour over apple mixture and toss lightly.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

notes.text: Serve this dish with a whole wheat roll for a hearty meal.

name: Walleye Chowder
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231035308/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/walleye-chowder
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 pound walleye, thawed, cut into chunks (2 8-ounce fillets)
2 tablespoons fresh parsley or green onions, chopped

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat butter in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add celery and onions and sauté until softened.
Stir in flour to form a roux -- which is a mixture of fat and flour used to thicken sauces or soups. Slowly whisk in the milk.
Add the potatoes and bacon and stir gently. Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes or until potatoes are cooked through.
Add fish chunks and cook for an additional 6 to 8 minutes or until fish reaches the appropriate internal temperature.
Season to taste with salt and pepper. Garnish with parsley or green onions and serve.

name: Watermelon Gazpacho
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032201/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/watermelon-gazpacho
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: In a small bowl, mix 1 cup of cubed watermelon and 1/2 of chopped cucumber; set aside.
Process remaining ingredients in a food processor or blender until puréed.
Transfer all ingredients to a large bowl and stir.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of non-fat milk and whole-grain pita bread/chips with hummus.

name: Wheat Berry Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050520/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/wheat-berry-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 teaspoons chili powder, or to taste
1 8-ounce can tomato sauce, no salt added
2 cups beef broth, 99% fat free, reduced sodium

steps: Cook wheat berries in 3 cups of water for 1 hour until tender; add more water if necessary; drain.
Rinse with cool water and drain thoroughly.
In the microwave on medium heat, cook onions and green and yellow peppers for 1 minute, or until desired softness.
In a 4-quart pot, combine remaining ingredients with wheat berries and microwaved vegetables.
On stovetop, bring to a boil and simmer uncovered 1 hour or until desired consistency is reached, stirring occasionally.

name: White Bean Bruschetta
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260109215359/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/white-bean-bruschetta
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 whole-wheat French baguette, cut into 12 thin slices along the bias
1 cup canned navy beans, rinsed and drained

steps: Slice the baguette on the diagonal into thin slices (about 12 slices for a baguette).
In a large sauté pan, heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil over medium heat.

Place the bread slices in the pan and cook on medium high heat until sizzling and golden. Before flipping the bread, add an additional tablespoon of olive oil to the pan and cook the second side until golden.
For the topping, cook the onions and the remaining tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat until the onions are soft, about 7 minutes.
Add the garlic, basil, and oregano and cook another minute or two, until fragrant.
Add beans and continue cooking for another five minutes on low heat. Add the tomatoes and turn off the heat, allowing tomatoes to warm without cooking.
Drizzle the balsamic vinegar into the pan and gently stir.
Scoop heaping spoonsful of the tomato-bean mixture onto the grilled bread and enjoy.

name: White Chicken Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020820/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/white-chicken-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
2 cans (15.5 ounces each) low-sodium Great Northern Beans

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large saucepan.
Add onion and cook until tender.
Add green chilies, beans (do not drain), chicken broth, garlic powder, pepper, ground cumin, and chicken. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes or until desired thickness.
Serve hot, topped with cheese. Add parsley if desired.

notes.text: To reduce sodium content of soups, drain and rinse canned beans, use low-sodium broth, and add your own spices instead of using a seasoning packet.

name: White Chili
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231014644/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/white-chili
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)
1 chopped green chili (can adjust to taste)
6 corn tortillas (toasted and cut into 1 inch squares)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Sauté peppers and onion in oil.
Add green chili, garlic, spices, and chicken broth. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add milk, cooked beans, and cooked chicken. Allow to thicken before adding cilantro. Heat through.
Top chili with crisp tortillas before serving.

notes.text: *See our recipe to learn how to cook beans.

name: White Sauce - Thin
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041843/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/white-sauce-thin
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small pot, melt butter over low heat.
Add flour, salt, and pepper to mixture.
Add milk gradually.
Heat to boiling, stir constantly until mixture is smooth and bubbly. (The consistency should be like thin cream.)
Remove from heat.

notes.text: * Substitute low-fat (skim) milk with 1/3 cup powdered milk and water to equal 1 cup. Use for cream soups and stews.

serving_size: variable, label is for entire recipe

name: Whole Grain Strawberry Pancakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231033551/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/whole-grain-strawberry-pancakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Heat griddle to 375 °F or heat 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Grease with canola oil if necessary (or spray with cooking spray before heating).
In large bowl, mix flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt; set aside.
In medium bowl, beat eggs, vanilla yogurt, water, and oil with egg beater or wire whisk until well blended.
Pour egg mixture all at once into flour mixture; stir until moistened.
For each pancake, pour slightly less than 1/4 cup batter from cup or pitcher onto hot griddle.
Cook pancakes 1 to 2 minutes or until bubbly on top, puffed and dry around edges. Turn; cook other sides 1 to 2 minutes or until golden brown.
Top each serving (2 pancakes) with 1/4 cup sliced strawberries and 1 to 2 tablespoons strawberry yogurt.

name: Whole Wheat Garlic Bread Sticks
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231043605/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/whole-wheat-garlic-bread-sticks
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons olive oil (or cooking oil of choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 300 degrees F.
Spread each slice of bread with one teaspoon oil.
Sprinkle with garlic powder and Italian seasoning.
Cut each slice into 3 equal parts.
Bake in preheated oven for about 25 minutes or until crisp and lightly browned.

name: Whole Wheat Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041934/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/whole-wheat-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup margarine or butter, melted (or 1/4 cup vegetable oil)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F. Lightly oil or coat with non-stick spray the cups of a 12 cup muffin pan, or use paper muffin cups.
Mix together white sugar and cinnamon for topping and set aside.

In a large bowl, stir together flour, salt, baking powder, and brown sugar. In a glass liquid measuring cup, measure milk, then add eggs, vanilla (if using), and melted margarine or oil. Mix with a fork until egg is well combined with other ingredients.
Pour milk mixture over flour mixture and stir with a spoon, about 20 strokes, until flour is just moistened. Batter will be lumpy and thick.
Fill prepared muffin cups about 2/3 full with batter. Sprinkle about 1/4 teaspoon of cinnamon/ sugar topping over each muffin.
Bake in oven for 20 to 25 minutes until golden brown. Serve warm. Leftovers may be frozen.

name: Wild Rice Muffins
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021102/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/wild-rice-muffins
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 400 °F. Spray a 12-cup muffin pan with cooking spray.
In a medium bowl, mix bakery mix, sugar, and cinnamon.
In a separate bowl, mix bananas, milk, and applesauce.
Add banana mixture to dry mixture and stir.
Fold in wild rice and nuts.
Spoon 1/4 cup of the batter into each muffin cup. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes.

notes.text: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.

name: Winter Crisp
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231021204/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/winter-crisp
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Combine sugar, flour, and lemon peel in a medium bowl and mix well.
Stir in apples and cranberries.
Spoon into a 6-cup baking dish.
Combine oats, brown sugar, flour, and cinnamon in a small bowl.
Stir in melted margarine.
Sprinkle topping over filling.
Bake at 375 degrees F for 40 minutes or until filling is bubbly and top is brown.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
Wash hands with soap and water. Filling: Topping:

name: Wobbly Wonders
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041026/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/wobbly-wonders
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 3 tablespoons flavored gelatin, choose your favorite

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium bowl, dissolve gelatin in boiling water. Cool at least 30 minutes.
Pour milk into large mixing bowl and add pudding mix. Using an electric mixer, beat 1 minute.
Gradually add and beat in gelatin mixture. Pour into a 9x13 inch baking pan. Chill in fridge for several hours.
Cut fun shapes with cookie cutters or knife. Store in refrigerator.

name: Yellow Potato and Red Pepper Shrimp Sauté
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032733/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/yellow-potato-and-red-pepper-shrimp-saute
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 12 ounces frozen jumbo shrimp (peeled and deveined, no sodium-added)
1 medium fresh zucchini (cut in small chunks)

steps: Pierce the skin of each potato with a fork; microwave potatoes on high for 2 minutes. Turn potatoes over and microwave 2 more minutes. Remove from microwave and let cool slightly.
While potatoes are cooling, heat olive oil in large saucepan. Add garlic, onion, and bell pepper, and cook about 3 to 4 minutes.

Cube potatoes. Add juice, water, and vinegar to saucepan; bring to boil. Add shrimp, zucchini, potatoes, and seasoning. Return to boil, and simmer 5 to 8 minutes, until shrimp, potatoes, and zucchini are done. The flesh of the shrimp should be an opaque color.
Cut the lemon in half; squeeze juice from half the lemon into the saucepan.
Serve the Parmesan cheese and lemon wedges cut from the remaining lemon half.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with an 8 ounce glass of fat-free (skim) milk, one slice whole-grain bread, and 1/2 peach, sliced.

name: Yogurt Berry Parfait
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020511/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/yogurt-berry-parfait
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups low fat yogurt (or fat-free, any flavor*)
other optional fruit (raspberries, peaches, pineapple and/or mangos)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Line up 4 parfait or other tall glasses.
Spoon 1/2 cup of yogurt into each glass.
Sprinkle with granola.
Top with about 1/4 cup of fruit.

notes.text: *Low-fat vanilla yogurt used for costing and nutrient analysis. Note: Optional ingredients are not included in the nutrient or cost analysis.

name: Yogurt Fruit Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042702/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/yogurt-fruit-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix yogurt, cinnamon, and orange juice in a medium bowl.
Wash and chop the fruit and add to the yogurt mixture. Stir and serve.

name: Yogurt Pops
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231040516/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/yogurt-pops
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put the yogurt and juice in a bowl.
Stir together well.
Pour the mix into paper cups.
Stick a popsicle stick in the center of the mix in the cup.
Place the yogurt pops in the freezer until they turn solid.

notes.text: Here are some good flavor mixes for yogurt pops: You can buy popsicle sticks in a crafts store, or in the crafts department of a discount store. You can also use a popsicle mold.

name: Yogurt Popsicles
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042225/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/yogurt-popsicles
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 6 us fluid ounces frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a medium bowl, combine thawed juice concentrate and yogurt. Stir until smooth.
Place paper cups close together on a baking sheet.
Pour yogurt/juice mixture into paper cups.
Cover the cups with a sheet of aluminum foil.
Insert stick for each freezer pop by making a slit in foil over the center of each cup. The aluminum foil serves to keep the sticks in place as the juice/yogurt mixture freezes.
Freeze popsicles until firm.
Run warm water on the outside of each cup to loosen each popsicle from the cup.
Store leftovers in a sealed container in the freezer.

name: Zesty Citrus Coleslaw
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041003/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zesty-citrus-coleslaw
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 4 cups shredded cabbage (or 16 ounce bag of coleslaw mix)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix together the coleslaw mix, Mandarin oranges, and peanuts (if using) in a large bowl.
Stir in the Italian salad dressing and soy sauce.

name: Zesty Herb Salad Dressing
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041638/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zesty-herb-salad-dressing
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all the ingredients in a jar or bottle with a lid.
Put on the lid. Shake well.
Chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour before serving.

notes.text: Try this dressing on cut vegetables or salad. After serving, keep any leftover dressing in the fridge.

name: Zesty Lemon Fish
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034256/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zesty-lemon-fish
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/2 pound fish fillets (whitefish, cod, or halibut)
1/2 teaspoon canola oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Separate fish into two serving size pieces. Place on an ungreased baking sheet.
Top with onion slices.
Drizzle lemon juice and oil evenly over fish.
Sprinkle lemon pepper, parsley, and dust with paprika (optional).
Cover and let stand for 5 minutes. Bake at 350 °F for 20 minutes, or until fish flakes easily with fork.

notes.text: Cod used for costing and nutrition analysis. Use other herbs or seasonings as desired.

name: Zesty Orange Carrots
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042023/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zesty-orange-carrots
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 16 ounces carrots (peeled and cut into strips)
1 tablespoon butter alternative spread (0 g trans fat)
parsley, fresh (1 tablespoon, for appearance, optional)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Bring about 2 cups of water to a gentle boil in saucepan.
Add carrots and cinnamon. Cook for about 10 minutes, until just tender.
While carrots are cooking, wash an orange and cut in half.
Squeeze juice out of the orange (remove seeds).
Use a sharp paring knife to carefully remove the orange 'zest' from the peel. Try not to get any of the white part as it will taste bitter. Cut the zest into small slices.
When carrots are done, drain well.
Add the honey, margarine, and orange zest and toss into mix. Serve while hot.

notes.text: Could also use baby carrots

name: Zesty Pasta Primavera Salad
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020714/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zesty-pasta-primavera-salad
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 cups whole grain rotini pasta, uncooked*
*Other types of whole grain pasta may be used in place of the whole grain rotini.

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook pasta according to the package directions.
Drain and set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk oil, lemon juice, Italian seasoning, and red pepper flakes.
Add cooked pasta, cucumber, tomato, carrots, red onion, and Parmesan cheese to the dressing.
Mix well and chill for 2 hours before serving.

name: Zesty Skillet Zucchini
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231032119/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zesty-skillet-zucchini
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel the onion. Chop it into small pieces.
Chop the tomato.
Drain the water from the can of mushrooms.
Cut each zucchini into slices.
Put the tomato juice and pepper in a skillet or pan. Cook on high heat for 3 minutes.
Add the onion, tomato, and mushrooms.
Reduce the heat to medium-high. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the zucchini. Cover and cook for another 5 to 7 minutes.

notes.text: Serve this dish over rice or noodles, or eat it “as is.”

name: Zingy Lemon Chicken Pasta
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231045310/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zingy-lemon-chicken-pasta
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 1/4 lbs. boneless, skinless chicken breast (cut into 3/4-inch pieces)
2 tablespoons chopped chives or green onions (scallions)

steps: Combine flour, salt, pepper, and cayenne in a saucepan; gradually add chicken broth and skim milk, stirring with a wire whisk until smooth.
Place over medium heat and cook, stirring constantly, until thickened. Add mustard and lemon juice. Allow to cool.
Heat margarine and oil in a skillet. Add chicken pieces, green onions, and garlic. Sauté until chicken is just firm and cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Prepare pasta according to package directions and drain. Combine sauce, chicken, and pasta mixture.
Put into a 2 1/2 quart casserole dish. Sprinkle top with almonds, chopped chives, and paprika (if using).
Bake at 375 °F for 10 minutes or until heated through.

notes.text: Serving Suggestions: Serve with steamed broccoli, skim milk, and apple slices.

name: Zucchini And Tomatoes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231050959/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zucchini-and-tomatoes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 2 tablespoons butter (or cooking oil of your choice)
2 tomatoes (peeled and diced, or a 16 ounce can of diced tomatoes, drained)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Melt butter or oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add onion and garlic.
Cook until tender, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Add zucchini, tomatoes, and seasonings.
Cover pan, reduce heat, and cook until vegetables are tender.

name: Zucchini Au Gratin
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231041627/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zucchini-au-gratin
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and slice vegetables. Place zucchini, onion, water, margarine, and pepper in a frying pan. Cover and cook over medium heat for one minute.
Remove cover and cook until crisp-tender, about 10 minutes.
Turn with large spoon to cook evenly.
Sprinkle with cheese; toss lightly.
Serve at once.

name: Zucchini Bread
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231020845/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zucchini-bread
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1/4 cup vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 °F
Lightly grease and flour a 9x5 loaf pan.
In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs lightly. Add sugar, oil, zucchini, and vanilla and beat.
In a separate bowl, measure dry ingredients and stir to combine. Add raisins.
Add dry ingredients to the egg mixture. Stir just until all ingredients are moistened.
Spoon into loaf pan.
Bake at 325 °F for 50 minutes. Test for doneness by inserting a toothpick in the center. It should come out dry.
Allow loaf to cool 5 to 10 minutes before turning out onto a cooling rack.
Serve warm or allow to cool before slicing.

name: Zucchini Casserole
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231024754/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zucchini-casserole
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 can low-sodium canned tomatoes (14.5 oz Italian stewed)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Brown sausage and onion together in a skillet; drain.
Mix all ingredients together and place in a casserole dish.
Cover with foil and bake at 350 °F for 45 minutes.

notes.text: Instead of using the Italian stewed tomatoes, you could use fresh diced tomatoes with some Italian spices added.

name: Zucchini Coleslaw
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231042229/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zucchini-coleslaw
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain zucchini by pressing between layers of paper towels.
Put zucchini in large bowl; add cabbage, carrots, onions, and radishes.
In a small bowl, combine remaining ingredients.
Pour over vegetables and toss well.
Cover and chill at least one hour.

name: Zucchini Pancakes
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231034512/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zucchini-pancakes
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg
steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Grate zucchini and mix with the other ingredients, except the oil. Blend well.
Form the mixture into patties 3 to 4 inches in diameter.
Heat the oil. Cook pancakes for 3 to 4 minutes per side. Remove and drain on paper towels.

name: Zucchini Stir Fry
attribution: USDA MyPlate Kitchen recipe, public domain. Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20251231022416/https://www.myplate.gov/recipes/zucchini-stir-fry
conversion_note: vitamin D converted from mcg at 40 IU per mcg

ingredients.display: 1 tablespoon vegetable oil (or cooking oil of your choice)

steps: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and chop the onion.
Cut the yellow squash and zucchini into small pieces.
Chop the red pepper into small pieces.
Heat the oil in a frying pan. Add the onion.
Cook over medium heat, stirring quickly for 1 minute.
Add the spices and stir a few times.
Add remaining vegetables and cook for 3 to 5 minutes until vegetables are just tender.
serving_size: 1 1/2 cup prepared stir fry, 1/4 of recipe
